name: Un Mes Un Fan Tres 1+1=3 Cava Brut
description: A tender ribbon of golden bubbles carries through this non‑vintage Cava a melody of green apple blossom, citrus peel and a hint of chalky salinity, delivering both lift and minerality in refined balance. The mousse is lively yet gentle, sustaining a poised brightness that invites effortless enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in flute or tulip glass; pairs beautifully with seafood tapas or light shellfish for an elegant aperitivo.
palate: crisp citrus, mineral undertow

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville Napa Valley
description: A striking expression of Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon, this 2018 Acclaimed captures ripe dark fruit nuance and oak‑inspired warmth with refined restraint, offering a polished profile that honours its Napa Valley heritage. It displays structural harmony and textural elegance befitting a wine crafted from a celebrated vintage and a first‑rate hillside site.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below ambient to showcase its layered fruit and balanced tannins. Pairs beautifully with rich red meats or aged cheeses.
palate: rich black plum and black cherry core with mocha subtlety
finish: bold, firm texture with lasting oak‑tinged depth

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Acentor Garnacha Do Calatayud
description: This 2021 Acentor Garnacha by Isaac Fernández Selección hails from Calatayud in Aragón, Spain, crafted from century‑old bush vines planted on iron‑rich red clay at high elevation. It offers a layered aromatic tapestry of tar, allspice‑dusted red currants and cran‑pomegranate, unfolding into a dense yet lithe palate of citrus rind, fresh red fruits and saline mineral tension, finishing with depth and salinity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in medium‑bodied red glass to accentuate freshness. It pairs beautifully with roasted lamb, grilled chorizo or tomato‑based stews, inviting both meatiness and spice.
aroma: tar, allspice dusted red currants, cran‑pomegranate
palate: fresh, fat, juicy citrus rind and saline red fruits

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Acentor Rioja
description: An elegant expression from Rioja’s heartland this wine offers a seductive balance of ripe black fruits and subtle tobacco framed by gently integrated oak spices. Its refined structure unfolds with melting tannins and an earthy persistency that lingers graciously.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to reveal its nuanced fruit character; pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops, roasted mushrooms, or aged Manchego.
palate: ripe fruit driven with soft tannic support

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A wine of elegant gravitas from Napa Valley, the 2018 Acre Cabernet Sauvignon showcases dark plum and cassis aromas layered with leather, earth, and an exotic spice‑box perfume. Its palate unfolds with silky tannins and echoes of black cherry, cedar, black tea, and pencil‑lead, culminating in a supple, refined finish that speaks to its organic origins in Yountville.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in large Bordeaux glasses allow gentle aeration pair with grilled rib‑eye, truffle‑accented mushroom dishes, or aged Manchego.
palate: silky tannins black cherry cedar black tea pencil‑lead

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A refined expression of Napa Valley cabernet with regal poise that speaks of a storied vineyard heritage. The aromatic tapestry weaves bright black cherry and raspberry threads with sage and cedar nuances falling into a palate shaped by boysenberry, plum, graphite and a whisper of blood orange, all anchored by balanced tannins and vivid acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in a large-bowled glass to allow the raspberry and cedar notes to blossom; pairs exquisitely with rib‑eye steak or aged gouda.
palate: boysenberry and graphite underpinned by lively acidity

name: Adamvs Quintvs Cabernet Sauvignon Howell Mountain
description: A profoundly concentrated mountain Cabernet drawn from the steep, volcanic ash–lined slopes of Howell Mountain this 2018 Quintvs is an aristocratic and powerfully structured wine with a heart of wild cherry and blackberry framed by subtle woodland florals and forest floor nuance. Elegant yet forceful its texture is velvety and mineral‑infused with a vertical drive suggesting both youth and poised maturity.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a firm decant to soften the stately tannins and pair with richly roasted lamb or game dishes; its structure will reward cellaring of ten to fifteen years.
aroma: wild cherry, blackberry, lavender, wild rose, forest floor
palate: ripe fruit, fresh bay, wild sage, mineral‑laced drive

name: Gran Vinum Esencia Divina Albarino Do Rias Baixas
description: A refined Albariño from Rías Baixas that exudes pale straw hues and delicate green reflections, lifted by white blossoms, elderflower and orchard fruits. The palate unfolds with a gentle touch of sweetness and persistent floral echoes, its poised acidity imparting a fresh, inviting vitality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 – 12 °C. Elegant with shellfish, light fish or as an aperitif that draws the diner back sip after sip.
palate: delicate sweetness, balanced acidity, floral return

name: Paul Aegerter Bourgogne Rouge
description: The 2021 Paul Aegerter Bourgogne Rouge presents a refined interplay of bright red berries and subtle floral nuances supported by gentle oak undertones, all framed in a poised structure that speaks of Burgundian temperament.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature to heighten vibrancy; pairs beautifully with roast chicken, mushroom‑accented dishes, or soft ripened cheeses.
palate: structured yet supple
drinkWindow: to drink now or within 5–10 years

name: Château Grand Portail Bordeaux Rouge
description: A finely balanced expression of Bordeaux from the 2018 vintage elegantly centred on generous Merlot with supporting Cabernet structure offering dark bramble fruit framed by subtle spice and gentle oak nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled; this plush Bordeaux Rouge welcomes roasted lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes with poise.
palate: rich Merlot‑driven fruit with structured Cabernet depth

name: Ano Cero Cabernet Sauvignon la Consulta Mendoza
description: A terroir‑driven Cabernet Sauvignon from La Consulta in Mendoza, offering a graceful fusion of ripe black‑plum and cassis framed by subtle Asian spice and a whisper of savory herbaceousness. The palate is plush yet refined with soft tannins enveloping dark berry fruit and a hint of smoky nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in broad Bordeaux glasses to reveal its fresh fruit and spice layers, ideal alongside grilled red meats or aged cheeses.
aroma: ripe black plum and cassis with Asian spice
palate: plush dark berries with soft tannins and smoky nuance

name: Ano Cero Malbec la Consulta Mendoza
appellation: La Consulta, Valle de Uco, Mendoza
description: From La Consulta in Mendoza this 2024 Malbec Año Cero by Altocedro offers a richly perfumed bouquet of currant and violet with savory dried‑herb notes it unfolds with silky, medium‑to‑full body and inviting dark‑fruit depth that is both lively and beautifully balanced. The wine’s concrete‑fermented pedigree showcases terroir elegance and restrained power.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C ideally with grilled meats or hearty vegetarian dishes its freshness and silky tannins make it a versatile companion.
aroma: currant and violet with dried‑herb nuance
palate: silky medium‑full body, juicy dark fruit
finish: balanced and lingering with gentle tannins

name: La Consulta Select Blend Mendoza
description: A deep ruby Mendoza red wine that exudes finesse and old‑world character, featuring co‑fermented Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Tempranillo, Petit Verdot, and Syrah. It reveals plush, velvety tannins embraced by layers of ripe black fruit, dried lavender and a whisper of pepper.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in broad glasses to showcase the wine’s elegant structure. Ideal companions include grilled lamb or rich mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe black fruit, dried lavender, pepper
palate: velvety, layered, harmonious co‑ferment complexity

name: Malbec Gran Reserva
description: This 2019 Altocedro Malbec Gran Reserva, born at altitude in La Consulta within Mendoza’s Uco Valley, unfolds with a presence of ripe plum, cedar and soft violet notes, wrapped in smoky oak from an extended 24‑month French barrel aging. It offers a polished, full‑bodied expression of Malbec marked by depth and finesse, its intricate texture and saline undercurrent offering sustained complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 16–17 °C, perhaps after an hour’s decanting, to appreciate the wine’s layered fruit, refined tannins and lingering finish alongside red meats or aged cheeses.
palate: full‑bodied refined tannins depth

name: Malbec Gran Reserve
description: A richly textured Malbec drawn from century‑old vines in La Consulta, this 2021 Altocedro Gran Reserva exhibits a deep ruby hue and a compelling fusion of black and blue fruit with savory accents. The palate is full‑bodied yet harmoniously balanced, showcasing polished tannins, saline nuance and a refined finish that speaks of its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at about 15 °C to highlight its vivid fruit and elegant acidity. Pairs beautifully with grilled lamb or aged cheeses.
aroma: blackberry and plum with savory spice
palate: full‑bodied, polished tannins with saline accent

name: Malbec Reserva
description: A sumptuous Mendoza Malbec that weaves together dark plum and blackberry fruit with sensuous mocha and Asian spice notes, offering a plush texture and a gracefully composed presence on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature to reveal its creamy texture and pair with grilled red meats or savory aged cheeses to mirror its dark fruit and chocolate undertones.
palate: plush, creamy, mocha-inflected dark fruit

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Sonoma County
description: A wine of noble bearing with deep black cherry and cassis at its core framed by violet and sage whispers it unfolds in the glass with polished structure and lingering spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperatures to elevate its silkiness, ideal with grilled lamb or aged gouda.
palate: cassiss, blackberry, plum with vanilla bean and clove

name: Domaine Grand Romane Gigondas Cuvee Prestige
description: A refined and generous Gigondas that marries ripe dark berry and subtle plum elements with an undercurrent of pepper and soft herbes de Provence, framed by a gentle kiss of oak that imparts precision without excess.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature around 16 °C, to accompany richly flavored grilled meats or classic Provençal stews.
aroma: ripe dark berries with peppery spice
palate: supple plum fruit with subtle herbes de Provence

name: Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: This 2009 Ambroise Clos Vougeot Grand Cru unfurls with intense violet‑tinged ruby hues enticing the eye, offering scents of raspberries intertwined with licorice and pepper and a palate that feels rich velvet‑like, opulent and persistent yet balanced with savoury tension
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to 15 °C alongside tender roast lamb or succulent veal—this wine revels in slow revelation yet is approachable now with graceful ageing ahead
palate: rich, opulent, velvety, persistent

name: Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Vaucrains
description: This Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Les Vaucrains” from Maison Ambroise 2009 unfolds with formidable depth and refined power, exhibiting poised dark red fruit underpinned by a clay‑limestone minerality. It is robust and opulent yet balanced by structure, evolving from wild berry perfume toward subtle underbrush and leather nuance over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C with rich game or aged Époisses or Langres cheese, and allow a decant to reveal its evolving complexity.
aroma: wild red berries evolving to underbrush
palate: robust, fruity, slightly spicy
drinkWindow: drink from 2014 onward; long‑term cellaring possible

name: Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Vaucrains
description: This 2011 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Les Vaucrains” from Ambroise carries an aristocratic intensity and vibrant red fruit character emerging from layers of clay‑limestone terroir, refined by patient élevage in new oak. It offers compelling presence while retaining an elegant framework, marrying power and finesse in the classic Burgundy fashion.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15°C, and pair with richly flavored game or aged regional cheeses to balance its depth and structure.
palate: robust, fruity, slightly spicy

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: Amiral de Beychevelle 2019 presents a cloak of deep, dark ruby purple, the bouquet unfolding layers of black cherry, blackberry and violet with an undercurrent of fine spice. The palate is fresh and balanced, the tannins noble and caressing, leading to a generous yet elegant finish framed by lingering fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 17 °C to enhance its freshness, pairing beautifully with richly roasted meats or savory pâtés.
palate: fresh, balanced, noble tannins

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: A radiant expression of Saint‑Julien borne of dedicated plots and careful vinification this wine presents floral overtones, spice and vivid freshness balanced by structured yet supple tannins drawn with refined poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in a large Burgundy‑style glass allow a swirl to reveal red and black fruit nuances. Pair with roast duck or aged comté cheese.
aroma: floral spice and fresh red berries
palate: silky tannins with red fruit and gentle spice

name: Amiral de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: A luminous and refined Saint‑Julien, this 2022 Amiral de Beychevelle greets with a dense brilliant robe and immediate freshness that sets its fruit aglow: poised blackberry, black cherry and cassis threaded with subtle spice and velvety tannins, delivering early appeal tempered by structural promise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool to enhance its poised freshness: ideal with roast lamb, aged duck breast or a mushroom‑dotted cassoulet.
aroma: ripe black cherry, cassis, subtle spice
palate: velvety tannins, fresh vibrant fruit, smooth structure
finish: balanced, long and energetic with a velvety close

name: Domaine Yannick Amirault Bourgeuil la Coudraye
description: Yannick Amirault's 2017 Bourgueil La Coudraye is a rounded Cabernet Franc with fresh red and dark fruit, woodland nuance, and gentle spice. Oak aging adds breadth while the wine retains the croquant freshness of its sandy terrace soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14-16°C with white meats, rabbit, black pudding, or Loire goat cheese.
palate: Round, ample, fresh, softly structured

name: Flare Sparkling Moscatel Do Valencia
description: This non‑vintage Flare Sparkling Moscato from Valencia presents a pale straw hue with delicate effervescence and floral‑fruited aromas of pear, lychee, melon and white blossom brightened by a whisper of spice. The palate offers frothy sweetness tempered by mineral lift and a vivacious, crystalline energy that prevents the finish from feeling cloying.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as a celebratory aperitif or alongside a platter of fresh fruit or light desserts for a playful, refreshing contrast to its sweet charm.
aroma: pear, lychee, melon and white flowers with nutmeg brightness
palate: frothy tropical fruit sweetness enlivened by mineral spice

name: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Pomone
description: This 2018 Bourgogne Rouge Sélection Pomone by Domaine Anne Parent conjures an elegant expression of Pommard terroir distilled into regional Burgundian finesse, revealing vibrant red fruits with a whisper of earthbound complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C to showcase its graceful structure; pair with mushroom ragout or roasted poultry.
palate: ripe cherry, plum, mushroom

name: Domaine Anne Parent Bourgogne Selection Pomone
description: A most refined Bourgogne, this 2018 “Sélection Pomone” by Domaine Anne Parent presents a graceful depth that belies its regional classification, born of venerable Pommard and Premier Cru plots, yielding an elegant yet profound expression of Pinot Noir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 13 °C, in a large-bowled red glass to highlight its red fruit and underbrush nuances; pairs exquisitely with game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: strawberry cherry with subtle rustic underbrush
palate: ripe cherry and plum with a soft tannic grip
finish: elegant, lingering of earth and red fruit

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru Croix Noires
description: This 2018 Pommard 1er Cru Les Croix Noires from Anne Parent reveals a delicate perfume of wild red berries and pressed rose petals, unfolding toward a refined structure of silky tannins and well‑integrated oak. The wine’s sophistication speaks of both the textural grace and terroir‑driven depth that define this rare Premier Cru from a revered Burgundian domaine.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool around 15 °C after gentle decanting to coax its floral spice forward. Pair with roast duck, game birds or mushroom‑rich dishes to complement its earthy elegance.
aroma: wild red berries and rose petals
palate: silky tannins with refined structure

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru les Epenots
description: A weighty and poised Burgundy bearing a signature of fine-boned red fruit and earthy grace, this 2018 Pommard Premier Cru Les Épenots by Anne Parent unfolds with an expressive bouquet of violet, cherry and morello cherry wrapped in nuanced terroir notes of tilled earth and subtle gunpowder. On the palate it delivers concentrated flesh and sappy structure, underpinned by velvety tannins and a polished, savory finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar temperature with roasted duck, braised poultry or gamebirds; its graceful power complements rich meats and aged cheeses.
aroma: violet and morello cherry with earthy nuance
palate: fleshy red fruits framed by supple tannins

name: Domaine Anne Parent Pommard 1er Cru les Epenots
description: The 2018 Domaine Parent Pommard 1er Cru “Les Épenots” is a richly structured yet refined red burgundy exhibiting delicious dark cherry and wild strawberry fruit enfolded in perfumed underbrush and subtle floral nuance. It balances concentration with elegance and an underlying soil‑borne character that lends poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15–18 °C with slowly roasted poultry or lightly game‑flavoured dishes to highlight its supple tannins and earthy complexity.
palate: supple red fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Pinot Noir
description: Anthony & Dominic's 2018 Pinot Noir is a fruit-led California expression with bright red berries, supple texture, and softly integrated oak. In three-liter format, it is designed for generous service while retaining Pinot Noir's natural freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly cool and allow the large format to open in the glass; pair with salmon, roast poultry, or herb-roasted pork.
palate: Supple red fruit, gentle oak, fresh acidity

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumuir Blanc les Perrieres (St-Cyr-En-Bourg)
description: A finely poised Saumur Blanc from Arnaud Lambert the 2021 Les Perrières reveals a pale straw hue and delivers a luminous expression of Chenin Blanc purity. Its aromatic profile suggests dried apricot, citrus and stone‑mineral nuances, while the palate unfolds with saline tension, sinewy structure and a chalk‑tinged vitality that speaks of its limestone‑rich terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12–14 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass; pair with almond‑buttered mussels, fresh goat’s cheese or light shellfish dishes to complement its mineral brightness.
palate: saline tension, sinewy texture, savory fruit
finish: citrus pith shimmering into delicate saline persistence

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Clos de la Rue (Breze)
description: A crystalline Saumur Blanc from the Clos de la Rue vineyard in Brézé bearing the delicate clarity of Loire Chenin: ripe pear and citrus blossom entwine with subtle toasted wood whispers, delivering an elegant, terroir‑driven expression that feels both poised and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C in tulip glasses to highlight the wine’s tension and minerality; pairs splendidly with shellfish, médaillons of veal in light cream sauce or dishes featuring preserved lemons.
palate: refined texture with toasted wood and chalky minerality

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Clos de la Rue ( Breze)
description: A crystalline Saumur Blanc from the Clos de la Rue vineyard in Brézé bearing the delicate clarity of Loire Chenin: ripe pear and citrus blossom entwine with subtle toasted wood whispers, delivering an elegant, terroir‑driven expression that feels both poised and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C in tulip glasses to highlight the wine’s tension and minerality; pairs splendidly with shellfish, médaillons of veal in light cream sauce or dishes featuring preserved lemons.
palate: refined texture with toasted wood and chalky minerality

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Rouge Clos Tue-Loup (Breze)
description: This 2020 Saumur Rouge Clos Tue‑Loup from Arnaud Lambert reveals delicate yet vivid notes of small red and black fruits framed by subtle tobacco and violet nuances. The palate is graceful and poised, with silky tannins, bright acidity and a refined purity that honors the sandy‑limestone terroir of Brézé.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at 14 – 16 °C and pair with richer yet nuanced fare such as veal liver with raspberry vinegar or slightly sweet venison, allowing acidity and fruit to lift the dish.
aroma: red and black fruits with violet and tobacco
palate: silky tannins, bright acidity, pure fruit expression

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A refined Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils, the 2021 vintage displays a garnet hue, offering a plush bouquet of cherry raspberry and wild berries complemented by a subtle whisper of spice drawn from gentle wild‑yeast vinification and partial new‑oak aging
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 14 to 16 °C to showcase its silken tannins; pairs elegantly with a rustic charcuterie board or grilled red meats
palate: full‑bodied generous crunchy texture

name: Bodegas Arrocal Arrocal Seleccion Especial Do Ribera Del Duero
description: A dense, refined Ribera del Duero of serious poise, this 2021 Arrocal Selección Especial unites bright ripe black fruit with a subtle weave of spice and toasted oak. It conveys a sense of structured elegance, its plush texture and concentrated substance framed by velvety tannins and a lingering balsamic echo.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at 15–17 °C, ideal alongside richly flavored roasted lamb, aged manchego or game in red‑wine reduction.
palate: concentrated, velvety and structured

name: Bodegas Arrocal Arrocal Tintoi Fino Do Ribera Del Duero
description: This youthful Arrocal Tinto Fino 2022, drawn from estate vineyards perched at 830 m above Ribera del Duero, unfolds in the glass with polished depth ripe dark berries and whispers of coffee bean and cigar wrapper balanced by gracious oak restraint
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to 16 °C, decanting prior to pouring to open its generous dark fruit core; pairs beautifully with roast lamb or aged cured cheeses
aroma: dark berries, coffee bean, cigar wrapper
palate: structured, full‑bodied, with ripe tannin and soil grip

name: Red Wine Napa Valley
description: Arrow & Branch's 2012 Napa Valley Red Wine is a Cabernet Franc-led Bordeaux blend with blackberry depth, floral lift, and a polished mocha undertone. Integrated tannins and lively acidity give the mature wine shape without sacrificing generosity.
sommelierNotes: Give the wine an hour of air and serve with herb-crusted lamb, beef tenderloin, or roasted mushrooms.
palate: Rounded dark fruit, bright acidity, integrated tannin

name: Bodegas Los Astrales Astrales(do Ribera Del Duero)
description: A wine of serious stature drawing from ancient Tinto Fino vines, this 2003 Astrales from Bodegas Los Astrales offers cultivated power and steadfastness with refined Old World restraint, layers of dark fruit interwoven with subtle underbrush and cigar box nuances, delivering a dignified yet expressive presentation.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperatures around 16 °C after gentle decanting to reveal its fragrant depth, pairing best with grilled game, roasted lamb or mature hard cheeses.
palate: structured fruit and cedar spice

name: Atomique 3 Chardonnay le Basalt Eola-Amity Hills
description: Atomique³ Le Basalt Chardonnay 2022 unfolds with a graceful tension between sleek mineral clarity and a subdued, rounded texture. It presents a delicate interplay of citrus and white orchard fruits carried through a crystalline, volcanic-laced essence.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its bright acidity. Pair with rich shellfish, creamy pasta, or subtly spiced poultry to complement its mineral freshness.
aroma: Zest of lime and cool stone minerality
palate: Focused pear fruit with volcanic tension
foodPairings: Roasted chicken with lemon herb sauce

name: Chardonnay le Sedimanetaire Willamette Valley
description: This 2021 Atomique³ Le Sédimentaire Chardonnay is poised between two geological worlds in the Willamette Valley: sedimentary soils deliver a textured breadth while volcanic influence grants crystalline structure and minerality, resulting in a composed and energetic expression of the valley.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip‑shaped glassware to highlight its focused acidity and layered nuances, pairing beautifully with seared scallops or creamy crab bisque.
aroma: chalky lemon and green orchard fruit
palate: textural breadth with mineral tension

name: Chardonnay le Sedimanetaire Willamette Valley
description: This 2022 Atomique³ Le Sédimentaire Chardonnay is poised between two geological worlds in the Willamette Valley: sedimentary soils deliver a textured breadth while volcanic influence grants crystalline structure and minerality, resulting in a composed and energetic expression of the valley.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip‑shaped glassware to highlight its focused acidity and layered nuances, pairing beautifully with seared scallops or creamy crab bisque.
aroma: chalky lemon and green orchard fruit
palate: textural breadth with mineral tension

name: Chardonnay le Village Willamette Valley
description: This 2022 Atomique3 Village Chardonnay from Willamette Valley presents an elegant balance of vibrant citrus and subtle mineral tension. The wine evokes a sense of finesse with stone fruit nuances layered over a foundation of distinct terroir expression. It carries the legacy of Burgundian inspiration transferred to Oregon’s volcanic soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip-shaped glass to highlight its bright acidity; pairs beautifully with rich shellfish or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: bright citrus, wet stones, medium body

name: Domaine Paul Autard Cotes du Rhone
description: A full‑bodied southern Rhône blend that feels both grounded and generous, offering warm raspberry and black cherry tones framed by gentle smoke and garrigue notes, with an inviting suggestion of black pepper and licorice on the nose. The wine shows a plush yet structured palate melding ripe fruit intensity with subtle herbal spice, all wrapped in a lingering peppery finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature, around 16–18 °C in a large bowl glass. A fine companion to grilled lamb chops or a Provençal vegetable terrine.
aroma: garrigue and licorice over raspberry and cherry
palate: ripe dark fruit with smoky, herbal depth

name: Autre Monde Pinot Noir Willamette Valley
description: The 2024 Autre Monde Pinot Noir from Oregon’s Willamette Valley offers an elegant thread of bright red cherry and wild strawberry framed by subtle forest-floor earthiness and light herbal nuance, all carried on a delicate, silk‑textured core of cool‑climate Pinot Noir fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in large Burgundy glasses allow modest decanting to reveal perfumed lift; pair with game birds or mushroom‑rich dishes to echo its woodland tones.
aroma: bright cherry, wild strawberry, forest floor hint
palate: silky red fruits with herbal whispers
foodPairings: roasted duck breast with mushroom jus

name: Az Agricola Bianchi Luminae Bianco
description: An elegant northern Italian white marked by Erbaluce’s crisp clarity this 2022 Luminae Bianco from Azienda Agricola Bianchi presents lifted aromas of fresh pear green herbs and a saline undertone. The palate is laser‑focused with fine acidity subtle almond nuance and a refined mineral backbone that carries delicacy to the finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped white glass, a sublime match for simply dressed shellfish or herbed goat cheese on crostini.
palate: fine acidity, almond nuance, mineral clarity
foodPairings: light pasta with lemon and herbs

name: Château des Bachelards Fleurie
description: A refined expression of Fleurie from Château des Bachelards, this 2016 Gamay offers floral elegance anchored in depth. Its fine structure frames vibrant red fruit and delicate violet notes with precision and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 15 °C in a medium‑bowled glass. Perfect with soft‑rind cheeses or simply enjoyed on its own to reveal its finesse.
palate: elegant structure with silk‑textured fruit

name: Château des Bachelards Saint Amour
description: This 2016 Château des Bachelards Saint‑Amour unveils a tapestry of floral and mineral elegance, its garnet hue framing an expressive bouquet of violet and orange blossom. The palate offers a silken yet tension‑filled journey with depth and precision, culminating in a finish of unwavering clarity and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 15 °C, to reveal its fine floral perfume. Pairs elegantly with roast poultry or subtly sauced white meats.
palate: Silken tension with depth

name: Bourgogne Rouge
description: This Burgundy rouge is a refined village‑level Pinot Noir from Denis Bachelet, presenting a bright ruby hue with an elegant aromatic profile of blue‑purplish fruit, sweet tobacco and licorice, leading to a supple well‑balanced palate that captivates with its refined charm. A poised statement of Côte de Nuits terroir, it marries grace and approachability.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14–15 °C so that the wine’s freshness and delicate red berries shine beautifully alongside modestly structured tannins, especially with rustic French fare.
palate: medium‑bodied, raspberry and strawberry fruit, fine tannins

name: Cotes de Nuits Villages
description: This 2011 Domaine Denis Bachelet Côtes de Nuits‑Villages delivers an elegant red Burgundy of refined poise, with supple red cherry and raspberry notes framed by cool minerality and delicate herbal nuance. The wine exhibits an understated structure, silky texture and buoyant freshness characteristic of the Côte de Nuits in this vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 15 °C in a tall Pinot Noir glass to reveal the fine red fruit and subtle spice tones; pairs gracefully with roast duck or mushroom risotto.
palate: silky, fresh, minerally

name: Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes
description: This 2011 Domaine Denis Bachelet Gevrey‑Chambertin Vieilles Vignes presents deeply concentrated red and black cherry fruit, underlined by a subtly earthy mineral streak and a hint of undergrowth, its texture finely smooth and elegantly balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in tulip‑shaped glasses to reveal its layered nuance; pairs beautifully with roasted game birds or mushroom‑accented preparations.
palate: silky smooth, balanced acidity
finish: sensual, lingering red fruit and mineral undertone

name: Domaine Bachey-Legros Maranges Vieilles Vignes
description: This wine unfolds in the glass with scented layers of cherry and wild blackberry underpinned by whispers of spice and a hint of smoky nuance, elegant and poised even in its youth.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C, opening an hour ahead to reveal harmony with roasted game or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: ripe cherries and forest berries with subtle spice
palate: velvety red fruit with graceful tannins
finish: linger of spice and fresh citrus

name: Domaine Bachey-Legros Meursault les Grands Charrons
description: This Meursault Les Grands Charrons 2021 from Domaine Bachey‑Legros presents an elegant harmony of ripe orchard fruit and delicate nutty nuance, framed by subtle vanilla and mineral reserve. The texture is generous yet precise culminating in a long, persistent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in classic white Burgundy glasses, to pair elegantly with seared scallops or poultry in cream sauce.
aroma: ripe yellow fruit with a hint of vanilla
palate: generous yet precise with nutty citrus balance

name: Domaine Bachey-Legros Santenay les Champs Claude
description: This is a refined expression of Santenay from the historic Domaine Bachey‑Legros, drawn from the lieu‑dit Les Champs Claude. The 2021 vintage reveals restrained yet concentrated Pinot Noir from old vines, offering compelling minerality and a vibrant sense of southern Côte de Beaune terroir. A graceful wine of poise and earnest character.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature in a medium Burgundy glass to allow its spice‑tinged fruit and mineral undertow to emerge. Pairs beautifully with roasted chicken or tender game birds.
aroma: fragrant dark cherry with subtle spice
palate: concentrated, full‑bodied with fine mineral structure

name: Domaine Patrick Badouin Coteaux du Layon les Couteaux
description: An elegant Coteaux du Layon from Domaine Patrick Baudouin’s 2011 vintage Les Coteaux presents luminous golden hues a delicate interplay of ripe orchard fruit and fine honeyed nuances leads to a texture both vibrant and richly soulful reminiscent of old‑world sweetness with poise.
sommelierNotes: Chill gently to about 10°C and serve with pâtisserie‑style desserts or a foie gras mousse to highlight its balance of residual sweetness and bright acidity.
aroma: ripe orchard fruit with honeyed nuance
palate: creamy yet lively balance of sweetness and freshness

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A seamless expression of Napa Valley, this Cabernet Sauvignon opens with ripe blackcurrant and boysenberry followed by subtle notes of cocoa nib and dried rose petal, framed in a gentle cloak of spice and tobacco. The texture is broad yet balanced, with firm tannins and bright acidity delivering an elegant, food‑friendly Napa Cabernet.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to around 60 °F in a large bowl glass to draw out its aromatic layers. Pair with grilled rib‑eye or mushroom‑rich dishes.
aroma: blackcurrant, lavender, cocoa nib subtly spiced
palate: fruit‑driven, firm tannins, balanced acidity
finish: savory herbal edge with toasted spice

name: Pinot Noir Willamette Valley
description: The 2024 Band of Vintners Pinot Noir Willamette Valley greets the eye with a shimmering crimson hue a hint of allure from Oregon’s cool‑climate pedigree, where ripe cherry and mountain strawberry aromas mingle with plum and wildflower tones drawn lightly from forest floor. The palate is silky and elegant supported by bright acidity and subtle sage spice, culminating in a clean vibrant finish that feels poised and charming.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55 °F to accentuate its freshness; pairs exquisitely with roast duck or mushroom‑savory dishes.
aroma: ripe cherry, mountain strawberry, plum, wildflower underbrush
palate: silky red fruit lifted by bright acidity and subtle sage spice

name: Sauvignon Blanc Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Band of Vintners Sauvignon Blanc Napa Valley greets the senses with a lively bouquet of white florals and ripe grapefruit, leading to a supremely dry and crisp palate that dances with vibrant acidity and light citrus energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled, ideally in a slender tulip glass. Pair with fresh oysters, goat cheese crostini, or a citrus‑spritzed summer salad.
palate: super‑dry, crisp and lively

name: Baron de Brane Margaux
description: A supple Margaux second wine that entices with plush Merlot charm and graceful structure, weaving notes of black cherry, plum and a touch of menthol into a harmonious, inviting expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in a Burgundy glass allow the wine a moment to breathe before pairing with lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes.
aroma: black cherry and plum with menthol whisper
palate: silky, fruit‑driven, medium‑bodied

name: 3 Year Kentucky Bourbon Whisky
description: Noble and unvarnished this Kentucky Straight Bourbon offers a refined balance of corn‑sweetness and rye‑driven spice its three‑year journey beginning in American oak then moving into Cabernet Sauvignon wine barrels brings velvet texture and a whisper of dark fruit complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or with a single large ice cube to reveal vanilla and brown sugar layers, excellent with aged cheddar or chocolate‑dipped dried cherries.
aroma: vanilla bean with candied orange and subtle pink peppercorn
palate: rich maple syrup and toffee underscored by dark cherry and spice
finish: long velvety toast and smoked oak resonance

name: Domaine Bart Marsannay la Montagne
description: The 2019 Domaine Bart Marsannay “La Montagne” is an elegant village‐level Pinot Noir rendered with restraint and clarity, revealing vibrant purple fruit framed by an energetic spine of tannin and a note of mineral nuance from its clay‐rich parcel, offering medium weight with seamless balance and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to awaken its floral and red fruit perfume; pairs beautifully with roast chicken or duck confit to echo its refined structure.
aroma: lavender and violet on spicy purple fruit
palate: silky mid‑palate, cola‑tinged cherry with firm tannins

name: Domaine Bart Marsannay les Ouzeloy
description: This 2020 Marsannay “Les Ouzeloy” from Domaine Bart offers a graceful expression of northern Côte de Nuits with energetic structure and refined concentration. It presents floral lift and tensile power without heaviness nurturing an elegant yet muscular presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to highlight its clarity of fruit and lift, pairing beautifully with mushroom‑accented dishes or roasted meats.
palate: structured concentration, mouthwatering balance

name: Domaine Bart Marsannay Saint Jacques
description: A vibrant Marsannay from Domaine Bart that captures crystalline dark berry purity with notable energy and a subtly juicy core, its cool fruit framed by a refined tension that speaks of Burgundian subtlety and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 14 °C; excels with roast duck breast or mushroom‑dusted pork tenderloin, enhancing the wine’s freshness and nuanced tannic structure.
aroma: fresh dark berries with a hint of cool purity
palate: juicy, refined, energetic dark fruit

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Barbera D'asti DOCG la Villa
description: An expressive Barbera d’Asti from the storied hills of Incisa Scapaccino, La Villa 2023 is vibrant and vinous with luminous ruby red color and violet hues that beckon the eye. On the nose it reveals fine, intense notes of cherry and wild berries, while the palate is full‑bodied yet balanced, carrying refreshing acidity into a long, pleasant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its brisk freshness; pairs beautifully with rich salumi, simple pasta dishes or vitello tonnato.
aroma: fine, intense cherry and wild berries
palate: full‑bodied, fresh, balanced

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Gavi Di Gavi DOCG
description: A graceful and luminous Gavi di Gavi from Tenuta Olim Bauda, crafted from Cortese grapes grown in the storied hills of Gavi, unfolds with delicate floral and citrus whispers that glide atop a crystalline mineral spine, offering poise and old‑world refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve very chilled around 10 °C to accentuate its freshness, a delightful companion to light springtime fare or simply to sip on its own in serene company.
palate: pure minerality with citrus brightness

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Moscato D'asti Centive
description: A pale straw colored Moscato d’Asti that charms with its aromatic elegance notes of elderflower sage and citrus waft from the glass introducing a delicately sweet yet bracingly fresh character textured by fine spritz giving a creamy sensation that lingers with poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 6‑8 °C in slender stemware to preserve effervescence delightfully paired with light fruit desserts or as a graceful aperitivo.
palate: sweet freshness with creamy mousse
foodPairings: bruschetta with figs gorgonzola and honey
verrines with ricotta and mixed berries

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Moscato D'asti DOCG Centive
description: This Moscato d’Asti “Centive” 2024 from Tenuta Olim Bauda offers an elegant, gently sparkling expression of Moscato that captivates with its fragrant bouquet of citrus blossom and elderflower over a light straw‑yellow hue. It reveals pristine, slightly sweet orchard fruit and floral notes with just enough vivacity to balance its aromatic richness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C in tulip or small white wine glasses to highlight its delicate perlage and carry it through to fruity desserts or light cheeses.
palate: sweet orchard fruit balanced by freshness

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Moscato D'asti DOCG Centive
description: This Moscato d’Asti “Centive” 2024 from Tenuta Olim Bauda offers an elegant, gently sparkling expression of Moscato that captivates with its fragrant bouquet of citrus blossom and elderflower over a light straw‑yellow hue. It reveals pristine, slightly sweet orchard fruit and floral notes with just enough vivacity to balance its aromatic richness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C in tulip or small white wine glasses to highlight its delicate perlage and carry it through to fruity desserts or light cheeses.
palate: sweet orchard fruit balanced by freshness

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Nizza DOCG Riserva
description: This crystalline Barbera distils the noble essence of Piedmont with elegant fruit and measured oak melding into poised harmony on the palate. A dignified expression of Nizza Riserva, the wine unfolds with interpretive grace rather than showy bravura.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its red cherry brightness; pairs beautifully with rich ragu and roasted game or aged mountain cheeses.
aroma: intense red fruit, subtle balsamic nuance
palate: full‐bodied, balanced tannin and acidity

name: Bodegas Luna Beberide Paixar Do Bierzo
appellation: Bierzo (Vino de Paraje A Serra, Dragonte)
description: Paixar 2021 from Bodegas Luna Beberide is a refined expression of old‐vine Mencía from the slate‐strewn slopes of A Serra in Dragonte Villafranca del Bierzo, presenting a harmonious weave of intensely concentrated black and red fruit accented with mineral intrigue and a subtle herbal underpinning. The wine’s clarity and poised medium‐bodied silk carry a sense of austerity balanced by freshness a graceful emblem of its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 15‑17 °C in a tall wine glass to reveal its fine structure paired with grilled lamb chops or wild mushrooms on toast for contrast and harmony.
palate: elegant core of fruit with fine‑grained tannins

name: Benjamin Leroux Auxey Duresses Blanc
description: A precise and crystalline village white from Côte de Beaune, the 2022 Auxey‑Duresses Blanc by Benjamin Leroux opens with bright citrus and Granny Smith pear notes underpinned by mineral clarity and gentle orchard fruit. Elegant and balanced this Chardonnay reveals both freshness and subtle flesh, offering restrained depth that calls for graceful indulgence.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 10–12 °C in a slender white glass to accentuate its citrus drive and minerality, a handsome companion to delicate seafood or soft goat cheese.
palate: bright orchard fruit with fine acidity

name: Auxey Duresses Blanc
description: A precise and crystalline village white from Côte de Beaune, the 2023 Auxey‑Duresses Blanc by Benjamin Leroux opens with bright citrus and Granny Smith pear notes underpinned by mineral clarity and gentle orchard fruit. Elegant and balanced this Chardonnay reveals both freshness and subtle flesh, offering restrained depth that calls for graceful indulgence.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 10–12 °C in a slender white glass to accentuate its citrus drive and minerality, a handsome companion to delicate seafood or soft goat cheese.
palate: bright orchard fruit with fine acidity

name: Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: The 2016 Benjamin Leroux Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru in magnum presents an elegant and classically structured expression of Chardonnay from one of Burgundy’s most hallowed terroirs. It offers a precise interplay of mineral tension and luminous white fruit framed by a quiet oak presence—a composition both majestic and reserved.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 12–13 °C to reveal its poised minerality and precise citrus core; pairs beautifully with lightly butter‑poached lobster or aged Comté.
aroma: white orchard fruit and toasty nuance
palate: precise mineral tension with citrus brightness
foodPairings: seared scallops with lemon beurre blanc

description: This 2018 Benjamin Leroux Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru magnum exudes an elegant interplay of ripe orchard fruits, delicate florals and a whisper of pastry richness, framed by crystalline minerality and seamless texture. It unfolds with an air of poised opulence, maintaining energy and finesse throughout.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 11–12 °C in a large-bowled white glass to showcase its layered complexity; pair it with lobster in cream sauce or fine seafood dishes.
aroma: orchard fruit and pastry with floral lift
palate: creamy yet energetic with finely layered minerality

name: Benjamin Leroux Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: This 2020 Benjamin Leroux Bâtard-Montrachet Grand Cru presents regal opulence tempered by mineral precision, its orchard fruit and beeswax tones enveloped in delicate acidity and weightless silkiness. There is a graceful interplay of buttery texture and crystalline structure that speaks of terroir and cool nights, conveying latent power with poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in fine stemware to reveal its tension and lingering minerality, a poised companion to rich seafood or even subtly seasoned poultry.
palate: balanced, silky tension
bottleSize: 750 ml (magnum only for this bottling since 2016)

name: Benjamin Leroux Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: A graceful expression of Bonnes‑Mares in magnum, this 2018 Leroux unfurls with perfumed black cherry, violet and bramble, underlain by whispers of earthy minerality and floral lift, the medium‑full frame built on fine‑grained tannins giving the wine a poised yet powerful presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature in large Burgundy glasses; pairs exquisitely with roasted duck or wild mushroom risotto.
palate: fine‑grained tannins, ripe acid, saline minerality
finish: long saline finish with dark spice and truffle hints

name: Bourgogne Aligote
description: A refined expression of Burgundian Aligoté from Benjamin Leroux, the 2021 Bourgogne Aligoté displays a pale lemon hue and exudes an elegant, graceful bouquet with fine texture and remarkable length, steering clear of the variety’s usual rustic leanings. Crafted from old‐vine Aligoté Doré parcels in Meursault and vinified with precision in WineGlobes, foudre and seasoned ovals, it offers a poised clarity and vibrant energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve cold at 10 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its precision and freshness, ideal as an aperitif or alongside oysters, shellfish or subtly herbed goat cheese.
aroma: pale lemon, orange blossom, light patisserie
palate: fresh with orange rind nuance and clarity

name: Benjamin Leroux Bourgogne Aligote

name: Bourgogne Rouge
description: A supple expression of Burgundy finesse from Benjamin Leroux’s 2023 Bourgogne Rouge, it presents a core of red cherry and raspberry framed by mineral clarity and subtle floral lift, finishing with a whisper of spice and poised elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to enhance its vibrant red fruit and graceful structure; pairs beautifully with roasted poultry or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: pure red fruit, lively acidity, balanced tannins
finish: minerally with spice and lasting clarity

name: Benjamin Leroux Chambertin Grand Cru
description: An ethereal expression of Grand Cru Chambertin from the hands of Benjamin Leroux in the radiant 2018 vintage, this magnum reveals a poised elegance and refined tension: layers of black cherry and forest undergrowth emerge with spice and mineral precision, offering a measured intensity and smooth, taffeta‑like texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve with careful decanting to reveal its layered complexity and pair with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑infused dishes to complement its earth‑toned nuance.
palate: etching mineral tension, fine‑grained tannins

description: A refined village Pinot Noir from Chambolle‑Musigny, the 2017 Benjamin Leroux offers an elegant weave of perfumed red cherry and cranberry with delicate floral undertones, lifted by a subtle chalky minerality and superfine tannins. It exudes graceful finesse and clear definition, a poised tribute to its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar‑cool temperature to allow its perfume to flourish, ideal with lightly seasoned poultry or mushroom‑framed dishes.
palate: elegant, silken texture with chalky minerality

description: A discreetly intense Grand Cru that exudes Burgundy elegance, offering a vivid ribbon of red and dark berries enlivened by whispered floral and earth‑tinged complexity, culminating in a lithe yet beautifully structured expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in large Burgundy goblets to allow the complex aromatics to thrive, and pair with herb‑crusted lamb or sautéed wild mushrooms in butter and thyme.
aroma: red and dark berries with floral‑earth nuance
palate: supple yet structured, vibrant fruit with fine tannins

name: Benjamin Leroux Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
appellation: Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
description: An elegant expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis Grand Cru in magnum, this 2018 Clos de la Roche from Benjamin Leroux offers deep ruby hues and a radiant bouquet of ripe red fruit threaded with plummy exuberance and seamless structure. It unfolds with precision and energy delivering sustained depth in a magnum format that enhances its expressive breadth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool, around 16 °C, decanted gently to reveal youthful concentration; pairs beautifully with roast duck or aged Comté.
palate: precision, energy, sustained depth

name: Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: The 2011 Benjamin Leroux Clos Vougeot Grand Cru emerges with a lithe yet concentrated profile, weaving spiced whole‑bunch nuance through dense black and red cherry fruit. Firm structure and elegant grain of tannin suggest both immediate allure and prolonged maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–17 °C in Burgundy‑style stemware after gentle decanting, pairing beautifully with rich game, roast lamb or aged cheeses to match its perfume and structure.
aroma: black and red cherry laced with spice
palate: dense fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Clos Vougeot Petit Maupertuis Grand Cru
description: An exuberant Grand Cru from one of Burgundy’s most thoughtful vignerons, this 2017 Clos de Vougeot Petit Maupertuis unfolds with bright purple hues and a headily aromatic scent that hints at balsamic lift over ripe red and dark fruits. The palate delivers elegant, fine-grained tannins and mineral undercurrent while vibrant brambly and dried cranberry tones dance across a poised yet persistent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C to let the red and dark fruit notes blossom, ideally with richly textured fare like duck breast with cherry jus or aged saddle of lamb.
aroma: heady deep red fruit with balsamic lift
palate: elegant tannins with bramble and dried cranberry

sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar‑temperature, around 15°C, pairing beautifully with roasted lamb, duck breast, mushroom risotto, or soft‑ripened cheeses.
palate: sappy red fruit, fine‑grained tannins

name: Cellars Ee Red Wine Napa Valley
description: A profound expression of Napa Valley intensity this wine melds dark cassis and violet tones with hints of espresso and graphite reflecting a stately minerality and poised power. Its layered structure reveals ultra‑fine tannins and a seamless core of black fruit that suggest regal depth and aging potential. Truly majestic, this wine offers both immediacy and a long future.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted in large Bordeaux glasses to accentuate aromatics, pair with rich game or aged steak for resonance.
palate: full‑bodied seamless black fruit concentration
finish: long and regal with dusty tannins

name: Cellars Ontogeny Red Wine Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Ontogeny Red Wine from Bevan Cellars is a lush, expressive Napa Valley Bordeaux‐style blend grounded in bold Cabernet Sauvignon from Tench Vineyard, softened by Merlot from Sugarloaf Mountain, and lifted by small additions of Cabernet Franc, Malbec, and Petit Verdot. It opens with luxurious dark berry and mocha notes threaded through with graphite and violets, supported by polished tannins and bright acidity, offering both immediate depth and cellar potential over the next decade or more.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at 16–18 °C to let the floral spice and chocolate nuances emerge; pairs beautifully with grilled rib‑eye, aged cheeses, or herb‑roasted game.
palate: polished tannins, graphite, layered fruit

name: Cellars Sauvignon Blanc Dry Stack Vineyard Bennet Valley
appellation: Dry Stack Vineyard, Bennett Valley AVA, Sonoma County
description: The 2023 Dry Stack Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc from Bevan Cellars reveals a polished interplay of tropical allure and refined structure, with its expressive nose of ripe citrus and exotic fruit leading to a layered, mouth-filling core framed by vibrant acidity and subtle oak nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 50–52 °F, ideally alongside buttery shellfish, fresh goat cheese or grilled white fish, to showcase its elegant texture and refreshing lift.
palate: bright mouth‑filling with subtle creaminess

name: Bevan Cellars Sauvignon Blanc Stack Vineyard Bennett Valley
description: The 2024 Bevan Cellars Dry Stack Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc from Bennett Valley unfolds with radiant energy, offering tropical fruit facets framed by an undercurrent of refined freshness, its structure elevated by a judicious marriage of French oak and steel aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 50‑55°F in a tulip glass to showcase its aromatic lift; splendid with shellfish or tangy goat cheese.
palate: vibrant, refined texture

name: Bevan Cellars Sentinal Ridge Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: Bevan Cellars’ 2023 Sentinel Ridge Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon unfurls in the glass with a perfumed architecture of graphite, lavender and slate-laced red and blue fruits, underpinned by a whisper of crushed herbs and underbrush. The palate is full‑bodied yet refined, framed by polished tannins and a texture that is both supple and delineated.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to about 60‑62°F in large tulip glasses; pair with rosemary‑infused lamb loin or wild mushroom ragout to echo the wine’s forest‑floor and herb‑tinged character.
palate: Polished, supple blue and black fruit
finish: Elegant lingering tannins and earthy spice

name: Cellars Sugarloaf Mountain Proprietary Red Wine
description: From the rugged hills of Napa’s southeast, this 2023 Proprietary Red from Sugarloaf Mountain Vineyard blends Cabernet Franc, Merlot, and a touch of Cabernet Sauvignon in a wine of intense precision and grace. Vibrant dark‑blue fruit—mulberries, blueberries, blackberry bramble—moves into dusty earth and lavender over a silky frame of integrated tannins and lingering elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature: this wine’s lifted blue‑fruit character and fine texture pairs beautifully with herb‑crusted lamb or aged Gouda.
palate: silky blue‑fruit core with gentle acidity

name: Bevan Cellars Tench Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A grand expression of Napa Valley power and poise Cabernet Sauvignon from the Tench Vineyard in Oakville reveals concentrated layers of blue and black fruits underscored by graphite and crushed rock nuance, all presented with a seamless richness and velvety polish.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a large Bordeaux glass at 64–66 °F after decanting for an hour Pair with rich lamb or aged cheeses for balanced counterpoint.
palate: dense, polished tannins, dark chocolate, dried herbs

name: Cellars Tench Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Bevan Cellars Tench Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon from Oakville, Napa Valley, unfurls with concentrated aromas of blue and black berries, graphite, crushed rock, and a whisper of espresso, seamlessly layered in depth and richness. The palate is plush and expressive showcasing currant and dried herb tones supported by polished tannins leading into a long and lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 60°F in a large crystal glass to allow the wine’s brooding fruit and graphite notes to unfold. Pair it with grilled rib‑eye, aged cheddar, or herb‑crusted lamb for a harmonious match.
aroma: blue and black berries, graphite, crushed rock, hint of espresso
palate: currants, dried herbs, ripe polished tannins

name: Bevan Cellars Tench Vineyard Calixtro Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville Napa Valley
description: This 2018 Bevan Cellars Tench Vineyard The Calixtro Cabernet Sauvignon is a wine of concentrated intensity and Old‑World poise framed in Napa’s regal Oakville district. Inky dark‑red fruit veils layers of licorice cedar and espresso while graphite‑tinged mineral spine underlies the sumptuous structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted in wide bowls to open its depth, matching richly flavored red meats or aged cheeses enhances its layered complexity.
aroma: inky dark fruit with licorice and cedar (found)
palate: rich espresso, graphite, spice (found)
