name: Bevan Cellars Tin Box Cabernet Sauvignon Nape Valley
description: This young Tin Box Cabernet Sauvignon reveals compelling Oakville power and focus drawing from venerable vines that yield dense cassis tones and graphite-tinged berry depth, all wrapped in a framework of polished structure and poised energy. Its presence is refined and agile yet resolute, a modern nod to old‑world gravitas tempered with Napa intensity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in generous Bordeaux glasses to showcase its textural layers, pairing beautifully with herb‑accented lamb or aged hard cheeses.
palate: concentrated dark fruit framed by firm grainy tannins

name: Az Agicola Bianchi Ghemme
description: This Ghemme from Agricola Bianchi reveals noble Nebbiolo bearing the imprint of Alto Piemonte : its voice is austere yet refined, breathing gently of rosehip, subtle citrus underbrush and an undercurrent of iron-laced earth. With ten years of quiet evolution it remains intriguingly persistent and complex on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve near cellar temperature in a large balloon glass to let its layered aromas open and pair elegantly with braised game or aged cheeses.
palate: elegant, intricate, salmastra note

name: Az Agricola Bianchi Luminae Biancho
description: This 2021 Luminae Biancho is an elegant expression of Erbaluce from Piedmont refined and bright offering subtle floral lift and a refreshing mineral precision
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at about 10 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its freshness, excellent with light seafood or vegetable terrines
palate: crisp minerality with lemon peel nuance

name: Biutiful Cava Brut Nature
description: This Biutiful Cava Brut Nature presents a refined crystalline persona with brisk orchard fruit and a chalky mineral halo, carrying an elegant tension between delicacy and structure. It unfurls gently yet with clarity, guided by a bright spine of acidity and lithe, precise mousse.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled as a singular aperitif or alongside razor‑thin oysters, grilled seafood or mild Valencian rice dishes to underscore its vibrant purity.
aroma: orchard fruit kissed by chalky mineral
palate: bright citrus acidity with fine mousse

name: Biutiful Cava Brut Rose
description: A graceful non‑vintage rosé cava that offers a refined dance of blood orange and wild strawberry framed by delicate mineral tones, with a fine, persistent mousse and a poised, lingering presence. The wine’s polished structure and subtle spiciness recall old‑world poise fashioned in modern guise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip flute to highlight its fizz and lift the citrus‑red fruit interplay. Pair with elegant hors d’oeuvres or delicate seafood to complement its brightness.
aroma: blood orange, wild strawberry, floral lift
palate: crisp, full‑bodied, mineral undercurrent
finish: long and tangy with floral nuance

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: An elegantly poised Argentine Cabernet Sauvignon that offers a graceful interplay of ripe red and dark fruits and subtle oak spice, its character refined yet approachable
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to open vibrant berry and cassis layers; pair with grilled lamb or empanadas to harmonize its peppery notes
aroma: ripe cassis and red fruits with a hint of pepper and tobacco
palate: mellow berry jam framed by gentle tannins and oak spice

name: Malbec
description: A ripe yet refined Malbec from Mendoza with layered plum and cherry fruit, edged by lifted strawberry brightness and a whisper of vanilla from gentle oak, delivering a succulent and balanced presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to coax out its vibrant fruit; a graceful match with grilled meats or tomato‑based pasta.
aroma: Plum, cherry, strawberry, hint of vanilla
palate: Juicy red and dark berries with soft oak spice

name: Malbec
description: A ripe yet refined Malbec from Mendoza with layered plum and cherry fruit, edged by lifted strawberry brightness and a whisper of vanilla from gentle oak, delivering a succulent and balanced presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to coax out its vibrant fruit; a graceful match with grilled meats or tomato‑based pasta.
aroma: Plum, cherry, strawberry, hint of vanilla
palate: Juicy red and dark berries with soft oak spice

name: California Chardonnay
description: A graceful, food‑friendly California Chardonnay crafted for everyday enjoyment, offering clean citrus clarity with a hint of cool‑fermented brightness and varietal purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to highlight its crisp acidity; an elegant opener before dinner or a light accompaniment to poultry or vegetable dishes.
palate: medium‑bodied with refreshing acidity

name: California Shiraz
description: A generous and smooth Shiraz drawn from a lively California blend, this non‑vintage Black Ridge offers rich ripeness and gentle spice wrapped in a supple texture. It presents opulent black‑berry and ripe plum notes with a touch of sweet spice and smooth, juicy structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 60–62 °F in a tulip glass to showcase its plush fruit, pairing beautifully with grilled meats or hearty pasta.
palate: rich, smooth and juicy black‑berry and plum

name: Blanc de Lynch Bages Bordeaux Blanc Sec
description: This 2023 Blanc de Lynch‑Bages offers a refined yet vibrant expression, showcasing a lively interplay of citrus, floral grace and exotic fruit underpinned by a fine sculpted structure. It captures both the freshness of youth and the poised depth characteristic of subtle Quebec gravel derived terroirs.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in tulip‑shaped glasses at 10–12 °C to reveal its floral lift and exotic brightness. It partners splendidly with shellfish, creamy cheeses or light fish dishes.
palate: fresh and lively with floral elegance

name: Blason D'issan Margaux
description: This Margaux second wine from Château d’Issan reveals an elegant frame of pure dark berries, violet blossom and fine tobacco, its rounded fruit reflecting the estate’s gravelly identity yet presenting with immediacy and refined freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar cool temperature with roast duck or lamb in herb jus to accentuate the wine’s floral lift and balanced structure.
palate: silky tannins balanced fruit

name: Blason D'issan Margaux
description: This Margaux second wine from Château d’Issan reveals an elegant frame of pure dark berries, violet blossom and fine tobacco, its rounded fruit reflecting the estate’s gravelly identity yet presenting with immediacy and refined freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar cool temperature with roast duck or lamb in herb jus to accentuate the wine’s floral lift and balanced structure.
palate: silky tannins balanced fruit

name: Blason D'issan Margaux
description: This Margaux second wine from Château d’Issan reveals an elegant frame of pure dark berries, violet blossom and fine tobacco, its rounded fruit reflecting the estate’s gravelly identity yet presenting with immediacy and refined freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar cool temperature with roast duck or lamb in herb jus to accentuate the wine’s floral lift and balanced structure.
palate: silky tannins balanced fruit

name: Boedgas Margon Pricum Valdemuz
description: Elegantly fragrant and deeply noble this 2008 Pricum Valdemuz reveals its heritage in silky echoes of lavender and graphite and a tapestry of dark and blue fruits, layered with subtle Asian spices and pain grille nuances, all framed by impeccable balance and enduring intensity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at fifteen to seventeen degrees Celsius in large Bordeaux glasses to unlock its aromatic depth. Pair with roast lamb infused with rosemary or aged manchego for graceful harmony.
palate: blue fruit intensity with spice and structure

name: Bodegas San Roman Prima Do Toro
description: An elegant, gently perfumed Toro red that balances expressive dark fruit and subtle spice. The 2022 Prima is approachable yet refined, with fine‐boned structure and a velvety midpalate that gives way to lingering ripe fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to preserve freshness. Pairs beautifully with grilled aged Manchego or roasted autumn vegetables.
aroma: dark cherries, coffee bean, gentle leather
palate: ripe, plush fruit, polished tannins

name: Bodegas San Roman San Roman Do Toro
description: A wine of noble gravitas: the 2021 San Román reveals rich black‑fruit allure under elegant restraint, earthy graphite and ink accents lending depth and old‑world gravitas. Its polished oak support is seamless giving the impression of calm power.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature in large tulip glasses; decant lightly and pair with braised beef cheeks or aged manchego for a balanced, evocative contrast.
palate: concentrated, finely polished tannins

name: Bodegas Y Vinedos Merito Otaola Pacharan Casera
description: An artis anal pacharán that unfolds in the glass with a refined harmony of dark cherry sloe berries and gentle aniseed warmth, offering a balanced, inviting character with subtle sweetness and complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender liqueur glass as a contemplative digestif or delicately over ice for modern flair, ideally after hearty fare.
palate: lightly sweet, savory with sloe and anise

name: Boigey Freres Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A graceful Bourgogne Rouge from Boigey Frères whose vibrant ruby hue opens to scented notes of cherry and crushed strawberry. The palate is delicate yet expressive with supple tannins and a hint of peppered spice weaving through bright red fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14°C in a medium tulip glass, pairing elegantly with roast duck or mushroom risotto.
palate: supple tannins and peppery spice

name: Boigey Freres Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Boudots
description: A precise expression of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges of rarefied elegance reflecting its storied terroir, this wine offers refined red fruit and mineral clarity in a delicately framed structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool temperature to highlight its tension and pair with generously sauced poultry or lightly grilled lamb.
aroma: red cherry and spicy herb nuance
palate: silky, mineral‑edged with fine tannins

name: Boigey Freres Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Damodes
description: A luminous expression of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges, this 2023 Boigey Frères 1er Cru Les Damodes exudes refined concentration and finely wrought structure. It offers a vivid bouquet of black and red berries with spice undertones and displays elegant balance polished by velvety, precise tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature, around 16 °C, with game birds or mushroom‑accompanied poultry to complement its lively fruit and gentle spice.
aroma: ripe red and black fruit with spice
palate: elegant, concentrated, fine‑grained tannins

name: Boigey Freres Vosne Romanee
description: A refined expression of Vosne‑Romanee from the emerging Domaine Boigey Frères in the radiant 2023 vintage, this wine displays a core of vivid red and black fruit framed by a fine weave of spice and terroir nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in tall tulip glasses let the wine breathe gently to reveal its elegant structure and layered fruit; ideal with game birds or delicate lamb preparations.
aroma: ebb of red‑berry perfume with a hint of spice
palate: silky fruit framed by poised tannins

name: Boigey Freres Vosne Romanee les Jachees
description: This Vosne‑Romanée Aux Jachées from Domaine Boigey Frères 2023 unfolds with voluptuous red and black fruit such as Morello cherry and wild strawberry joined by delicate spice and a floral undercurrent. The texture is sensual and refined, with velvety tannins and a supple, lingering finish that speaks of terroir finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑like coolness around 16 °C in elegant stemware to enjoy its grace. It partners beautifully with dishes like roasted duck or herb‑crusted lamb, where its layered fruit and spice complement game and aromatics.
aroma: perfumed wild strawberry and Morello cherry
palate: medium‑bodied with candied red fruit and orange peel nuances

name: Boigey Freres Vosne Romanee les Ormes
description: This 2023 Boigey Frères Vosne‑Romanée “Les Ormes” emerges as the inaugural expression of a rare single‑vineyard plot adjacent to Aux Jachées, its voice infused with red berries and floral life and framed by delicate stem presence and new oak tension. The wine unfolds with an earnest clarity and poise revealing purity and finely drawn structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C to reveal its subtle aromatic layers, pairing elegantly with mushroom‑scented poultry or herb‑accented pork.
palate: refined structure with subtle stem spice and red fruit clarity

name: Bonnamy Cremant de Loire Blanc Brut
description: This Crémant de Loire Blanc Brut NV from Bonnamy presents fine persistent bubbles and a pale yellow color lifted by a delicate interplay of pear and orchard fruit nuances. Earthy whispers from its Chenin Blanc base merge gracefully with floral accents and bright citrus highlights, all given texture by gentle toasty undercurrents from extended lees aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 to 10 °C as an elegant aperitif or pair with soft cheeses and light fruit desserts to complement its freshness.
palate: fresh orchard fruits with mineral undertone
finish: clean, lingering with gentle nutty echo

name: Bonnamy Cremant de Loire Rose Brut
description: An elegant rosé bubble from the Loire Valley this wine unfolds in the glass with fine, persistent bead and a soft coral hue. Bright red berry and citrus threads meet subtle earthiness from Cabernet Franc on a dry yet generous base. The overall impression is refined and inviting, evoking conviviality and timeless tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a flute or tulip glass, as an aperitif or alongside light seafood, delicate poultry or creamy hors d’oeuvres.
aroma: bright red berries with a hint of earthiness
palate: juicy red fruit with citrus freshness
drinkWindow: Drink now to within a few years

name: Cru Barrejats Sauternes
description: A wine of regal Sauternes pedigree from a discreet artisan estate this 2003 Cru Barréjats unfolds with a gracious tapestry of dried fig and candied apricot followed by a whisper of exotic mango and passion fruit, all framed in a silken, liqueur‑rich texture yet tempered with graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in slender stemmed glasses to reveal its regal sweetness, a splendid match for foie gras or delicate fruit‑based desserts, or enjoy contemplatively on its own.
aroma: dried fig, candied apricot, exotic tropical fruit
palate: silken, liqueur‑rich, generous fruit

name: Daniel Bouland Cote de Brouilly Cuvee Melanie
description: From a modest, sunlit parcel atop Mont Brouilly Daniel Bouland’s 2018 Cuvée Mélanie offers vivid red and black fruit framed by expressive mineral nuances and subtle violets, all carried on a refined structure that unites power and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to unveil its vivid fruit and fine tannins, pairing beautifully with roasted lamb or a fricassée of mushrooms.
aroma: smoky berry and cassis with spice accents
palate: succulent layered fruit with vibrant minerality
finish: fresh lively finish with perfectly mature tannins

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Chiroubles Chatenay
description: An elegant and generous Gamay from the slopes of Chiroubles, this wine offers a harmony of ripe red and dark berries woven with floral spice and subtle mineral undercurrents, all framed by a whisper of structure yet buoyant with vivacity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its bright fruit and finesse; pairs beautifully with charcuterie, roasted poultry or light regional dishes.
aroma: ripe red and black berries with floral spice
palate: vivid fruit core, silky texture, subtle mineral lift

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Schiste Bellevue
description: Daniel Bouland’s 2018 Morgon Bellevue Schiste is an elegant expression of Gamay that balances vibrant energy and mineral clarity: scented with blue and red berry florals and deep cherry, it is richly textured yet precise, finishing with a long saline and spice-tinged flourish.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool in a Burgundy glass to soften its youthful tannins; this wine will shine alongside roast duck with cherries or aged Comté.
aroma: mineral‑tinged cherry and dark berry florals
palate: sappy boysenberry and candied licorice underpinned by smoky graphite

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Vieilles Vignes Corcelette
description: A thoughtful expression of Morgon from the venerable holdings of Domaine Daniel Bouland, the 2018 Vieilles Vignes Corcelette reveals black and red cherry woven through whispers of violet and fine graphite dust, structured with old‑vine concentration yet lifted by mineral energy from its sandy‑stone soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 14 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass. Pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast or a mushroom‑and‑herb galette, matching the wine’s depth and sapidity.
aroma: black and red cherry, violet, graphite minerality
palate: silky concentrating old‑vine fruit with mineral backbone

name: Bourgeois Sancerre D'antan
description: This 2016 Sancerre d’Antan by Henri Bourgeois delivers a refined and soulful expression of old‑vine Sauvignon Blanc, where flinty minerality and gauzy citrus notes unfold gracefully, touched by soft oak whispers. It offers an elegant balance of depth and precision preserving Loire authenticity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12‑13 °C to greet its vibrant minerality. Ideal with delicate shellfish or subtly sauced white meats.
palate: grapefruit, almonds, gentle oak

name: Henri Bourgeois Sancerre le Cotelin
description: From a venerable single‑vineyard site perched on Kimmeridgian marls in Maimbray, this 2018 Henri Bourgeois Le Cotelin reveals a refined richness and smooth intensity, with echoes of lemon‑pie brightness and ripe orchard fruit adding an elegant, old‑world allure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 12–13 °C: it charms with delicate texture and mineral clarity, a fine match for subtle white meats or aged goat cheeses.
palate: Supple and smooth texture with toasty and mineral clarity

name: Henri Bourgeois Sancerre les Cotes aux Valets
description: A golden‑hued Sancerre crafted from a quiet clay‑limestone parcel in the southern appellation this 2018 Les Côtes aux Valets unfolds with refined dried fruit and citrus nuances underpinned by saline mineral notes. It is supple and round on the palate with a fine mineral structure and a refreshing saline finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C alongside mature goat cheese or delicate shellfish to enhance its saline freshness.
palate: supple, round, mineral‑driven
finish: fresh and saline with mirabelle and citrus zest

name: Famille Bourgeois Sancerre Rose les Jeunes Vignes
description: A pale and poised rosé from Sancerre this wine offers bright red-berry layers underscored by a refined salinity drawn from the Loire’s limestone soils, rounded by a whisper of youthful vitality from the youngest Pinot Noir vines. It wears its minerality with grace and clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10 – 12 °C to preserve its fresh fruit and mineral vivacity: ideal with oysters, light seafood or a summer apéritif in elegant simplicity.
palate: fresh, linear, elegantly mineral

name: Napa Valley Brio Red Blend Napa Valley
description: BRAND Napa Valley's 2014 Brio is a full-bodied Pritchard Hill red centered on blackberry, cocoa, coffee, and licorice tones. Dense mountain fruit is carried by polished tannins and a long, layered finish.
sommelierNotes: Decant for one to two hours and serve with ribeye, braised short ribs, or rosemary-roasted lamb.
palate: Dense dark fruit, silky tannin, layered spice

name: Napa Valley Brio Red Wine
description: A profound and full‑bodied red born of storied soils high above Napa Valley, this 2015 Brio Red Wine exudes vivacity and gravitas in equal measure. Its expressive core of blackcurrant, violet, cedar and dark chocolate reveals both elegance and energy rooted in the Pritchard Hill terrain.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature to allow the ripe fruit and structured tannins to harmonize: ideal with grilled lamb, aged cheeses or roasted gamey meats.
aroma: violets, herb bouquet, cedar, dark chocolate
palate: dense tannins around bramble, black cherry, blueberry and melted chocolate

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A resonant expression of Pritchard Hill Cabernet Sauvignon from 2012 thoughtfully balanced between muscular structure and refined resonance, offering compelling layers of dark fruit and volcanic minerality with poised restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a large Bordeaux-style glass gently decanted to reveal its depth, pairing elegantly with grilled lamb or aged cheddar.
palate: structured black cherry with oak spice

name: Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
description: BRAND Napa Valley's 2014 Cabernet Sauvignon is a powerful Pritchard Hill wine with black cherry, cassis, spice, and dark chocolate tones. Lush fruit is held by mountain-grown structure, giving the palate both breadth and a long future.
sommelierNotes: Decant for two hours if serving now and pair with ribeye, roast lamb, or braised beef.
aroma: Black cherry, cassis, spice, dark chocolate
palate: Lush dark fruit, muscular tannin, balanced acidity

name: Napa Valley Proprietary Red
description: This 2012 BRAND Napa Valley Proprietary Red is a deeply concentrated expression of Cabernet Sauvignon grown on the volcanic slopes of Pritchard Hill, presenting power and elegance in equal measure. It reveals lush dark fruit suffused with nuances of dark chocolate and licorice, framed by refined, velvety tannins. Aged thoughtfully in French oak, it balances structure and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool with hearty fare such as grilled lamb or braised short ribs; decanting is advised to allow the wine’s perfumed layers to bloom.
aroma: lush dark fruit with dark chocolate and licorice
palate: powerful yet elegant, velvety tannins

name: Napa Valley Proprietary Red Blend Napa Valley
description: The 2016 BRAND Napa Valley Proprietary Red Blend is a profound expression of Pritchard Hill’s volcanic soils combining Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon into a resonant tapestry of dark fruit and mineral-inflected structure. It unfolds with a refined depth that speaks of mountain-grown concentration and poised elegance. The texture is layered, inviting patience and reflection.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60–62 °F, ideally decanted for an hour to reveal its floral and cassis nuances. A splendid match for roasted lamb or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: crushed black cherries and mulberries with a hint of incense
palate: full‑bodied energy framed by grainy tannins

name: Al Dente Red Wine Sonoma County
description: A whispered invitation to summer repose this 2024 Al Dente from Breaking Bread coaxes brightness from 90 percent Mourvèdre and 10 percent Grenache with delicacy and restraint, a lean and earth‑touched red made for food and unhurried company. Whole‑cluster fermentation lends a lively, gentle grip and subtle complexity, while its organic Dry Creek Valley roots offer an elegant expression of place.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55‑60°F in a medium glass to preserve fresh vibrancy and gently coax out herbal nuance; ideal with grilled vegetables, seafood dishes or light farm‑to‑table fare.
aroma: earth‑tinged red cherry with gentle herb brush
palate: sleek, tender red fruit framed by soft tannin
finish: cool, food‑anchoring lingering with delicate earthiness

name: Cabernet Franc Mizany Vineyard
description: This light‑hearted Cabernet Franc from Mizany Vineyard blossoms with a flinty bouquet underscored by dusty cherry fruit and a gentle whisper of herbs, achieving a Chinon‑inspired freshness that feels both effortlessly graceful and engaging.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to accentuate its brightness alongside rustic stews or grilled seasonal vegetables for elegant simplicity.
palate: herb‑tinged cherry freshness

name: Marmalade Orange Wine Dry Creek Valley
description: A luminous and playful orange wine that captures the spontaneity of Dry Creek Valley in a glass, this vintage weaves together floral citrus and stone fruit underpinned by gentle textural lift from skin contact. The interplay of Muscat Blanc, Chardonnay and Sauvignon Blanc creates vibrant layers that unfurl with elegance and a kiss of marmalade brightness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a stemmed glass to highlight its juicy acidity and aromatic clarity, delightful with bright, citrusy dishes or lighter fare that welcomes its textured freshness.
aroma: zesty orange blossom and apricot framed by gentle spice
palate: bright tangerine and stone‑fruit with a subtle textured grip

name: Pet Nat Dry Creek Valley
description: A naturally effervescent Pétillant Naturel from Dry Creek Valley brought to life by 100 percent heritage Zinfandel, this 2024 “Pet Nat” presents youthful energy alongside nuanced minerality. Guava and wild strawberry notes weave through a fine Champagne‑like mousse, yielding a wine that is both vivacious and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender tulip glasses to preserve the delicate bubbles and bright acidity. Pairs luxuriously with grilled shellfish or light charcuterie under warm evening light.
aroma: guava and wild strawberry with wet gravel minerality
palate: Champagne‑like weight and fine bubbles with fruit‑forward youth
drinkWindow: Drink young for vibrant fruit and bubbles

name: Breaking Bread Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast
description: A graceful expression of Breaking Bread’s 2025 Pinot Noir from Sonoma Coast emerges with vibrant red cherry and forest floor undertones enlivened by muted baking spice, its texture silky yet lithe perched on hushed coastal freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to accent vibrant acidity: excellent with roasted duck breast or mushroom risotto for earthy nuance.
palate: silky texture with baking spice

name: Domaine Denis Breussin Vouvray Demi-Sec
description: The 2020 Denis Breussin Vouvray Demi‑Sec unfurls with a subtle bouquet of chalk‑tinged florals and exotic orchard fruits its texture caressing the palate with gentle sweetness tempered by a bright undercurrent of freshness, capturing both elegance and approachability.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–11 °C as an aperitif or alongside dishes that play with sweet‑savory balance: think lightly spiced fare or creamy cheeses.
palate: onctueux avec fruit gourmand et fraîcheur

name: Giacomo Brezza Barbera D'alba DOC Vigna Santa Rosalia
description: A noble Barbera crafted with subtlety and clarity from Santa Rosalia, this 2021 offers an alluring weave of ripe red berries and delicate floral whispers, framed by gently integrated oak. Silky in texture yet structured, it expresses elegance more than power, inviting a contemplative sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to highlight its fresh acidity; pairs exquisitely with roasted pork shoulder or mushroom–risotto.
aroma: ripe red berries with floral nuance
palate: silky texture, balanced acidity, gentle oak

name: Giacomo Brezza Barbera D'alba Vigna Santa Rosalia
appellation: Barbera d’Alba DOC Vigna Santa Rosalia
description: A fleshy Barbera from one of Langa’s treasured sites, bearing generous aromas of blackberry, plum and cassis with accents of blond tobacco and nutmeg, all framed by a supple sense of minerality and polished acidulous precision
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its juicy fruit and fine tannins Pair with heirloom tomato salad or charcuterie and aged salumi
palate: juicy black cherry, redcurrant, Quetsche plum

name: Giacomo Brezza Barolo Cannubi DOCG
description: An elegant expression of Cannubi’s historic grace, this Barolo offers perfumed rose petal and mint entwined with crushed red berry fruit underpinned by cedar and orange zest. The texture is refined and silky, the structure built on poised tannins and bright acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted, pairing beautifully with richly sauced game or slow‑braised beef, enhancing harmony without overpowering.
palate: silky, refined red berries with cedar and orange zest

name: Giacomo Brezza Barolo Castellero DOCG
description: A lithe and noble Barolo from Brezza’s single‑vineyard Castellero within Barolo commune refined yet vibrant revealing crimson‑fruited clarity with threads of wild rose and minty spice anchoring a firm structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in generous stemware with time to breathe allowing the wine’s poised tannins and aromatic tension to unfold alongside red meats or aged alpine cheeses.
palate: crimson berry, red cherry, subtle baking spice

name: Giacomo Brezza Barolo DOCG
description: An elegant Barolo of generous charm, the 2019 Giacomo Brezza Barolo DOCG opens with refined notes of bright red fruit underpinned by a whisper of sweet spice and floral nuance, framed by the noble Nebbiolo’s finesse. The palate delivers supple cherry and plum tones lifted by delicate violet and sage accents balanced beneath fine-grained tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool, around 16 °C, decanted for an hour to unveil layers of floral and savory depth, and pair with braised beef, aged hard cheese or porcini‑infused pasta.
aroma: bright red cherry with violet and sweet spice
palate: supple plum and sage with fine tannins

name: Giacomo Brezza Barolo Sarmassa DOCG
description: This 2018 Giacomo Brezza Barolo Sarmassa is a refined Barolo of noble bearing with intricate layers of dark cherry and violet infused with subtle underbrush and mint accents, all framed by elegant, polished tannins. It offers a poised, regal presence that reveals nuance and clarity even in its youth.
sommelierNotes: Serve in large goblets after decanting, particularly with roasted game or aged cheeses, to showcase its freshness and structural finesse.
palate: ripe marasca cherry, tobacco, licorice

name: Giacomo Brezza Chardonnay Langhe DOC
description: A graceful expression of Chardonnay from Piedmont that shows clarity and poise: pale straw hues open to delicate floral hints and crisp citrus framed by a refined mineral undertone. The palate feels lithe and balanced bringing fresh orchard fruit and subtle salinity with a restrained, elegant character.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled beside simply prepared seafood or soft raw cheeses to highlight its freshness and harmony; enjoy within its youthful phase for most vivacity.
palate: fresh orchard fruit with subtle mineral lift

name: Giacomo Brezza Langhe Chardonnay DOC
description: A finely wrought Langhe Chardonnay from the house of Giacomo Brezza, the 2019 vintage reveals an eloquent mineral core framed by pale yellow orchard fruit and gentle floral lift, all carried with elegant structure. The stainless steel–driven fermentation yields clarity and a lively tension, inviting early youthful drinking yet promising graceful charm in the short term.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled and bright alongside fresh shellfish or subtly seasoned vegetable dishes to accentuate the wine’s crisp mineral poise and floral nuance.
palate: lithe orchard fruit with vivid freshness
foodPairings: light pasta with butter and herbs

name: Giacomo Brezza Nebbiolo D'alba Vigna Rosalia DOC
appellation: Nebbiolo d’Alba DOC Vigna Santa Rosalia
description: A wine of alluring elegance this Nebbiolo d'Alba Vigna Santa Rosalia 2022 from Brezza offers a gracious bloom of violet and blackcurrant with a gentle mineral undertone, framed by fine-grained tannins and a sleek structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to showcase its subtle floral character and pair with refined white meats or mushroom‑infused risotto for an elegant match.
aroma: violet and blackcurrant with mineral nuance
palate: sleek, finely tannic with black fruit and floral lift

name: Giacomo Brezza Rosato Langhe DOC
description: A pale rosé of refined Nebbiolo character from the cool Langhe hills of Piedmont offering floral rose blossom and soft peach aromas with a framing of red berries and a whisper of minerality, finely sculpted and vibrant with gentle structure and refreshing acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled as an elegant aperitivo or alongside lightly grilled fish dishes or summer salads.
palate: refreshing acidity, gentle structure, fruity red berry

name: Vineyards Estate Pinot Noir
description: The 2019 Broadley Vineyards Estate Pinot Noir offers an elegant expression of Oregon’s gentle terroir offering bright cherry and raspberry tones beneath a silken overlay of earth and forest floor. Its texture unfolds with velvety tannins and subtle cedar warmth that echo the careful whole‑cluster fermentation and judicious oak aging. The wine conveys a poised balance between lively fruit and grounded, savory depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature to accentuate its freshness and pair with grilled lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes, allowing its nuanced earthiness to harmonise with savory fare.
palate: silken texture with cedar and earth

name: Vineyards Willamette Valley Pinot Noir
description: A graceful and inviting Pinot Noir born of Broadley’s Willamette Valley terroir this 2024 release marries vibrant red fruits with gentle earthiness in a refined expression. Its elegant structure and supple tannins evoke a sense of poised complexity, delivering an approachable wine that belies its modest price.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a large Burgundy glass to showcase its brightness, pairing beautifully with roasted duck breast or mushroom ragout.
palate: silky with bay leaf and black tea

name: Brulieres de Beychevelle Saint Julien
description: A well‑crafted Haut‑Médoc that gently balances youthful energy with classic Bordeaux structure, offering enticing blackcurrant and subtle spice framed in an approachable yet confident manner.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool around 17 °C, ideally alongside rich red meats or game dishes to complement its rounded fruit and modest tannic grip.
aroma: blackcurrant and red fruit with spice
palate: powerful and fruity with roundness

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: A commanding expression of Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru from Bruno Clair’s 2018 vintage offering an intense garnet hue, layering dense black cherry and sloe fruit with undercurrents of boysenberry and violet, finishing with disciplined power and remarkable length. This refined wine reveals both depth and purity in its structure.
sommelierNotes: Best served slightly below cellar temperature around 14 °C in large Burgundy glasses to reveal its floral aromatics and vibrant mid‑palate. It will reward decanting and pairs beautifully with roast duck, game birds or wild mushroom‑accented dishes.
palate: sappy black fruit, powdery texture

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: A commanding expression of Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru from Bruno Clair’s 2019 vintage offering an intense garnet hue, layering dense black cherry and sloe fruit with undercurrents of boysenberry and violet, finishing with disciplined power and remarkable length. This refined wine reveals both depth and purity in its structure.
sommelierNotes: Best served slightly below cellar temperature around 14 °C in large Burgundy glasses to reveal its floral aromatics and vibrant mid‑palate. It will reward decanting and pairs beautifully with roast duck, game birds or wild mushroom‑accented dishes.
palate: sappy black fruit, powdery texture

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: A commanding expression of Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru from Bruno Clair’s 2020 vintage offering an intense garnet hue, layering dense black cherry and sloe fruit with undercurrents of boysenberry and violet, finishing with disciplined power and remarkable length. This refined wine reveals both depth and purity in its structure.
sommelierNotes: Best served slightly below cellar temperature around 14 °C in large Burgundy glasses to reveal its floral aromatics and vibrant mid‑palate. It will reward decanting and pairs beautifully with roast duck, game birds or wild mushroom‑accented dishes.
palate: sappy black fruit, powdery texture

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Clos du Fonteny Monopole
appellation: Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Clos du Fonteny Monopole
description: This Bruno Clair 2020 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Clos du Fonteny Monopole offers a ruby‑red hue and a refined nose of morello cherry underpinned by subtle spice and musk, revealing an air of finesse and poise. On the palate it unfolds with silken texture and well‑measured mineral energy, finishing with a saline grace and lingering tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 16 °C in a large Burgundy glass after decanting to highlight its red‑fruit perfume and elegant structure, and pair with game birds or roasted duck.
palate: Silken, mineral‑tinged red‑fruit layer

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Petite Chapelle
description: A lavishly concentrated premier‑cru Pinot Noir from Bruno Clair this 2020 Gevrey‑Chambertin Petite Chapelle offers a deep red robe and a commanding framework with ripe red and black fruit aromas and a persuasive tannic underpinning drawn from its finely wrought limestone soils and prudent oak élevage.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature, allowing the wine to open with aeration and pairing beautifully with richly flavoured fare or aged cheeses.
palate: powerful tannic structure

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay les Charmes aux Pretres
description: This 2019 Marsannay “Le Charme aux Prêtres” from Domaine Bruno Clair presents poised, fresh red‑fruit aromatics and an elegant purity of expression drawing the taster in from the first swirl. The palate unveils crunchy cherry and raspberry tones framed by refined structure and supple underlying tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in decanted form to balance its vibrancy: pairs wonderfully with roast duck or herb‑coated pork loin and regional charcuterie.
palate: crunchy red fruits with refined tannins

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay les Charmes aux Pretres
description: A refined expression of Marcel Bruno Clair’s Marsannay Les Charmes aux Prêtres from the 2020 vintage presents a luminous ruby hue and aromas of fresh red fruit with a subtle floral lift balanced by gentle poultry notes and chalky mineral undertones, expressing both clarity and a hint of earth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature alongside poultry or mushroom dishes to complement its bright fruit and fine tannic texture.
aroma: Fresh red fruits with floral lift
palate: Crunchy, vibrant red fruit with elegant structure

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Marsannay les Charmes aux Pretres
description: A gracious village‑marsannay offering from Domaine Bruno Clair the 2021 “La Charme aux Prêtres” unfolds with poised red‑ruby clarity and an engaging bouquet of fresh red berries refined by gentle oak nuance. Its palate is distinguished by a crisp, elegant fruit core framed in finely integrated structure, delivering harmonious Burgundian restraint with subtle textural depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C to accentuate its freshness and finesse; pairs beautifully with classic coq au vin or mild roasted game, complementing the wine’s red‑fruit clarity and refined structure.
aroma: fresh red berries with subtle oak nuance
palate: crisp elegant red‑fruit core with refined structure

name: Domaine Bruno Clair Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru Blanc en la Rue de de Vergy
description: A yellow gold robe reveals a wine of crystalline minerality and poised elegance its mineral clarity quietly commanding with a refined aromatic breadth that unfolds across the palate maintaining exceptional length and precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 C in fine white Burgundy glasses allow its chalky tension to accentuate shellfish or lightly grilled river fish.
aroma: crystalline minerality, lemon zest, white flowers
palate: taut chalky tension with elegant citrus breadth

name: Morey Saint Denis Blanc en la Rue de Vergy
description: A precise and crystalline white Burgundy of rare pedigree from Côte de Nuits, this 2010 Morey‑Saint‑Denis “En la rue de Vergy” by Bruno Clair displays a yellow‑gold hue and chiselled mineral character plying a wide aromatic palette across a strikingly long finish
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to best reveal its mineral drive, a perfect companion to refined shellfish or buttery white fish
palate: broad, elegant, chalk‑inflected

name: Morey Saint Denis Blanc en la Rue de Vergy
description: This 2011 Morey‑Saint‑Denis “En la Rue de Vergy” Blanc by Bruno Clair presents a yellow‑gold hue and unfolds with an elegant mineral core supported by subtle floral and toasty nuances, with remarkable length. It conveys understated power and poise evocative of rare white expressions from the Cote de Nuits.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12‑14 °C, ideally with delicate cream‑sauced poultry or refined shellfish preparations.
palate: mineral‑driven, ample and harmonious

name: Morey Saint Denis Blanc en la Rue de Vergy
description: Bruno Clair's 2015 Morey-Saint-Denis Blanc En la Rue de Vergy is a mineral, tightly drawn Chardonnay from limestone soils above the village. Oak maturation adds breadth, but the wine's defining qualities are precision, aromatic range, and remarkable length.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 11-13°C and allow a little air; pair with turbot, roast poultry, lobster, or a restrained cream sauce.
palate: Broad yet linear, mineral, finely oaked

name: BW20 Champagne Pierre Gerbais Champagne Champ Viole Chardonnay
description: An enchanting blanc de blancs from a single historic lieu‑dit, this Extra‑Brut Champagne reveals a graceful balance of talc‑fine minerality and orchard fruit, caressed by a pillowy mousse and elegant structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in slender flutes to accentuate its fine bead, pairing beautifully with oysters or delicate seafood starters.
palate: chalky mineral spine with orchard fruit

name: BW20 Champagne Pierre Gerbais Champagne les Grandes Cotes Pinot Noir
description: This champagne blooms with gentle elegance, offering a subtle weave of vibrant red fruit and soft pastry nuances. The expression is precise and luminous revealing delicate layers of chalky minerality and graceful texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in slender flute or tulip glass to reveal its fine bead and vibrant energy, perfect with light seafood or creamy cheeses.
palate: elegant, mineral‐tinged fruit

name: Pinot Grigio Friuli
description: This 2025 Ca‑Stele Pinot Grigio from Friuli unfolds with elegant floral clarity and a delicate pear‑tinged freshness that speaks of its northeastern Italian origin, framed by a whisper of minerality and graceful poise on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8–10 °C to highlight its bright fruit and floral character, a superb match with seafood‑forward starters or light antipasti.
palate: ripe green fruits with fine acidity

name: Prosecco DOC
description: This NV Prosecco DOC from Ca’Stella offers fresh, bright charm with playful bubbles and lively lemon‑citrus and green apple notes accented by delicate floral undertones, evoking the gentle spirit of Veneto’s sparkling tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled as an aperitif or alongside light seafood and creamy risotto for a harmonious and elegant pairing.
aroma: lemon citrus and green apple with a hint of blossom
palate: bright, crisp and delicately effervescent

name: Prosecco DOC
description: Bright and lifted this Prosecco DOC shows a gentle orchard fruit character with crisp vitality and refined bubbles, offering poised charm and early pleasure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a flute its energetic sparkle and light body make it a versatile aperitif and a refreshing foil for light seafood or crisp salads.
palate: crisp, fruit‑driven, lively

name: De Reguengo Solsticio
description: This 2019 Solstício from Cabeças do Reguengo is a composed field blend woven of Trincadeira, Aragonez, Alicante Bouschet, Grand Noir, Tinta de Olho Branco and Castelão from ancient vines at nearly 600 metres on granitic soils in the Serra de S. Mamede. It matured patiently for 23 months in venerable French oak barrels resulting in a wine of fine structure and rustic elegance. Dark fruit melds with mineral undercurrents and a noble austerity that speaks of its place.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled near cellar temperature in a generous Burgundy‑style glass, ideally alongside rustic fare such as roast lamb with herbs or rich mushroom ragout to complement its dusty tannins and earthy fruit.
aroma: dark plum, forest floor, mild spice
palate: earth‑tinged red fruit, supple tannins, granite minerality

name: De Reguengo Vira Cabecas Tinto
description: Bold and grounded yet graceful this 2019 Vira Cabeças Tinto unfolds as a thoughtful tapestry of the Alentejo terroir drawing from centuries‑old vines, natural fermentation and extended aging in large oak tonels. The wine offers a harmonious interplay of ripe black and red fruit softened by subtle oak, delivering a refined, textural depth rather than overpowering power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C alongside stews or roasted lamb to coax out its balance of freshness and plush structure, or let it breathe if served nearer room temperature to fully reveal its layered complexity.
aroma: ripe black and red fruits with discreet oak nuances
palate: silky textured with balanced freshness and fine tannins

name: De Reguengo Vira Cabecas Tinto
description: Bold and grounded yet graceful this 2021 Vira Cabeças Tinto unfolds as a thoughtful tapestry of the Alentejo terroir drawing from centuries‑old vines, natural fermentation and extended aging in large oak tonels. The wine offers a harmonious interplay of ripe black and red fruit softened by subtle oak, delivering a refined, textural depth rather than overpowering power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C alongside stews or roasted lamb to coax out its balance of freshness and plush structure, or let it breathe if served nearer room temperature to fully reveal its layered complexity.
aroma: ripe black and red fruits with discreet oak nuances
palate: silky textured with balanced freshness and fine tannins

name: Five
description: Cain Five 2013 is a dense, structured Spring Mountain District blend with forest, wild-herb, and dark-fruit character. Cabernet-led depth is tempered by an earthy, distinctly site-driven savor that unfolds with air.
sommelierNotes: Decant for several hours if serving now and pair with roast lamb, wild mushrooms, or braised beef; the wine remains suited to further cellaring.
aroma: Forest floor, wild herbs, dark fruit
palate: Dense, warm, structured, generous

name: Estate Cvc Red Wine Chalk Hill Sonoma County
description: A dense and refined 2019 Bordeaux‐style red from Calluna’s Chalk Hill estate, its poise emerging from the blend of Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, Malbec and Petit Verdot showing both muscle and grace. Aromas of cassis, black cherry, cigar wrapper and soil rise on the nose and are framed by discreet new oak. The palate is focused with a pure core of fruit, fine balance and ripe tannins leading to a long layered finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve with short decanting at 16 °C. Ideal alongside roasted lamb or aged cheeses to complement its elegant structure.
palate: pure, full‑bodied, focused

name: Estate Estate Blanc Chalk Hill Sonoma County
description: This refined white Bordeaux–style blend from Chalk Hill melds 85 percent Sauvignon Blanc with 15 percent Sémillon to present a graceful yet layered expression. It opens with bright citrus blossom and Honeycrisp apple lifted by gentle mineral undercurrents and a hint of vanillin oak, culminating in striking depth and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at about 50–54 °F to preserve its vibrancy. It pairs elegantly with simply grilled shellfish or creamy goat cheese, and its bright acidity also balances richer poultry dishes.
aroma: citrus blossoms, apple, mineral, vanillin oak
palate: lively citrus and stone fruit with rounded Semillon honeyed depth

name: Le Chambertin Grand Cru
description: A commanding expression of Chambertin Grand Cru from Camille Giroud vintage 2011, where poised cherry and black currant fruit evolve into deeper tones of spice and discreet earth, framed by firm yet refined structure. The wine reveals both gravity and silkiness, an elegant ambassador of Côte de Nuits power and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tall Burgundy glass at cellar temperature around 16 °C, decant for an hour to allow its steely core and earthy grace to emerge. Ideal with game birds, truffled dishes, or aged Comté.
palate: elegant cherry, spice, firm structure

name: Camille Giroud Vosne Romanee 1er Cru les Suchots
description: The 2017 Camille Giroud Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru “Les Suchots” offers a refined expression of Vosne‑Romanée: a graceful palette of dark cherry and floral fruit entwined with a whisper of spice and delicate cocoa‑tinged undergrowth. It unfolds with elegant depth and polished tannins drawing one toward a lingering finish of subtle minerality and red berry clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15°C in a tall Burgundy glass to showcase its finesse; pairs beautifully with roast duck, wild game terrine or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: elegant, polished tannins with cocoa‑tinged depth

name: Champagne Camille Saves Anais Jolie Coeur Brut Grand Cru
description: A gracefully expressive Champagne that evokes the refined power of Bouzy Grand Cru terroir with gentle generosity : the 2015 Camille Savès Anaïs Jolie‑Coeur unfolds in the glass with fine, creamy effervescence and a poised interplay of bright red fruits and chalk‑tinged minerality. It offers elegant texture and tension marrying breadth and freshness in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 °C in tulip glasses to preserve the mousse and highlight the breadth of Pinot Noir; perfect with rich shellfish or buttery preparations to complement the wine’s creamy texture.
aroma: red apple and ripe pear with chalky minerality
palate: warm, enveloping and fleshy with creamy effervescence

name: Champagne Camille Saves Carte Blanche Brut Grand Cru
appellation: Champagne (Premier/Grand Cru blend from Bouzy region)
description: This non‑vintage Carte Blanche Brut from Camille Savès marries the noble intensity of Bouzy Grand Cru with a graceful poise rooted in meticulous ageing in chalk‑lined cellars. The wine reveals a vinous character marked by bright red fruit and fine structure that reflects both precision and generosity of terroir. Its long élevage bestows depth while preserving vibrant freshness and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10 °C in tall flute or white wine glasses to highlight its chalky minerality and precise mousse: pairs beautifully with delicate seafood such as oysters or smoked salmon, or with soft‑washed cheeses.
palate: fresh, structured, intense fruit fuse with a subtle crystallised tension

name: Rioja Joven Tinto
description: A youthful Rioja brimming with vivacity and vibrant fruit expression. The wine pours a deep ruby‑purple hue and unfurls aromas of cherry, raspberry and bramble with a whisper of violet and a hint of licorice. On the palate it is juicy and harmonious with generous body, fruit depth and a subtle, playful mineral edge.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C in medium‑bowled red wine glasses to showcase its bright fruit character. Pair with rustic grilled vegetables or mild cured meats to complement its freshness.
palate: juicy, balanced, medium‑bodied
finish: gently persistent with a touch of licorice

name: Carmes de Rieussec Sauternes
description: A refined half‑bottle of Sauternes from Château Rieussec’s second label that offers luminous waves of golden complexity elegant and fresh with candied citrus, dried fruit and honeyed undertones
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass around 10 to 12 °C, ideal with foie gras, blue cheese or delicate fruit‑based desserts
palate: lush sweetness balanced by vibrant acidity

name: Carnes de Rieussec Sauternes
description: A refined, golden‑hued Sauternes bearing the hallmark elegance of Château Rieussec’s second wine, Carmes de Rieussec 2019 half‑bottle, offering a delicate bouquet of citrus blossom and honeysuckle that evolves into honey‑edged pear, apricot and subtle spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass alongside foie gras, blue cheeses or fruit‑based desserts to highlight its sweet‑acid balance.
palate: honey‑edged apricot, bright acidity, refined sweetness

name: Domaine Castagnier Bourgogne Rouge
description: A refined Bourgogne Rouge from Domaine Castagnier 2014 that reveals a gentle crescendo in the glass its bouquet opens to ripe red fruit laced with subtle licorice and a floral hint its palate offers fine, integrated tannins and an elegant sense of poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 14 – 15 °C, allow gentle aeration and pair with duck breast or red berry–glazed game dishes.
palate: fine integrated tannins with poise
drinkWindow: now to within 5–7 years of vintage

name: Domaine Castagnier Coteaux Bourguignons
description: This bottle, if indeed the 2015 Dom Castagnier Coteaux Bourguignons from the Côte de Nuits, likely presents a radiant garnet hue carrying a promise of youthful fruit. One might anticipate a bright, accessible character, combining juicy red berries within a framework of supple Pinot Noir elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperature around 14–15 °C to reveal red fruit aromatics; pair gently roasted poultry or summer charcuterie for harmony.
palate: supple fruit with gentle structure

name: Domaine Castagnier Coteaux Bourguignons Pinot Noir
description: This 2017 Coteaux Bourguignons Pinot Noir from Dom Castagnier presents a delicate translucence, opening on whispers of red berries and a faint hint of fresh garden herbs. The palate conveys an agile, lively texture supported by crisp acidity and a subtle peppery undertone, all framed in a refined, ethereal form.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C in tulip-shaped stemware, paired with delicate charcuterie or a young comté to lift the wine’s tender fruit and clean lines.
palate: lively, crisp, peppery undertone

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Aligote
description: A gracefully poised Bourgogne Aligoté from Jérôme Castagnier’s domaine near Morey‑Saint‑Denis offering refined simplicity and clarity, where pale lemon hues give way to a crisp interplay of citrus blossom and stone fruit, lifted by an underlying mineral tension and subtle floral nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled as an elegant aperitif or alongside delicate seafood; its lively acidity and structure make it equally suitable with goat cheese or light shellfish preparations.
palate: fresh orchard fruit and bright acidity

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Passetoutgrain
description: A lithe and perfumed Bourgogne Passetoutgrain from Domaine Jérôme Castagnier’s 2020 vintage this wine offers energetic red fruit brightness and a whisper of spice framed by a mineral thread that carries the wine with effortless poise
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to elevate its fresh vibrancy and pair it with simple fare—charcuterie or grilled chicken—so that its vivacious fruit and fine structure can sing
palate: energetic fruit with subtle spice

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Passetoutgrains
description: A luminous and elegant Bourgogne Passetoutgrains rendered by Castagnier from the modest yet refined 2019 vintage, beautifully balanced between Pinot Noir and Gamay in a co‑planted parcel near Morey‑Saint‑Denis. The bouquet opens with vibrant red berry and delicate floral lift, underpinned by a refreshing tensile texture and a mineral‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to accentuate its vivacity, particularly lovely alongside charcuterie, light pâtés or fresh chèvre salads.
palate: lively acidity with mid‑palate grip

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: An elegant expression of Burgundy with restrained suppleness and clarity. The 2018 Dom Jérôme by Castagnier offers bright cherry tones and understated earthiness in a crystalline frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature in a tall Burgundy glass and pair with roasted duck breast or wild mushroom risotto to balance its finesse.
aroma: bright cherry and subtle forest herbs
palate: silky red fruit with mineral clarity

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: An elegant expression of Burgundy with restrained suppleness and clarity. The 2019 Dom Jérôme by Castagnier offers bright cherry tones and understated earthiness in a crystalline frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature in a tall Burgundy glass and pair with roasted duck breast or wild mushroom risotto to balance its finesse.
aroma: bright cherry and subtle forest herbs
palate: silky red fruit with mineral clarity

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru
description: A refined expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin’s most revered slope, this wine reveals elegant aromas of spiced cherry and cassis enfolding a sinewy core of red fruit and subtle woodland nuance, delivering presence with poise rather than opulence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a large Burgundy glass to open its perfume pairing beautifully with richly flavoured poultry or game birds.
palate: sinewy red fruit with subtle woodland nuance

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
description: This 2019 Dom Jérôme Castagnier Clos de la Roche Grand Cru emerges from Morey‑Saint‑Denis with an elegant density of red and black fruits suffused with toasty oak, crafting a wine of firm structure and noble restraint, destined for graceful maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in the cellar between 14 and 16 °C alongside game birds or rich red meat, allowing its tension and depth to unfold.
aroma: red and black fruits with toasty oak
palate: ample, dense, structured tannins
finish: harmonious, long return of fruit and warmth

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Clos Saint Denis Grand Cru
description: This 2019 Domaine Castagnier Clos‑Saint‑Denis Grand Cru unfolds with refined purity: a polished marriage of dark red fruit and delicate spice framed by a mineral undercurrent that bespeaks its Côte de Nuits terroir. The texture is silken yet structured with fine-grained tannins promising depth and poise with age.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a large Burgundy glass at 16 °C after gentle decanting; pairing shines with roasted game birds or lamb in herb jus.
palate: silken, concentrated, mineral

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: In an elegant and refined manner this 2018 Domaine Jérôme Castagnier Clos‑de‑Vougeot Grand Cru unfolds with layered rose petal and wild red‑berry perfume, a mouthfeel graced by dense yet admirably fine tannins, reflecting both a vivid sense of its southern Clos‑de‑Vougeot terroir and the generous 2018 vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve at approximately 16 °C in a large Burgundy glass after gentle decanting to showcase its balance alongside richly flavored preparations such as roast veal or game birds.
aroma: rose petal and wild red berries
palate: dense yet fine tannins with vivid terroir expression
foodPairings: soft washed‑rind cheese such as Époisses

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: In an elegant and refined manner this 2019 Domaine Jérôme Castagnier Clos‑de‑Vougeot Grand Cru unfolds with layered rose petal and wild red‑berry perfume, a mouthfeel graced by dense yet admirably fine tannins, reflecting both a vivid sense of its southern Clos‑de‑Vougeot terroir and the generous 2019 vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve at approximately 16 °C in a large Burgundy glass after gentle decanting to showcase its balance alongside richly flavored preparations such as roast veal or game birds.
aroma: rose petal and wild red berries
palate: dense yet fine tannins with vivid terroir expression
foodPairings: soft washed‑rind cheese such as Époisses

name: Domaine Jerome Castagnier Coteaux Bourguignons Pinot Noir
description: This 2019 Dom Jérôme Castagnier Coteaux Bourguignons Pinot Noir reveals crystalline clarity and vibrant energy drawing you into a fragrant whirl of wild cherry and bright red berry aromas edged with subtle saline tension. On the palate the wine offers silky ripeness underscored by graceful tension and a whisper of licorice on the finish
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 14 °C to temper the vivacity: a superb partner for roasted poultry or autumnal game birds.
aroma: wild cherry and bright red berries with saline clarity
palate: silky, gently fresh, red fruit framed by fine structure

name: Sarl Jerome Castagnier Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: Crimson‑tinged and resonant the 2018 Jérôme Castagnier Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru murmurs of red cherry and bramble on the nose enriched by gentle floral and forest floor hints derived from its storied slopes between Morey‑Saint‑Denis and Chambolle‑Musigny ([bourgognewine.dk](https://bourgognewine.dk/products/bonnes-mares-grand-cru-2018?utm_source=openai)) The palate reveals concentrated depth and structure with firm yet refined tannins underpinning an expansive, lingering, racé finish touched by spice and dark fruit ([hachette-vins.com](https://www.hachette-vins.com/guide-vins/les-vins/jerome-castagnier-2015-2018-1/201829601/?utm_source=openai))
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15–16 °C, decant if young to coax forth its layered complexity, pairing beautifully with roasted game or truffle‑accented fare ([bourgognewine.dk](https://bourgognewine.dk/products/bonnes-mares-grand-cru-2018?utm_source=openai))
palate: firm tannins, concentrated dark fruit, spice
foodPairings: duck breast fillet stuffed with foie‑gras

name: Sarl Jerome Castagnier Echezeaux Grand Cru
description: This is an elegant expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis Grand Cru from Jérôme Castagnier, showing delicate red fruit and rose petal nuances laced with fine spice and an undercurrent of sanguine earth, framed by supple tannins and refined structure. It offers an impression of effortless grace with an underlying depth that promises enduring allure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15° C in a large Burgundy glass, ideally paired with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑studded terrine where the wine’s finesse and rose‑tinged aromatics will shine.
aroma: red fruit, rose petal, fine spice
palate: supple tannins, refined structure

name: Sarl Jerome Castagnier Echezeaux Grand Cru
description: This is an elegant expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis Grand Cru from Jérôme Castagnier, showing delicate red fruit and rose petal nuances laced with fine spice and an undercurrent of sanguine earth, framed by supple tannins and refined structure. It offers an impression of effortless grace with an underlying depth that promises enduring allure.

palate: supple tannins, refined structure

name: Al Poggio Bianco
description: A refined and luminous expression of Chardonnay from the slopes of Ama this 2017 Al Poggio offers a pure and polished profile with delicate floral allure and bright orchard fruit lifted by a cool mineral whisper, marked by clarity and elegance in modest golden hues. It conveys an old‑world charm grounded in Tuscan terroir while celebrating the grape’s natural poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at cellar‑cool temperature in slender white wine glasses to enhance its finesse; splendid with shellfish, mild cheeses or simply on its own in quiet contemplation.
palate: crisp orchard fruit with mineral backbone

name: Castello Di Uzzano Chianti Classico
description: A graceful expression of Chianti Classico character the Castello di Uzzano 2019 presents bright cherry and crushed berry aromas softened by gentle herbal spice nuances, framed in a supple structure that balances freshness with refined depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature to reveal soft red fruit and savory herbs, an ideal match for hearty tomato‑based pastas or rustic Tuscan fare.
palate: bright cherry fruit with balanced acidity

name: Castelnau de Suduiraut Sauternes
description: A lovely golden yellow Sauternes carrying early‑appealing charm from Château Suduiraut’s secondary cuvée cast from specific early‑ripening parcels. The nose unveils a dainty interlude of tropical fruit segueing into gingerbread and candied citrus alongside gentle spice and barrel nuance. The palate is weighted yet crisp, offering freshness that complements botrytised richness, while the finish lingers in candied fruit and spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, consider decanting for an hour if youthful, ideal alongside blue‑veined cheese or fruit‑based desserts.
palate: smooth, powerful, fresh botrytis‑driven
finish: long on candied fruit and spice

name: Castelnau de Suduiraut Sauternes
description: A lovely golden yellow Sauternes carrying early‑appealing charm from Château Suduiraut’s secondary cuvée cast from specific early‑ripening parcels. The nose unveils a dainty interlude of tropical fruit segueing into gingerbread and candied citrus alongside gentle spice and barrel nuance. The palate is weighted yet crisp, offering freshness that complements botrytised richness, while the finish lingers in candied fruit and spice.

finish: long on candied fruit and spice

name: Cave de Sancerre Sancerre Blanc les Garennes
description: This Sancerre Blanc from Cave de Sancerre’s single‑parcel ‘Les Garennes’ offers bright citrus lift and fine limestone‑tinged florals framed by a graceful spine of mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled near 12 °C to highlight its vivacious clarity; superb with delicate white fish or classic goat‑cheese crottin.
palate: precise mineral‑driven fruit intensity
foodPairings: lightly roasted turbot with baby vegetables

name: Cave de Saumur Saumur Blanc les Pouches
description: A luminous Chenin Blanc from Cave de Saumur etching vineyards of clay‑silty sands above crayeux tuffeau, this 2023 Les Pouches reveals a pale gold hue with silver glints, offering a poised nose of white peach, Williams pear and acacia‑lime flowers with a subtle flint‑tinge drawn from its terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve quite chilled around 10 °C, ideal as an aperitif or alongside delicate seafood in cream or fresh goat cheese to mirror its purity and finesse.
aroma: white peach and Williams pear with acacia‑lime floral note
palate: light‑bodied, crisp, hint of flintiness

name: Ayni Rose Nature Sparkling
description: This wine offers an elegant mousse with delicate strawberry and peach nuances set against a creamy, toasty backdrop, finishing crisp and finely balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a flute to preserve the pristine effervescence; pairs beautifully with light seafood or festive canapés.
aroma: strawberry and peach interwoven with creamy toast
palate: creamy, fruit-forward with tart cherry and peach

name: Estate Chardonnay
description: The 2018 Chakana Estate Selection Chardonnay from Mendoza offers a graceful expression of ripe stone fruit and citrus framed by gentle oak. It shows an appealing, slightly pulpy mid‑palate texture that balances richness with freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 50–54 °F in tulip‑shaped white wine glasses. It partners beautifully with grilled white fish in lemon butter or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: oily yet fresh, with nectarine and citrus
foodPairings: grilled sea bass with lemon butter

name: Estate Red
description: This 2017 Chakana Estate Red exhibits focused dark berry and plum fruit laced with violet florals, underpinned by subtle exotic spice and mocha nuances, resulting in a poised and elegant expression of high‑elevation Mendoza.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature to highlight its refined structure; try with grilled lamb or mushroom ragù to complement its savory layers.
palate: dark berry and plum with mocha undertones

name: Champagne Camille Saves Carte Blanche Brut 1er Cru
description: An elegant Champagne of character and old‑world poise showing fine interplay of Pinot Noir depth and Chardonnay brightness in each shimmering sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender flute around 8 °C to highlight its lively bead and pair it gracefully with seafood or rich hors d’oeuvres.
aroma: discreet floral and brioche notes emerging to peach, almond, nuts
palate: fresh, poised, subtly tannic in finish

name: Champagne de Sousa Avec le Temps Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut Grand Cru
description: A radiant non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs Extra Brut drawn purely from Grand Cru parcels in Avize, Oger, Le Mesnil and Cramant, it exudes crystalline citrus and blossom lifted by the chalky spine of Côte des Blancs terroir. It balances purity and texture with an elegant richness that unfolds with each sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C in a tulip glass to reveal its mineral poise; it partners beautifully with oysters, sushi or delicate cheeses.
aroma: brioche and white flowers with citrus essence
palate: round chalk‑driven minerality with juicy finesse

name: Champagne de Sousa Chemin des Terriors
description: This non‑vintage cuvée is elegantly dense yet vivid in character, offering a refined tapestry of orchard fruits and gentle spice framed by chalk‑anchored minerality, presenting a vinous expression that invites close attention.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 °C in a fine flute or tulip glass to showcase its delicate bead; pairs divinely with oysters, creamy cheeses or light seafood preparations.
palate: fresh orchard fruit, citrus tension, subtle wood note

name: Champagne Edouard Duval Blanc D'eulalie
description: A pale golden and refined expression of Côte des Bar terroir, this Blanc d’Eulalie is crafted from 100 percent Chardonnay vines over fifty years old on the sunlit L’Epicéa parcel it unfolds with gentle fruit and a mineral blossoming that speaks of limestone and oyster fossil soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at circa 10 °C in an elegant flute or tulip glass it pairs beautifully with lobster, light-white fish or delicate shellfish.
aroma: floral with wet stone, red apple, butter
palate: buttered apple, pear, marzipan

name: Champagne Edouard Duval Noir D'eulalie
description: A generous blanc de noirs from Champagne’s Côte des Bar offering noble intensity and supple texture, Noir d’Eulalie unfurls with a refined presence that balances richness and minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in tulip‑shaped flutes or white wine glasses, ideal with shellfish or delicate poultry preparations.
palate: textural depth framed by chalky minerality

name: Champagne G Gruet et Fils Brut Reserve
description: A refined nonvintage Champagne from G Gruet & Fils whose generous expression evokes mature orchard fruits and toasted brioche notes with graceful structure and velvety texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C as an elegant aperitif or alongside delicate hors d’œuvres such as smoked salmon or mild cheeses.
palate: creamy texture with vibrant fruit and fine mousse

name: Champagne Hugues Godme Grand Jardins-Le Blanc de Noirs Grand Cru
description: A radiant Champagne born from the Grand Cru terroirs of Verzenay and Verzy this Blanc de Noirs Grand Cru offers a luminous core of dried pear and brioche framed by chalky mineral tension and a whisper of orchard spice. The texture is supple yet poised delivering a svelte mousse and a nervy structure that speaks of vertical energy and refined restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10–12°C in a large white wine or universal Champagne glass to reveal its subtle red fruit tones, perfect with gently spiced lamb tagine or aged Comté.
aroma: dried pear and brioche with gentle spice
palate: supple mousse, orchard fruit, mineral tension

name: Champagne Hugues Godme Jardins Premiers-La Reserve 1ER Cru
description: An elegant blend from Hugues Godmé in Champagne’s Montagne de Reims, Jardins Premiers “La Réserve” Extra‑Brut unveils mineral grace and subtle orchard fruit. The wine offers delicate pear and honeysuckle aromas underpinned by equal parts Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, reflecting biodynamic care. The texture shows refined depth and a lively, precise mousse.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 9 °C in a tulip‑shaped flute to highlight its fresh acidity and minerality; excellent with scallop carpaccio or buttery fish.
palate: mineral and orchard fruit

name: Champagne Jean Hanotin Brut Tradition Grand Cru
description: Jean Hanotin Brut Tradition Grand Cru NV unfolds with pale golden hues and delicate effervescence, guided by two‑thirds Pinot Noir and one‑third Chardonnay from the Grand Cru terroir of Verzy. It offers an inviting bouquet of red‑fruited and lightly floral notes, all framed by fresh, balanced restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an aperitif, or accompany shellfish or seafood; its finesse and gentle fruit echo beautifully with delicate dishes.
palate: fresh entry with balanced structure and gentle fruit

name: Champagne Jose Dhondt Brut Blanc de Blancs
description: This non‑vintage Champagne Blanc de Blancs from José Dhondt offers an elegant expression of Côte des Blancs terroir with bright citrus and floral whispers underscored by a subtle chalky minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender flutes to highlight its vivacious acidity and refined bubbles; pairs beautifully with shellfish and soft cheeses.
palate: creamy texture with chalky mineral and ripe pear
foodPairings: poached white fish with lemon beurre blanc

name: Champagne Jose Dhondt Brut Blanc de Blancs
description: A finely wrought non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs from a small family estate in Oger, this Champagne offers a silken, creamy texture over a precise, chalk‑inflected frame with bright notes of lime, pear and almond.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip flute, it will elevate shellfish, delicate seafood and mild cheeses with its freshness and subtle richness.
palate: creamy texture with chalky minerality and pear

name: Champagne Leclerc Briant Chateau D'avize Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs Brut Zero
description: This Grand Cru blanc de blancs is luminous and richly expressive while retaining an elegant clarity. The delicate interplay of pastry‑like cream, chalk and lemon hints carries through to a saline and tender mineral frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender flute to reveal its fine mousse and pair it with scallop carpaccio or butter‑poached lobster for a harmonious match.
aroma: pastry cream, lemon zest, chalky nuance
palate: elegant mousse, refined creaminess, saline lift

name: Champagne Leclerc Briant Chateau D'avize Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs Brut Zero
description: This Grand Cru blanc de blancs is luminous and richly expressive while retaining an elegant clarity. The delicate interplay of pastry‑like cream, chalk and lemon hints carries through to a saline and tender mineral frame.
