palate: elegant mousse, refined creaminess, saline lift

name: Champagne Leclerc Briant Extra Brut Champagne
description: A crystalline and refined expression from Champagne Leclerc Briant, this vintage Extra Brut 2019 glows with pale straw hues and reveals an energetic core of citrus, crushed stone, and pear. The vibrant mousse and brisk acidity frame a mineral-laced core of Meyer lemon and lemongrass lifted by floral grace and hints of toasted bread.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender flute to preserve its vivacity: it pairs exquisitely with shellfish, fresh oysters, or elegant seafood starters.
palate: energizing citrus acidity with mineral concentration

name: Champagne Leclerc Briant Reserve Extra Brut
description: This Champagne reveals an ethereal pale yellow hue and a luminous fluid appearance, drawing you into a world of almond‑paste, praline and exotic spice. The palate unfolds with tensile lemon acidity atop fleshy, crunchy fruit‑driven depth creating a refined, energetic experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10 – 12 °C as a festive aperitif or alongside fusion cuisine featuring pork, lamb or Comté, where its crisp vibrancy and minerality harmonise elegantly.
aroma: Almond paste, praline and oriental spices
palate: Crunchy fruitiness underpinned by taut lemon acidity

name: Champagne Serveaux Fils Carte Noir Brut
description: Serveaux Fils Carte Noire Brut captivates with a luminous golden hue and a refined bead of persistent bubbles, offering an elegant interplay of ripe red fruit and rose petal nuances tempered by a poised minerality. The palate reveals a supple yet vibrant texture with bright acidity, a graceful balance between flesh and finesse, and a lingering finish of subtle almond and citrus lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled as an aperitif or alongside shellfish and soft cheeses to complement its delicate charm and refined freshness.
palate: silky mouthfeel with bright acidity

name: Champagne Vazart-Coquart Brut Reserve Grand Cru Blanc de Blancs
description: An elegant non‑vintage Blanc de Blancs that expresses the chalky terroir of Chouilly with supple, airy texture and a harmonic weave of white stone fruits and gentle brioche, finishing with a mineral poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled as an aperitif or alongside refined shellfish and delicate crustacean dishes to complement its citrus‑lifted freshness.
aroma: white stone fruit and light pastry nuance
palate: supple, airy texture with citrus and brioche elements
foodPairings: white meats with buttery breadcrumb crust
drinkWindow: Non‑vintage, enjoy within 5 years of disgorgement

name: Chapelle Saint Theodoric Chateauneuf du Pape Guigasse
description: A noble expression of pure Grenache from the storied lieu-dit La Guigasse in Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape, this 2022 Chapelle St. Théodoric unfurls layers of mulled red fruit and Provençal garrigue, wrapped in velvety tannins and an ethereal, light‑footed structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool, ideally decanted for a sumptuous hour before drinking, pairing beautifully with herb‑crusted lamb or Provençal stews.
palate: silky, layered and savory with fine tannins

name: Chapelle Saint Theodoric Chateauneuf du Pape le Grand Pin
description: An elegant expression of pure old‑vine Grenache from sand‑rich Pignan, Le Grand Pin 2022 conveys a lifted floral and red‑fruit perfume with exotic spice underpinned by bright minerality and seamless structure, offering both intensity and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16°C to reveal its perfumed complexity; pairs with herb‑crusted lamb or Provençal stews.
palate: silky red cherry fruit and savory garrigue

name: Chapelle Saint Theodoric Chateauneuf du Pape le Grand Pin
description: An elegant expression of pure old‑vine Grenache from sand‑rich Pignan, Le Grand Pin 2022 conveys a lifted floral and red‑fruit perfume with exotic spice underpinned by bright minerality and seamless structure, offering both intensity and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16°C to reveal its perfumed complexity; pairs with herb‑crusted lamb or Provençal stews.
palate: silky red cherry fruit and savory garrigue

name: Charles Lachaux Aloxe Corton 1er Cru les Valozieres
description: This 2021 Charles Lachaux Aloxe‑Corton 1er Cru Les Valozières reveals its noble pedigree from the first swirl, offering a poised ensemble of vivid red fruit, floral complexity, and subtle mineral underpinnings. Born of meticulous low‑yield farming and gentle extraction this wine balances generous ripeness with sculpted structure and a whisper of earth‑anchored depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled to 15 °C in a Burgundy glass to best coax forth its fragrant bouquet; pair it with lightly seasoned roast duck or wild mushroom risotto to mirror its elegance and tensile grip.
aroma: lifted red fruit and floral perfume with mineral subtlety
palate: structured red fruit framed by fine tannins and fresh acidity
foodPairings: grilled red meats in light sauce

palate: structured red fruit framed by fine tannins and fresh acidity

name: Charles Lachaux Bourgogne Aligote les Champs D'argent
description: From a petite 0.6‑hectare parcel at the foot of Vosne‑Romanée this 2021 Bourgogne Aligoté Les Champs d’Argent offers crystalline precision and mineral clarity in a modest bottle, revealing subtle pear and citrus blossom framed by chalky white‑marle soils, with a delicate whisper of spice underpinned by elegant structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 ˚C in a fine stemmed glass to highlight its taut acidity, perfect with oysters or a lemon‑drizzled goat cheese tart.
palate: mineral‑driven, fresh and refined

name: Charles Lachaux Bourgogne Aligote les Champs D'argent
description: From a petite 0.6‑hectare parcel at the foot of Vosne‑Romanée this 2022 Bourgogne Aligoté Les Champs d’Argent offers crystalline precision and mineral clarity in a modest bottle, revealing subtle pear and citrus blossom framed by chalky white‑marle soils, with a delicate whisper of spice underpinned by elegant structure.

name: Charles Lachaux Bourgogne Aligote les Champs D'argent
description: From a petite 0.6‑hectare parcel at the foot of Vosne‑Romanée this 2023 Bourgogne Aligoté Les Champs d’Argent offers crystalline precision and mineral clarity in a modest bottle, revealing subtle pear and citrus blossom framed by chalky white‑marle soils, with a delicate whisper of spice underpinned by elegant structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 ˚C in a fine stemmed glass to highlight its taut acidity, perfect with oysters or a lemon‑drizzled goat cheese tart.
palate: mineral‑driven, fresh and refined

name: Charles Lachaux Cote de Nuits Villages aux Montagnes
description: The 2022 Charles Lachaux Côtes de Nuits‑Villages “Aux Montagnes” presents as a refined and elegant expression of Pinot Noir from Burgundy combining purity of red berries with a gently spiced, mineral undercurrent, wrapped in fine, chalk‑infused terroir character. The wine shows poise and length anchored by its organic hillside origins in Comblanchien where stony, limestone soils and a whole‑cluster, indigenous fermentation give it a graceful, terroir‑driven profile.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at approximately 55–57°F in a Burgundian goblet to appreciate its vivacious red fruit and delicate spice. Pair with roast chicken with herbes de Provence or quail with earthy mushrooms.
aroma: fresh red cherry and wild strawberry with a hint of violet
palate: silky red fruit layered over chalky minerality
finish: elegant, lingering with a touch of spice

name: Charles Lachaux Cotes de Nuits Villages aux Montagnes
description: A poised and finely wrought Pinot Noir from the hills of Côte de Nuits this 2021 Charles Lachaux “Aux Montagnes” expresses a gracious marriage of vivid red cherry and rose petal, threaded through with subtle lavender and gentle earth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature; pairs beautifully with game birds, mild farmhouse cheeses or pork confit.
aroma: rose petal and cool red cherry
palate: elegant red fruits with floral lift and supple texture

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Bourgogne Blanc
description: This 2012 Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot Bourgogne Blanc unfolds in an elegant and restrained style it reveals a pale golden hue with a scent of delicate orchard fruit and gentle white flowers layered over subtle mineral undertones. The palate is refined and harmonious with fine balance and a touch of savoury depth that is typical for Chardonnay from Côte de Beaune in 2012.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C it complements light fish and subtly seasoned poultry dishes admirably offering grace without overpowering nuance.
aroma: orchard fruit with white flowers and mineral undertones
palate: refined, balanced, with savoury depth

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Chablis Vieilles Vignes
description: Brimming with racy energy this wine presents a crystalline core of green apple and flinty mineral overtones, reflecting the austerity and poise of Chablis’s limestone soils, all framed in a lean, graceful structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a slender white-wine glass to showcase its tensile acidity, ideal with oysters or delicate seafood preparations.
palate: precise citrus, steely minerality

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: This 2013 Clos‑de‑Vougeot Grand Cru by Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a brooding and noble profile with layers of black‑cherry and cassis underpinned by a whisper of forest floor elegance, all framed in refined, velvety structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in classic Burgundy stemware and pair with rich game birds or beef in jus to echo the wine’s dark fruit and subtle earth tones.
aroma: black cherry and cassis with forest floor nuance
palate: velvety texture with ripe black fruit and refined tannins

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey-Chambertin les Evocelles
description: This Gevrey‑Chambertin “Les Evocelles” 2013 from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot unfolds with a refined ballet of black cherry, underbrush and subtle earthy spice, its texture graceful yet grounded in minerality. It offers a poised harmony that reflects the village’s chalk‑scored soils rather than flamboyance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled, around 14 °C, to highlight its freshness. Ideal with roasted game birds or herb‑accented mushroom dishes.
palate: elegant, mineral‑tinged, silky

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes Morceaux
description: A striking expression of old‑vine Pinot Noir from Gevrey‑Chambertin, this 2013 Vieilles Vignes Morceaux displays a noble blush of dark cherry and cassis, enriched by subtle underbrush and smoked‑meat whispers, supported by a silken yet lively texture and an exacting finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 14–16 °C to unwind its vivacity, and pair with classic coq au vin or gently roasted game birds.
palate: silky, fruit‑driven, poised acidity

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay les Echezots
description: This Marsannay Les Échezots 2013 from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a serenely elegant expression of Pinot Noir from the north of the Côte de Nuits. It reveals bright red cherries and raspberries laced with subtle cola‑spice nuances and a touch of earthy mineral clarity. The structure is supple yet persistent, with medium acidity and polished tannins framing a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in large Burgundy glasses. Ideal with roast duck, wild mushroom‑accented dishes or autumn game.
palate: supple red fruits with earthen mineral lift

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay les Echezots
description: This Marsannay Les Échezots 2013 from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a serenely elegant expression of Pinot Noir from the north of the Côte de Nuits. It reveals bright red cherries and raspberries laced with subtle cola‑spice nuances and a touch of earthy mineral clarity. The structure is supple yet persistent, with medium acidity and polished tannins framing a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in large Burgundy glasses. Ideal with roast duck, wild mushroom‑accented dishes or autumn game.
palate: supple red fruits with earthen mineral lift

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Monchenevoy
description: A refined Marsannay Pinot Noir from Charlopin‑Parizot’s En Montchenevoy lieu‑dit vintage 2012 reveals delicate red fruit and woodland aromas opening with air. The palate offers a supple, light‑bodied expression that emphasises finesse over power, concluding in a softly lingering, pleasure‑driven manner.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 13–15 °C. Pair with classic blanquette de veau or gentle white meat dishes to complement its graceful red‑fruit character.
palate: supple, light‑bodied, elegant

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Bourgogne Rouge
description: Crystal clear garnet in hue this 2011 Bourgogne Rouge by Charlopin‑Parizot presents a neatly focused bouquet of red berries and earth with a subtle hint of sauvage. On the palate it reveals a poised structure where bright cherry fruit is anchored by fine tannins and a touch of forest floor intimacy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in classic Burgundy stemware, pairing effortlessly with roast quail or a fricassée of chanterelles.
palate: bright cherry fruit with fine tannins

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey Chambertin la Justice
description: This 2011 Gevrey‑Chambertin La Justice from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot reveals a poised, fresh red Burgundy character, gently redolent of wild red berries with a vein of forest floor. It is elegantly structured, slender in frame yet resonant with subtle spice and mineral clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to bring forth its refined balance, ideally alongside lightly seasoned game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes to complement its delicate complexity.
aroma: Wild red berries and forest floor
palate: Elegant, slender structure with subtle spice notes

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes Morceaux
description: This 2011 Gevrey‑Chambertin Vieilles Vignes “Morceaux” from Charlopin‑Parizot offers a deeply coloured expression of Pinot Noir, delivering brooding cherry and earth tones, with framing hints of mushroom and cola drawn discreetly through time. Its palate is muscular yet fresh, the mid‑palate showing surprising tension without any sense of heaviness, concluding with a subtly dry note that underscores the wine’s poised structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14–16 °C slightly below room temperature to accentuate its balance; pair with roasted game or richly sauced poultry to complement its robust but refined character.
palate: muscular yet fresh mid‑palate with tension

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes Morceaux
description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes is a savory, firmly built Pinot Noir with dark cherry, earth, and woodland spice. Old-vine depth is balanced by the vintage's freshness, leaving a long, composed finish.
sommelierNotes: Decant gently for sediment and serve at 15-16°C with duck, venison, or beef bourguignon.
palate: Layered fruit, firm fine tannin, fresh core

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Gevrey-Chambertin Vieilles Vignes Morceaux
description: This 2015 Vieilles Vignes "Morceaux" from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot is an elegant expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin, offering a nuanced interplay of red‑fruit vibrancy and forest‑floor depth. It presents an engaging tension between earthy notes and cherry fruit framed by fine-grained structure and poised concentration.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 14 °C, and enjoy with roasted game birds or a classic Coq au vin, allowing the wine’s layered character to complement rich, savory flavors.
palate: balanced red fruit, refined tension

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay les Echezots
description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Marsannay Les Échezots is a ripe, expressive Pinot Noir with ruby fruit, floral lift, and carefully integrated oak. The palate combines generosity with a fresh acid spine and enough structure for a savory close.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature with roast pork, duck confit, or mushrooms; a brief decant will help the mature fruit open evenly.
palate: Juicy fruit, polished oak, fresh acidity

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Montchenevoy
description: An elegant expression of Marsannay from Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot the 2011 “En Montchenevoy” unfurls with graceful red fruit charm and a whisper of undergrowth and mocha. Silky and poised it shows a delightful interplay of supple ripeness and fresh clarity, exuding a refined, all‑around allure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C with rustic poultry or slow‑braised game to highlight its finesse and nuanced structure.
palate: silky fresh supple fruit

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Montchenevoy
description: An elegant and harmonious Pinot Noir that reveals dark berry fruit wrapped in subtle woody spice, graceful structure and refined balance hinting at gentle evolution in bottle.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to unveil its purity alongside roasted game or classic Burgundy fare.
palate: round yet precise with fine tannins

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Marsannay Montchevevoy
description: This 2015 Marsannay “En Montchenevoy” from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot reveals a poised elegance rooted in its limestone soils, with delicate aromas of peony and rose unfolding into subtly spiced red fruit. The palate is refined and lithe with silky tannins and an airy finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a Burgundian stem to showcase its floral nuance and graceful structure; pairs beautifully with roasted poultry or herb‑scented charcuterie.
palate: silky red fruits, refined structure

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Morey-Saint Denis Clos Solon
description: This 2011 Morey‑Saint‑Denis Clos Solon by Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a richly brooding profile of tar smoke plum and black licorice set within a framework of firm powerful structure, with dark sepia‑toned fruit and an energetic delineated finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55°F in a large Burgundy glass to coax out depth; pair with wild mushroom risotto or roasted duck to echo its smoky plum drive.
palate: dark sepia‑toned fruit

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Pernand Vergelesses Blanc les Pins
description: Philippe Charlopin-Parizot's 2014 Pernand-Vergelesses Blanc Les Pins is a Chardonnay of bright citrus, wet stone, and restrained beeswax. Its high-toned acidity and firm mineral backbone frame a mature but still energetic white Burgundy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 11-12°C and give the bottle a modest amount of air; pair with shellfish, sole, asparagus risotto, or soft cheese.
aroma: Lemon zest, wet stone, matchstick, beeswax
palate: Bright citrus, firm acidity, mineral depth

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Pernand Vergelesses Blanc les Pins
description: This 2015 Pernand‑Vergelesses Blanc “Les Pins” from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot offers a graceful core of white orchards and bright citrus enlivened by a whisper of oak and a refined mineral undercurrent, capturing the subtle tension of its clay-limestone hillside origin. The wine carries a measured breadth without heaviness and the signature freshness of Côte de Beaune Chardonnay elevated by finesse and precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at about 50 °F in a tulip glass to emphasize its clarity and detail, and consider pairing with poached white fish in herb butter or creamy goat cheeses to complement its texture and mineral lift.
aroma: white orchard fruit with subtle oak and mineral hints
palate: fresh, focused, with citrus and gentle wood spice

name: Domaine Philippe Charlopin-Parizot Vosne Romanee
description: This 2011 Vosne‑Romanée from Domaine Philippe Charlopin‑Parizot unfolds with gracefully brooding depth full fruit and a whisper of mocha underbrush, its texture rich yet supple beckoning with poised elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature around 14 °C its velvety tannins and generous mid‑palate fruit pairing beautifully with game bird terrines or simply roasted pork.
palate: dense and solidly built, yet fresh and supple

name: Margaux
description: An accomplished Margaux from Château Cantenac Brown, the 2006 vintage offers a sumptuously structured expression of firm black fruit and spicy underpinning, framed with fine-grained tannins and a poised sense of balance that reflects a rare precision in this warm yet refined year.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 17 °C after gentle decanting; ideal with heritage roast poultry or game in rich jus.
palate: velvety structure with concentrated dark fruit

name: Château Cantenac Brown Margaux
description: An accomplished Margaux from Château Cantenac Brown, the 2015 vintage offers a sumptuously structured expression of firm black fruit and spicy underpinning, framed with fine-grained tannins and a poised sense of balance that reflects a rare precision in this warm yet refined year.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 17 °C after gentle decanting; ideal with heritage roast poultry or game in rich jus.
palate: velvety structure with concentrated dark fruit

name: Château Cantenac Brown Margaux
description: An accomplished Margaux from Château Cantenac Brown, the 2018 vintage offers a sumptuously structured expression of firm black fruit and spicy underpinning, framed with fine-grained tannins and a poised sense of balance that reflects a rare precision in this warm yet refined year.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 17 °C after gentle decanting; ideal with heritage roast poultry or game in rich jus.
palate: velvety structure with concentrated dark fruit

name: Château Chauvin Saint Emilion Grand Cru
description: A wine of graceful power Château Chauvin 2010 blends rich black cherry fruit with evocative notes of garrigue and spice box, all carried in a frame of broad textured elegance and savoury depth. Its character is expansive yet refined, suggesting both immediate appeal and long‑term evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at cellar cool temperature to reveal layers of fruit and spice. Pairs beautifully with roasted red meats or aged hard cheeses.
palate: Savory spice box with textured fruit

name: Château Coutet Barsac
description: The 2018 Château Coutet Barsac half‑bottle reveals a luminous pale gold hue and unfolds in the glass with refined notes of bitter orange zest, white peach and ginger, softened by subtle floral accents of jasmine and acacia. The palate is elegant and velvety, offering a lively core of citrus and sweet spices balanced by unctuous texture and enduring freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled though not ice‑cold to preserve its acidity and complex nuance. Pair with light fruit‑based desserts or rich foie gras for elegant harmony.
palate: velvety, citrus‑laced, sweet spice

name: Château D'aiguilhe Castillon Cotes de Bordeaux
description: A refined expression of Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux from Château d’Aiguilhe vintage 2018 The wine harmoniously balances energetic freshness with the solidity of its Right Bank origins offering a graceful interplay of chalky red fruits and mineral underpinnings
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled at 16–18 °C with lamb racks or mushroom‑rich dishes to highlight its supple texture and subtle tannic structure
aroma: chalky red berries with violet lift
palate: linear energy framed by fine tannins

name: Château D'aiguilhe Castillon Cotes de Bordeaux
description: A refined expression of Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux from Château d’Aiguilhe vintage 2022 The wine harmoniously balances energetic freshness with the solidity of its Right Bank origins offering a graceful interplay of chalky red fruits and mineral underpinnings

aroma: chalky red berries with violet lift
palate: linear energy framed by fine tannins

name: Château D'yquem Sauternes
description: An enchanting portrait of 2016 Château d’Yquem in half‑bottle form offering sublime clarity of honeyed fruit and citrus nuance, woven through with floral whispers and a silk‑like viscosity that speaks of pure Sauternes tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled alongside rich foie gras or delicate fruit‑based pastries to balance sweetness with acidity, or enjoy solo as a contemplative finale.
palate: silky citrus‑tinged sweetness with resinous complexity

name: Château D'yquem Sauternes
description: The 2019 Château d’Yquem unfurls like liquid gold, offering radiant aromas of apricot, honeysuckle and verbena that evoke both sweetness and lift. On the palate it balances sumptuous botrytis richness with crystalline acidity in a refined, elegant structure destined to age beautifully.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a narrow tulip glass, ideally alongside foie gras, fruit‑based desserts or blue cheese, or simply for quiet contemplation by candlelight.
palate: sumptuous yet crystalline balance

name: Château de Beauregard Pouilly Fuisse
description: A bright expression of Mâconnais Chardonnay from the house of Château de Beauregard this 2022 Pouilly‑Fuissé delivers a refined tensile energy with floral elegance. Subtle accents of honeyed pear and citrus interplay over a mineral frame that speaks of its limestone‑rich soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 10–12 °C to highlight the wine’s tension, pairing beautifully with shellfish or goat cheese.
palate: mineral‑driven with tensile texture

name: Château de Beauregard Pouilly Fuisse Grand Beaurgard
description: An exuberant white Burgundy from Chateau de Beauregard’s Grand Beauregard selection of their finest Chardonnay barrels, this 2014 vintage marries richness with finely tuned clarity, unveiling a layered profile that speaks of both warmth and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 11 °C in a tulip glass to reveal its textural depth, ideal with subtly buttery dishes or soft autumnal game.
palate: velvety, nuanced stone fruit with gentle oak
foodPairings: soft goat cheese on toasted brioche

name: Château de la Bouyere Bordeaux Rouge
description: This Bordeaux Rouge 2020 from Château de La Bouyère presents a refined blend of ripe red and black fruits with gentle spice notes and an elegant, smooth expression. The palate is supple, with graceful texture and a harmonious balance that speaks to classic Bordeaux styling.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature and pair with richly flavored meats or aged cheeses to complement its smooth fruit profile.
aroma: ripe red and black fruit, soft spice
palate: supple, elegant, fruity

name: Château de la Greffiere Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A graceful Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Château de la Greffière, its ruby‑bright hue conceals a delicate elegance balanced between bright cherry and raspberry scents and an undercurrent of forest floor. On the palate the texture is silky and refined with fine, caressing tannins framing a poised, persistent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cooled in a generous Burgundy glass to accentuate its freshness; pairs beautifully with earthy mushroom dishes or simply alongside roast poultry.
palate: Silky, refined texture with caressing tannins

description: A graceful white Burgundy from Château de la Greffière the 2022 Mâcon La Roche Vineuse Vieilles Vignes reflects the clarity of its limestone soils with crisp citrus blossom and subtle baked‑apple richness enlivened by fine spiciness and a whisper of minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 10–12 °C to enhance its refreshing acidity and delicate spice it pairs beautifully with simply prepared white fish or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: lean apple richness edged by peppery clarity

name: Château de la Greffiere Macon la Roche Vineuse Blanc Vieilles Vignes

name: Château de la Greffiere Macon Milly-Lamartine
description: This 2023 Château de la Greffière Mâcon‑Milly‑Lamartine reveals a pale straw‑gold hue and offers a delicate interplay of citrus and white fruit notes. With a subtle mineral underpinning and a graceful menthol nuance on the finish, it balances freshness and roundness with refined poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–12 °C to accentuate its brightness; it pairs elegantly with light poultry, seafood or goat cheese.
palate: gracious mineral freshness

name: Château de la Maltroye Bourgogne Aligote
description: This Bourgogne Aligoté from Château de la Maltroye unfurls with crisp citrus brightness and subtle mineral nuance, framed by an undertone of refined phenolic texture. It offers elegant tension with poised acidity and a serene, lightly austere finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–12 °C in a tulip glass to showcase its vibrant citrus and mineral core, splendid alongside oysters or shellfish and light hors d’oeuvre.
palate: lithe, textured mid‑weight with phenolic grip

name: Château de la Maltroye Bourgogne Blanc
description: This 2020 Château de la Maltroye Bourgogne Blanc unfolds in the glass with refined clarity and subtlety, offering a poised interplay of citrus brightness and delicate orchard fruit framed by a whisper of mineral tension. The wine exudes a gentle yet persistent energy that speaks to the restraint and elegance of Burgundian Chardonnay from the Côte de Beaune
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass, and pair it with simply prepared crustaceans or creamy chicken dishes where its bright acidity and textural depth will shine
palate: elegant mineral‑tinged fruit

sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass, and pair it with simply prepared crustaceans or creamy chicken dishes where its bright acidity and textural depth will shine

name: Château de la Maltroye Chassagne Montrachet 1er Cru Dent de Chien
description: This 2020 Château de la Maltroye Chassagne‑Montrachet 1er Cru “Dent de Chien” exudes refined power and crystalline tension. Bright notes of green apple citrus and white flowers mingle with compelling mineral drive, unfolding in a poised, resonant structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled in a large tulip glass, perfect with delicately grilled sea bass or beurre blanc‑dressed scallops; allow the wine to open as it warms to fully reveal its breadth.

palate: bright, energetic, finely textured

name: Château de la Maltroye Chassagne Montrachet 1er Cru la Romanee
description: A luminous expression of Chassagne‑Montrachet 1er Cru, the 2021 Château de la Maltroye “La Romanée” unveils delicate notes of citrus blossom and crushed limestone gently interwoven with hints of honeyed white orchard fruit, culminating in an elegant yet compelling profile distinguished by texture and clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to showcase its crystalline minerality, a graceful companion for shellfish in beurre blanc or poultry with a light cream sauce.
palate: honeyed white orchard fruit with vibrant mineral drive

name: Château de la Maltroye Chassagne Montrachet Rouge 1er Cru Clos du Chateau
description: A noble expression of Pinot Noir, this Château de la Maltroye Chassagne‑Montrachet Rouge 2021 reveals a concentrated core of red and black fruits laced with violet and gentle spice, framed by silky tannins and a firm but graceful structure. It conveys both the power and finesse of clay‑limestone terroir nurtured within a historic walled clos in the heart of Chassagne‑Montrachet.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperatures to highlight its fruit and freshness. Pairs beautifully with lamb or game dishes, or mellowing in the cellar over the next decade.
palate: concentrated, supple with fine tannins

description: A beautifully poised red Burgundy from Château de la Maltroye, this 2020 Chassagne‑Montrachet 1er Cru Clos Saint‑Jean displays an elegant bouquet of red and dark berry notes lifted by violet and gentle spice, framed in a refined medium‑weight structure reminiscent of classic Côte de Beaune reds.

palate: elegant medium‑weight with fine tannins

palate: elegant red fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Château de Manissy Tavel Cuvee des Lys Rose
description: With a vibrant, sunlit hue this 2025 Château de Manissy Tavel Cuvée des Lys Rosé embodies the soulful expression of Tavel in each sip, showing succulent red fruit elegance with a savory, herb‑dusted depth and a finish that lingers with tension and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled, ideally alongside Mediterranean fare: think tapenade‑kissed grilled vegetables, grilled fish or lamb, where the wine’s structure and vibrant acidity elevate the dish.
aroma: ripe raspberry, blood orange, wild thyme
palate: broad textured red fruit with savory garrigue

name: Blanc
description: An elegant Chardonnay from the northern gateway to the Côte d’Or this Marsannay Blanc 2020 presents pale yellow hues framing aromas of honeysuckle, vanilla and toasted hazelnut caressed by marzipan richness on the palate, upheld by bright freshness and mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C. Lovely as an aperitif or alongside shellfish, crustaceans or delicate white meats.
palate: ample round with marzipan

name: Bourgogne Rouge en Montre Cul
description: A wine of graceful intensity this Bourgogne Rouge En Montre‐Cul 2022 from Château de Marsannay offers a powerful and expressive bouquet of ripe black fruits and aromatic spices, framed by the lithe freshness of its mid‑slope clay‑limestone terroir. On the palate it is refined yet ample and fleshy, showing excellent balance and lingering persistence that speaks of old‑world poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature around 15 °C to highlight its freshness. Pair with Burgundy snails or grilled meats to echo its earthy fruit and spice notes.
palate: refined, ample and fleshy

name: Rouge
description: This 2021 Château de Marsannay Marsannay Rouge presents an old‑world elegance rooted in Côte de Nuits tradition with supple, fresh expression of ripe black fruits, spice and undergrowth, framed by gentle oak. A delicate balance conveys both structure and grace, reflecting the layered parcels of its appellation.
sommelierNotes: Best served at cellar cool temperature alongside classic Burgundian fare such as red meats and mushroom‑based dishes or Burgundy‑style fondues for a harmonious match.
palate: supple, fresh, layered

name: 1er Cru Charmes
description: This 2022 Meursault Premier Cru Charmes from Château de Meursault exhibits an elegant balance of richness and delicacy its floral bouquet of almond and warm baked bread leads into succulent orchard fruit and pastry nuances, all framed by a graceful textural depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 – 14 °C to highlight the silk‑like texture. Pair with buttery lobster, foie gras or delicate mushroom risotto for an ideal match.
palate: orchard fruit and pastry

name: 1er Cru Charmes Dessus
description: A resplendent Meursault Premier Cru from Château de Meursault, the 2022 Les Charmes‑Dessus embraces the opulence of its mid‑slope, east‑facing terroir with Chardonnay’s signature grace, offering ripe stone fruit and toasted brioche woven with a fine mineral thread.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in a generous white glass to allow its rich texture and mineral streak to unfold. Pair it with buttery lobster, veal in cream sauce, or fine aged cheeses.
palate: rich and textured with mineral lift

name: 1er Cru les Charmes
description: The 2019 Château de Meursault Meursault Premier Cru Les Charmes is a refined white Burgundy exhibiting luminous pale‑golden colour, a graceful aromatic signature of acacia blossom, vanilla and grilled bread, complemented by subtle anise‑mint nuance. The palate unfolds with a silken texture, weighty yet fresh, presenting warm brioche and nutty complexity framed by bright citrus and mineral underpinnings.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large white‑wine glass to allow the wine to breathe. Ideal with rich poultry, delicate shellfish or creamy fish preparations.
palate: silky texture, brioche, warmed almond, citrus mineral balance
finish: long mineral‑tinged finish with anise‑mint echo

name: 1er Cru les Perrieres
description: The 2018 Château de Meursault Perrières Premier Cru presents a crystalline core of minerality framed by luminous fruit tones It offers poised structure and seductive weight without heaviness
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its chiselled mineral energy Ideal with rich shellfish or creamy seafood dishes
palate: fresh, wide and mineral-driven

sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its chiselled mineral energy Ideal with rich shellfish or creamy seafood dishes
palate: fresh, wide and mineral-driven

sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its chiselled mineral energy Ideal with rich shellfish or creamy seafood dishes

sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its chiselled mineral energy Ideal with rich shellfish or creamy seafood dishes
palate: fresh, wide and mineral-driven

name: Bourgogne Clos de Chateau
description: The 2022 Château de Meursault Bourgogne Clos du Château is an elegant expression of Burgundian Chardonnay, offering yellow fruits lifted by toasted freshness, generous and beautifully balanced on the palate with a delicate oaky underpinning.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in a tulip glass, ideal alongside salmon tartare or gougères for a refined aperitif.
palate: Generous, balanced with delicate oak

name: Charmes
description: A luminous and generous wine, offering a polished interplay of stone fruit lushness and refined oak nuance, ripe apricot and warm brioche recalled with captivating clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C, it will complement rich poultry or creamy shellfish preparations.
palate: apricot and citrus oil with velvety texture
finish: long elegant finish with anise‑mint lift

name: Corton Vergennes Grand Cru
description: This 2019 Château de Meursault Corton‑Vergennes Grand Cru reveals a luminous golden hue, layered with orchard‑fruit generosity and compelling mineral vigor redolent of its storied terroir. The impression is one of refined opulence and length rendered with restraint reflecting its Grand Cru heritage.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled near 12 °C (54 °F) to temper its richness and showcase its crystalline minerality; sublime with cream‑sauced veal or oysters, or cellar for up to fifteen years for deeper nuance.
palate: full‑bodied, rich, with creamy texture and vibrant mineral core
finish: extraordinary length and lingering mineral clarity
foodPairings: veal piccata with cream and spiced sauce

name: Savigny les Beaune Rouge
description: An elegant village‑level Pinot Noir from Savigny‑lès‑Beaune that speaks of its brown, stony terroir with poised red‑fruit aromas and gentle spice, supported by a structured yet silky palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 60 °F in a medium‑bodied Burgundy presentation and pair with classic French bistro fare for graceful harmony.
aroma: red cherry and wild strawberry with subtle spice
palate: juicy raspberry and fine mineral tension
foodPairings: duck confit salad with walnut vinaigrette

name: Terroir D'exception
description: An elegant white Burgundy from Château de Meursault this 2020 Bourgogne “Terroir d’Exception” reveals bright citrus and white floral notes with a delicate vanillin nuance, its palate refined by a taut mineral line and lees‐driven freshness providing poised structure
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12°C to showcase its purity this wine partners beautifully with light shellfish dishes or creamy risotto accented with mushroom or alpine cheese
palate: fine minerality with lees‐borne creaminess

name: Château des Arnauds Cuvee Capucins Lalande de Pomerol
description: A wine of youthful elegance and classical bearing that melds ripe plummy fruit with delicate spice and earthy undertones, all rendered in a vivid garnet hue. It exudes modest power yet refinement, anchored by fine-grained tannins and subtle oak nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in large tulip glasses to reveal cherry‑stone freshness and supple structure, ideal with slow‑roasted game or mushroom‑rich dishes.
palate: firm, structured, youthful with elegant tannins

name: Château des Quarts Pouilly Fuisse 1ER Cru aux Quarts
appellation: Pouilly‑Fuissé Premier Cru Clos des Quarts Monopole
description: A refined Pouilly‑Fuissé 1er Cru from Château des Quarts’ Clos des Quarts monopole; the 2022 vintage shows an elegant harmony between stone fruit and chalk‑spiced power with a fine oak presence that is beautifully integrated, all framed by the unique clos’s limestone‑tinged terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10–12 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its bracing acidity and minerality; pairs exquisitely with beurre blanc seafood or delicate poultry in cream sauces.
aroma: white‑peach and stone fruit with discreet oak
palate: elegant amplitude with iodized minerality

name: Château des Quarts Pouilly Fuisse 1ER Cru aux Quarts
appellation: Pouilly‑Fuissé Premier Cru Clos des Quarts Monopole
description: A refined Pouilly‑Fuissé 1er Cru from Château des Quarts’ Clos des Quarts monopole; the 2023 vintage shows an elegant harmony between stone fruit and chalk‑spiced power with a fine oak presence that is beautifully integrated, all framed by the unique clos’s limestone‑tinged terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10–12 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its bracing acidity and minerality; pairs exquisitely with beurre blanc seafood or delicate poultry in cream sauces.
aroma: white‑peach and stone fruit with discreet oak
palate: elegant amplitude with iodized minerality

name: Château des Quarts Pouilly Fuisse 1er Cru L'orangeris du Chateau des Quarts
description: The 2023 Pouilly‑Fuissé Premier Cru “L’Orangerie du Château des Quarts” is poised with refined poise offering poised aromas of orchard stone fruit and citrus blossom framed by subtle, integrated oak. On the palate it strikes a balance of generous texture and crystalline freshness with a mineral-tinged vitality drawn from its southeast‑facing clay‑limestone plateau.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled alongside shellfish or white meats with butter‑based sauces to accentuate its creamy vivacity.
palate: creamy, fresh, mineral‑tinged

name: Margaux
description: The 2018 Château Deyrem Valentin Margaux unfolds with a refined yet compelling presence, marked by plush ripe berry tones and subtle floral nuances. The structure reveals firm but ripe tannins underpinning a seamless interplay between freshness and depth with an elegant mineral lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 17 °C in a medium‐bodied Bordeaux glass to enhance its finely wrought texture; ideal alongside charcoal‑grilled lamb or a terrine of game.
palate: silky texture with refined tannins and mineral precision

name: Château Dufort Vivens les Plantes Margaux
description: An elegant Margaux second label from the celebrated Château Durfort‑Vivens, the 2019 “Les Plantes” offers a gracious interplay of ripe black currant and cherry youth framed by a whisper of spice and polished texture, all delivered with refined clarity and Bordeaux distinction
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar cool temperatures to accent its freshness; pairs beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes that mirror its subtle complexity
aroma: ripe black fruits and gentle spice
palate: silky tannins, expressive fruit and supple balance

name: Château Grand Puy Ducasse Pauillac
description: This 2018 Grand‑Puy‑Ducasse is a commanding yet finely structured Pauillac, with layers of dense blackcurrant and stewed plum woven through cedar‑tinged oak and savory graphite notes. The palate is muscular and focused, delivering energetic dark fruit framed by elegant tannins beneath a long, silken finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool (16–18 °C) with richly flavored meats such as roast lamb or prime rib to complement the wine’s plush fruit and nurturing tannin structure.
palate: dark plum, graphite, savory herbs
foodPairings: rack of lamb with herb jus

name: Château Haut Bages Liberal Pauillac
description: In this 2009 vintage the grand vin of Château Haut‑Bages Libéral unfolds with a beautifully rich texture and an inky purple presence its core of cassis is laced with incense and forest floor nuance rendering a savory, opulent complexion.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in large Bordeaux‑style glasses allow gentle aeration to reveal layered black‑fruit and subtle mint where lamb or beef in rich jus will complement its structure.
palate: opulent and savory with refined black‑fruit and spice

name: Château Haut Rian Bordeaux Blanc
description: A crystalline 2022 Bordeaux Blanc from Château Haut‑Rian offering bright notes of white flowers and zesty lemon rind underscored by gentle honeydew nuance it exhibits a lively, dry character with no oak influence, its freshness informed by stainless steel fermentation and lees aging for four months
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled and enjoy within its youthful window alongside shellfish, seafood platters or a simply dressed green salad
palate: crisp, crunchy and fruit‑driven

name: Château Haut Rian Cremant de Bordeaux
description: This 2023 Château Haut‑Rian Crémant de Bordeaux reveals a poised fine bubble and a pale hue, inviting with delicate notes of white flowers and citrus. It is light‑footed and elegant in style, offering a refined expression of Bordeaux’s sparkling tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 °C as an aperitif or alongside fresh shellfish and light hors d’oeuvres to highlight its crisp fruit and floral finesse.
palate: light, fresh, delicate acidity

name: Château Haut Sarthes Bergerac Rose
description: A lithe and crisp rosé from Bergerac, Château Haut‑Sarthes 2024 offers a fresh frame of red berry and melon that speaks of dew‑kissed Dordogne mornings, with a delicate mineral undertone lending poise and refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10 °C; elegant enough for an aperitif yet subtle enough to partner light charcuterie or grilled fish.
palate: fresh, balanced acidity with mineral lift

name: Château Haut Selve Graves Blanc
description: A refined white Bordeaux from the Graves produced in 2024, Château Haut Selve Graves Blanc combines the varietal elegance of Sauvignon Blanc, Sauvignon Gris and Sémillon into a lively wine that balances freshness with subtle oak integration.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at approximately 50 °F in a tulip‑shaped glass, ideal with grilled white fish or as an elevated aperitif.
palate: balanced acidity with mango and white fruit

name: Château Haut Selve Graves Rouge
description: Born of the storied terroirs of Graves this 2022 Château Haut Selve Graves Rouge offers a refined expression of Bordeaux allure, where concentrated blackcurrant and dark cherry emerge with a whisper of licorice and subtle cedar underpinned by mineral tension, all carried on poised, velvety tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool to allow the layers of black fruit and gentle spice to unfold, pairing beautifully with roasted lamb or aged hard cheeses.
palate: structured, silky tannins framing ripe cassis

name: Château la Commanderie Saint Emilion Grand Cru
description: This 2019 Château La Commanderie unfolds with intense layers of black fruits—ripe blackberry and blueberry—framed by complex spicy cassis notes and gently integrated oak, offering a harmonious texture and refined depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 to 18 °C with rich dishes such as grilled côte de boeuf or tournedos with truffle butter to complement the wine’s structured fruit and spice profile.
aroma: blackberry, blueberry, cassis and gentle spice
palate: harmonious, layered fruit with fine-grained tannins

name: Château la Conseillante Pomerol
description: The 2018 Château La Conseillante is a refined Pomerol of regal bearing, offering a plush tapestry of dark berries, violet florals and forest floor nuances, all framed by velvety tannins and a mineral undercurrent.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted at cellar temperature around 60 °F; matches elegantly with roasted lamb or truffle‑infused dishes.
palate: silky texture, layered fruit, fine tannins

name: Chateau la Rabotine Sancerre Blanc
description: A refined Sancerre Blanc from Château la Rabotine 2024 presents crystalline freshness with bright floral and citrus notes over a foundation of stony minerality reflecting its Terres Blanches and Caillottes terroirs. The wine’s delineated structure and energetic clarity evoke sunlit hillsides and pure Loire expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve lively, slightly chilled; an elegant companion to goat cheese or delicate seafood.
aroma: white flowers, freshly cut grass, grapefruit
palate: luminous citrus framed by minerality
foodPairings: goat cheese such as Crottin de Chavignol
poached sole in white wine sauce
light seafood like oysters or scallops

name: Chateau la Rabotine Sancerre Blanc les Petites Perrieres
description: This 2022 Château La Rabotine Sancerre Blanc “Les Petites Pierres” is a glimmer of Loire elegance its vibrant citrus aromas woven with subtle herbal nuances unfold with grace its mineral clarity carries a fine sensuous texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–12 °C it is lovely with oysters, soft chèvre, or delicate white fish.
aroma: fragrant citrus and herbal notes on the nose
palate: green apple, grass and pineapple balanced by lively minerality

name: Chateau la Rabotine Sancerre Blanc les Petites Perrieres
description: An eloquent Sauvignon Blanc of crystalline purity drawn from the steely terroir of Sancerre this wine presents a poised interplay of zesty citrus brightness and subtle minerality resting on a supple frame of lees‑inspired texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its fine tension, ideal alongside oysters or herb‑bright goat cheese vintages.
palate: sleek minerality and lemon‑pith freshness

name: Chateau la Rabotine Sancerre Rouge
description: A refined and graceful expression of Sancerre Rouge from Château la Rabotine, the 2023 vintage offers supple red fruit undercurrents with whispers of earth and subtle floral nuance, unfolding with poise and clarity in the glass.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled for optimum elegance, pairing beautifully with charcuterie or simply grilled vegetables, allowing its restrained finesse to shine.
palate: elegant poise with refined tension

name: Château la Rose Pourret Saint Emilion Grand Cru
description: The 2019 Château La Rose‑Pourret Saint‑Émilion Grand Cru offers a gracious bouquet of rose petal and wild berry framed by subtle spice and fine oak, leading to a fluid, rounded palate of fresh red fruit and ripe tannins with discreet oak accents.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16°C, ideally decanted gently to reveal the wine’s graceful fruit and texture. It partners beautifully with roasted lamb or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: rose petal, wild berries, fine oak
palate: fluid and rounded fresh red fruit with ripe tannins

name: Château la Rose Pourret Saint Emilion Grand Cru
description: The 2019 Château La Rose‑Pourret Saint‑Émilion Grand Cru offers a gracious bouquet of rose petal and wild berry framed by subtle spice and fine oak, leading to a fluid, rounded palate of fresh red fruit and ripe tannins with discreet oak accents.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16°C, ideally decanted gently to reveal the wine’s graceful fruit and texture. It partners beautifully with roasted lamb or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: rose petal, wild berries, fine oak
palate: fluid and rounded fresh red fruit with ripe tannins

name: Château Lalaudey Moulis en Medoc
description: This voluptuous 2018 Château Lalaudey from Moulis‑en‑Médoc reveals a concentrated ruby hue and offers a refined interplay of cassis and brambly black fruit underscored by subtle vanilla‑smoke nuances derived from its barrel élevage, embodying the firm structure and purity of fruit of the terroir. Charming yet precise, the ensemble is built on a sturdy backbone of Cabernet‑Sauvignon draped in tender Merlot silk.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at cellar temperature allowing its fruit and fine tannins to unfold, an ideal companion to roast lamb or aged hard cheeses.
palate: pure fruit with gentle structure

name: Château Latour Martillac Pessac-Leognan Rouge
description: The 2016 Château Latour‑Martillac Rouge exudes classic Pessac‑Léognan elegance, offering a perfume of crème de cassis and black cherry enfolded in delicate floral and spice notes. On the palate it is ample and plush yet structured, its polished tannins carrying layers of cherry liqueur and licorice underpinned by a thrilling freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 61‑64°F in a large Bordeaux glass after gentle decanting to reveal its depth. Pairs beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑studded game dishes.
aroma: Crème de cassis and black cherry with floral spice
palate: Ample and plush with cherry liqueur, licorice and freshness
finish: Long and lively with refined structure

name: Château Lilian Ladouys Saint Estephe
description: 2018 Château Lilian Ladouys Saint‑Estèphe reveals an elegant yet powerful expression of Left Bank Bordeaux, combining refined red fruit and graphite nuances with a noble, structured profile. It shows a supple volume and impressive length grounded in concentrated Cabernet Sauvignon fruit and subtle saline richness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at cellar temperature alongside richly flavored meats or hearty dishes to match its elegant tannins and layered complexity.
palate: noble Cabernet‑driven amplitude with salted butter caramel detail
finish: long and succulent salted butter caramel

name: Château Lilian Ladouys Saint Estephe
description: This Saint‑Estèphe classic unfolds in layered shades of dark plum and violet with a softly spiced, mineral‑tinged backbone, refined yet powerful, poised between tradition and vivacity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at approximately 16°C, decanted if young. Ideal with rich red meats or aged Comté for balance and depth.
palate: silky tannins, layered dark fruit

name: Château Loumelat Bordeaux Blanc
description: A bright youthful white from the storied Château Loumelat estate on the Côtes de Blaye this vintage presents a limpid pale yellow hue with pale green glints Imitating the coastal terroir of sand clay and limestone it offers a crystalline aroma of grapefruit lemon and white flowers and a palate that balances vivacity and minerality with delicate richness
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C as a refined aperitif or alongside fresh seafood and simply grilled fish to complement its citrus clarity
palate: vivacious, mineral‑balanced, gently rich

name: Château Marechaux Bordeaux Superieur
description: This 2016 Château Maréchaux Bordeaux Supérieur presents an elegant harmony of mellow dark cherry and nuanced cedar, bearing the soft imprint of oak ageing and an undertone of refined earthiness. The wine evokes a quiet grace, rich yet balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in broad Bordeaux-style glasses to reveal its supple texture; pairs beautifully with slow‑roasted duck or mushroom‑scented terrine.
palate: soft tannins with earthy depth

name: Château Marjosse Bordeaux Rouge
description: The 2020 Château Marjosse Bordeaux Rouge presents rich black fruit tones and poised minerality borne of clay‑limestone soils in Entre‑Deux‑Mers, framed by elegant structure and refreshing clarity. It conveys a striking harmony of ripe plum and subtle spice wrapped in silken tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 16 °C after gentle decanting: it marries beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe black plum with fine spice
palate: silky tannins, vibrant fruit, precise minerality
finish: persistent freshness with a mineral echo

name: Château Marjosse Bordeaux Rouge
description: The 2022 Château Marjosse Bordeaux Rouge presents rich black fruit tones and poised minerality borne of clay‑limestone soils in Entre‑Deux‑Mers, framed by elegant structure and refreshing clarity. It conveys a striking harmony of ripe plum and subtle spice wrapped in silken tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 16 °C after gentle decanting: it marries beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe black plum with fine spice
palate: silky tannins, vibrant fruit, precise minerality
finish: persistent freshness with a mineral echo

name: Château Monplaisir Bordeaux Rouge
description: Deep ruby in hue this elegant Bordeaux Rouge unfolds generous aromas of cassis, blackberry and warm plum, interlaced with soft spice and a hint of graphite that speak of its gently ripened 2022 character. On the palate it offers ample red and black fruit framed by polished tannins and a refreshing undercurrent of acidity for poised balance. The finish lingers with subtle earthy nuance and a whisper of tobacco.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in heavy Bordeaux glasses to lift its vibrant fruit. Pair with roast lamb, mushroom‑rich dishes or firm cow’s‑milk cheeses to enhance its supple texture and savory finish.
aroma: cassis blackberry plum with soft spice
palate: supple red and black fruit with polished tannins
finish: earthy nuance and a whisper of tobacco

name: Château Pajzos Essencia
description: This Essencia 2016 from Château Pajzos in Tokaj is a nectar of sublime refinement, where the rarefied sweetness of noble‑rot concentrates into a remarkably viscous yet finely balanced elixir. A beam of honeyed apricot suffused with blood‑orange candy and delicate undercurrents of mint unfolds in the glass in an elegant embrace of power and finesse. The sheer purity of fruit is cut by electric acidity anchoring the wine’s silk‑like richness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 °C in petite dessert wine glasses, pairing exquisitely with foie gras on brioche, almond financiers, or intensity‑tempered blue cheese.
aroma: honeyed apricot, blood‑orange pâte de fruit
palate: lush viscous texture balanced by mouthwatering acidity
finish: long resonant closure with mint and citrus echo

name: Château Pajzos Furmint Sec T Dry
description: A lithe and crystalline expression of Tokaj Furmint this 2023 “T‑style” embodies the region’s trademark balance of vivid acidity and subtle mineral drive, framed by delicate notes of white blossom and orchard fruit. A seamless interplay unfolds between its taut structure and gentle generosity, yielding a dry wine of refined poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled, ideally between 6 and 8 °C, to accentuate its zesty acidity; an ideal partner for citrus‑bright seafood or subtly seasoned poultry.
palate: crisp orchard fruit with mineral tension

name: Château Pajzos Tokaji Aszu 5 Puttonyos
description: An opulent expression of Tokaji tradition this 2017 Château Pajzos Tokaji Aszú 5 Puttonyos reveals apricot and honeyed saffron nuances lifted by a vivid thread of pink‑grapefruit acidity suggesting both richness and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C alongside foie gras or rich pâtés or as a contemplative dessert on its own.
palate: lively acidity with candied ginger and citrus lift
drinkWindow: Enjoy now through 2035, with potential for graceful aging

name: Château Paveil de Luze Margaux
description: The 2018 Paveil de Luze Margaux reveals deep garnet hues and a subtly floral perfume weaving ripe cassis and violet notes with a whisper of graphite and tobacco: refined yet vibrating with energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at roughly 16 °C in a Bordeaux goblet: allows the silky cassis and graphite to evolve gracefully over a meal of roast lamb or mushroom‐infused dishes.
palate: ripe black fruit with tea‐leaf and tobacco accents

name: Pauillac
description: A noble Pauillac that blends power and poise, Château Pibran 2018 presents brambly blackcurrant and graphite with a fine-grained tannic backbone, balanced by a subtle violet and tobacco nuance that speaks of its gravelly hillside terroir. It carries itself with a gracious structure that promises longevity, yet retains an inviting generosity in youth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar chill to reveal its depth, pairing splendidly with roast lamb or aged duck breast.
palate: structured black fruit with fine-grained tannins

name: Château Pibran Pauillac
description: A noble Pauillac that blends power and poise, Château Pibran 2018 presents brambly blackcurrant and graphite with a fine-grained tannic backbone, balanced by a subtle violet and tobacco nuance that speaks of its gravelly hillside terroir. It carries itself with a gracious structure that promises longevity, yet retains an inviting generosity in youth.

palate: structured black fruit with fine-grained tannins

name: Château Prieure Lichine Margaux
description: The 2016 Château Prieuré‑Lichine Margaux unfolds with alluring depth, its bouquet threaded with richly perfumed blackcurrant and violet underlaid by an earthy graphite nuance, all framed in refined structure and supple texture. The palate reveals layered dark fruit, elegantly balanced by fine-grained tannins and a persistent, silky finish, speaking of Margaux classicism with graceful poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16‑18 °C in a large-bowled glass after decanting to appreciate its floral and mineral complexity. Pair with herb‑crusted lamb or roasted duck to match its refined yet structured character.
palate: layered dark fruit, fine‑grained tannins

name: Château Puynormand Montagne Saint Emilion les Vieilles Vignes
description: This 2022 Château Puynormond “Les Vieilles Vignes” from Montagne‑Saint‑Émilion offers a luminous garnet hue with violet glints, unveiling generous scents of red and black fruit interlaced with warming spices such as vanilla and cinnamon. The palate is supple and opulent revealing ripe fruit, harmonious oak and a lingering, contemplative finish that invites lingering enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled between 16 and 18 °C, preferably after decanting to reveal its velvet‑smooth structure; pairs elegantly with roasted duck, grilled red meats or refined chocolate desserts.
palate: supple ripe fruit, rounded oak

name: Château Rauzan Segla Margaux
description: The 2010 Château Rauzan‑Ségla is a refined Margaux of poised intensity and alluring depth, unfolding layers of blackcurrant and violet perfume with a hint of rosemary on the supple yet structured palate. It marries precision and class in a manner befitting its Second Growth heritage, suggesting both grace and latent power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at 16 °C with rich meats or roasted game to highlight its aromatic elegance and refined tannic structure.
palate: supple structure with precision and class
