sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at 16 °C with rich meats or roasted game to highlight its aromatic elegance and refined tannic structure.
palate: supple structure with precision and class

name: Château Rauzan Segla Margaux
description: The 2019 Château Rauzan‑Ségla is a refined Margaux of poised intensity and alluring depth, unfolding layers of blackcurrant and violet perfume with a hint of rosemary on the supple yet structured palate. It marries precision and class in a manner befitting its Second Growth heritage, suggesting both grace and latent power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at 16 °C with rich meats or roasted game to highlight its aromatic elegance and refined tannic structure.
palate: supple structure with precision and class

name: Château Reynier Bordeaux Blanc Sec
description: A springtime serenade from Bordeaux, the 2023 Château Reynier Bordeaux Blanc Sec marries crisp citrus brightness with a delicate whisper of apricot and pink grapefruit, supported by a soft, inviting texture. Crafted under organic and vegan principles, it lends purity and elegance to every pour.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to preserve its floral lift and lively freshness, an elegant companion to shellfish or goat cheese salads.
palate: soft texture with brightness

name: Château Roustaing Bordeaux Rouge Vieilles Vignes
description: A graceful expression of Médoc terroir this 2018 Château Roustaing Bordeaux Rouge Vieilles Vignes offers a refined presence of red berries and subtle violet notes layered over a gentle Cabernet framework, delivering a polished and inviting profile.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C after brief decanting to reveal its poised structure. Pairs superbly with roast duck or a mushroom‑rich terrine.
palate: supple Cabernet‑driven red fruit

name: Château Sainte Roseline Cotes de Provence Cru Classe Rose Lampe de Meduse
description: An elegant Provence rosé offered from Château Sainte‑Roseline’s iconic Lampe de Méduse line vintage 2021, this wine presents a delicately pale salmon hue and a refined aromatic profile of exotic fruits white peach and mango balanced with crystalline minerality
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8–10 °C with light Mediterranean fare to accentuate its freshness and fruit nuance
aroma: fine exotic fruits and white peach
palate: round yet fresh with mango and minerality
drinkWindow: drink within 2–3 years of vintage for peak vibrancy

name: Château Sainte Roseline Lampe de Meduse Cotes de Provence Rose
description: This 2021 Lampe de Méduse from Château Sainte‑Roseline is a pale salmon‑tinged rosé that marries mineral clarity with a delicate perfume of yellow peach, apricot and orange blossom. The palate offers a graceful tension balancing juicy stone‑fruit ripeness and citrus freshness with a subtle mineral undertone.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10°C in a tulip glass, ideal alongside light Provençal fare or simply enjoyed as an elegant aperitif.
palate: fresh stone‑fruit with citrus tension

name: Château Sociando Mallet Haut Medoc
description: The 2018 Château Sociando‑Mallet Haut‑Médoc unfolds in the glass a deep garnet‑purple hue. It offers a layered bouquet of ripe black fruits, cedar, earthy sous‑bois and a refined mineral undertone suggesting gravel and graphite. Plush yet structured on the palate it builds through cassis, plum and tobacco framed by polished tannins, before finishing long, fresh and subtly spiced.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 17‑18 °C after decanting, pairing beautifully with roasted lamb or smoked duck, where the wine’s clarity and structure will shine.
aroma: ripe black fruits with cedar and mineral
palate: cassis, plum, tobacco and polished tannins

name: Château Suduiraut Sauternes
description: The 2016 Château Suduiraut 375 ml reveals a fine golden hue, with an elegant weave of candied apricot, kumquat and yellow peach that segue into gentle vanilla, light caramel and rose‑flower tones. The palate is silken and vibrant delivering candied pineapple, orange and red‑fruit warmth with a bright spice‑tinged persistence.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a tulip glass, pairing its honeyed charm with blue‑cheese profiteroles or a delicate foie gras terrine for sublime harmony.
palate: silken, candied pineapple and red‑fruit warmth

name: Château Tertre Roteboeuf Saint Emilion
description: An opulent Saint‑Émilion that marries sumptuous black and red fruit with exotic spice and silken texture; it reveals layered aromas of red cherry, dark chocolate and clove, while the palate unfolds with velvety depth and refined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve with quiet confidence after decanting to allow its complex aromas to blossom; pairs splendidly with rich red meats or game in jus.
palate: velvety, deep, structured

name: Château Tertre Roteboeuf Saint Emilion
description: An opulent Saint‑Émilion that marries sumptuous black and red fruit with exotic spice and silken texture; it reveals layered aromas of red cherry, dark chocolate and clove, while the palate unfolds with velvety depth and refined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve with quiet confidence after decanting to allow its complex aromas to blossom; pairs splendidly with rich red meats or game in jus.
palate: velvety, deep, structured

name: Château Thieuley Bordeaux Blanc
description: This bright pale‑gold Bordeaux blanc exudes a refined aromatic bouquet of white‑fleshed and exotic fruits with subtle floral accents, leading to a mouthfeel that is both rounded and fresh, displaying poised citrus lift and textural elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8–10 °C in slender white wine glasses, paired simply with fresh seafood or soft cheeses to complement its vivacious balance.
palate: rich and rounded with citrus freshness

name: Château Thieuley Bordeaux Blanc
description: This bright pale‑gold Bordeaux blanc exudes a refined aromatic bouquet of white‑fleshed and exotic fruits with subtle floral accents, leading to a mouthfeel that is both rounded and fresh, displaying poised citrus lift and textural elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8–10 °C in slender white wine glasses, paired simply with fresh seafood or soft cheeses to complement its vivacious balance.
palate: rich and rounded with citrus freshness

name: Château Thieuley Bordeaux Rouge
description: A classically styled Bordeaux rouge offering from Château Thieuley, the 2018 vintage presents a harmonious blend of plummy Merlot, structured Cabernet Sauvignon and a whisper of Petit Verdot. The wine unfolds with gentle spice and dark fruit, supported by supple yet firm tannins and a polished sense of balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a broad glass to allow the fruit and spice to glow; an elegant companion to grilled lamb, roasted vegetables or aged cheeses.
palate: smooth fruit underpinned by refined structure

name: Château Tour Sieujean Pauillac
description: This 2023 Château Tour Sieujean Pauillac is a classic left bank red with a polished richness, carrying layers of black currant and cherry framed by gentle cedar and spice nuances. There is a finely structured core and captivating textural depth that offers early promise and graceful ageing potential.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in broad glasses to reveal its spice‑lined fruit and refined tannins, pairing beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑crusted beef.
aroma: black currant and cedar with spice highlights
palate: silky‑textured dark fruit with polished tannins
finish: elegant lingering cherry and graphite echo

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru aux Thorey
description: This 2013 Chauvenet‑Chopin Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru Aux Thorey reveals a noble character at a youthful stage, with vibrant red and black cherry aromas framed by subtle cedary oak and savory soil complexity, underscoring its origin in a steep, southeast‑facing slope of Côte de Nuits. The palate is full‑bodied and structured, showing firm integrated tannins and a promising depth that suggests it will evolve gracefully with time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool temperatures around 14 °C in Burgundy style stemware let the wine breathe briefly before pouring; pair with roasted game or mushroom‑rich dishes to mirror its earth‑driven elegance.
aroma: red and black cherries with cedary oak and soil complexity
palate: full‑bodied structured with firm integrated tannins

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Chaignots
description: A wine of refined structure and old‑world grace, this 2012 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Les Chaignots” by Domaine Chauvenet‑Chopin reveals an intense core of black cherry, violet and gentle spice, framed by firm and elegant tannins mellowing beautifully with time.
sommelierNotes: Best decanted briefly and served at 15 °C, this Pinot Noir makes an inviting companion to roast lamb or rich game dishes.
palate: firm yet elegant tannins, rich core of fruit

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Chaignots
description: A wine of refined structure and old‑world grace, this 2013 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Les Chaignots” by Domaine Chauvenet‑Chopin reveals an intense core of black cherry, violet and gentle spice, framed by firm and elegant tannins mellowing beautifully with time.
sommelierNotes: Best decanted briefly and served at 15 °C, this Pinot Noir makes an inviting companion to roast lamb or rich game dishes.
palate: firm yet elegant tannins, rich core of fruit

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Murgers
description: This 2012 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Les Murgers” from Domaine Chauvenet‑Chopin presents a refined yet powerful character. It opens with restrained floral and spiced notes overlaying a plush core of ripe red fruit. The structure is robust and well‑balanced suggesting a noble capacity for maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in Burgundian stems to allow the fine spice and fruit layers to emerge. Couples beautifully with roast duck or earthy mushroom risotto.
palate: ripe red fruit with firm structure

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Chopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Murgers
description: This 2013 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Les Murgers” from Domaine Chauvenet‑Chopin presents a refined yet powerful character. It opens with restrained floral and spiced notes overlaying a plush core of ripe red fruit. The structure is robust and well‑balanced suggesting a noble capacity for maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in Burgundian stems to allow the fine spice and fruit layers to emerge. Couples beautifully with roast duck or earthy mushroom risotto.
palate: ripe red fruit with firm structure

name: Domaine Chauvenet-Shopin Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru aux Thorey
description: This 2012 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Aux Thorey” from Chauvenet‑Chopin presents a poised and refined expression of Pinot Noir from a celebrated Côte de Nuits vineyard, offering a blend of bright red fruit purity and fine-grained structure, framed by subtle spice and earth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C, allowing it to open in the glass. Enjoy now through the next decade with rich poultry or soft game preparations.
palate: velvety red fruit, integrated tannins, mineral undertone

name: Jl Chave Selection Crozes Hermitage Rouge Silene
description: A gracious Crozes‑Hermitage from J.L. Chave Sélection the 2018 Silène unfurls elegant black‑and‑blue fruit framed by mineral tension and a whisper of olive and licorice, all threaded through with floral lift and refined structure. The plush dark‑berry core resolves into poised tannins and a lingering, flower‑tinged finish that speaks of granite hillside origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature to coax its fragrant layers. Ideal with cassoulet or braised beef short ribs for seamless harmony.
aroma: mineral‑accented black and blue fruit with olive and licorice
palate: supple blackberry and boysenberry framed by fine‑grained tannins

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru aux Thorey
description: This 2019 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru “Aux Thorey” from Domaine Georges Chicotot reveals a refined cloak of dark cherry and subtle floral notes underpinned by gentle spice and graphite nuances, its lineage rooted in venerable vines striking a balance between poise and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in a large goblet to reveal its velvety texture. Pair with roast duck, mushroom‑rich sauces or aged Comté to echo its structure and elegance.
palate: silky texture, gentle spice and balanced acidity

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru Rue de Chaux
appellation: Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru « Rue de Chaux »
description: A wine of noble bearing this 2019 Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Premier Cru “Rue de Chaux” offers a profound and richly textured expression of its rocky Côte de Nuits terroir, presenting ripe black‑cherry and raspberry fruit framed by layers of licorice cedar and exotic spice
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool with red meats and game to complement its structured tannins and vibrant black‑fruit complexity
aroma: black cherry, raspberry, licorice, cedar, exotic spice
palate: densely concentrated, energetic yet structured

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges aux Allots
description: This 2019 Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits‑Saint‑Georges “Aux Allots” offers a refined expression of old‑vine Pinot Noir with poised concentration, showcasing red and brambly fruit wrapped in supple texture and subtle spice. It moves with grace and reserve inviting contemplation rather than showmanship.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature around 16 °C to reveal its silky mid‑palate. Pairs beautifully with earthy dishes such as mushroom tarts or light game preparations.
aroma: Elegant red fruit and gentle spice
palate: Supple bramble‑fruit core with refined texture

name: Domaine Georges Chicotot Nuits Saint Georges aux Saint Juliens
description: This 2019 Domaine Chicotot Nuits‑Saint‑Georges “Aux Saint Juliens” is an elegant, finely structured Pinot Noir displaying delicate floral perfume and bright cherry fruit, with lace‑like precision and a persistent, refined presence
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in a large-bowled glass and pair with subtly flavored white meats or regional poultry preparations
palate: lace‑like cherry and floral interplay

name: Classic Dry Cider
description: This nonvintage Classic Dry Cider from The Cider Farm is an elegant expression of orchard craftsmanship: it blends five traditional English cider apples with an American tart Liberty apple to deliver firm tannins, balanced acidity, and a clean, refreshing finish. The palate reveals nuanced complexity and crisp effervescence while showcasing the character of true cider apples rather than dessert varieties.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its tactile tannins and vibrant acidity; pairs beautifully with aged cheeses or herb‑crusted poultry.
aroma: bright orchard fruit with subtle tannic earthiness
palate: structured yet refreshing with nuanced apple depth

name: Cyser Cider
description: This lightly golden Cyser bridges the old‑world charm of tart cider apples with the sweet floral richness of locally sourced honey, yielding a semi‑dry libation that still carries approachable warmth. The palate offers a gentle interplay of orchard‑fresh apple and mellow honey that unfolds with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve just chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its honeyed aromatics and pair with nutty cheeses or roasted poultry.
palate: balanced tart‑sweet, soft honeyed texture

name: Dabinett Cider
description: This organically crafted cider from The Cider Farm expresses the noble Dabinett apple in a rare single‑variety form enhanced by select additions of Liberty, Chisel Jersey, and Porter’s Perfection, creating a semi‑dry, floral elegant offering with lush caramel and tropical undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its floral freshness and medium‑plus tannin structure, ideal with creamy cheeses or spiced pork dishes.
aroma: tropical and floral with rich caramel
palate: fresh apple juice, guava and cooked pineapple with balanced medium‑plus tannins

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: This oak‑aged cider unfurls with whisperings of vanilla and toast, the subtle medium‑toast American oak enriching the orchard fruit’s brightness in an elegant, wine‑like embrace. It carries a refined clarity and balance that evokes a polished Chardonnay nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip or white wine glass to highlight its gentle oak nuance: an ideal match for roast poultry or creamy alpine cheeses.
palate: bright orchard fruit with toast

name: Oak Aged Cider
description: A refined and elegant cider gently matured in medium‑toast American oak, offering a soft interplay of vanilla warmth and subtle toast complexity rooted in heritage apple character.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in slender stemware alongside roast poultry or mushroom‑topped fare to uplift the cider’s nuanced oak and orchard fruit interplay.
palate: balanced orchard fruit framed by oak

name: The Cider Farm Belgian Saison
description: This Belgian‑style farmhouse cider unfolds with layered citrus and spice on a background of restrained apple tannins, reminiscent of old‑world saison but refined by orchard depth and aromatic subtlety.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip or stemmed glass to enhance its citrus‑spice perfume and pair with soft cheeses or light seafood fare.
palate: tannic apple with bergamot and gentle hop lift

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Five Year
description: Opulent and orchard‑driven this aged apple brandy offers a refined amber hue and envelops the senses in a gentle embrace of orchard fruit framed by warm oak and bourbon‑barrel whispers each bottle uniquely carries the story of its single‑barrel origin.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to appreciate its depth or with a single small ice cube to soften its warmth; pairs elegantly with rich pâté or aged cheeses.
aroma: deep orchard fruit and charred oak
palate: fruit‑forward with bourbon‑barrel warmth

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Apple Brandy Aged Two Years
description: A quietly beguiling Wisconsin apple brandy that speaks in orchard whispers, aged two years in charred bourbon barrels with the subtle presence of wild apple wood from the farm, offering a soft interplay of barrel echoes and orchard purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a tulip glass to admire its clarity and gentle warmth, or use as a refined substitute for bourbon in classic cocktails.
palate: soft apple flesh and gentle oak spice

name: The Cider Farm Wisconsin Pommeau Aged Three Years
description: A refined and mellow fortified apple aperitif, this Pommeau from The Cider Farm is crafted in Wisconsin using their orchard‑grown cider apples and apple brandy, patiently aged for three years to reveal a soft golden hue and layered orchard fruits
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a small tulip glass as a refined aperitif or alongside nut‑forward desserts, aged cheeses, or fruit tarts
palate: smooth orchard fruit sweetness with a hint of raisin
drinkWindow: drink now to medium term (5 years)

name: Tremlett's Cider
description: This rare American dry cider offers a refined tannic structure and bright acidity that elevate its orchard fruit character into something truly graceful and complex. Aromatic floral top notes lead into a palate marked by green grape, apricot and a whisper of minerality conjuring a gently dusty orchard.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to accentuate floral aromas, lovely with oysters, shrimp cocktail or poached white fish.
palate: green grape, apricot, subtle minerality

name: Tremlett's Cider
description: This artisanal cider presents a beautifully poised balance of tannin and acidity in the old‑world tradition. Vibrant floral and pome fruit aromas gracefully lead into a dry yet gently fruity sip marked by green grape, apricot and apple skin nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip or white wine glass; ideal with light seafood such as shrimp cocktail, oysters, poached white fish and simply grilled poultry.
palate: dry yet fruit‑driven with green grape and apricot
finish: lingering apple skin and subtle minerality

name: La Mission Haut Brion Pessac Leognan Rouge (Full Case Only)
description: Château La Mission Haut-Brion 2016 is a profound Pessac-Léognan built on ripe fruit, broad texture, and exceptionally refined tannins. Richness and power gather through the palate, while freshness keeps the wine articulate and complete.
sommelierNotes: Decant for two to three hours if serving now and pour with roast beef, lamb, or truffle-accented dishes; patient cellaring remains well rewarded.
aroma: Ripe black fruit, cedar, graphite, warm spice
palate: Broad, concentrated, powerful, polished

name: Petit Clos Pinot Noir
description: This Petit Clos Pinot Noir 2020 from Clos Henri evokes an old‑world sensibility rendered in Marlborough finesse: vibrant aromas of cherry and plum linger above subtleties of spice and licorice, while a lush palate offers macerated red fruit framed by fine textural tannins in balanced harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 15 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass to release its lifted red fruit and spice character; pairs beautifully with roasted duck or pork fillet, and will evolve gracefully through 2028.
palate: dense red fruit, refined tannins

name: Petit Clos Sauvignon Blanc
description: The 2021 Clos Henri Petit Clos Sauvignon Blanc presents a vivid and elegant expression of youthful Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc with beautifully concentrated bright fruit and a whisper of stony minerality, all framed by a lively and textural profile
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip wine glass to reveal its citrus and minerality; pairs gracefully with fresh shellfish or as a refined aperitif
aroma: citrus and white flower with chalky minerality
palate: zesty and round with juicy exotic fruit and minerality

name: Pinot Noir
description: This 2018 Clos Henri Pinot Noir from Marlborough offers a refined and layered expression of New Zealand Pinot Noir. It unfolds with vibrant cherry and raspberry fruits, a whisper of earthy mushrooms and spice, and is built on a framework of sleek tannins and bright acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 12 °C in a glass that accentuates its red fruit and elegant structure; it will pair beautifully with roasted duck or lamb dishes, and will reward cellaring through the late 2020s.
aroma: cherry and raspberry with dried florals and earthy spice
palate: bright acidity, sleek tannins with brambly berries and mushroom undertones

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: This 2019 Clos Henri Sauvignon Blanc from Marlborough embodies refined minerality and vibrant citrus, unfolding with notes of lime, passion fruit and subtle wet-stone accents. The wine carries a delicate salinity and crisp, energetic structure that reflects its organic, biodynamic origins and telltale Greywacke river‑stone terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a medium tulip‑shaped glass alongside oysters, pan‑fried snapper or simply enjoy as a refreshing aperitif.
aroma: lime and passion fruit with wet‑stone minerality
palate: zesty citrus, herbal lift, elegant texture

name: Clos Marie Pic Saint Loup Olivette
description: This 2023 L’Olivette from Clos Marie offers an elegant Mediterranean red born of biodynamic vines in Pic Saint‑Loup, where Grenache, Syrah and a whisper of Mourvèdre coalesce to produce ripe raspberry, olive brininess and fragrant rosemary, all wrapped in fine-grained tannins and vibrant freshness. The travel‑worn calcareous soils and gentle elevation of Lauret lend a graceful structure and mineral undercurrent that elevate its fruit with finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in a large glass to unveil its red‑fruit perfume and herbal nuance. Pair with roast lamb, Provençal stew or aged sheep’s cheese for a refined match.
palate: supple red fruit framed by lively tannins

name: Domaine du Clos Salomon Givry 1er Cru Clos Salomon
description: The 2019 Clos Salomon Givry Premier Cru unveils a graceful marriage of ripe red fruit and limestone‑inflected minerality, its silk‑textured palate unfolding layers of cherry and spiced earth beneath subtle vitality.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature allow its soft tannins and saline minerality to elevate roasted duck or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: silky, mineral‑tinged red fruit

name: Clotilde Legrand Saumur-Champigny les Lizieres
description: The 2020 Clotilde Legrand Les Lizières presents an elegant rendition of Saumur‑Champigny Cabernet Franc with a perfumed bouquet of bramble and raspberry over subtle spice and tobacco nuances, leading to a vibrant, juicy palate and refined tannic grip.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature, pairing beautifully with simply grilled lamb or mushroom‑rich poultry dishes.
palate: juicy, vibrant acidity, fruit‑forward with ripe cherries

name: Clotilde Legrand Saumur-Champigny les Terrages
description: A dense, vibrant Saumur‑Champigny from Clotilde Legrand, this 2019 “Les Terrages” offers a core of ripe black fruits and redcurrant framed by hints of dried almond and earth, all wrapped in supple, velvety tannins and refined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature it will charm alongside herb‑roasted poultry or nuanced terrines.
aroma: ripe black fruit with almond nuance
palate: supple black and red fruit with silky texture

name: Chardonnay California
description: Bright and unpretentious this Coastal Ridge 2023 California Chardonnay offers ripe orchard fruit and soft honeyed notes wrapped in a gentle creamy texture with a refreshing lift of acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in tulip glasses with fresh seafood or creamy poultry dishes for a beautifully balanced sip.
palate: creamy texture with honey and citrus
foodPairings: grilled sea bass with herb butter

name: Merlot California
description: A supple and inviting young Merlot from Coastal Ridge in California offering bright red fruit tones that speak of raspberry and plum wrapped in gentle warmth, this wine unfolds with a graceful ease and accessible charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature around 60°F, ideal with roasted poultry or rich tomato‑based pastas.
palate: soft, fruit‑driven mid‑palate
finish: gentle, smooth fading of berry echoes

name: Pinot Noir
description: This 2016 Coastal Ridge Pinot Noir from California offers a gently lithe structure with soft tannins, framing ripe red fruits such as strawberry, black cherry, and plum. The texture is graceful and inviting suggesting effortless drinkability in an unpretentious, old‑world spirit.
sommelierNotes: Chill lightly and serve in a tulip‑shaped glass to enhance the wine’s red fruit charm; pairs simply with roasted chicken or mushroom‑based dishes.
aroma: soft red fruits and subtle oak
palate: ripe cherry, plum with gentle tannins

name: White Zinfandel California
description: A graceful pale rose hue ushers in Coastal Ridge White Zinfandel 2024 California, offering a gentle sweetness framed by apricot, strawberry and melon nuances in a softly lush garland of fruit. Velvety yet bright this wine seduces with its charming fruit and just-off‑dry finish that beckons another sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender tulip glass to emphasize freshness, and pair alongside light summer fare or a fruit‑topped dessert to echo its delicate sweetness.
palate: fruit‑driven, gently off‑dry

name: Coastal Ridge White Zinfandel California
description: A graceful pale rose hue ushers in Coastal Ridge White Zinfandel 2024 California, offering a gentle sweetness framed by apricot, strawberry and melon nuances in a softly lush garland of fruit. Velvety yet bright this wine seduces with its charming fruit and just-off‑dry finish that beckons another sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender tulip glass to emphasize freshness, and pair alongside light summer fare or a fruit‑topped dessert to echo its delicate sweetness.
palate: fruit‑driven, gently off‑dry

name: Domaine Collotte Marsannay en Combereau
description: A refined Marsannay from venerable vines, this 2019 Marsannay “Combereau” by Domaine Collotte reveals a poised interplay of red and black cherry framed by a whisper of smoked meat and pomegranatelaced minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C to accentuate its youthful vibrancy; complements rich autumnal fare such as mushroom risotto or roasted game in delicate sauces.
aroma: red and black cherries with a hint of smoked meat
palate: pure and mineral driven, layered and precise

name: Bourgogne Blanc
description: Domaine Collotte's 2015 Bourgogne Blanc is a fresh, unadorned Chardonnay shaped by orchard fruit, citrus, and chalk. Stainless-steel aging preserves clarity and gives the palate a clean, direct line.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 10-12°C with shellfish, grilled river fish, or a young goat cheese.
palate: Clean orchard fruit, brisk acidity

name: Bourgogne Pinot Noir Noble Souche
description: Domaine Collotte's 2015 Bourgogne Rouge Cuvée de Noble Souche is a supple Pinot Noir with cherry fruit, light spice, and a gentle mineral accent. Fine tannins and a graceful frame make this a mature, understated red Burgundy.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly cool with charcuterie, roast chicken, mushroom dishes, or mild washed-rind cheese.
palate: Supple fruit, fine tannin, light earth

name: Domaine COLLO9TTE Gevrey Chambertin les Evocelles
description: An expressive Gevrey‑Chambertin showing a luminous nose of black fruits warmed by a suggestion of toast and spice its structure gracious and plush with fine tannins that support generous depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 60 °F to reveal its layered fruit and subtle toastiness, and pair with roast duck or gamebirds to enhance its refined power.
aroma: intense black fruit with toast and spice
palate: generous, plush structure with fine tannins

name: Domaine Collotte Fixin les Champstions
description: A noble expression of Fixin from Domaine Collotte the 2019 “Les Champstions” shows black cherry perfume underpinned by composed noble tannins generous yet refined, a wine of both muscle and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature around 14 °C after decanting to reveal its full aromatic depth. An excellent match for richly sauced red meat or a subtly bittersweet chocolate dessert.
aroma: black cherry with dark fruit nuance
palate: structured yet velvety tannins, full-bodied
finish: long with spice and earthy echo

name: Domaine Collotte Fixin les Crais de Chene
description: A wine of understated pedigree, offering a refined ribbon of black cherry and soil-born nuances, framed by elegant, velvety structure and a poised, enduring finish. It delivers true Côte de Nuits temperament without fanfare.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 55 °F to reveal its pure fruit and fine tannins. Pair with roasted pork with herbs or mushroom risotto.
palate: velvety, focused, mineral-tinged core

name: Domaine Collotte Gevrey Chambertin les Evocelles
description: A gracious expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin vividness, this 2020 Domaine Collotte “Les Evocelles” carries a high‑toned bouquet of black fruit and floral perfume with an elegant framework revealing fine structure even at this youth. The palate offers generous warmth with refined tannins and poised energy, suggesting harmony between ripeness and tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to reveal its lifted floral and black fruit character, ideally with rich game birds or roasted duck to mirror its generosity and fine structure.
aroma: vibrant black fruit and floral perfume
palate: generous structure with refined tannins

name: Domaine Collotte Marsannay Blanc
description: A refined white Burgundy from Marsannay, this 2019 Domaine Collotte Marsannay Blanc offers an inviting presence of green apple, quince and subtle white florals with a fine overlay of vanillin oak. The palate is broad and virile yet refined, showing depth, malted undertones and waves of sappy structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in large Burgundy glasses and pair with game birds or roasted duck to complement its savory depth.
aroma: bramble berries, brown tobacco, citrus rind
palate: broad, virile, malted, sappy

name: Domaine Pierre Damoy Marsannay la Bretigniere
description: A quietly refined Marsannay that marries earth‑tinged dark berry fruit with a noble sense of structure, offering both density and poise in equal measure. Its presence is contemplative not flamboyant, suggested by understated power rather than flamboyant expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to let the firm structure and mineral‑tinged finish emerge, pairing especially well with lightly gamey dishes or rosemary‑accented roasted meats.
aroma: earthy dark berries with wood spice
palate: precise, intense, energetic dark fruit

name: Domaine Pierre Damoy Marsannay les Longeroies
description: A brooding expression of Marsannay from Domenie Pierre Damoy’s 2015 Les Longeroies, this Pinot Noir offers an alluring balance of vibrant red fruit and earth with an undertone of smoky oak and licorice, wrapped in seamless texture and structural poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55 °F to showcase its finesse alongside game birds or rich poultry stews.
palate: tar balanced with ripe red‑fruit concentration

name: Pierre Damoy Bourgogne Rouge
description: A wine of elegant burgundy character from Domaine Pierre Damoy these Pinot Noir vines reveal a refined palette of subtle undergrowth and ripe red fruit, framed by silky tannins and a graceful tension that lingers
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in the mid fourteens Celsius alongside delicate poultry dishes or light game to accentuate its finesse
palate: silky yet structured with ripe cherry and underbrush

name: Pierre Damoy Marsannay la Bretigniere
description: Pierre Damoy's 2014 Marsannay La Bretignière is a poised Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir with dark cherry fruit, subtle spice, and a firm mineral line. Bottle age has softened the structure while preserving a distinctly savory center.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature after a brief decant for sediment; pair with duck, veal, or lentils with smoked bacon.
palate: Layered fruit, fine tannin, mineral tension

name: Danica Elegance Rose Aop Cotes de Provence
description: This vibrant rosé presents a pale salmon hue with an inviting perfume of pear blossom and delicate redcurrant, offering refined clarity and grace true to its Provençal heritage. On the palate it shows light cherry and citrus notes, underpinned by a mineral tension and clean precision that speaks of elegant craftsmanship.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled near 48 °F in a medium tulip glass to preserve its freshness. It elevates delicate seafood such as ceviche or shellfish as well as light goat cheese hors d’oeuvres.
palate: light cherry and citrus with mineral tension

name: Danica Elegance Rose Aop Cotes de Provence
description: This vibrant rosé presents a pale salmon hue with an inviting perfume of pear blossom and delicate redcurrant, offering refined clarity and grace true to its Provençal heritage. On the palate it shows light cherry and citrus notes, underpinned by a mineral tension and clean precision that speaks of elegant craftsmanship.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled near 48 °F in a medium tulip glass to preserve its freshness. It elevates delicate seafood such as ceviche or shellfish as well as light goat cheese hors d’oeuvres.
palate: light cherry and citrus with mineral tension

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Beaujolais Blanc
description: A graceful Beaujolais Blanc rendered with clarity and poise aromas of pear, yellow stone fruit and gentle floral breath weave through a supple, mineral‑tinged core revealing subtle richness underlined by poised acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 50°F in a white Burgundy glass, as an aperitif or alongside simply prepared seafood, creamy soft cheeses, or delicately seasoned poultry.
aroma: pear and white peach with faint florals
palate: soft stone fruit framed by fine mineral streak

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Chiroubles Chatenay
description: This 2020 Chiroubles “Chatenay” from Daniel Bouland offers a vivid expression of Cru Beaujolais, with succulent plums and pomegranate threaded through fragrant spices reflecting a steep, high‑altitude terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature alongside rich poultry or herb‑accented dishes to temper its vivacious fruit and fine structure.
palate: bright, medium‑full body with velvety tannins
finish: ample core of fruit with lively brightness

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Cote de Brouilly Cuvee Melanie
description: This 2017 Daniel Bouland Côte‑de‑Brouilly Cuvée Mélanie opens with a richly poised bouquet of blackberry and wild berries underlined by savory dark chocolate and subtle licorice nuances, balanced by smoky mineral undertones from its volcanic hillside terroir. The palate is full‑bodied yet fresh with lush dark fruit framed by compelling structure and restrained tannins lingering into a layered, spice‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled at cellar temperature, alongside rabbit in wine sauce or softly poached egg pairing, to accentuate its fruit‑driven depth and mineral elegance.
aroma: blackberry, dark chocolate, licorice, smoky mineral
palate: lush dark fruit, structured, restrained tannins

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Pre Jourdan
description: This 2020 Daniel Bouland Morgon “Pré Jourdan” unfolds with profound black‑fruit intensity evocative of cassis and ripe cherry tempered by an undercurrent of smoke and gentle salinity. The wine’s structure is supple yet vivid with fine tannins caressing the palate alongside a subtle hint of salted caramel and a smoky echo.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to highlight the fruit clarity and smoked nuances; pairs beautifully with roasted pork, earthy mushroom dishes or charcuterie boards.
palate: velvety, fine‑tannin structure with salted caramel nuance

name: Domaine Daniel Bouland Morgon Vieilles Vignes Corcelette
description: A graceful and perfumed Morgon from Daniel Bouland’s historic Corcelette enclave, the 2017 Vieilles Vignes displays focused energy and depth, woven with red and black cherry, floral lift and mineral precision. It offers structure and cachet, with an undertow of dusty earth and savoury nuance that suggest long‑term refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below ambient cellar temperature in thin crystal, pair with roast pork, aged cheeses or wild mushrooms to complement its perfume and fine tannin.
aroma: red and black cherry with dried flowers and mineral dust
palate: velvety, concentrated, perfumed core with fine tannins

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Heart Arrow Ranch
description: This single‑vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon from biodynamic Heart Arrow Ranch in Mendocino’s Eagle Peak exudes dark, structured elegance, with layers of blackberry, cassis and plum threaded through graphite and forest‑floor nuances in a deep purple‑black hue
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 62 °F in a large Burgundy‑style glass; pairs beautifully with herb‑crusted lamb or mushroom‑scented sauces
palate: structured with balanced acidity and complex fruit
finish: persistent with mineral and black pepper spice

name: Cellars Cabernet Sauvignon Heart Arrow Ranch
description: This 2018 Dashe Cellars Heart Arrow Ranch Cabernet Sauvignon evokes the noble austerity of old‑world claret, with concentrated notes of black cherry and cassis underpinned by graphite and violets, all framed by mineral tension and velvety structure. It displays a refined power reminiscent of fine Bordeaux yet expresses the unique terroir of Mendocino’s Eagle Peak with poised composure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in large glasses, pair with herb‑accented roast lamb or aged Gouda to highlight its structure and mineral undertones.
palate: velvety mid‑palate, structured like Bordeaux with complex fruit and mineral spectrum

name: Cellars Chenin Blanc Concrete Cuvee les Enfants Terribles
description: A pale golden Chenin Blanc born of Clarksburg’s cool, delta-cooled vineyards, this Concrete Cuvée offers finely textured apricot and pear framed by lively citrus-tinged tension and a flinty mineral underpinning, all rendered with subtly layered spice and creamy lees.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its precise acidity and stone‑fruit clarity, ideal with shellfish or gently spiced vegetable tagine.
palate: stone‑fruit richness, crisp acidity, mineral thread

name: Dashe Cellars Chenin Blanc les Enfants Terrible
description: This 2023 Dashe Cellars “Les Enfants Terribles” Concrete Cuvée Chenin Blanc glimmers pale gold in the glass with a refined clarity that sings of Clarksburg’s cool Sacramento River delta. Its expressive aromas of pear, apricot, grapefruit, honeycomb and mineral weave into a rich yet lithe palate layered with stone‑fruit and citrus flavors, underpinned by vibrant acidity and a long, lively finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to emphasize its bright acidity and textural richness: pairs beautifully with grilled sand dabs, shellfish, light creamy cheeses, or as a crisp aperitif.
palate: viscous stone‑fruit and citrus with crisp acidity

name: Cellars Late Harvest Zinfandel
description: This 2019 Dashe Cellars Late Harvest Zinfandel offers a refined, seductively sweet profile with an elegant clarity uncommon in dessert wines, a product of concentrated Lily Hill Vineyard fruit that retains vibrant acidity even after extended hang time.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled alongside dark chocolate desserts or artisan aged cheeses to play off the wine’s intense red‑fruit and spice notes while balancing its sweetness.
aroma: wild cherry and pomegranate with lavender and vanilla spice
palate: bright red fruit mingled with dark berry depth
finish: lingering sweet‑spicy finish with crisp acidity

name: Cellars Zinfandel Vineyard Select
description: An elegant and poised Zinfandel whose core of black cherry and raspberry is woven with fine pepper and sage, offering a graceful, lithe texture rather than muscular weight. Bright acidity lifts the luscious fruit, while the frame of refined tannins carries a lingering whisper of clove and dark cocoa powder.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature, ideal alongside herb‑spiced meatloaf or penne with fennel sausage where its spicy generosity and freshness will sing.
aroma: Pomegranate, black cherry, raspberry with cassis and pepper spice
palate: Lush, lively texture with bright fruit and spice
finish: Long, lively, with clove, licorice and cocoa powder
foodPairings: Penne with fennel sausage and lemon

name: Chenin Blanc Concrete Cuvee les Enfamts Terribles
description: This 2018 Dashe Cellars Les Enfants Terribles Concrete Cuvée Chenin Blanc reveals a pale golden hue and carries pear and apricot tones lifted by mineral undertones, honeycomb sweetness, and a bright hint of grapefruit, all woven into a rich, viscous texture and a long, succulent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 55 °F to unveil its crystalline acidity and layered stone‑fruit profile, pairing beautifully with shellfish or creamy cheeses.
palate: rich, viscous stonefruit

name: Wines Eola-Amity Hills Pinot Noir
description: An elegantly poised Oregon Pinot Noir reflecting the cool‑climate signature of the Eola‑Amity Hills AVA. Bright cherry and earth‑touched nuances mingle with a whisper of early‑season wild strawberry and forest floor in a wine of graceful complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 58 °F in a large bowl glass to draw out its layered red fruit and subtle truffle notes. Pairs beautifully with duck breast or wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: dusty raspberry, spearmint and forest floor
palate: bright red fruit interwoven with truffle, soy and earth
drinkWindow: instantly approachable, will evolve over 5–8 years

name: Wines Pinot Noir Chehalem Mountains
description: A refined expression of Oregon Pinot Noir from the Chehalem Mountains, this 2019 David Paige vintage reveals dusky violet florals wrapped in sweet spice and sinewy black fruit tapestry, all framed by a caressing mineral undercurrent. It offers a soft, tactile presence with a discreet firmness and gently bitter lift that lingers in the glass.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a large Burgundy stemware to highlight its nuanced red fruit and mineral drive: pairs beautifully with roasted game hen, mushroom‑crusted pork loin or an autumnal beet and goat cheese salad.
aroma: dusty violet florals and sweet spice
palate: soft and round with tactile mineral bite and crisp black fruit
finish: pleasantly bitter tinge tapering to a light structure

name: Wines Pinot Noir Eola-Amity Hills Rpg Vineyard
description: This singular‑vineyard Pinot Noir from RPG in the Eola‑Amity Hills carries restrained elegance with lithe red fruit and subtle earthen nuance Balanced and graceful with an undercurrent of forest floor and savory detail
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or at cellar cool to showcase its florals and fine tannins, ideal with lightly seasoned game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes
aroma: red currant and wet terra cotta
palate: sweet Lambert cherry, clove, fresh mint

name: Wines Same Paige Pinot Noir Willamette Valley
description: This release offers a bright playful expression of Willamette Valley Pinot Noir capturing energetic cherry and red berry lift with subtle whispers of earth. Its texture is light and nimble with a polished frame and just enough structure to feel satisfying yet graceful.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55 °F in a large glass to accentuate its vivid fruit and gentle acidity. Pairs elegantly with roasted duck breast or creamy mushroom risotto.
palate: juicy red berries, elegant tannins

name: Black Noble
description: An exquisite and regal dessert wine that whispers of time’s alchemy in oak solera barrels, revealing a tapestry of dark raisin and mandarin peel underscored by coffee and toffee notes.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a small dessert glass, ideal with sticky date pudding or a fine blue‑veined cheese platter.
palate: rich dried fruit, citrus peel, caramel, viscous
drinkWindow: Ready to drink now; will keep for several years

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Grand Cru Schlossberg
description: An austere and riveting expression of Alsace’s granitic terroir, this 2019 Schlossberg Grand Cru from Domaine Marcel Deiss reveals crystalline depth with concentrated orchard fruit and stony minerality, all suffused with electric precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in a tall white glass to showcase its vertical energy; pairs beautifully with grilled or baked fish or shellfish to underscore its saline freshness.
aroma: orchard fruit, baked peach, wet stone
palate: electric minerality, vertical structure, intense purity

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Grand Cru Schlossberg
description: An austere and riveting expression of Alsace’s granitic terroir, this 2020 Schlossberg Grand Cru from Domaine Marcel Deiss reveals crystalline depth with concentrated orchard fruit and stony minerality, all suffused with electric precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in a tall white glass to showcase its vertical energy; pairs beautifully with grilled or baked fish or shellfish to underscore its saline freshness.
aroma: orchard fruit, baked peach, wet stone
palate: electric minerality, vertical structure, intense purity

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Langenberg
description: This 2019 Langenberg from Domaine Marcel Deiss captivates with crystalline clarity and a minerally precision born of granite soils, offering an interplay of ripe citrus and subtle herbal nuance in elegant balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 10 – 12 °C in a slim-stemmed white wine glass, ideal alongside dishes that mirror its freshness and finesse, or enjoy as a contemplative aperitif.
palate: energetic minerality with citrus clarity
foodPairings: light seafood like sole or sea bream
fresh shellfish such as oysters or scallops
delicately seasoned poultry or choucroute de la mer

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Ribeauville
description: This 2020 Ribeauvillé from Domaine Marcel Deiss, born of complantation and biodynamic conviction, reveals an elegant tension between limestone clarity and layered orchard fruit. Its mineral drive frames golden apple and candied citrus in a refined, terroir‑defined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 50–54 °F to draw out its saline energy and pair with delicate, iodized dishes such as beurre blanc fish or spring vegetables.
aroma: orchard fruit and candied citrus with subtle floral lift
palate: minerally, precise, tensioned

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Ribeauville
description: A crystalline Alsace Riesling from Domaine Marcel Deiss 2021 offers vivid clarity: a sheer mineral frame enriched with citrus zest and delicate orchard fruit. The wine’s biodynamic roots lend it an elegant austerity while a thread of subtle white stone ripples through its poised structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8 °C in a slender tulip glass. Pair with simply prepared seafood or nuanced Asian dishes to enhance the wine’s refined minerality and tension.
palate: precise mineral tension, vibrant citrus core

name: Champagne Denis Chaput Lombre D'amand Reserve Brut
description: This non‑vintage Champagne is born of a masterful blend of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay, aged gracefully over more than a decade thus offering an elegant richness with whisper of almond and brioche, while bright citrus and marly minerality lend freshness and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at roughly 8 °C in a tall tulip glass to preserve the fine mousse: ideal with buttery fish, poultry, or refined shellfish preparations.
palate: creamy with lemon‑tinted minerality
foodPairings: sea bass with butter sauce and chanterelles
drinkWindow: Drink now through 2028 (NV with long lees ageing retains freshness)

name: Domaine Digioia-Royer Chambolle Musigny
description: This refined village‑level Chambolle‑Musigny offers a poised interplay of vibrant red cherry and ripe plum accentuated by subtle underbrush and violet nuance, the expression underscored by seamless structure and a gentle breadth.
sommelierNotes: Best decanted lightly and served at cellar‑cool temperature alongside delicate game or roasted poultry with autumnal herbs.
aroma: red cherry and plum with violet whispers
palate: silky, structured mid‑palate with sous‑bois depth

name: Domaine Digioia-Royer Chambolle Musigny Vieilles Vignes les Fremieres
description: This Chambolle‑Musigny Vieilles Vignes “Les Fremières” from 2012 exudes classic Côte de Nuits allure with deep red fruit and elegant structure. A nose of cherry and blackberry unfolds into a long, poised palate framed by refined yet present tannins that speak of old vines and limestone terroir. The finish lingers with finesse and a whisper of licorice and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–17°C after decanting for thirty minutes to allow the wine’s complexity to bloom; pairs beautifully with roasted poultry or soft regional cheeses.
palate: long poised palate with refined tannins

name: Tokaji Late Harvest
description: Golden amber in hue this 2019 Disznókő Tokaji Late Harvest displays honeyed orchard fruit framed by bright citrus and a whisper of spice echoing old‐world elegance, structured by a vibrant balancing acidity that lifts its richness into a serene, luminous expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an inviting aperitif or alongside creamy pâtés or goat’s cheese; its balancing sweetness and acidity bring finesse to both savory bites and fruit‑based desserts.
palate: rich fruit balanced by crisp acidity

name: Domaine Alain Burguet Vosne Romanee
description: This 2019 Domaine Alain Burguet Vosne‑Romanée village reveals an elegant perfume of rose petal and fine spice over a vivid core of red cherry and subtle forest floor, the texture refined and radiant, presenting a luminous portrayal of the Côte de Nuits terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to enhance clarity of detail pair with classic pairings such as roast quail or wild mushroom risotto.
palate: vivid red cherry core, forest floor nuance

name: Domaine Alary Cotes du Rhone la Gerbaude
description: A richly resonant Côtes du Rhône from Domaine Alary with a plush core of black and red fruit enlivened by a whisper of herbes de garrigue and lavender notes, all wrapped in a smooth frame of gentle tannins and dusty spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature with grilled lamb chops or pork sirloin; also charming with a spinach and goat cheese tart.
aroma: ripe red berries with garrigue spice
palate: smooth, juicy medium‑bodied with dusty tannins

name: Domaine Albert Mann Riesling Scholssberg
description: The 2020 Albert Mann Schlossberg Grand Cru Riesling presents a refined expression of its granitic terroir with a luminous core of Amalfi lemon, yellow peach and mirabelle that unfolds with crystalline energy and an undercurrent of vibrant minerality. The palate is straight and sleek, balanced by silken texture and impeccable acidity that carries through a long linear finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender white wine glass to reveal its citrus and stony clarity. Ideal with delicate seafood such as sole with lemon, grilled lobster or goat cheese platters.
palate: Straight and sleek with stony minerality and creaminess
finish: Very long and linear, mineral purity

name: Domaine Anne Gros Bourgogne Chardonnay
description: A graceful Bourgogne Blanc from Domaine Anne Gros vintage 2022 offering delicate aromas of honeyed apple and pear, underpinned by a buttery nuance drawn from gentle oak ageing, all balanced by a lithe acidity that brings refinement rather than weight.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–14 °C paired with creamy poultry dishes or silky soft cheeses for a harmonious match.
palate: elegant, with gentle oak and freshness

name: Domaine Anne Gros Bourgogne Hauts Cotes de Nuits Cuvee Marine Blanc
description: A graceful Bourgogne blanc from Domaine Anne Gros, the 2022 Cuvée Marine reveals tender citrus blossoms and exotic fruit underpinned by a gentle saline minerality, imparted by extended lees ageing. It offers a refined structure, aromatic clarity and a poised balance between freshness and roundness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 12 °C in slender, tulip‑shaped glasses, ideal for early drinking and perfect with delicate seafood or goat cheese.
palate: bright citrus acidity, subtly creamy texture

name: Domaine Anne Gros Chambolle Musigny la Combe D'orvaux
description: This 2022 Chambolle‑Musigny “La Combe d’Orveau” from Domaine Anne Gros entices with a luminous ruby hue and red‑fruit perfume of pomegranate and cranberry interwoven with fresh floral accents and light tea nuance, all delivered in a poised and refined frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to reveal its lifted red fruit and graceful structure; pairs beautifully with roast duck or game birds.
palate: elegant red berries, silky texture

name: Domaine Anne Gros Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: A classic expression of Clos‑Vougeot Grand‑Cru from Domaine Anne Gros this 2022 vintage unfolds in deep velvety purple, offering ripe black‑cherry and plum fruit joined by invigorating spice accents of pepper, clove and nutmeg, all framed by fine supple tannins in balanced harmony, evoking both power and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C after decanting to reveal its depth pair with roasted game, aged French cheeses or richly sauced meats.
aroma: ripe black cherry and plum with pepper spice
palate: harmonious, supple tannins with earthy spice

name: Domaine Anne Gros Echezeaux Grand Cru
description: The 2022 Domaine Anne Gros Grands‑Échezeaux Grand Cru unfolds with an elegant yet potent frame, revealing dark berry and crushed limestone aromas framed by delicate rose petal nuance. The mouthfeel is refined and tensile with filigree tannins, a sense of freshness and subtle power that promises graceful evolution over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in large Burgundy glasses after decanting; pairs superbly with richly scented local aged cheeses or herb‑accented charcuterie.
aroma: dark berry fruit with crushed limestone and wilted rose petals
palate: medium‑bodied, filigree tannins with tensile structure and freshness

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Cremant de Loire Rose
description: This rosé Crémant de Loire from Domaine Arnaud Lambert unveils a pale pink glimmer adorned with a delicate effervescence. The bouquet offers charming red berry whispers underscored by a hint of floral grace and a caress of minerality. On the palate the mousse remains featherlight balanced by a vivid freshness and gentle fruit, leading to a refined subtle finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled between 8 and 10 °C in slender flutes or tulip glasses. Ideal as an elegant apéritif or paired with shellfish, light poultry, or summery hors d’œuvres.
aroma: red berries softened by floral grace, subtle minerality
palate: feather‑light mousse, crisp freshness, gentle fruit

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Cremant de Loire Rose
description: This rosé Crémant de Loire from Domaine Arnaud Lambert unveils a pale pink glimmer adorned with a delicate effervescence. The bouquet offers charming red berry whispers underscored by a hint of floral grace and a caress of minerality. On the palate the mousse remains featherlight balanced by a vivid freshness and gentle fruit, leading to a refined subtle finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled between 8 and 10 °C in slender flutes or tulip glasses. Ideal as an elegant apéritif or paired with shellfish, light poultry, or summery hors d’œuvres.
aroma: red berries softened by floral grace, subtle minerality
palate: feather‑light mousse, crisp freshness, gentle fruit

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc la Rue (Breze)
description: From the celebrated slopes of Brézé in Saumur this 2020 Saumur Blanc “La Rue” by Domaine Arnaud Lambert presents a crystalline core of Chenin Blanc that marries bright citrus and orchard nuances with a whisper of chalky minerality, crafting an impression of purity and poise. Matured for twenty months in both barrel and concrete this wine unfolds with a gentle creaminess from élevage yet retains a vivid tension that drives through the palate with elegant clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve between 11 °C and 13 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its limestone‑infused vibrancy and pair it with subtly spiced seafood or white fish dishes that echo its saline finish.
aroma: lemon confit, white flowers, wet chalk
palate: bright citrus and green apple with a mineral spine

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc la Rue ( Breze)
description: From the celebrated slopes of Brézé in Saumur this 2021 Saumur Blanc “La Rue” by Domaine Arnaud Lambert presents a crystalline core of Chenin Blanc that marries bright citrus and orchard nuances with a whisper of chalky minerality, crafting an impression of purity and poise. Matured for twenty months in both barrel and concrete this wine unfolds with a gentle creaminess from élevage yet retains a vivid tension that drives through the palate with elegant clarity.

aroma: lemon confit, white flowers, wet chalk
palate: bright citrus and green apple with a mineral spine

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc les Perrieres (Breze)
description: This Saumur Blanc Les Perrières 2022 by Arnaud Lambert presents a refined expression of Chenin Blanc rooted in clay‑limestone soils of Saint‑Cyr‑en‑Bourg and Brézé, lifted by 60‑year‑old vines and a year’s ageing equally split between barrel and large foudre, offering clarity and a poised interplay of citrus and mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in elegant white Burgundy glasses to reveal the tension and freshness, and pair with shellfish or chèvre for a graceful match.
palate: focused with saline tension

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Midi(breze)
description: The 2024 Arnaud Lambert Saumur Blanc Brézé “Midi” emerges with crystalline precision and a whisper of limestone in its core energy, intertwined with subtle floral lift and the sparkle of green orchard fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve very chilled, around 8 °C, and match with delicate seafood or chèvre for an elegant harmony.
aroma: lemon zest, green apple, faint honeysuckle
palate: taut, mineral-driven, bone‑dry with white peach and pear skin tones

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Champigny Terres Rouges Saint Cry en Bourg
description: A refined expression of Cabernet Franc from the chalky, silty clay soils of Saint‑Cyr‑en‑Bourg: the 2023 Les Terres Rouges offers vivid red‑berry clarity and a lithe, structured frame that speaks of terroir‑driven elegance. Its youthful energy is underpinned by crystalline precision and a subtle mineral nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 14–16 °C with roasted lamb or terrines to allow the wine’s freshness and gentle tannins to frame savory flavors with grace.
aroma: bright red berries with a mineral edge
palate: lithe, structured, precisely lifted

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Champigny Terres Rouges Saint Cyr en Bourg
description: The 2023 Terres Rouges from Domaine Arnaud Lambert is an inviting Cabernet Franc that radiates striking ruby clarity, offering vivid red‑berry fruit layered with a savory mineral undercurrent that speaks of its chalk and clay‑sand soils. It delivers its charms with seamless balance, its fine‑grained tannins woven into a frame of energetic freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 14 °C to showcase its lifted fruit and lively structure; excellent with modestly bold fare such as lamb shank, charcuterie or soft cheeses.
aroma: red berries with subtle mineral spice
palate: vivid fruit framed by fine tannins
foodPairings: lamb shank with lentils and peppers

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Champigny Terres Rouges (St-Cyr-En-Bourg)
description: An elegantly perfumed Saumur‑Champigny from Arnaud Lambert, this 2022 Terres Rouges offers a graceful ruby hue, vibrant red and black fruit aromas and a gentle mineral lift over supple, refined tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 15 °C, pairing beautifully with grilled meats or terrines, enjoying youthfully over the next 4–6 years.
aroma: red and black fruit with a mineral lift
palate: supple refined tannins and vibrant fruit
foodPairings: lamb shank with lentils and peppers
ham off the bone with sweet mustard

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Rouge Tue-Loup (Breze)
description: A finely chiselled Saumur Rouge crafted from 100 percent Cabernet Franc, Clos Tue‑Loup 2022 emanates from a sandy limon‑calcaire terroir near Brézé, its voice sculpted through twelve months of aging in both barrels and concrete egg, imparting precision and supple fruit in elegant harmony (found).
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 14–16 °C, ideally alongside dishes that complement its refined freshness—veal with raspberry‑vinegar sauce or game with tangy reductions (found).
aroma: red berries with sly violet lift
palate: sleek Cabernet Franc purity

name: Domaine Arnaud Lambert Saumur Rouge Tue-Loup(breze)
description: A finely chiselled Saumur Rouge crafted from 100 percent Cabernet Franc, Clos Tue‑Loup 2022 emanates from a sandy limon‑calcaire terroir near Brézé, its voice sculpted through twelve months of aging in both barrels and concrete egg, imparting precision and supple fruit in elegant harmony (found).

aroma: red berries with sly violet lift
palate: sleek Cabernet Franc purity

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere et Fils Bourgogne Aligote
description: Pale gold in the glass with a pale yellow to slightly golden robe this elegant Bourgogne Aligoté from Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils offers a refined array of fresh white‑fleshed fruit and delicate lemony brightness. The palate is remarkably fresh and lively with a subtle saline undercurrent and bright fruit‑driven acidity that carries through to a pleasingly long, crisp finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 9 to 10 °C and enjoy in its youth with light seafood, goat cheese or as a sophisticated aperitif.

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere et Fils Chorey les Beaune
description: A graceful Pinot Noir from Chorey‑lès‑Beaune that unfurls with vibrant ruby hues and a fragrant interplay of Morello cherry and raspberry overlaid by subtle woodland hints, its supple pulse grounded in gentle tannins and refined structure.

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Beaune 1er Cru en Genet
description: This 2020 Beaune Premier Cru “En Genêt” from Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils unfolds with a bright ruby robe and an inviting bouquet of redcurrant, cherry, blackberry and blackcurrant layered with subtle underbrush notes as it matures. aroma: red‑ and black‑fruit bouquet with undergrowth
palate: silky texture, roundness and elegance expressing terroir

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A gracefully vibrant Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Domaine Arnoux Père et Fils 2020 offers a seductive bouquet of cherry and raspberry softened by wild berry nuances. The palate is generous and crunchy with silky tannins and velvety textures inviting early enjoyment yet promising gentle evolution.

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Corton Rognet Grand Cru

name: Domaine Arnoux Pere & Fils Savigny les Beaune
description: A mid‑weight Burgundy of refined pedigree, this 2022 Savigny‑lès‑Beaune from Domaine Arnoux Père & Fils unfurls with a deep ruby hue and a compelling bouquet of small red and black fruits framed by a whisper of spice. The palate shows discreet tannins and graceful volume that carries the vivid fruit with harmony and finesse.

description: A harmonious Bourgogne Rouge that reveals the tempered elegance of Volnay and Pommard fruit, presenting red-cherry brightness suffused with a gentle earthiness that feels both refined and welcoming, finishing with a poised clarity that belies its regional level.

name: Domaine B & T Glantenay Bourgogne Coted D'or
description: This supple Bourgogne Côte d’Or 2022 by Domaine Bernard & Thierry Glantenay delivers a refined expression of Volnay’s modest elevation and Burgundian pedigree, offering pure, medium-bodied fruit of cherry, raspberry and plum underpinned by a delicate licorice nuance.

name: Domaine B & T Glantenay Pommard 1er Cru les Rugiens

name: Domaine B & T Glantenay Puligny Montrachet 1er Cru les Folatieres

description: A noble Volnay Premier Cru born of Bernard and Thierry Glantenay’s Clos des Chênes delights with layers of ripe black cherry, violet petal and subtle spice intertwining with gentle smokiness in an elegant, structured frame. name: Domaine B & T Glantenay Volnay 1er Cru Clos des Chenes

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Meursault 1er Cru Perrieres
description: From the fabled Côte de Beaune estate of Domaine des Comtes Lafon this 2023 Meursault 1er Cru Perrières offers crystalline clarity of fruit married to a striking mineral sinew. Framed by pear, citrus zest and white florals it unfolds with salinity and a hint of praline, unfolding into a lithe and dynamic expression of its limestone‑rich terroir. The texture is satiny yet incisive with a persistent, lightly spiced finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 52 °F in a tulip wineglass, allow brief air time to reveal its layered aromas, pair with butter‑poached lobster or seared scallops for a match of finesse and minerality.
palate: saline, satiny, mineral‑driven

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Meursault
description: The 2023 Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault unfurls with a refined harmony of citrus‑kissed orchard fruit and hazelnut nuances, framed by a sleek mineral undercurrent this is an elegant white burgundy with a poised texture and saline tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine stemware to appreciate its silk‑textured mid‑palate; pair with delicate seafood or creamy poultry to echo its balance.
palate: silky mineral core with orchard fruit

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Meursault
description: The 2023 Domaine des Comtes Lafon Meursault unfurls with a refined harmony of citrus‑kissed orchard fruit and hazelnut nuances, framed by a sleek mineral undercurrent this is an elegant white burgundy with a poised texture and saline tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine stemware to appreciate its silk‑textured mid‑palate; pair with delicate seafood or creamy poultry to echo its balance.

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Meursault Clos de la Barre
description: A refined Meursault from the prestigious Clos de la Barre monopole the 2023 vintage displays layered pear and sweet citrus aromas mingled with white florals and toasted almond nuance, all framed by a mineral undertow and gentle smoke. On the palate it unfurls with satiny texture and structural depth its lush fruit enlivened by luminous acidity promising both early appeal and graceful evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass to highlight the wine’s floral and mineral facets. Ideal with delicate dishes such as sole meunière or a creamy poultry preparation.
aroma: pear and citrus Blossom, white flowers, toasted almond with mineral depth
palate: satiny-textured, layered, vibrant acidity
finish: linger of citrus and mineral persistence

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Meursault Desiree
description: An elegant Meursault from the venerable Domaine des Comtes Lafon, the 2023 “Desirée” blossoms with orchard‑fruit richness: honeyed melon and ripe apple bloom with tender citrus blossom and acacia undertones. The texture is sumptuous and layered yet balanced by a lithe mineral verve that hints at Meursault’s chalky soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass, it harmonizes gorgeously with subtly buttered shellfish or delicate poultry in cream, and will reward cellaring over the next decade.
palate: layered, satiny, fleshy
foodPairings: roasted chicken in herb cream sauce

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Puligny Montrachet
description: An ethereal village‐level Chardonnay from the celebrated Domaine des Comtes Lafon offering crystalline pale lemon hues, a bouquet of delicate white blossoms and mown hay underpinned by chalky soil signature and fine framed elegance
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 11–13 °C where its graceful structure complements seafood or subtly creamy poultry preparations
palate: elegant, chalk‑driven, fine fruit

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Volnay 1er Cru Champans
description: This Volnay 1er Cru Les Champans 2023 from Domaine des Comtes Lafon unfolds with perfumed red cherry and raspberry framed by violet and rose petal aromas the texture is silky and the fruit precise with an elegant lift
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C, pairing beautifully with roast poultry, veal with mushrooms or a delicate lamb dish
palate: silky, precise red fruit

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Volnay 1er Cru Clos des Chenes
description: From one of the Côte de Beaune’s most hallowed texts of terroir this Volnay Premier Cru Clos des Chênes 2023 by Domaine des Comtes Lafon unfolds with radiant depth and floral refinement. Silky layers of black cherry and plum intertwine with violet and a whisper of spice, all carried on an elegant structure that promises both immediacy and longevity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C, decant when young to reveal its scented charm; beautifully suited to roast pigeon or lamb with herb crust.
aroma: black cherry, plum, violet, subtle spice
palate: silky texture, refined tannins, balanced, elegant

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Volnay 1er Cru Santenots du Milieu
description: A compelling Volnay premier‑cru from Domaine des Comtes Lafon it reveals ripe blackberries, subtle forest smoke and spiced underbrush with an admirable textural concentration that speaks of depth without heaviness
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in a tulip glass to unwind its layers pair with gamebirds or filet of beef to complement its noble structure
palate: textural and layered with spiced dark fruit

name: Domaine des Comte Lafon Volnay
description: A graceful Burgundian pinot noir that delicately balances youthful charm and subtle complexity, this 2023 Domaine des Comtes Lafon Volnay is perfumed with red cherry, raspberry and violet, layered with soft spice, and framed by a velvety texture. It offers early allure with enough structure to reward gentle cellaring. Sommelier Notes: Serve with slight aeration to soften its youthful vivacity, pairing beautifully with poultry or refined mushroom dishes.
sommelierNotes: Best enjoyed with slight aeration at cellar temperature, it complements roasted poultry or veal with mushrooms.
palate: supple red fruit, velvety texture
drinkWindow: Drink young and through medium term

name: Domaine des Corbillieres Touraine Sauvignon Blanc
description: This Touraine Sauvignon Blanc from Domaine des Corbillières reveals crystalline notes of white peach and citrus blossom, traced with a stony Sologne minerality that lends both grace and tension. The palate is poised and energetic, delivering a bright core of melon and orchard fruit framed by clean, refined freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at around 10 °C to awaken its zesty clarity. A deft companion to shellfish, goat cheese or summer herb salads.
aroma: white peach and citrus blossom with flinty minerality
palate: bright melon and orchard fruit with refined freshness

name: Domaine des Epeneaux Auxey Duresses 1ER Cru Rouge
description: This 2018 Auxey‑Duresses Premier Cru Rouge from Domaine des Épeneaux (Comte Armand) is elegantly perfumed with fresh red and black cherry and violet pastille nuances, framed by cool earth undertones and a graceful mid‑weight structure of poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14 °C in a stemmed glass: it will complement herb‑accented poultry or pork, while its lithe tannins and red‑berry clarity also suit charcuterie and soft cheese.
aroma: red and black cherry with violet and forest floor
palate: mid‑weight, elegant, mineral‑tinged

name: Domaine des Epeneaux Auxey Duresses 1ERE Cru Rouge
description: A wine of refined Burgundy pedigree, the 2020 Domaine des Epeneaux Auxey‑Duresses Premier Cru Rouge presents an elegant juxtaposition of vibrant red‑berry lift and savoury earth nuances, held together by polished structure and a whisper of old‑world spice. The wine reveals finesse in a medium‑weight frame delivering delicate intensity, insinuating both immediate charm and longer term poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cool, at around 16 °C, after brief aeration to allow the aromatic complexity to unfold; pairs beautifully with classic regional fare or simply toasted country ham.
palate: medium‑weight, fresh with fine tannins

name: Domaine des Epeneaux Auxey Duresses Rouge
description: From the storied cellars of Domaine des Épeneaux, this 2019 Auxey‑Duresses Rouge unfolds with an aristocratic clarity of red and black fruit over a subtly chalky plume, refined tannins offering both velvet and sinew in equal measure. It is precise and elemental, a wine of poise rather than flamboyance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled and coax open through slow breathing: perfect with tender veal loin or a classic roast chicken in herbs.
aroma: red and black fruit with chalky undergrowth
palate: refined tannins balanced with vibrant fruit
finish: elegant, persistent finish with mineral lift

appellation: Pommard Premier Cru Clos des Epenaux
description: An elegant expression of Pommard’s noble terroir, this 2019 Clos des Epenaux Premier Cru from Domaine du Comte Armand offers fine red berry and plum depth with whispers of violet, spice and leather, framed by supple yet assured tannins and a poised structure that promises graceful development.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool, around 16 °C, allowing its poised fruit and spice to shine alongside roasted game birds or wild mushroom fricassée.
palate: elegant tannins, spice, plum core

description: This solidly structured Volnay Premier Cru “Les Frémiets” from Domaine des Epeneaux 2020 offers elegant red berry and earth tones underscored by subtle anise and tobacco, framed in refined oak integration and fine grip.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14 °C in wider glasses to reveal red fruit clarity and minerality; pairs splendidly with roasted poultry or game in rich sauces.
palate: medium‑bodied, fresh red fruit, saline, white pepper

name: Domaine des Epeneaux Volnay 1ER Cru les Fremiets
description: From the legendary Domaine Comte Armand, also known as Domaine des Epeneaux, this Volnay 1er Cru Les Frémiets 2021 unfolds with refined aromas of ripe raspberry, gentle florals and a whisper of smoke and spice. The palate offers an elegant structure and velvety texture lifted by poised freshness and lingering length.
sommelierNotes: Serve this Pinot Noir at 14–16 °C to highlight its silky texture and poised acidity, and expect graceful complexity to evolve over the next decade.
aroma: ripe raspberry with floral and smoky spice
palate: elegant, refined, with velvety texture and balanced freshness
