name: Domaine des Geslets Bourgueil les Geslets
description: An elegant expression of classic Bourgueil offering bright raspberry and blackberry over gentle spice, carried by refined cabernet franc clarity, finishing with a subtle mineral grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled between 12 and 14°C, and pair with charcuterie, roasted poultry or a soft goat’s cheese to complement the wine’s freshness.
palate: fresh fruit with gentle mineral lift

name: Domaine des Geslets Saint Nicolas de Bourgueil la Contrie
description: A fine rendition of Cabernet Franc from Saint‑Nicolas‑de‑Bourgueil this La Contrie 2020 reveals a luminous ruby hue with violet glints and a vivid translation of gravel‑inflected terroir its character unfolds in a chorus of red berries vibrant and succulent with supple freshness and refined textural grace
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C to accentuate its fruit‑driven clarity and match with subtly flavored fare
aroma: open red fruits with violet nuances
palate: round, supple and fruity with fine tannins

name: Domaine des Moirots Givry Rouge
description: An elegant Bourgogne rouge from Givry by Domaine des Moirots offering delicate floral perfume alongside ripe dark fruits and spice, framed by a refined structure that balances freshness and supple tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool, ideally between 12 and 14 °C. Pair with game birds, veal in sauce, or refined poultry dishes.
aroma: peony and black fruit with subtle spice
palate: fresh and fruity with fine tight tannins

name: Domaine Dezat / Cellier des Marnes Sancerre Blanc
description: A finely balanced Sancerre blanc from Domaine Arnaud et Stéphanie Dezat under the Cellier des Marnes label, the 2025 expresses luminous orchard fruit enlivened by Loire’s signature minerality with understated elegance and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve refreshed in slender white glassware at 10–12 °C alongside delicate seafood or chèvre for best harmony.
aroma: pear blossom and green apple with flinty lift
palate: crisp citrus core and chalky minerality

name: Chambolle Musigny
description: This 2013 Chambolle‑Musigny from Domaine Digioia‑Royer reveals an inviting floral perfume of red cherry and subtle earth tones, enriched by a silk‑textured mid‑palate. Its elegance and succulent fruit are carried with grace rather than power.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 16 °C to temper the silk‑like texture, enjoy with mushroom‑accented poultry or fine pork dishes.
aroma: floral red cherry with earthy nuance
palate: silky cherry‑driven with refined texture
foodPairings: roasted duck breast with wild mushrooms

name: Chambolle Musigny Vieilles Vignes les Fremieres
description: An alluring offering from Domaine Digioia‑Royer the 2013 Chambolle‑Musigny Vieilles Vignes Les Fremières summons deep red cherry and cranberry with a hint of spice and limestone undercurrent, its texture concentrated yet refined and its minerality lending an elegant framework.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature around 17 °C and pair with gently roasted red meats or game to complement its density and subtle spice.
aroma: ripe red cherry, cranberry, faint Sichuan pepper
palate: medium‑bodied concentration, grainy texture, mineral spine

name: Domaine Dominique & Janine Crochet Sancerre le Grand Chemarin
description: A crystalline expression of Sancerre from the revered Crochet family this 2022 Le Grand Chemarin captivates with its taut precision and mineral clarity, its limestone‐driven purity offering whispers of citrus blossom and chalky tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in tulip‑shaped glasses, ideal with refined seafood or a goat cheese platter.
palate: taut, precise, mineral‑driven

name: Domaine du Clos Salomon Givry 1er Cru Clos Salomon
description: A lithe expression of Givry’s Côte Chalonnaise elegance this 2020 Clos Salomon delivers luminous cherry and underbrush notes with a hint of spice, framed by refined structure and noble poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled around 60–62 °F in a tall tulip glass to showcase its bright fruit and graceful clarity: pairs beautifully with roast duck or mushroom‑dusted game.
aroma: bright red cherry and woodland spice
palate: silky texture with elegant structure and purity of fruit

name: Domaine E & J Durand Cornas Confidence
description: The 2019 Confidence from Domaine Éric & Joël Durand is a noble Cornas, offering a concentrated bouquet of mulled plum and raspberry framed with clove and black pepper. It is broad‑shouldered and powerful on the palate with ripe, layered dark fruit and polished tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at cellar‑cool temperatures alongside richly spiced lamb or roasted game to complement its muscle and depth.
palate: dense dark fruit, polished tannins

name: Domaine E & J Durand Cornas Confidence
description: The 2020 Confidence from Domaine Éric & Joël Durand is a noble Cornas, offering a concentrated bouquet of mulled plum and raspberry framed with clove and black pepper. It is broad‑shouldered and powerful on the palate with ripe, layered dark fruit and polished tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly decanted at cellar‑cool temperatures alongside richly spiced lamb or roasted game to complement its muscle and depth.
palate: dense dark fruit, polished tannins

name: Domaine E & J Durand Cornas Empreintes
description: The 2018 Cornas Empreintes by Domaine Eric & Joël Durand is a powerful rendition of Northern Rhône Syrah, crafted with compelling precision and depth. It reveals a richly perfumed nose of blackberry and violet threaded with graphite tension, leading to a palate of finely structured, dense dark fruit and polished tannins that linger with poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature after decanting to soften the structure: this generous yet refined Cornas pairs beautifully with richly flavored red meats or game dishes.
palate: Dense dark fruit with polished tannins

name: Domaine E & J Durand Cornas Empreintes
description: The 2020 Cornas Empreintes by Domaine Eric & Joël Durand is a powerful rendition of Northern Rhône Syrah, crafted with compelling precision and depth. It reveals a richly perfumed nose of blackberry and violet threaded with graphite tension, leading to a palate of finely structured, dense dark fruit and polished tannins that linger with poise.

palate: Dense dark fruit with polished tannins

name: Domaine E & J Durand Cornas Premices
description: This 2020 Cornas “Prémices” by Domaine Éric et Joël Durand delivers an elegant yet powerful expression of Northern Rhône Syrah, its dark fruit richness framed by mineral and floral accents that speak of its granitic soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in medium-bowled glasses to best appreciate the wine’s freshness and silken tannins, perfect with roast lamb or truffle‑accented dishes.
palate: juicy black raspberry and bitter cherry with fine balanced tannins

name: Domaine Emmanuel Darnaud Crozes Hermitage Mise en Bouche
description: A captivating youthful Syrah from the northern Rhône, this Crozes‑Hermitage ’Mise en Bouche’ 2023 offers immediate appeal in a refined guise. It presents a polished texture, ripe dark‑berry fruit framed by gently spiced warmth, and enchanting freshness that tempts cellaring yet invites early enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 14°C and decant if possible to coax forward its scented cherry and eucalyptus nuance; pairing with roasted game birds or herbed pork will highlight its supple red‑fruit charm.
palate: silky with dark‑berry fruit and gentle spice

name: Domaine Emmanuel Darnaud Saint Joseph la Dardouille
description: This offers the classic Darnaud signature of vibrant Syrah from sun‑baked granitic Saint‑Joseph, with expressive black cherry and violet aromas weaving through gently savory earth and graphite undertones, finishing with polished structure and poised minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve around 16 °C in a tall Bordeaux glass after gentle decanting; offers compelling harmony with grilled lamb or aged hard cheeses.
palate: minerally, structured, fresh acidity

name: Domaine Eric Morgat Savennieres Fides
description: A brilliantly poised Savennières from Domaine Eric Morgat the 2021 Fidès reveals crystalline purity and tensile energy. It unfolds with ripe orchard fruit edged by schistous minerality and lifted by spice‑tinged oak the texture is silken yet taut delivering both power and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 10–12 °C in a gently opened white glass to frame its tension and minerality. Ideal for cellaring through the 2030s or decant briefly if enjoyed young.
aroma: ripe apple nectarine with spice and flint energy

name: Domaine Gauby Cotes du Roussillon Muntada
appellation: IGP Côtes Catalanes (formerly Côtes du Roussillon Villages)
description: The 2019 Domaine Gauby Muntada reveals a richly textured expression from old vines rooted in marly‑limestone soils in the Roussillon, offering layered aromas of blackberries, garrigue and subtle floral incense, woven together with anise and crushed pepper for a deeply resonant bouquet derived from the finest casks.

name: Domaine Gauby Vieilles Vignes Rouge
description: A glass of Domaine Gauby Vieilles Vignes Rouge 2020 reveals a tapestry of dense dark berries and garrigue herbs woven through with spice and a mineral spine, its texture both pulpy and structured as the old vines impart depth and precision derived from Roussillon’s complex schist and limestone soils ([vigneronsdexception.com](https://www.vigneronsdexception.com/fr/domaine-gauby/6259-domaine-gauby-vieilles-vignes-rouge-2020.html?utm_source=openai)).

palate: velvety yet structured, with spice and depth

description: The 2016 Domaine Georges Noellat Meursault 1er Cru “Les Cras” emerges from a rare northerly parcel bordering Caillerets and overlooking Volnay Santenots, presenting a luminous golden hue and a refined aromatic veil of white orchard fruit, citrus and delicate florals, underpinned by a whisper of toasted almond and stone. sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a generous white Burgundy glass after aerating for 15 minutes to reveal its depth and allow its subtle saline nuance to emerge
palate: voluminous yet gracefully balanced with creamy texture
finish: salty, gently bitter recast of citrus rind

name: Domaine Guy Bocard Meursault 1er Cru les Charmes
description: This Meursault 1er Cru “Les Charmes” 2023 from Domaine Guy Bocard is finely poised and luminous, offering refined floral whispers and a gentle almond‑tinged bitterness within an elegant, airy frame. Its delicate texture and extended, bright finish signal both poise and potential.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12‑14 °C in a fine white Burgundy glass for full aromatic lift. Pairs beautifully with shellfish in buttery or creamy sauces and subtly roast poultry.
palate: airy, refined, gently textured

name: Domaine Guy Bocard Meursault 1er Cru les Genevrieres
description: This 2019 Meursault Premier Cru “Les Genevrières” from Domaine Guy Bocard unveils an expressive and mineral profile, combining ripe orchard fruit and subtle herbal inflections with compelling power and enduring structure. The wine is crafted with careful élevage, revealing both richness and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–13 °C, ideally opened an hour before tasting or allowed to rest in the glass to reveal its layered elegance; pairs exquisitely with lobster or delicate seafood, and will reward patient cellaring.
aroma: ripe orchard fruit with herbal nuance
palate: mineral and powerful yet poised
drinkWindow: will evolve beautifully over the next decade+

name: Domaine Guy Bocard Meursault les Narvaux
description: The 2022 Domaine Guy Bocard Meursault “Les Narvaux” presents a refined expression of the Meursault terroir: fresh citrus and chalky minerality unfold with a gentle richness supported by elegant oak nuance and a firm backbone of tension. It speaks with clarity and precision revealing both the steely structure of Narvaux and the warmth of its vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 11 °C in fine white Burgundy stems; superb with pan‑seared scallops in butter or a herb‑infused roast chicken.

palate: rich yet poised with subtle oak and lively tension

description: This 2023 Meursault Limozin from Domaine Guy Bocard unfolds with sunlit generosity its yellow orchard fruit and a whisper of spice layered over enticing creaminess, gently supported by saline restraint and radiant clarity. Its structure is polished, the texture generous yet refined in true Meursault tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve around 12 °C in fine white Burgundy glasses. Pair with delicate seafood in butter sauce or subtly herb‑accented white meats.
aroma: yellow orchard fruit with light spice
palate: generous, creamy texture balanced by saline clarity

name: Domaine Guy Bocard Meursault Vieilles Vignes
description: Refined and generous Meursault whose old‑vine complexity reveals a pale golden hue and a gently layered profile of white‑fleshed fruit and floral grace suffused with toasted nuance, this wine is both poised and richly expressive.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature, ideally with delicate fish dishes or subtly seasoned poultry to accent its graceful texture.
aroma: white‑fleshed fruit, delicate flowers, gentle toast
palate: round yet vibrant acidity balanced by soft oak
foodPairings: sole meunière with brown butter and toasted almonds

description: The 2022 Hubert Lamy Chassagne‑Montrachet 1er Cru Les Chaumées presents an elegant tension of minerality and poise, blending pear, citrus oil and toasted hazelnut nuances with a cool, textural depth and refined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to highlight its crystalline clarity with fine white meats or subtly spiced shellfish, and allow a few years of cellar time to reveal its polished finesse.
palate: taut, textural, mineral-driven
foodPairings: roasted halibut with lemon and herbs
poached chicken in light cream sauce

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Criots Batard Montrachet Grand Cru Haute Densite
description: An exceptionally refined Grand Cru from Domaine Hubert Lamy the 2023 Criots‑Bâtard‑Montrachet Haute Densité offers a luminous core of pear blossom and orange peel beneath subtle whispers of beeswax and freshly baked bread, delivering a poised expression of power and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature around 12 °C to highlight its mineral clarity and pair with delicacies such as grilled lobster or poultry in a light cream sauce.
palate: elegantly muscular, layered texture, chalky dry extract

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Criots Batard Montrachet Hautes Densite
description: The 2022 Domaine Hubert Lamy Criots‑Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru “Haute Densité” is a jewel from Burgundy’s Côte de Beaune, drawn from one minuscule 0.05‑hectare parcel where vines planted in 1975 thrive at an extraordinary 24 000 per hectare. This rare Chardonnay unfolds with sweet orchard fruit, citrus blossom and oyster‑shell minerality, supported by satiny layers and vibrant energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large tulip glass around 10–12 °C; pairs beautifully with lobster, scallops or rich shellfish sauces.
palate: satiny, layered and minerally

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin 1er Cru Clos de la Chateniere
appellation: Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru Clos de la Chatenière
description: A compelling expression of Saint‑Aubin’s limestone‑kissed identity this 2022 Clos de la Chatenière reveals orchard‑bright citrus and honeyed toast interwoven with crystalline mineral energy and refined texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cool to temper its vibrant acidity, delightful with shellfish in butter sauces or subtly spiced white meats.
palate: crystalline mineralité with ripe orchard fruit

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin 1er Cru Derriere chez Edouard Blanc Haute Densite
appellation: Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru “Derrière Chez Édouard” Haute Densité
description: A brilliantly mineral‑inflected Saint‑Aubin that marries crystalline structure with pure orchard fruit in impeccable poise. Elegant yet powerful, it unfolds with depth and tension born of dense planting and revered Burgundian terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at approximately 11 °C in fine white Burgundy glasses: awaits aeration and reward, pairing beautifully with shellfish or creamy cheeses.
palate: crystalline fruit, saline tension, refined texture

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin 1er Cru en Remilly
description: A refined and crystalline Chardonnay from Saint‑Aubin’s distinguished En Remilly premier‑cru, this 2023 Hubert Lamy reveals a luminous straw hue underpinned by tensile, mineral‑inflected precision. The glass opens to a fragrant interplay of orchard fruit and white florals sustained by racy acidity and a saline‑tinged, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine stemware to accent its freshness: ideal with simply grilled sea bass or a delicate risotto with herb butter.
palate: textural and open‑knit with crisp orchard fruit and minerality

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin 1er Cru Frionnes
description: The 2022 Hubert Lamy Les Frionnes pours pale straw, refined yet incisive, with a crystalline core of orchard and citrus fruit held in stony tension. The wine captures the steep marly‑limestone terroir with subtle mineral lift and sculpted structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–12 °C in fine white glassware, pairing superbly with pristine shellfish or delicate poultry in beurre blanc.
aroma: nashi pear, white flowers, citrus, oyster shell
palate: chiselled orchard fruit, taut and saline

appellation: Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru ‘Les Murgers des Dents de Chien’
description: A luminous portrait of Côte de Beaune artistry it enchants with lemon confit, Anjou pear and white flowers unfolding gracefully in the glass, offering depth and crystalline minerality drawn from its stony calcaire soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve around 11–12 °C in fine white Burgundy glassware; pairs harmoniously with rich shellfish dishes or beurre noisette lobster, and will gain complexity over a decade or more.
aroma: lemon confit, Anjou pear, white flowers
palate: medium‑to‑full body, bright acidity, chalky extract

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin la Princee
description: A lithe and mineral‑driven Saint‑Aubin that exudes pear and white floral perfume with the gentle warmth of freshly baked brioche, framed by energetic citrus and tensile limestone clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to highlight its racy freshness: divine with simply grilled sea bass or a salade de chèvre chaud.
palate: bright, chalky, layered

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Saint Aubin Rouge 1er Cru Derriere chez Edouard Vieilles Vignes
appellation: Saint‑Aubin Premier Cru Derrière chez Edouard
description: This Saint‑Aubin Premier Cru Derrière chez Edouard 2023 from Domaine Hubert Lamy offers elegantly structured Pinot Noir with deep red‑berry aromas intertwined with delicate floral and mineral notes, unfolding in a velvety, sapid mouthfeel of polished tannins and fine energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in burgundy glasses around 16 °C, ideally with roasted game birds or mushroom‑crusted poultry to complement its sapidity and minerality.
palate: velvety sapidity, fine tannins
foodPairings: filet de pigeon with reduced jus

name: Domaine Humbert Freres Bourgogne Cote D'or
description: This Bourgogne Côte d’Or from Domaine Humbert Frères emerges with refined poise a regional Pinot Noir of elegant structure yet delightful generosity, bearing a pure expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin terroir, framed by subtle minerality and delicate red‑berry nuance. It unfolds in the glass with an understated moreish charm that speaks of authenticity rather than overt extraction.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 15 °C, to reveal its silky fruit and lift; pairs beautifully with roasted game birds or mushroom‑rich dishes.
palate: silky fruit, balanced mineral spine

name: Domaine Humbert Freres Charmes Chambertin Grand Cru
description: A refined expression of Charmes‑Chambertin from Humbert Frères, unveiling fresh black fruit and violet-toned florality layered with gentle toast and a hint of smoked licorice. The palate reveals poised tannins and vivid freshness, culminating in sustained, elegant persistence.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in a large Burgundy glass to reveal its floral and smoky nuance. Excellent with roast duck or truffle‑infused dishes.
aroma: fresh black fruit, violet, toasted nuance
palate: fresh, tannic, violet, smoke

name: Domaine Humbert Freres Charms Chambertin Grand Cru
description: This 2022 Domaine Humbert Frères Charmes‑Chambertin Grand Cru is at once sumptuous and refined, its velvet texture embracing layers of bright Morello cherry, black fruit and a perfume of peony and rose petals, while underpinned by whispers of cocoa, fresh mocha and noble forest floor. The craftsmanship of the Humbert brothers yields a wine of profound depth and satin‑smooth tannins that reveal generous fruit yet retain poised tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C after decanting for an hour, to best unveil its aromatic florality and luxuriant texture, and allow it to show its long‑term aging potential from 2030 onward.
palate: velvety density with fine, enveloping tannins
finish: impressively long with forest‑floor and spice whispers
foodPairings: aged Comté or mild hard cheeses

name: Domaine Humbert Freres Fixin Vieilles Vignes
description: A refined and graceful village‐level Pinot Noir from old vines in Fixin, this 2021 Vieilles Vignes from Domaine Humbert Frères brings harmonious depth and poise. The nose exudes poised red and dark fruits interwoven with subtle spice and earthy nuance. The palate glides with supple texture, framed by gentle tannins and a smoky underpinning for a polished expression of terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in rounded tulip glasses to reveal its layered aromas. Pair with roast duck breast, mushroom ragout or a selection of soft surface‐ripened cheeses.
aroma: poised red and dark fruits with subtle spice and earthy nuance
palate: supple texture with gentle tannins and smoky depth

description: A richly textured Pinot Noir from one of Gevrey‑Chambertin’s most esteemed 1er Cru climats, this 2023 from Domaine Humbert Frères displays refined dark‑fruit depth balanced with a cool, mineral spine.

description: This Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru “Petite Chapelle” 2022 from Domaine Humbert Frères offers an alluring blend of noble Pinot Noir charm and sinewy structure, born of clay‑limestone soils and mature mid‑slope vines. The wine unfurls in the glass with concentrated black fruit enveloped in floral nuance and subtle earth that suggests both generosity and discipline.

The wine is structured yet elegant its fine-grained tannins providing poise and clarity.

name: Domaine J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Prestige
description: A silky, sun‑warmed Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape built on lush Grenache‑driven fruit with a firm undertow of Mourvèdre structure, the 2018 “Prestige” offers a refined composition of black raspberry and cherry liqueur over hints of lavender and spice, wrapped in poised sophistication. The balance is radiant, the texture seamless and the expression elegantly resonant.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to illuminate its floral lift; pair with herb‑crusted lamb, Provençal stew or aged cheeses to echo its savory spice and dark fruit core.
aroma: black raspberry, cherry liqueur, lavender pastille
palate: juicy red and blue fruit, floral spice, velvety texture
finish: long and spicy with seamless tannins

name: Domaine Jacques Parent Corton Grand Cru Blanc
description: A lithe yet compelling white Burgundy of silk and mineral poise, this 2018 Domaine Jacques Parent Corton Grand Cru Blanc unfurls pear and yellow stone‑fruit underpinned by grilled almond and a whisper of Provençal minerality, its texture rich and refined, its tension precise and finessed.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tall white tulip glasses to emphasize its graceful minerality, ideal with shellfish in buttered cream or subtly fatty foie gras.
palate: rich minerality with elegant tension

name: Domaine Jacques Parent Corton Grand Cru les Renardes
description: A noble Grand Cru Pinot Noir of measured power and refined structure, this 2020 Domaine Jacques Parent Corton "Les Renardes" unfolds with a serenely serious bouquet of black raspberry and sauvage earth warmed by subtle floral whispers, the palate resonant with sleek, muscular fruit and a beguiling inner‑mouth perfume.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature alongside richly roasted game or truffle‑rich dishes to accentuate its noble silk and depth.
aroma: black raspberry, sauvage earth, delicate florals
palate: sleek muscular fruit, inner‑mouth perfume

name: Domaine Jacques Parent Monthelie Rouge
description: A refined village‑level Pinot Noir from the heart of Monthelie in the Côte de Beaune. This 2019 Domaine Jacques Parent Monthelie Rouge reveals elegant red and black cherry with subtle violet florality framed by gentle earthy nuances. Its texture is poised between velvety and uplifted, offering poised structure and graceful presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 14 °C in clear Burgundian glasses. Pair with buttery poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes to echo its fruit and subtle earth tones.
aroma: red and black cherry with violet florality
palate: elegant, velvety with fine tannins

name: Domaine Jacques Parent Pommard 1ER Cru Charmots
description: This 2020 Pommard Premier Cru “Les Charmots” from Domaine Parent exudes noble Burgundy character, with a core of vibrant red fruit layered with earthy spice and delicate floral nuance. It offers refined structure and polish that belie its textural power, drawing the taster into a lingering interplay of finesse and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to reveal its nuanced red-berry aromas, pairing beautifully with roast duck or aged Comté.
palate: textured, earthy, subtle floral lift

name: Domaine Jacques Parent Pommard 1ER Cru Rugiens
description: This 2020 Pommard 1er Cru Les Rugiens from Domaine Parent offers a sumptuous expression of ripe black cherry and boysenberry enveloped by whispers of black pepper and clove, all lifted with a subtle floral undercurrent rooted in its distinguished terroir, presented with a gracious yet powerful frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperature around 16 °C, allow gentle aeration or a brief decant to coax open its layered aromas; pairs admirably with rich game dishes or rustic mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe black cherry and boysenberry with black pepper and clove
palate: medium-bodied, succulent entry, fleshy and expressive
finish: long and refined though seeking a touch more precision

name: Domaine Jean Fery Bouzeron les Corcelles
description: A graceful Bouzeron rendered in pale gold with lifted notes of pear, white flowers and a hint of lemon pith, framed by subtle toasted undertones and a seam of wet stone minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to bring forward its lively clarity, paired superbly with shellfish or soft goat’s cheese.
palate: bright citrus with floral lift

name: Domaine Jean Fery Corton Grand Cru les Chaumes
description: This Domaine Jean Féry & Fils Corton Grand Cru “Les Chaumes” 2020 arrives with noble gravitas showing deep ruby hue layered with rich dark cherry and cassis, violet floral lift, and hints of forest undergrowth giving weight and breadth in regal restraint.

aroma: deep black cherry, violet, earthy forest floor
palate: structured yet silky tannins enveloping dark fruit and spice

name: Domaine Jean Fery Cotes de Nuits Villages Clos Magny
description: In the glass this 2020 Domaine Jean Féry & Fils Côte‑de‑Nuits‑Villages “Clos de Magny” displays a deep ruby hue with a subtle floral perfume that hints at ripe red cherries and woodland nuance. The palate unfolds with firm yet polished structure, offering plush red fruit framed by gentle earthy undertones and fine-grained tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a Burgundy glass, pairing beautifully with roasted game birds or herb‑accented red meats after a short decant to open its bouquet.
palate: structured red fruit with polished tannins

name: Domaine Jean Fery Meursault les Narvaux
description: A crystalline village Meursault from a revered lieu-dit, this 2020 reveals a tonal interplay of pear and citrus zest with subtle hazelnut and almond accents, revealing both energy and elegance in seamless harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 12 °C to 14 °C and pair with delicate seafood or butter‑sautéed fish to echo its citrus lift and textural complexity.
palate: satiny texture with racy acidity and concentrated core

name: Domaine Jean Fery Morey Saint Denis Champ de la Vigne
description: Refined Morey‑Saint‑Denis from Domaine Jean Fery that marries the elegance and finesse of Chambolle‑Musigny with the structured backbone of Gevrey‑Chambertin: deep aromas of cherry and cassis threaded with subtle spice linger on a plush and focused palate, culminating in a noble finish that hints at leather. 100 percent Pinot Noir delivers a wine that is both graceful and grounded in its Côte de Nuits identity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in Burgundy stems: pairs exquisitely with roasted lamb, mushroom‑scented dishes or noble cheeses, allowing the wine’s red and black fruit tones to harmonize with savory richness.
palate: plush, focused structure

name: Domaine Jean Fery Savigny les Beaune en Connardise Blanc
description: The 2020 Domaine Jean Féry Savigny‑lès‑Beaune “Ez Connardises” Blanc offers refined old‑world elegance with softly rounded texture and subtle oak nuance. Hints of white flowers and citrus peel intermingle with a caressing richness that remains lively and poised.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass around 12 °C. Particularly lovely alongside delicate seafood in butter sauce or creamy poultry preparations.
palate: creamy texture with fine freshness

name: Domaine Jean Fery Savigny les Beaune Rouge 1er Cru Vergelesses
description: A lustrous Pinot Noir from Savigny‑lès‑Beaune’s esteemed Vergelesses premier‑cru peers with polished depth of dark berry fruit and a whisper of smoke supported by refined oak spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 14–16 °C in a large Burgundy glass enjoy with rich poultry or game dishes to complement its velvety texture and lingering finish.
palate: supple yet structured fruit with gentle oak

name: Domaine Jean Fery Vosne 1er Cru en Orveauix
description: This 2020 Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru En Orveaux from Domaine Jean Féry exudes graceful refinement with its subtly perfumed red‑cherry and forest‑floor echoes, revealing delicate spice and a fine limestone‑tinged minerality. It unfolds with poised depth and elegant restraint, offering both aromatic allure and a poised structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool around 14 °C with refined dishes such as veal tournedos or roasted pigeon, or let it age gracefully through the mid‑2020s. It rewards gentle decanting and will harmonize with mushroom‑accented preparations.
aroma: red cherry, forest floor, fine spice
palate: silky, poised depth, mineral lift

name: Domaine Jean Fery Vosne Romanee aux Reas
description: This Vosne‑Romanée “Aux Réas” from Domaine Jean Féry & Fils 2019 is a refined expression of Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir radiant with nuanced red and dark berry perfume layered with forest‑floor undertones. The palate offers a silken texture, precise acidity and chalk‑fine tannins bringing depth and elegance to its long mineral‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a tulip wineglass to let the aromas open. Exceptional with roast duck or mushroom‑rich poultry dishes or game birds dusted with winter spice.
aroma: red and dark berries with forest‑floor depth
palate: silken texture, precise acidity, chalk‑fine tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Luc Burguet Bourgogne Rouge le Pince Vin
description: This Bourgogne Rouge ’Les Pince Vin’ 2022 by Domaine Jean‑Luc (et Eric) Burguet offers refined clarity of red‑fruited elegance: vivid cherry and raspberry aromas with delicate floral and spice undertones that unfold with poise. The palate is silky‑textured, ripe yet animated by freshness and fine, integrated tannins in perfect harmony with its Burgundian finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool to slightly below room temperature: perfect with roasted chicken, mushroom‑accented pork or a lightly aged Brie for a seamless reflection of its gentle power and terroir clarity.
aroma: bright red cherry and raspberry with floral spice
palate: silky and balanced with fresh fruit and fine tannins
finish: lingering finesse with subtle earthy spice

name: Domaine Jean-Luc Burguet Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Lavaut Saint Jacques
description: This wine offers an enthralling union of deep garnet hue and layered black‑fruit perfume, where cassis and bramble entwine with graphite accents and a whisper of dried florals, all supported by a mineral spine; the palate unfolds with sumptuous texture, integrated structure and a saline, expansive finish that lingers with poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar temperature to allow the mineral depth and fine tannins to open; pairs beautifully with roasted veal loin, morel‑and‑truffle sauce or an aged Langres cheese.
palate: sumptuous texture, integrated structure
foodPairings: roasted veal loin with morel and truffle sauce
filet of venison in game jus

name: Domaine Jean-Luc Burguet Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru les Champeaux
description: This elegant 2022 Gevrey‑Chambertin “Les Champeaux” from Domaine Alain Burguet delivers a refined expression of Côte de Nuits terroir, where pure red‑berry perfume gently unfolds with fine spice and mineral clarity, framed by supple structure and silken energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool temperature, ideally around 15 °C, and allow to breathe briefly in the glass; pairs beautifully with earthy poultry or pork and nuanced mushroom dishes.
palate: silken energy and fine mineral lift

name: Domaine Jean-Luc Burguet Gevrey Chambertin Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes
description: A refined signature of Gevrey‑Chambertin, this 2022 “Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes” springs from meticulously chosen seventy‑plus‑year‑old vines. It unfolds with layered red cherry and raspberry underpinned by rose petal and subtle spice, gorgeously framed by fresh earth and silken structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature, this velvety Pinot Noir harmonizes with roast game, lightly seared duck or aged Comté for refined balance.
palate: silky raspberry with gentle spice
foodPairings: filet of beef in reduced jus

name: Domaine Jean-Luc Burguet Gevrey Chambertin Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes

description: A poised village‐level Pinot Noir from Gevrey‑Chambertin crafted under the fresh stewardship of Jean‑Luc Burguet, this 2022 Symphonie offers softly seductive dark red berries framed by delicate floral spice notes and subtle French oak, all wrapped in silky tannins and a lingering mineral finish.

aroma: dark red berries with floral spice

appellation: Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru “Les Rouges du Dessus”
description: A graceful showing from a storied Vosne‑Romanée 1er Cru this Dom Jean‑Luc Burguet 2022 “Les Rouges du Dessus” reveals vibrant red and black fruit framed by sanguine earth and a whisper of spice, leading to a refined structure with tensile energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to cellar temperature, pairing elegantly with game birds or roasted veal to echo its noble tension.
palate: silky red and black fruit, fine minerality

name: Domaine Jean-Luc et Eric Burguet Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Lavaut Saint Jacques
description: The 2020 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Lavaut‑Saint‑Jacques from Jean‑Luc & Eric Burguet unfolds with refined dark berry intensity complemented by whispers of violet and forest floor. The texture is silky yet structured with mineral drive and poised tannins that suggest noble longevity.

palate: silky, mineral‑tinged, poised tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Luc et Eric Burguet Gevrey Chambertin Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes
description: From the ancient pinot noir vines of Gevrey‑Chambertin the 2020 Mes Favorites Vieilles Vignes reveals a deep garnet hue with an eloquent blend of bramble fruit and noble spice enveloped in elegant structure and refined power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in large Burgundy-style glasses to appreciate the interplay of vibrant red fruit and subtle earthiness. Excellent with classic Côte de Nuits dishes.
palate: elegant red fruit with fine tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Luc et Eric Burguet Vosne Romanee 1er Cru Rouge du Dessus
appellation: Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru « Les Rouges du Dessus »
description: This wine lingers with elegant red fruit nuances of raspberry and cherry framed by a whisper of rose and spice drawing the taster into a refined Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru signature, its texture supple yet focused with a mineral thread that speaks of its clay‑limestone marls.

palate: supple red fruit with elegant tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Burgaud Beaujolais Lantignie
description: This 2024 Jean‑Marc Burgaud Beaujolais Lantignié shows lifted aromas of crunchy red fruit and violets weaving a floral allure, framed by a fleshy, supple body and fine grainy tannins that gracefully carry a polished, vibrant energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C in slender wine glasses to emphasize its fresh red‑berry brightness, and pair with charcuterie or roasted poultry to complement its purity and tension.
palate: fleshy with fine grainy tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Burgaud Beaujolais Villages Blanc
description: A refined white from Beaujolais‑Villages, this 2024 Jean‑Marc Burgaud expresses the generosity of Chardonnay grown on clay soils at Lantignié with a harmonious blend of rounded fruit and graceful freshness. The charmer’s golden robe conceals a sophisticated balance between generosity and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled; it partners beautifully with delicate shellfish or poultry in creamy sauces and is equally at ease as an aperitif.
palate: rich fruit with vibrant freshness

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Burgaud Morgon la Roche
description: The 2024 Morgon La Roche by Jean‑Marc Burgaud presents a graceful and refined expression of Cru Beaujolais. It recalls delicate rose petal and dark cherry nuances with a poised structure that balances clarity and elegance without excessive depth. The linear profile and fine-grained tannins give it a harmonious poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to highlight its fresh red‑fruit character: excellent with roasted chicken or mild charcuterie.
aroma: perfumed rose petal and dark cherry
palate: balanced, linear, fine‑grained tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Burgaud Morgon Ruyere
description: This Morgon Ruyère 2024 from Dom Jean‑Marc Burgaud unfurls with the poise of old‑vine Gamay on granite soils, offering a gentle weave of red and black fruit and subtle stony nuance that exudes approachable elegance and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14 to 16 °C alongside grilled red meats or creamy soft cheeses, its fine tannins and vibrant fruit lifting rustic fare with grace.
aroma: red and black fruit with damp loam undertones
palate: medium‑bodied with pliant tannins and balanced acidity

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pavelot Bourgogne Rouge
description: An elegant Bourgogne Rouge from the house of Jean‑Marc and Hugues Pavelot offering bright red‑berry charm and understated warmth the essence of Savigny‑lès‑Beaune in a youthful Pinot expression
sommelierNotes: Serve cool to medium cool to enhance its red cherry lift and pair effortlessly with rustic charcuterie or roasted fowl
aroma: fresh red cherry with floral nuance
palate: elegant and supple with fine tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pavelot Bourgogne Rouge
description: An elegant Bourgogne Rouge from the house of Jean‑Marc and Hugues Pavelot offering bright red‑berry charm and understated warmth the essence of Savigny‑lès‑Beaune in a youthful Pinot expression
sommelierNotes: Serve cool to medium cool to enhance its red cherry lift and pair effortlessly with rustic charcuterie or roasted fowl
aroma: fresh red cherry with floral nuance
palate: elegant and supple with fine tannins

name: Domaine Jean-Marc Pavelot Corton Blanc
description: This grand cru Corton Blanc from Domaine Jean‑Marc Pavelot offers an elegantly structured richness, its fruit framed by chalk‑borne minerals. A subtle interplay of citrus blossom and noble oak lends both depth and poise, speaking of Burgundian terroir with refined clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass; pairs well with butter‑poached lobster or creamy poultry preparations.

description: A refined Savigny‑les‑Beaune Premier Cru from a venerable Burgundian domaine this wine offers poised ruby‑red clarity along with an expressive bouquet that balances vibrant red fruit and mineral nuance from its south‑facing marl clay terroir([domainepavelot.com](https://www.domainepavelot.com/fr/nos-vins/categorie/23-premier-cru-serpentieres.html?utm_source=openai)). sommelierNotes: Serve around 12 to 14 °C to frame its clarity and minerality: an ideal companion to shellfish in buttered nage or roast brill with subtle aromatics.
aroma: orchard fruit and delicate floral nuance
palate: mineral‑driven with saline backbone

name: Domaine Joseph Pascal Puligny Montrachet
description: A gracious Puligny‑Montrachet rouge from Domaine (now Joseph) Pascal, the 2023 vintage reveals delicate notes of red cherry, clove, mint and forest floor in a gentle, lingering expression. It is refined and poised, capturing a rare Burgundian village‑level Pinot Noir with elegance and earth‑tinged nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a tulip‑shaped red wine glass; pair with roasted duck, wild mushrooms or earthy soft cheeses to highlight its finesse.
palate: soft, forest floor, baking spice

name: Domaine Jouan Coteaux Bourguignon
description: Presents a lithe expression of Burgundy under the Coteaux Bourguignons AOC, domesticated yet soulful. The nose suggests fresh red berries and a subtle earthen nuance alive with Burgundy’s sinewy elegance. The palate glides with poised red fruit and polished tannins in a light, graceful frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in a stemmed red glass, perfect alongside roasted poultry or autumnal vegetable gratins.
aroma: Fresh red berries with an earthy undertone
palate: Lithe red fruit and polished tannins

name: Domaine Jouan Gevrey Chambertin aux Echezeaux
description: A deeply perfumed Burgundy in Dom Philippe Jouan’s quietly confident style the 2021 Gevrey‑Chambertin “Aux Echézeaux” opens with poised notes of red and black cherry mingled with pomegranate layered over subtle cedar, earth and tobacco undertones. The texture is refined yet grounded the fruit core vibrant and focused drawing one inward toward a long, mineral‑suffused finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large Burgundy glass and decant briefly this will pair elegantly with duck breast roasted mushrooms or aged hard cheese, its tension and earthy purity complementing richly textured dishes.
aroma: red and black cherry, cedar, tobacco
palate: pure fruit core with firm grip and mineral tension

The palate is suppler yet structured, lifted by fine‑grained chalky tannins and a cool mineral thread, delivering a refined, persistent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C, allowing time for the wine to open; pairs beautifully with roast duck or game birds where the wine’s freshness and tannic poise enhance rich, savory meats.
palate: structured yet supple chalky tannins

description: A refined expression of Chablis from the venerable Domaine Grossot, the 2020 vintage offers crystalline clarity and a minerally poise that evokes the calcareous slopes of Fleys, Buffing its profile with citrus brightness and subtle floral whispers. The wine is elegantly structured, delivering restrained power and an energy that unfolds with quiet refinement.

name: Domaine Juillot Mercurey 1er Cru Clos des Barraults
appellation: Mercurey Premier Cru Clos des Barraults
description: An opulent yet refined Premier Cru from Mercurey Clos des Barraults, the 2020 vintage unfolds with ripe raspberry and dark spice layers embraced by gentle oak influence, its character grounded in a whisper of minerality that speaks of the clay‑limestone terroir.

aroma: ripe raspberry, dark spice, subtle oak
palate: rich generous mid‑weight fruit, mineral undercurrent

name: Domaine Juillot Mercurey 1er Cru les Champs Martins
appellation: Mercurey Premier Cru Les Champs Martins
description: A refined white Burgundy from Domaine Michel Juillot this Mercurey Premier Cru Les Champs Martins 2020 unfolds with nuanced floral and mineral complexity enlivened by delicate citrus highlights and an undercurrent of salinity. The texture is graceful yet vibrant offering a harmonious palate framed by gentle oak influence and well‑integrated freshness.

name: Domaine la Bastide Blanche Bandol Rose
description: The 2023 La Bastide Blanche Bandol Rosé presents layered aromatics of red currant, rose petal and blood orange, wrapped in a poised Mediterranean salinity that gives an elegant sense of place. aroma: red currant, rose petal, blood orange
palate: creamy red berry, citrus, spice

description: An expressive and refined Bandol rouge from La Bastide Blanche’s organic and biodynamic estate. The 2021 vintage displays a vivid purple hue, and offers black fruit aromas lifted by licorice and spice, leading into a fresh and concentrated palate framed by elegant tannins and a floral spicy finish.

aroma: black fruits with licorice and spice
palate: fresh, dense, elegant tannins

name: Domaine la Bastide Blanche Rose
description: This Provençal rosé of commanding yet graceful character offers a vivid salmon hue and expressive aromatics of dried apricot, mango and subtle pomelo with a whisper of spice, culminating in a richly textured palate that is both generous and refined.

aroma: dried apricot and mango with pomelo essence
palate: ample, layered and perfumed with savory undernotes

name: Domaine la Berangeraie Cahors Cuvee Mauarin
description: A refined expression of pure Cahors Malbec from Domaine La Bérangeraie the 2023 Cuvée Maurin unfolds with a deep ruby hue and a generous aroma of ripe black fruit laced with sweet spice and a hint of menthol. The palate is dense yet elegant featuring concentrated flavors of black cherry and prune underscored by supple tannins and a mineral spine, concluding with a lingering tobacco‑tinged, elegantly structured finish.

palate: dense, elegant black cherry and prune with supple tannins

name: Domaine la Berangeraie Cahors Cuvee Maurin

description: A focused expression of Beaujolais from granitic Côte de Brouilly soils this 2021 Domaine Lafarge Vial attains poised power with concentration and clarity. Red and darker cherry fruit meld with hints of savory spice and iron‑tinged minerality enlivened by an elegant structure.

The wine marries youthful structure with an elegant, perfumed profile that reveals both energy and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in Burgundy stemware after decanting to soften tannins: ideal with roast lamb or beef bourguignon enriched with underbrush mushrooms.
palate: silky yet structured red fruit

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Saint Romain sous le Chateau
description: The 2018 Domaine Pierre Morey Saint‐Romain Sous le Château offers a graceful expression of Chardonnay from a distinguished Burgundian climat, presenting yellow plum, gentle jasmine and broom blossom aromas. The palate is elegantly rounded with a honey‑kissed entry followed by tangerine and apricot tones woven through a mineral spine.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 to 12 °C to accentuate its sappy acidity and floral‑fruit interplay. Pairs beautifully with delicate shellfish or subtly seasoned poultry.
palate: honeyed entry, tangerine and apricot highlights, mineral backbone

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Volnay 1er Cru les Pitures
description: This 2018 Volnay 1er Cru Pitures from Domaine Morey‑Blanc presents refined pinot noir with a poised interplay of floral violet notes and vibrant cherry fruit, underpinned by mineral energy and a subtly structured frame that speaks both of elegance and resolve.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16‑18 °C, decant gently to coax finesse; pairs beautifully with duck breast or herbed roasted chicken, its freshness lifting richer preparations.
palate: fine mineral‑driven red fruit

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Volnay 1er Cru les Pitures

sommelierNotes: Serve at 16‑18 °C, decant gently to coax finesse; pairs beautifully with duck breast or herbed roasted chicken, its freshness lifting richer preparations.

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Volnay 1er Cru les Santenots
description: A refined expression of Volnay’s famed terroir this 2017 Pierre Morey Les Santenots unfolds with plush dark cherry and damson richness overlaid by restrained floral and savory complexity. Elegant firm tannins underpin a velvety texture lending both depth and poised grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature around 16 °C after light decanting to ease open the supple tannins and reveal beguiling layers. Ideal with game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: bright cherry and damson with floral underbrush
palate: velvety dark fruit with firm refined tannins

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape
description: A wonderfully balanced Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape, this domaine’s 2020 vintage offers layers of ripe blackberry and darker cherry fruit with lifted spice, violets and subtle garrigue notes. It is supple and elegantly structured, medium‑bodied with a polished, layered texture and a generous, rounded finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to reveal red‑fruit complexity and softness. Pair with slow‑braised lamb shoulder or Provençal herb‑roasted leg of lamb to complement its garrigue character.
aroma: ripe blackberry, darker cherry, spice, violets, garrigue
palate: medium‑bodied, polished and layered texture

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee de Mon Aieul
description: This 2020 Cuvee de Mon Aieul from Domaine Pierre Usseglio et Fils is composed entirely of old‑vine Grenache from three distinct lieux‑dits, vinified intact and matured in used demi‑muids, offering a concentrated yet elegant expression of Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape. Aromas of raspberries, blackberries, spice and floral accents are framed by a plush, powerful mouthfeel that remains refined and balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to emphasize purity of fruit and spice layers: pairs beautifully with Provençal lamb, charcuterie or mushroom‑rich dishes.
palate: plush, powerful, refined red fruit core

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Premiere Pierre Blanc
description: The 2023 Première Pierre Blanc from Domaine Pierre Usseglio unfurls with vivid orchard and citrus fruit framed by a delicate brioche lift, revealing a texture both generous and finely balanced, its weight supported by a whisper of minerality yet retaining a crystalline freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled but not icy to highlight its brightness; exemplary with shellfish in butter sauces or a poignant goat cheese.
palate: rich orchard fruit with poised minerality
foodPairings: seared scallops with citrus beurre blanc

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Premiere Pierre Rouge
description: An elegant Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape that unfolds with refined balance and velvety texture, offering dark cherry and wild berry aromas laced with savory spice and menthol—a thoroughly graceful southern Rhône expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool 16‑18 °C, and pair with classic French rustic fare such as rich game or herb‑roasted lamb to complement the wine’s structured fruit and peppery nuances.
aroma: dark cherries, wild berries, bay leaf and spice
palate: elegant, fleshy and silky tannins

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Lirac
description: This Lirac 2021 from Domaine Pierre Usseglio & Fils conjures an evocative marriage of dark fruit intensity and refined spice with finely woven structure and freshness as its heart.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14‑16 °C, ideally alongside Provençal stews or simply grilled lamb for a luminous evening.
palate: fresh, elegant, with jammy black cherry notes
finish: elegant, balanced, with subtle tannic grip

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Lirac Blanc
description: A luminous Lirac blanc fashioned by Domaine Pierre Usseglio, this 2024 vintage marries freshness and grace through its youthful Grenache Blanc and Clairette vines enhanced by gentle barrel and stainless steel élevage, delivering pear‑blossom charm and a touch of toasty elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–12 °C to spotlight its vibrant fruit and subtle toast; an ideal companion to shellfish or creamy goat cheese.
palate: elegant, fresh with buttery and toasted undertones

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Lirac Rouge
description: This Lirac Rouge unfolds with a garnet‑tinged robe and reveals sumptuous notes of black cherry, ripe plum, liquorice and a hint of Provençal spice, layered over fresh forest floor undercurrents, capturing the sun‑kissed terroir of the southern Rhône. The palate is generous yet refined, its dense tannins enveloped in elegant freshness and underpinned by a bright, lingering finish that speaks of both power and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 16 °C in large-bowled glasses, decant if young to let the fruit and spice aromas open; pairs beautifully with grilled lamb, Provençal stews or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: black cherry, plum, liquorice and spice
palate: generous, refined, dense tannins with fresh elegance

name: Domaine Raimbault-Pineau Coteaux du Giennois Blanc
description: A graceful Loire blanc that offers a crystalline core of citrus brightness and a stony mineral thread balanced by gentle fruit sweetness, rendered in a light, elegant frame
sommelierNotes: Chill well and serve at 10 °C to 12 °C alongside delicate fish terrines or creamy goat‑cheese tarts to accentuate its freshness and finesse
palate: fresh fruit with subtle minerality

name: Domaine Raimbault-Pinieau Sancerre
description: The 2022 Raimbault‑Pineau Sancerre presents an elegant fusion of brisk citrus and delicate floral perfume backed by a flinty mineral spine. The palate is refined yet expressive, offering grapefruit and white flower flavors carried on vibrant freshness and a polished, rounded texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled alongside fresh goat cheese or shellfish to highlight the wine’s crisp acidity and mineral brightness, or enjoy purely as a refined aperitif.
palate: grapefruit and white flower with rounded freshness

name: Domaine Rapet Beaune 1er Cru les Cents Vignes
appellation: Beaune Premier Cru Les Cents Vignes
description: A nuanced Beaune Premier Cru from Rapet Père & Fils, the 2022 Les Cents Vignes marries the round structure and silkiness of Beaune with the depth and power worthy of extended aging. It offers a refined interplay of ripe dark fruit and subtle earthborne minerality, guided by Burgundian restraint and sophistication.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature around 16–17 °C in a Burgundy-style glass. Best alongside roasted game birds or veal sautéed with mushrooms to echo its layered complexity.
aroma: ripe dark berries with soft spice and soil‑borne nuance
palate: plush, balanced fruit framed by fine tannins and vibrant minerality

name: Domaine Rapet Beaune 1er Cru les Greves
description: A refined Pinot Noir from the hills of Beaune, this 2022 Domaine Rapet Beaune 1er Cru “Les Grèves” unfurls with delicate red fruit and a subtle mineral tension. It balances plush texture and graceful tannins, offering elegance anchored by the gravelly terroir of this famed slope.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a tulip glass to reveal its layered complexity. Ideal with roast duck or mushroom‑infused dishes, its finesse echoes classic Beaune tradition.
aroma: minty red berries with hints of plum and raw cocoa
palate: velvety and layered with supple tannins and mineral undercurrent

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: A grand white Burgundy of poised gravitas this wine unfurls with a luminous golden hue and a finely layered structure of orchard fruits and toasted nuts woven through with glints of citrus rind and delicate white florals, all anchored by a steely, mineral spine that speaks of its flinty terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C alongside refined shellfish, lobster or silky foie gras to allow its mineral-supported opulence to sing.
palate: textured, concentrated, mineral-driven

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: A grand white Burgundy of poised gravitas this wine unfurls with a luminous golden hue and a finely layered structure of orchard fruits and toasted nuts woven through with glints of citrus rind and delicate white florals, all anchored by a steely, mineral spine that speaks of its flinty terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C alongside refined shellfish, lobster or silky foie gras to allow its mineral-supported opulence to sing.
palate: textured, concentrated, mineral-driven

name: Domaine Rapet Pernand Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru sous Fretille
description: This 2022 Pernand‑Vergelesses Premier Cru Sous Frétille from Domaine Rapet Père & Fils exudes refined yellow orchard fruit and a sinewy mineral clarity lifted by delicate floral nuance and almond‑tinged depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 12 °C and pair with gently stewed langoustines or delicate white meats; the wine’s finesse and mineral frame also complement aromatic, aged cheeses like comté or munster.
palate: silky texture, almond depth, mineral tension

name: Domaine Rapet Pernand Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru sous Fretille
description: This 2022 Pernand‑Vergelesses Premier Cru Sous Frétille from Domaine Rapet Père & Fils exudes refined yellow orchard fruit and a sinewy mineral clarity lifted by delicate floral nuance and almond‑tinged depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 12 °C and pair with gently stewed langoustines or delicate white meats; the wine’s finesse and mineral frame also complement aromatic, aged cheeses like comté or munster.
palate: silky texture, almond depth, mineral tension

name: Domaine Rapet Savigny les Beaune aux Fournaux
description: The 2018 Domaine Rapet Père et Fils Savigny‑lès‑Beaune 1er Cru “Aux Fourneaux” displays a brilliantly vivid ruby hue, unveiling a smoky‑tinged bouquet of deep blue fruits such as myrtille framed by noble toast from well‑judged barrel élevage, giving way to a palate that begins with supple generosity before tightening with sinewy, refined tannins. The impression is of an elegant yet boldly grounded Burgundy that promises more silk and nuance with age.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at around 15 °C to reveal its brightness, pairing beautifully with mushroom‑accented poultry or gently roasted veal.
palate: round onset, firm structure

name: Arbois Rouge Clos Maire
description: This Arbois Rouge Clos Maire 2016 from Domaine Ratte reveals a fine, vibrant expression of Pinot Noir and Trousseau planted in an old‑vine complantation vineyard. The gently carbonic maceration imparts a fresh, lifted red‑fruit clarity and a subtle spiciness framed by minimal handling in biodynamic tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14‑15 °C to showcase its bright acidity and pure fruit, ideal with subtle spice and forest‑infused dishes.
aroma: bright red berry and fresh raspberry
palate: lithe, gently spiced fruit with fine acidity

name: Arbois Savagnin Ouille Nature
description: A luminous expression of Jura Savagnin bearing the subtle austerity of the region, this 2016 Dom Ratte Arbois Savagnin Naturé ouillé offers a gently floral frame and a reserve of mineral clarity that speaks to the blue‑grey marl soils and artisanal, biodynamic craft of the domaine.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its floral lift and mineral tension; a graceful companion to seafood or aged Comté.
palate: mineral tension

name: Arbois Trousseau a la Dame
description: A pure and poised expression of Jura’s indigenous Trousseau à la Dame from the biodynamic Domaine Ratte, the 2015 sings with bright red fruit and gentle earth underpinned by a refined structure. Delicate aromatic intensity meets a subtly concentrated palate that speaks of terroir without pretense.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C to highlight its finesse; pairs beautifully with grilled duck or rustic comté cheeses.
aroma: bright red fruit with earthy nuance
palate: elegant concentration framed by soft tannins

name: Domaine Raymond Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape
description: A deeply resonant Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape from Domaine Raymond Usseglio & Fils the 2023 Girard cuvée unfolds with ripe red fruit layers and a framework of savory spice underpinned by biodynamic purity. It melds power and finesse in a textural embrace where cherry, black pepper and garrigue intertwine in poised harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to unveil complexity, ideally matched with herb‑crusted lamb or rich Provençal stews.
aroma: ripe cherry and raspberry with black pepper and licorice
palate: full‑bodied and silky with fine tannins

name: Domaine Raymond Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Imperiale
description: A grand expression of centuries‐old Grenache from Domaine Raymond Usseglio this wine emanates captivating aromas of rose petals red raspberries and garrigue mingled with dark cherries and wild berries Constrained yields and biodynamic restraint lend it an ethereal purity and layered complexity
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar temperature pairing organically with herb‐crusted lamb or wild boar ragù to showcase its fine acidity and lingering floral‐garrigue resonance
palate: deep concentrated yet airy red and black fruits with floral nuance

name: Domaine Jl Chave Saint Joseph
description: This 2021 Saint‑Joseph from Domaine Jean‑Louis Chave is an elegant expression of northern Rhône Syrah, offering vibrant black and red fruit tempered by graphite and pepper underpinned by floral nuance. The wine unfolds with medium body and seamless texture, delivering remarkable length anchored in precise mineral structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in a large-bowled glass to reveal its floral and graphite nuances; pairs beautifully with lamb en croûte or mushroom‑laden dishes.
palate: seamless texture of red and black fruit with floral lift

name: Domaine Romain Reverdy Sancerre Florilege
description: A gracious white Sancerre from Domaine Romain Reverdy, the Florilège 2025 offers crystalline purity. The wine presents a bright, elegantly lifted character with energetic citrus and herbal notes, framed by the classic Loire minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled near 9°C in a slender glass to accentuate its zesty freshness, making it an excellent companion to delicate seafood or goat cheese.
palate: crisp orchard fruit, green herb nuance, vibrant energy

name: Domaine Romain Reverdy Sancerre Rose Florilege
description: This 2025 Sancerre Rosé Florilège by Domaine Bernard Reverdy et Fils conveys delicate rose‑tinged charm, a graceful interplay of red fruit brightness and subtle mineral undertones. It offers refined elegance and a whisper of warmth drawn from the flinty Sancerre soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8‑10 °C, a sublime match for fresh shellfish or light salads with goat cheese from Chavignol.
palate: bright fruit with gentle minerality

name: Domaine Romain Reverdy Sancerre Rouge
description: A lithe Sancerre Rouge whose delicate expression unfurls with vibrant red cherry and subtle peony floral notes framing a fine-grained structure. Gentle earthiness underpins the silky Pinot Noir texture evoking old-world poise with graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 13 °C to highlight its red-fruit clarity, an elegant match for charcuterie and soft cheeses.
palate: silky red fruit with fine-grained structure

name: Domaine Rondeau-Guinet Bugey Cerdon Methode Ancestral Rose Sparkling Wine
description: A delicate and radiant rosé sparkler from the Cerdon hills of Bugey, this non‑vintage Méthode Ancestrale offers an enchanting melody of wild strawberry and framboise framed by soft effervescence and a whisper of natural sweetness. The wine dances across the palate with a lithe, lifted fruit expression and feather‑light mousse, revealing charming purity and old‑world grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled, ideally between 6 °C and 8 °C, in slender flutes to preserve its ethereal fizz; pairs beautifully with fresh fruit tarts or a platter of soft cheeses and berry compotes.
palate: light, gently sweet fruit with fine bubbles

name: Domaine Rostaing-Tayard Ultreia Coteaux du Lyonnais Rouge
description: The 2021 Ultreïa from Domaine Rostaing‑Tayard offers a poised and radiant expression of Gamay from the Coteaux du Lyonnais. It unfolds in the glass with vivid red‑berry clarity laced with peppery accents and a whisper of licorice.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cooler than room temperature to enhance its freshness; an excellent companion to charcuterie or gently spiced poultry.
aroma: red berries with pepper and licorice
palate: juicy acidity with melting tannins

name: Domaine Roy et Fils Incline Dundee Hills Pinot Noir
description: This 2017 Dundee Hills Incline Pinot Noir from Domaine Roy & Fils presents a complex weave of beetroot, cherry, cola citrus rind and mineral layers. It offers refreshing acidity and subtle elegance that unfolds with precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a tulip glass to accentuate its lifted aromatics; pairs beautifully with herb‑roasted poultry or earthy mushroom dishes.
aroma: beetroot and cherry with mineral edge
palate: bright citrus‑tinged red fruit with sleek mineral structure

name: Domaine Roy et Fils Willamette Valley Pinot Noir
description: The 2021 Domaine Roy et Fils Willamette Valley Pinot Noir presents a graceful interplay of Bing cherry and red raspberry accented by balsamic undertones and a subtle spiciness that unfolds with plush red fruit texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar temperature with roast duck or mushroom‑based dishes to accentuate the wine’s layered fruit and spice.
palate: plush red fruit with spice

name: Domaine Saint Damien Cotes du Rhone la Bouveau
description: The 2020 Domaine Saint‑Damien Côtes du Rhône “La Bouveau” offers a refined Southern Rhône expression framed in purity and Mediterranean grace, with energetic notes of peppery garrigue, red and black fruits and a streak of wild strawberry, all held in poised harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or at cellar cool temperature in broad glasses to accentuate its perfume and refreshing fruit. It partners beautifully with roast lamb, Provençal stews or aged goat’s cheese.
aroma: red and black fruits with peppery garrigue
palate: pure fruit core with softly rounded tannins

name: Domaine Saint Damien Cotes du Rhone Plan de Dieu
description: This 2022 Domaine Saint‑Damien Côtes‑du‑Rhône Villages Plan de Dieu Vieilles Vignes unfolds with ripe black cherry and plum underpinned by garrigue herbs and a whisper of white pepper drawing from old‑vine intensity and Southern Rhône provenance
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C with roasted lamb or wild mushrooms, allow a short decant to unveil its layered fruit and earthy complexity
aroma: ripe black cherry, garrigue herbs, white pepper
palate: concentrated plum and spice with firm yet elegant tannins
finish: long, savory finish with mineral chalkiness

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas Clovis Saurel
description: A refined expression of old‑vine Gigondas from Saint‑Damien, this 2020 Clovis Saurel presents ripe black cherries and raspberries gilded by subtle vanilla‑tinged oak: medium‑ to full‑bodied yet seamlessly elegant, balanced by fine tannins and remarkable poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve with gentle decanting to reveal its layered complexity: succulent with lamb stew or grilled Provençal meats.
palate: silky, concentrated, balanced
finish: long silky finish with subtle spice

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas Clovis Saurel
description: A refined expression of old‑vine Gigondas from Saint‑Damien, this 2022 Clovis Saurel presents ripe black cherries and raspberries gilded by subtle vanilla‑tinged oak: medium‑ to full‑bodied yet seamlessly elegant, balanced by fine tannins and remarkable poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve with gentle decanting to reveal its layered complexity: succulent with lamb stew or grilled Provençal meats.
palate: silky, concentrated, balanced
finish: long silky finish with subtle spice

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas la Louisiane
description: This is a powerful expression of Gigondas from a historic parcel in La Louisiane offering rich, intense dark fruit and classic southern Rhône spice layered with garrigue, black pepper and meaty undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperature in large Burgundy‐style glasses after gentle decanting, and pair with lamb, Provençal stews or aged sheep’s cheese.
palate: pure, focused core, ultra‑fine building tannins

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas les Souteyrades
description: This 2022 Domaine Saint‑Damien Gigondas Les Souteyrades presents a vivid ruby hue and unveils an exotic perfume of floral spice and sweet red berries, enriched by whispers of garrigue and dried herbs. The palate is medium‑to‑full bodied with ripe red fruit, fine tannins and precise structure, finishing long and elegant.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in generous Bordeaux glasses and pair with herb‑crusted lamb rack or Provençal roast pork.
aroma: floral spice and sweet red berries with garrigue
palate: ripe red fruit framed by fine tannins and structure

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas Rose
description: The 2024 Domaine Saint‑Damien Gigondas Rosé presents an elegant pink‑salmon hue with vivid aromas of wild strawberry, raspberry and pink grapefruit intertwined with subtle floral and herbs of the garrigue.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled to awaken its lively fruit character and pair it with light seafood or Provençal salads.
aroma: wild strawberry, pink grapefruit, delicate garrigue herbs
palate: crisp, juicy red berry fruit with citrus lift

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas Vieiles Vignes
description: The 2020 Domaine Saint‑Damien Gigondas Vieilles Vignes is a generously perfumed southern Rhône red boasting aromas of darker berries, garrigue and spice with a supple yet structured mouthfeel that conveys both elegance and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in burgundy glasses, and pair with charred lamb chops atop herbed polenta or Provençal olive‑studded stews for a harmonious match.
palate: round lush fruits with elegant tannins
finish: long and savory with spice‑tinged grip

name: Domaine Saint Damien Gigondas Vieilles Vignes
description: A refined expression of Gigondas old‑vine vitality this 2023 Vieilles Vignes from Domaine Saint‑Damien reveals layered darker berries, garrigue spice and a hint of smoked meat unfolding with elegance and depth. The palate is medium‑ to full‑bodied with polished tannins and harmonious acidity offering pure structure and compelling length.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool around 60‑62 °F in large Burgundy‑style stemware; this wine partners beautifully with herb‑crusted lamb or Provençal lamb stew.
aroma: darker berries with garrigue and smoked‑meat nuances
palate: medium‑ to full‑bodied with pure layered mouthfeel and fine polished tannins

name: Domaine Saint Damien Vacqueyras
description: The 2021 Domaine Saint‑Damien Vacqueyras unfolds with vibrant southern Rhône character drawing from biologically cultivated Grenache‑led vines, offering a rich core of red and black fruit delicacy complemented by Provençal garrigue nuances and fine-textured tannins. It is an elegant expression of Vacqueyras restraint and freshness in a challenging vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C after brief decanting to reveal its layered fruit and subtle herbal tones, pairing ideally with roast lamb or Provençal stews.
aroma: red and black fruit, garrigue hint
palate: silky tannins around bright fruit

name: Domaine Schoffit Riesling Grand Cru Rangen de Thann
appellation: Alsace Grand Cru Rangen de Thann
description: The 2019 Domaine Schoffit Riesling Grand Cru Rangen de Thann emerges from the steep volcanic slopes of the Clos Saint‑Théobald in Alsace, radiating with refined power and crystalline poise. It offers a radiant blend of citrus‑tinged orchard fruit and smoked stone notes, threaded through with saline tension and lingering mineral clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in slender stemware to accentuate its precision; pairs beautifully with shellfish in beurre blanc or herb‑roasted poultry, offering harmony through its mineral energy.
aroma: citrus blossom and flint‑tinged orchard fruit
palate: bright saline verve with layered mineral depth

name: Domaine Schoffit Riesling Grand Cru Sommerberg
description: This 2017 Sommerberg Grand Cru Riesling from Domaine Albert Boxler presents crystalline minerality and dense vitality framed by tightly wound citrus notes and pure stone‑inflected structure. It offers a refined interplay of lemon‑y brightness and granite‑borne precision that is both intense and graceful.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 10 °C, ideally with seafood or subtly spiced fish to echo its salinity and taut acidity.
palate: crisp citrus and stony concentration
foodPairings: grilled sea bass with lemon and herbs

name: Domaine Serol Cote Roannaise Rouge chez Coste
description: This parcel expression of Côte Roannaise Rouge from Domaine Sérol presents a fine weave of red fruit delicacy and mineral clarity evocative of its gorrhe granite soils, with subtle structure shaped by extended amphora vinification. The wine offers an elegant balance of silky fruit and terroir‑driven precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 14 °C to reveal its fresh red‑berry charm; delightful with simply roasted poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: red berries with a hint of earth
palate: silky and mineral‑driven

name: Domaine Serol Cote Roannaise Rouge chez Muron
