name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rose Fleur de Pinot
description: This rosé unveils a refined elegance, marrying the clarity of Burgundy with vivid red‑berry generosity and a whisper of herb‑tinged complexity. It captures delicacy and depth in equal measure, articulating a notion of rosé as a wine of terroir rather than simplicity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10–12 °C to reveal its finesse alongside refined light dishes such as grilled fish or delicate carpaccios.
aroma: fresh wild strawberry and dried florals
palate: delicate yet structured with red fruits and fine minerality

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge
description: An emphatic and inviting Marsannay Rouge from Sylvain Pataille that blends vivacious red cherry and raspberry fruit with Burgundian freshness, framed by gentle savory spice and subtle earth‑tinged nuance. Light on oak and richly expressive, it reveals both energy and elegance in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15 °C in a Burgundy glass. Opens beautifully with minimal aeration, particularly appealing with poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with floral and earthy spice
palate: medium‑bodied, fresh, nuanced savory red fruit

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge
description: An emphatic and inviting Marsannay Rouge from Sylvain Pataille that blends vivacious red cherry and raspberry fruit with Burgundian freshness, framed by gentle savory spice and subtle earth‑tinged nuance. Light on oak and richly expressive, it reveals both energy and elegance in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15 °C in a Burgundy glass. Opens beautifully with minimal aeration, particularly appealing with poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with floral and earthy spice
palate: medium‑bodied, fresh, nuanced savory red fruit

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge
description: An emphatic and inviting Marsannay Rouge from Sylvain Pataille that blends vivacious red cherry and raspberry fruit with Burgundian freshness, framed by gentle savory spice and subtle earth‑tinged nuance. Light on oak and richly expressive, it reveals both energy and elegance in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15 °C in a Burgundy glass. Opens beautifully with minimal aeration, particularly appealing with poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with floral and earthy spice
palate: medium‑bodied, fresh, nuanced savory red fruit

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge Clos du Roy
description: A refined expression of Marsannay by Sylvain Pataille from the 2021 vintage this Pinot Noir offers layered cassis and bramble fruit with savory spice and smoky undertones over a poised, medium‑bodied frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature in a Burgundian tulip glass to reveal its mineral clarity; pair with venison medallions or roasted duck for a balanced, elegant match.
palate: medium‑bodied, taut, fresh with fine‑grain tannins

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge Clos du Roy
description: A refined expression of Marsannay by Sylvain Pataille from the 2022 vintage this Pinot Noir offers layered cassis and bramble fruit with savory spice and smoky undertones over a poised, medium‑bodied frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature in a Burgundian tulip glass to reveal its mineral clarity; pair with venison medallions or roasted duck for a balanced, elegant match.
palate: medium‑bodied, taut, fresh with fine‑grain tannins

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge en Clemengots
description: A refined and graceful Pinot Noir from Marsannay this 2021 En Clémengeots reveals finely woven red and black cherry fruit, underpinned by woodland herb and soft earth tones cloaked in a gentle cedar nuance, all framed by seamless oak integration.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a broad Burgundy glass after a brief decant to reveal its silken mid‑palate, pairing elegantly with tender game or simply roasted poultry.
aroma: red and black cherry with subtle cedar and forest floor
palate: silky, fresh, earthy fruit

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge en Clemengots
description: A refined and graceful Pinot Noir from Marsannay this 2022 En Clémengeots reveals finely woven red and black cherry fruit, underpinned by woodland herb and soft earth tones cloaked in a gentle cedar nuance, all framed by seamless oak integration.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a broad Burgundy glass after a brief decant to reveal its silken mid‑palate, pairing elegantly with tender game or simply roasted poultry.
aroma: red and black cherry with subtle cedar and forest floor
palate: silky, fresh, earthy fruit

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge le Chapitre
description: A vivid expression of Marsannay in its youth sourced from a revered lieu-dit, this 2021 Marsannay Le Chapitre presents ripe black cherry and boysenberry with a poised core of mineral clarity and structural precision. It conveys vertical energy and sapidity giving it vibrant momentum alongside an air of elegance born from whole-cluster vinification and extended élevage.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C after a brief 30‑minute aeration to awaken its floral and fruit layers; pairs beautifully with gently roasted pork or richer poultry dishes.
aroma: black cherry and boysenberry with floral lift
palate: vertical, sapid and finely framed

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Rouge le Chapitre
description: A vivid expression of Marsannay in its youth sourced from a revered lieu-dit, this 2022 Marsannay Le Chapitre presents ripe black cherry and boysenberry with a poised core of mineral clarity and structural precision. It conveys vertical energy and sapidity giving it vibrant momentum alongside an air of elegance born from whole-cluster vinification and extended élevage.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C after a brief 30‑minute aeration to awaken its floral and fruit layers; pairs beautifully with gently roasted pork or richer poultry dishes.
aroma: black cherry and boysenberry with floral lift
palate: vertical, sapid and finely framed

name: Domaine Sylvie Esmonin Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru le Clos Saint Jacques
description: This 2019 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru “Clos Saint‑Jacques” from Sylvie Esmonin unfurls in the glass with brooding black fruit and violet tones framed in supple yet powerful structure, its dark, layered elegance speaking of both vineyard prestige and a singular house imprint—rich, focused, compelling.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar cool to allow its fine-grained tannins and vibrant acidity to blossom; pairs beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: medium‑bodied with precise linear tannins

name: Domaine Sylvie Esmonin Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru le Clos Saint Jacques
description: This 2020 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru “Clos Saint‑Jacques” from Sylvie Esmonin unfurls in the glass with brooding black fruit and violet tones framed in supple yet powerful structure, its dark, layered elegance speaking of both vineyard prestige and a singular house imprint—rich, focused, compelling.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar cool to allow its fine-grained tannins and vibrant acidity to blossom; pairs beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: medium‑bodied with precise linear tannins

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis 1er Cru Cote de Lechet
description: A restrained yet charming Chablis premier cru that evokes the clear light of its Côte de Léchet vineyard, offering a delicate interplay of floral lift and chalky mineral freshness. The 2021 vintage brings gentle orchard fruit over a taut, refined frame with just a whisper of salinity at the close.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender tulip glass alongside delicate seafood preparations or creamy pasta; allow a few minutes of air to coax out its floral brightness.
palate: lithe mineral core with subtle yellow fruit
foodPairings: ricotta ravioli with spinach and cream

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis 1er Cru Mont de Milieu
appellation: Chablis Premier Cru Mont de Milieu
description: Bright and crystalline Chablis from the 2020 vintage crafted by Domaine Thierry Laffay this wine shows a refined mineral thread through vibrant orchard fruit and gentle chalky depth drawn from Kimmeridgian soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 50°F to accentuate its liveliness and pair with oysters or lightly grilled sea bass for elegant harmony.
palate: silky mouthfeel with golden apple and lemon custard

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis Cote de Lechet
appellation: Chablis Premier Cru Côte de Léchet
description: A luminous Chablis Premier Cru that marries the cool clarity of Kimmeridgian marl with a subtle generosity of fruit: the 2020 Côte de Léchet by Domaine Thierry Laffay reveals pale gold brilliance and a poised interplay of yellow orchard fruit framed in steely mineral drive inspired by its storied terroir. Gentle salinity and energetic acidity bring a refined tension that speaks of both precision and urbane charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at 12–14 °C in slender tulip glasses to draw forward its floral nuance and stony minerality: ideal with shellfish, herbed poultry or creamy risottos.
aroma: yellow orchard fruit and wet limestone
palate: vibrant acidity, chalky minerality

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis Grand Cru Vaudesir
description: A finely cut Chablis Grand Cru whose worldly poise strikes a balance between vibrancy and subtle richness, the 2021 Dom Thierry Laffay Vaudésir offers steely clarity overlaid with orchard tones and a whisper of reduction. Its profile evokes old‑school austerity tempered with genteel generosity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C to reveal its mineral tension and transparent fruit, and pair with delicate shellfish or richer white‑meat preparations to echo its balance of freshness and weight.
palate: precise mineral core with subtle richness

name: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Blanc
description: A radiant and crystalline Sancerre Blanc that marries Loire elegance with vivid energy Its minerally precise character speaks of flint and limestone soils, delivering citrus tension and refined textural depth
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8 °C, ideal with goats’ cheese or delicate seafood for clarity and grace
aroma: citrus zest with flinty mineral nuances
palate: crisp lime and pear framed by saline minerality

name: Domaine Yann Chave Crozes Hermitage Classique
description: This 2022 Crozes‑Hermitage Classique from Domaine Yann Chave presents bright crimson hues and expressive aromas of cassis and blackberry laced with subtle black pepper and elegant freshness. On the palate, it reveals a refined silkiness with delicate, velvety tannins and a harmonious interplay of fruit and spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in generous glasses, ideally decanted, alongside roast veal or a subtly spiced beef dish.
aroma: blackcurrant and blackberry with peppery spice
palate: silky texture with velvety tannins
foodPairings: roasted veal filet mignon with porcini and sweet potato mash
seared bavette steak with shallot butter and pommes Pont‑Neuf

name: Domane Serrig Riesling Vogelsang Grosse Lage
description: A crystalline Saar Riesling of near-ethereal purity, the 2020 Domäne Serrig Vogelsang Grosse Lage presents a refined interplay of flint‑like minerality and delicate white fruit, supported by laser‑sharp structure and invigorating tension. Its expression is at once generous and crystalline, culminating in a pristine, saline‑tinged finish that lingers endlessly.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in an elegant glass between 10 °C and 12 °C, perhaps decanted briefly to accentuate its lifted aromas. Pair with delicate seafood, fine shellfish or nuanced Asian fare to complement its vibrant minerality.
palate: taut structure with sea‑salt minerality
foodPairings: seared scallops with citrus beurre blanc

name: Domane Serrig Riesling Vogelsang Kabinett
description: A poised and svelte expression of Saar Riesling, the 2021 Domäne Serrig Vogelsang Kabinett reveals a delicate architecture of slate‑tinged citrus and orchard fruit, brightened by a fine saline undercurrent. There is an elegant tension between discreet sweetness and crystalline acidity that imparts refined energy within a finely sculpted frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its citrus brightness and mineral drive, ideal with light seafood or subtly aromatic dishes.
palate: discreet sweetness balanced by crystalline acidity

name: Domiane Lafarge Vial Fleurie Clos Vernay
description: A finely sculpted Fleurie that unfurls with an elegant silkiness the granite‐inflected structure is caressed by layers of sweet dark berries and subtle floral whispers, building with refined depth and poised serenity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‐shaped glass to reveal its floral perfume; ideal with roasted chicken, mushroom fricassee or soft chèvre.
aroma: sweet dark berries with floral whispers
palate: velvety depth with bright acidity and fine‐grained tannins

name: Domaine Dominique Mugneret Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Boudots
description: A polished and refined Burgundy of restrained tannins and bright red fruit elegance: this 2013 Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru Les Boudots from Domaine Mongeard‑Mugneret shows cherry‑stained silk textures, gentle mineral undercurrents and precise depth hinting at its Vosne‑Romanée proximity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at about 14 °C in large Burgundy glasses: fine with roast spring lamb or mushroom‑perfumed game, allowing the wine’s subtle spice and black fruit to harmonize.
aroma: perfumed wild red berries with faint herb and cedar
palate: silky cherry fruit underscored by fine acidity and mineral drive
finish: elegant lingering grip with subtle earthy spice

name: Dr Konstantin Frank Dry Riesling
description: A lattice of luminous orchard fruit and citrus precision interwoven with finger‑lakes minerality define this 2025 Dry Riesling from Dr Konstantin Frank: bright notes of orange zest, ripe apricot, pineapple and acacia blossom emerge from cool‑climate shale‑driven earth tones, culminating in a long layered finish of citrus brightness and mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled alongside fresh seafood, sushi or citrus‑accented salads to highlight its energy and precision.
aroma: orange zest, ripe apricot, pineapple, acacia blossom
palate: rich, crisp apple acidity, concentrated fruit, steely minerality
finish: long, layered citrus and mineral tension
foodPairings: savory spring salad with goat cheese

name: Dr Konstantin Frank Dry Rose
description: This Dry Rosé from Dr. Konstantin Frank reveals an elegant blur of red fruit energy and structural finesse hinting at kirsch and fresh berries lifted by bright acidity, capturing the old‑world soul of Finger Lakes rosé.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a graceful tulip‑shaped glass, ideally beside shellfish salads or summer vegetable terrines, to showcase its crisp clarity and lift.
palate: vivid cherry‑tinged acidity

name: Dr Konstantin Frank Rkatsiteli
description: A beguiling expression of an ancient Georgian variety rendered with Finger Lakes grace, this Rkatsiteli 2025 unfurls fragrant layers of tropical fruit, ripe pear and citrus zest with a subtle peppery note that commands attention. Its lively acidity and whisper of residual sweetness make it both vibrant and refreshingly complex, a modern homage to Dr Konstantin Frank’s pioneering spirit.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a graceful white stem glass and allow a moment to open, it pairs beautifully with bright seafood or summery salads.
aroma: tropical fruit and citrus zest with peppery intrigue
palate: vibrant acidity balancing a hint of sweetness

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A brooding Cabernet Sauvignon that melds weight and grace from Romania’s Dreambird estate, drawing its fruit from the Gipsy Hill and Izvin vineyards and matured in two‑year‑old French oak for twelve months. It unfolds with rich notes of wild berries and dark chocolate warmed by whispers of mint, cranberry and a gentle splice of clove and nutmeg, supported by a tight yet seamless backbone.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to 14 °C – 16 °C in classic goblets and pair with roasted red meats or hearty pasta finished with umami‑rich sauces.
palate: dense fruit, layered spice

name: Dreambird Pinot Grigio
description: This youthful 2024 Dreambird Pinot Grigio from Romania offers an elegantly poised expression of the variety, with vivid notes of grapefruit and peach that glide into a bright, melon‑tinged body kissed by citrus tension. It evokes delicate orchard fruit framed by crisp energy in a style both refreshing and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 to 10 °C, ideally alongside light seafood or subtly seasoned poultry to accentuate its fresh fruit character.
palate: melon‑tinged orchard fruit with citrus brightness

name: Pinot Noir
description: A modest Romanian Pinot Noir fashioned under the Dreambird label presents a charming red fruit character with gentle spice framing. There is a modest mid‑weight presence with subtle plum and cherry tones enfolded in a whisper of smoke. The balance is approachable and effortlessly pleasing rather than showy.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar cool to highlight its red fruit clarity. Pair it with simply prepared poultry, grilled mushrooms or soft cheeses.
aroma: red cherry and plum with a hint of smoke
palate: smooth red fruit mid‑weight

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This Romanian Dreamfish Cabernet Sauvignon evokes a forest’s hush and late‑night indulgence with its modest yet inviting persona, unfolding layers of dark cherry and earth‑tilled tobacco, underscored by a seam of smooth graphite and dusk‑fruited allure. It is an everyday luxury in the old‑world sense, generous yet unpretentious.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar temperature in a simple tumbler to frame its comforting fruit and easygoing structure, a fine match for hearty weekday fare.
palate: smooth graphite and soft earth tones

name: Chardonnay
description: This Romanian Dreamfish Chardonnay, presented in generous 1.5‑liter bottles, offers a bright pale straw hue and an appealing aroma of citrus, tropical fruit and fresh melon with undercurrents of lightly roasted oak that suggest elegance with vitality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to accentuate its crisp structure; ideal alongside simply grilled fish or delicate seafood.
aroma: citrus, tropical fruit, fresh melon, roasted oak
palate: vibrant, complex, crisp

name: Chardonnay
description: A gracious expression of modest heritage Chardonnay offering gentle orchard fruit and delicate citrus brightness, with a whisper of mellow oak that nods to its restrained elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its fresh clarity and pair with subtly flavored seafood or creamy pasta.
palate: light orchard fruit framed by soft oak

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Bonnes Mares Grand Cru
description: A deeply vermilion Grand Cru from Chambolle‑Musigny, this 2018 Bonnes‑Mares unveils discreet aromas of blackcurrant bud and violet, followed by a palate of spiced red fruit and delicate liquorice, all underpinned by a whisper of rose that brings finesse and noble density in an elegant expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at 16 °C to 18 °C to highlight its silken texture and pair with rich dishes such as roast Bresse chicken or foie‑gras‑stuffed duck to complement its spice and floral grace.
palate: spiced small red fruit with liquorice and rose
foodPairings: duck breast stuffed with foie gras

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Chambertin Clos de Beze Grand Cru
description: This 2019 Domaine Drouhin‑Laroze Chambertin‑Clos de Bèze Grand Cru displays noble intensity with lush red and black raspberry fruit lifted by a whisper of liquorice and violet florals, structured by refined precision and depth. It unfolds with plush density and clarity, the fruit on the cusp of red and black, culminating in a vibrant, subtly crunchy close.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C, decant if young to awaken its layers. Ideal alongside delicate game or aged Morbier, it also suits richly spiced dishes.
palate: dense red‑black fruit with refined structure

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Chapelle Chambertin Grand Cru
description: An elegant expression of Grand Cru Pinot Noir from Gevrey‑Chambertin its deep mid-purple robe gives way to a refined bouquet of ripe dark raspberry entwined with woody vanilla and a subtle floral whisper drawn from generous oak ageing. The palate is graceful yet stately its supple tannins and layered spiced fruit framing a poised, mineral‑inflected finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C to 18 °C, ideally paired with duck breast with morels or an Italian veal escalope to complement its elegant structure and savory depth.
aroma: woody vanilla with a fine floral touch
palate: elegant spiced fruit with supple tannins

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: This Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru 2013 from Domaine Drouhin‑Laroze reveals a brooding elegance grounded in its storied terroir. The bouquet unfolds slowly to reveal briary red fruit, bramble and subtle licorice. The mid‑palate is framed by fine acidity and tightly knit tannins delivering harmony and persistence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar cool temperatures around 16 °C, best decanted if young. Pair with richly flavored dishes such as truffle risotto or pepper‑crusted steak.
palate: fine acidity, tightly knit tannins, harmony

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Clos Prieur
description: A seamlessly poised expression of Gevrey‑Chambertin that marries supple black and Morello cherry tones with a soft whisper of salted caramel and toasted oak, framed by fine, silken tannins and a lithe structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in tulip‑shaped stems to reveal its nocturnal fruit and perfumed undergrowth; ideal with gently roasted poultry or mushroom‑accented game.
aroma: candied black fruit, Morello cherry, subtle toast
palate: silky texture, saline‑touched cherry, gentle oak

name: Domaine Drouhin-Laroze Latricieres Chambertin Grand Cru
description: The 2019 Drouhin‑Laroze Latricières‑Chambertin Grand Cru unfolds with concentrated dark‑ruby hues and a discreet, compelling perfume of blackberry, blueberry, liquorice and spice. On the palate it offers a seamless yet powerful structure, rich and aromatic with succulent black‑fruit depth, refined tannins and a long, elegant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 to 18 °C to reveal its aromatic complexity; pairs exquisitely with mushroom ravioli or duck breast with morels.
palate: rich black‑fruit depth with refined tannins
foodPairings: ravioles with mushrooms and foie gras

name: Estate Valley Karmen Isabella Pinot Noir Russian River Valley
description: The 2023 Dutton Estate Karmen Isabella Pinot Noir presents an elegant expression of Russian River Valley, weaving radiant red berry aromas with delicate floral notes in a manner that suggests both finesse and depth. The palate is supple and graceful, with polished tannins and a refined sense of balance that hints at Burgundian poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its fine detail; pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑infused risotto.
aroma: wild strawberry and rose petal lift
palate: silky red cherry with forest floor nuance
finish: lingering red fruit with soft earthy undercurrent

name: Estate Winery Kylie's Cuvee Sauvignon Blanc Russian River Valley
description: A luminous Sauvignon Blanc from Dutton Estate’s “Sisters Selection” this 2024 Kylie’s Cuvée unfolds with vibrant citrus blossom, white peach and mandarin orange, weaving in an undercurrent of honeydew melon and tangerine. Its elegant, creamy mid‑palate is enlivened by bright acidity, leading to a lingering finish of Meyer lemon zest and pink grapefruit warmth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip‑shape glass to highlight its fragrant bouquet enjoy with fresh shellfish or grilled fish accented with citrus salsa.
aroma: citrus blossom, white peach, mandarin orange
palate: creamy, bright acidity, honeydew melon, tangerine
finish: Meyer lemon zest and pink grapefruit linger
foodPairings: seared ahi tuna with citrus salsa

name: Estate Winery Kyndals's Reserve Chardonnay Russian River Valley
description: A luminous Russian River Valley Chardonnay that glimmers with orchard fruit and refined oak nuance, the 2023 Kyndall’s Reserve enchants with a ribbon of caramel‑tinged pear and preserved nectarine enfolded in soft spice. It offers a poised elegance rooted in bright acidity and lush mid‑palate weight.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its expressive fruit and creamy texture, and pair with dishes such as butter‑basted chicken or delicate seafood in citrus cream sauces.
palate: preserved pear, nectarine, subtle spice

name: Vineyards Zinfandel Amador County
description: This 2018 Easton Vineyards Amador County Zinfandel exudes an elegant depth of black cherry and ripe raspberry framed by wild sage and chaparral undercurrents balanced with a subtle cocoa note. A polished expression of Sierra Foothills terroir, it feels both lush and poised.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to enhance the spice and freshness; pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops or tomato‑braised sausages.
aroma: wild‑sage and chaparral over dark fruit
palate: concentrated raspberry and blackberry with cocoa hint

name: Château de L'echarderie Quarts de Chaume
description: The 2006 Château de l’Écharderie Quarts‑de‑Chaume is an opulent yet refined Chenin Blanc, presenting rich threads of apricot and honeyed flowers woven with clear minerality. The palate is lacy in texture, offering stone fruit and exotic nuances, all held aloft by a clean line of bright acidity and finishing with lingering floral nectar.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled; this wine complements foie gras and blue cheeses or an almond tart with poached pear.
palate: stone fruit with lively minerality

name: Château de L'echarderie Quarts de Chaume Clos Paradis
description: A refined and luminous Quarts‑de‑Chaume from Château de l’Écharderie, vintage 2005, where golden yellow hues yield to slow‑unfolding aromas of dried fruits and gently poached white fruit, leading to a palate rich with honeyed confection and an invigorating freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled, around 8–10 °C, alongside foie gras or gently spiced blue cheeses to balance sweetness with a whisper of botrytis‑driven vibrancy.
aroma: dried fruits and poached white fruit
palate: honeyed confection with freshness

name: Echo de Lynch Bages Pauillac
description: A richly textured youth from Pauillac that entices with dense black‑fruit and spice layers supported by sinewy, polished tannins, offering both immediate charm and the gravitas to reward cellaring.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 17 °C after decanting to let the dark fruit and cedar nuances open up; pairs gracefully with roast lamb or aged beef.
palate: powerful yet silky tannins, concentrated and structured

name: Vineyards Estate Chardonnay
description: The 2022 Eden Rift Estate Chardonnay emerges from the limestone‑inflected slopes of Cienega Valley, offering a pale lemon‑hued expression of California Chardonnay distilled to its essence. Its profile unfolds with ripe Anjou pear, golden Gala apple and a whisper of pineapple, underpinned by creamy malolactic texture and a chalk‑driven mineral spine.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 50‑55 °F in tulip‑shaped stemware to capture its elegance, a fine companion to grilled white meats or subtly spiced shellfish.
aroma: ripe pear, golden apple, light tropical suggestion
palate: creamy textured, chalky minerality, bright acidity

name: Vineyards Estate Pinot Noir
description: Framed by the limestone‑rich slopes of the Cienega Valley the 2022 Estate Pinot Noir from Eden Rift offers a harmonious weave of red and black cherry, damson plum and cranberry, threaded through sage and thyme accents that lend it both vibrancy and a subtle savory complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 55–60 °F after a brief decant to allow the layers of spices and herbs to gently unfurl; finely balanced acidity and moderate tannin carry through dishes with wild mushrooms or roasted duck.
aroma: layered red and black cherry with red cranberry and damson plum, sage and thyme
palate: rounded mouthfeel with clove and cinnamon, firm yet yielding tannins
finish: savory herbal lift with powdery tannins
foodPairings: roasted duck breast with sage butter

name: Vineyards Valliant Chardonnay
description: Bright and graceful this 2022 Valliant Chardonnay from Eden Rift presents a luminous, old‑world tempered style with clarity and poise. It offers a refined interplay of citrus lift and gentle creaminess that evokes a polished yet inviting expression of Central Coast Chardonnay.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 50–54°F allow the wine to breathe to reveal its nuance. A lovely aperture for buttery seafood or roasted chicken with lemon.
palate: silken texture with balanced acidity

name: Vineyards Valliant Pinot Noir
description: A luminous California Pinot Noir from Eden Rift’s celebrated Valliant program this 2023 vintage whispers of coastal heritage with bright cherry pit and brambleberry tones, framed by soft savory accents and a polished texture. Its energy and clarity echo the limestone‑rich site in a graceful, inviting expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in Burgundy‑style stemware to elevate its bright red fruit and silky texture, pairing splendidly with roast duck breast or wild mushroom risotto.
palate: soft silky texture with savory red berries

name: Edmond et Anne Vatan Sancerre Clos la Neore
description: The 2022 Edmond et Anne Vatan Sancerre Clos La Néore magnum is an exquisite expression of Chavignol’s finest terroir, revealing crystalline citrus and white orchard fruit threaded with saline precision. The wine unfolds with refined power and mineral tension, evoking both purity and depth in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C after decanting for 1–2 hours to coax open its layered aromas and reveal seamless interplay of fruit, mineral and vibrant acidity.
aroma: lime zest, white orchard fruit, saline undertone
palate: dense, mineral‑driven with citrus energy
foodPairings: Chilled langoustine carpaccio with citrus and herbs

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Egeo Verdejo Do Rueda
description: This 2023 Egeo Verdejo from the hand of Isaac Fernández is a graceful expression of Rueda that marries tender white peach and melon with a delicate spiced almond nuance giving the wine inner complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8–10 °C in a tulip glass to preserve its fresh vibrancy and pair with simply grilled sea bass or marinated shellfish.
palate: medium-bodied, polished with saline lift

name: Bodegas Elias Mora Vina Elias Mora Crianza Do Toro
description: A noble Crianza from Toro showing the sinewy essence of Tinta de Toro berries, deep and vivid in personality, with a frame of spicy mineral and fine oak offering both depth and restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐fresh 16–18 °C after decanting if young; match with roasted lamb or char‑grilled meats to mirror its bold structure.
aroma: black cherry and confit blackberry with mineral spice
palate: meaty concentration with cacao and dark plum underpinned by firm tannins

name: Bodegas Elias Mora Vina Elias Mora Do Toro
description: A wine of noble lineage drawn from Toro’s ancient, ungrafted Tinta de Toro vines, the 2021 Viñas Elías Mora weaves an elegant tapestry of deep dark fruit softened by gentle spice and finely integrated American oak.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature around 16 °C in large-bowled glasses allow a gentle swirl to coax out soft floral notes; pairs beautifully with roasted lamb or aged Manchego.
palate: ripe dark berries framed by toasty spice
finish: balanced tannins with lingering mineral grip

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A graceful Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon from the 2023 vintage this wine offers layered black cherry and blackberry aromas accented by cocoa and gentle caramel turning into a balanced and supple mid‑palate. The structure is supported by bright acidity and fine tannins culminating in a refined, clean finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60‑65°F in large Bordeaux glasses let the wine breathe slightly before pairing with grilled red meats or rich mushroom dishes.
palate: balanced mid‑palate, supple tannins

name: Chardonnay Napa Valley
description: This 2023 Elizabeth Rose Chardonnay from Napa Valley—crafted from organically farmed vineyards in Yountville—unfolds with elegant orchard fruit and citrus notes framed by gentle oak spice, its refined texture balanced by a lively, refreshing acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a classic white wine glass to enhance its delicate floral and fruit aromas; pairs beautifully with roasted chicken or creamy seafood dishes.
palate: smooth mid‑palate with balanced texture and citrus‑stone fruit interplay

name: Elizabeth Rose Chockablock Napa Valley Red Blend
description: A captivating Napa Valley red blend that marries dark cherry and blackberry fruit with gentle cocoa and caramel undernotes, framed by refined oak and supple tannins. The wine shows harmonious structure and elegant balance, offering a smooth, medium‑bodied profile with a clean, graceful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to highlight its freshness. Pair with grilled lamb, roasted mushroom risotto, or aged Manchego for a luxurious yet accessible experience.
palate: supple tannins, balanced acidity, refined oak

name: Pinot Noir Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Elizabeth Rose Pinot Noir Napa Valley unfolds with luminous clarity and red-berry poise, gently leaning into a refined, graceful profile. It offers bright notes of strawberry and cherry carried on a silken texture, framed by subtle forest‑floor nuances without ever tipping into earthiness. The overall effect is elegant and polished, a Pinot Noir that charms with its approachability and precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55 °F in a tulip‑shaped glass, and pair with roasted duck breast, mushroom‑risotto, or grilled salmon to accentuate its red fruit and soft spice tones.
palate: silky red fruit with forest‑floor undertones
finish: elegant and refined lingering of red fruit

name: Pinot Noir Napa Valley
description: The 2024 Elizabeth Rose Pinot Noir Napa Valley unfolds with luminous clarity and red-berry poise, gently leaning into a refined, graceful profile. It offers bright notes of strawberry and cherry carried on a silken texture, framed by subtle forest‑floor nuances without ever tipping into earthiness. The overall effect is elegant and polished, a Pinot Noir that charms with its approachability and precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55 °F in a tulip‑shaped glass, and pair with roasted duck breast, mushroom‑risotto, or grilled salmon to accentuate its red fruit and soft spice tones.
palate: silky red fruit with forest‑floor undertones
finish: elegant and refined lingering of red fruit

name: Napa Valley Red Wine
description: A layered and brooding red from Napa Valley showing classic Bordeaux blend virtues with dark fruit and gentle spice, cloaked in smooth velvety structure and refined oak nuance. It reveals depth and poise drawing the taster into its rich harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60–64 °F in generous glasses to coax the caressing fruit and spice forward; elegant enough for roast lamb or mushroom‑truffle risotto.
aroma: dark fruit with anise and chocolate
palate: velvety, layered dark‑fruit core

name: Vinho Verde Cans
description: A pale citrus elixir in can form that captures the youthful verve of Vinho Verde: this NV ESTE delivers a light, bright expression of lemon and green apple essence with a subtle spritz, offering immediate drinkability and pure refreshment.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8 °C for ideal refreshment: it partners beautifully with chilled seafood snacks or crisp salads.
palate: refreshing light sweetness with gentle fizz

name: Vinho Verde Rose
description: A charming and youthful rosé from Portugal’s storied Vinho Verde region offering a delicate salmon‑pink hue and a whisper of spritz, it delivers bright red‑berry aromas with a lively and refreshing feel, poised and graceful on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10 °C alongside light hors d’oeuvres or fresh seafood for an effortlessly elegant aperitif experience.
aroma: bright red‑berry with raspberry and gooseberry accents
palate: light, fresh, gently effervescent and lively

name: Vinho Verde Rose Cans
description: A lively rosé born of Portugal’s Vinho Verde tradition this NV can of Este Rosé offers radiant hues of pale coral and a vibrant personality rooted in the Minho region’s native Vinhão grape. The wine greets the senses with energetic red‑berry aromas and a playful whisper of gentle effervescence balanced by a lively freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 6–8 °C in a slender flute or tulip to heighten its effervescence, pairing superbly with light seafood, fresh salads or simply enjoyed at a leisurely outdoor gathering.
palate: refreshing, with lively cherry and strawberry tones

name: Susana Esteban a Centenaria Tinto
description: A cherry‑kissed red of elegant poise, the 2022 Susana Esteban A Centenária emerges from a field blend of centenarian vines in the Serra de São Mamede, sculpted by eight months resting in French oak to preserve its identity, freshness and delicate precision. Its allure lies in the interplay of refined tannins and lively red fruit tones promising graceful evolution through the years.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature to highlight its freshness, an ideal companion to roast lamb or grilled mushroom dishes accentuating its subtle tannic structure and nuanced red‑fruit character.
aroma: Fresh cherry with delicate herbal lift
palate: Silky yet firm tannins, red‑berry freshness

name: Susana Esteban Aventura Branco
description: The 2021 Aventura Branco by Susana Esteban emerges from the Alentejo highlands with poised elegance and clarity: its straw‑yellow hue invites a perfume of lavender, orchard‑ripened peach and whispers of herbs, all underscored by a stony minerality. On the palate it shows a sophisticated thread of fullness and freshness, weighty yet refined, culminating in a dry, taut and mineral‑charged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 – 10 °C in a tulip or white wine glass to preserve its freshness; pairs beautifully with grilled sea bream, creamy goat cheese salads or simple steamed shellfish.
aroma: lavender, peach and soft herbaceous tones
palate: fresh yet full‑bodied, stony and refined

name: Susana Esteban Aventura Branco
description: The 2022 Aventura Branco by Susana Esteban emerges from the Alentejo highlands with poised elegance and clarity: its straw‑yellow hue invites a perfume of lavender, orchard‑ripened peach and whispers of herbs, all underscored by a stony minerality. On the palate it shows a sophisticated thread of fullness and freshness, weighty yet refined, culminating in a dry, taut and mineral‑charged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 – 10 °C in a tulip or white wine glass to preserve its freshness; pairs beautifully with grilled sea bream, creamy goat cheese salads or simple steamed shellfish.
aroma: lavender, peach and soft herbaceous tones
palate: fresh yet full‑bodied, stony and refined

name: Susana Esteban Aventura Tinto
description: Susana Esteban’s 2023 Aventura Tinto emerges from Alentejo with an invigorating blend of elegance and spirit, offering vivid red fruit and a touch of florality framed by vibrant freshness and refined structure. The wine is softly textured and polished, carrying an approachable character with the promise of graceful evolution in bottle.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16–18 °C to highlight its lively fruit and floral nuances; pair with grilled pork tenderloin or wild mushroom risotto to complement its freshness and velvety texture.
aroma: fresh red fruit with floral whispers
palate: soft, velvety fruit balanced by vibrant acidity

name: Susana Esteban Aventura Tinto
description: Susana Esteban’s 2023 Aventura Tinto emerges from Alentejo with an invigorating blend of elegance and spirit, offering vivid red fruit and a touch of florality framed by vibrant freshness and refined structure. The wine is softly textured and polished, carrying an approachable character with the promise of graceful evolution in bottle.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16–18 °C to highlight its lively fruit and floral nuances; pair with grilled pork tenderloin or wild mushroom risotto to complement its freshness and velvety texture.
aroma: fresh red fruit with floral whispers
palate: soft, velvety fruit balanced by vibrant acidity

name: Susana Esteban Foudre White
description: A refined white of remarkable pedigree this wine reveals a captivating interplay of granite‑charged minerality and the foudre’s gentle oxidative imprint, offering depth and expansiveness that speak of its 80‑year‑old Serra de São Mamede origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10 to 11 °C to emphasize its mineral clarity and pair with subtly textured dishes such as soft‑curd sheep cheese or delicate oily fish.
palate: broad, deep and mineral

name: 1988 the Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Reserve Library Certified
description: Graceful and age-wise, this wine reveals the quiet poetry of Oregon’s early vinous achievements, offering an ethereal profile of preserved red cherry, dried rose petal and forest floor, all carried with refined clarity and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled in a large Burgundy glass to capture its subtle charm; offers a lyrical pairing with mushroom‑rich dishes or slow‑roasted duck.
aroma: dried rose petal and forest floor
palate: silky texture with preserved cherry elegance

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Daphne
description: A poised expression of Oregon’s storied terroir this Daphne Vineyard Pinot Noir is vibrant and crystalline in structure it features a vivid core of wild strawberry and cranberry intricately laced with herbal underbrush and a hint of citrus zest offering both grace and strength.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its tension pairing beautifully with roasted duck breast or a mushroom‑studded tart.
palate: focused herbal fruit with saline minerality

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir the Eyrie
description: An elegant and finely wrought Pinot Noir that captures the soul of Dundee Hills with layered impressions of rose petal cardamom and wild raspberry, framed by stony mineral undertones and a whisper of cedar.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to enhance its silken texture; pairs beautifully with mushroom‑risotto or roasted duck breast.
palate: minerally, tension‑packed red berried fruit

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Roland Green
description: A poised and radiant expression of Dundee Hills terroir this 2021 Pinot noir from the Roland Green Vineyard unfurls with layered red cherry and wild berry tones laced with lavender and alpine spice, all framed in graceful tannins and vivid acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled for elegance pair with roast duck or wild mushroom risotto to complement its earthy floral symmetry.
palate: savory conifer‑laced flavors, fine‑grained tannins

name: Vineyards Chasselas Dore
description: The 2017 Eyrie Vineyards Chasselas Doré presents a graceful lightness yet a surprising structure, offering a delicate interplay of tropical fruit and savory nuance. There's an elegant brightness reminiscent of poached pear and nectarine, set upon a crisp, stony frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to showcase its clarity; ideal alongside creamy cheeses or subtly spiced dishes.
aroma: poached pear and nectarine with subtle herb
palate: light tropical fruit with savory, stony undercurrent

name: Familia Carvalho-Martins Pacto Douro Tinto
description: A poised expression of modern Douro elegance this 2019 Pacto Douro Tinto by Família Carvalho Martins breathes youthful allure with soft red fruit, subtle floral lift and a fine-grained mineral core, culminating in gentle warmth from judicious maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C to refresh its bright fruit and vibrant mineral spine; an ideal partner to roasted mushroom risotto or grilled pork with herbs.
aroma: red cherry and wild berries with a hint of violet
palate: elegant fruit framed by fine mineral structure

name: Famille Bourgeois Petit Bourgeois Rose of Pinot Noir
description: A luminous pale‑pink rosé of Pinot Noir from the Loire Valley this Petit Bourgeois 2023 captivates with red‑berry ripeness and a maiden rose perfume bolstered by a crisp, welcoming balance
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C; pairs seamlessly with summer salads, grilled white meats, delicate Asian fare or seafood tempura
palate: fresh, crisp with subtle mineral clarity

name: Famille Bourgeois Petit Bourgeois Rose of Pinot Noir
description: A luminous pale‑pink rosé of Pinot Noir from the Loire Valley this Petit Bourgeois 2023 captivates with red‑berry ripeness and a maiden rose perfume bolstered by a crisp, welcoming balance
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C; pairs seamlessly with summer salads, grilled white meats, delicate Asian fare or seafood tempura
palate: fresh, crisp with subtle mineral clarity

name: Famille Gueguen Chablis 1er Cru Vosgros
description: A crystal‑bright Chablis Premier Cru from the talented Céline and Frédéric Gueguen, the 2022 Vosgros unfurls with refined citrus blossom and delicate white‑tea perfume against a chalk‑spiced mineral backdrop. Subtle ripeness adds a whisper of honey‑edged fruit while precise acidity lends structure with elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped white glass, pairing exquisitely with grilled white fish or creamy goat cheese to echo its mineral freshness and silk‑textured fruit.
palate: chalky minerality with honeyed fruit and bright acidity

name: Famille Gueguen Chablis
description: This village‑level Chablis from Famille Guéguen in the 2024 vintage offers refined floral and citrus expression with crystalline minerality and a bright tensile structure that conveys both precision and charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to emphasize clarity and lift: ideal alongside oysters or a light goat‑cheese salad.
palate: saline‑lifted orchard fruit framed by chalky minerality

name: Famille Rotalier Beaujolais Villages sous le Chemin
description: This 2021 Famille Rotalier Beaujolais‑Villages “Sous le Chemin” unveils lusciously ripe black cherry framed by subtle peppery spice, offering an immediate yet nuanced elegance. Its texture is both vibrant and refined with a bright core of dark fruit and a gentle lift of minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a medium tulip glass to amplify its fragrant Gamay clarity; pairs beautifully with charcuterie or roast chicken with herbs.
palate: dark fruit core with minerality

name: Spirits 4 Year Old Roknar Bonded Rye Whiskey
description: Far North Spirits Roknar Bonded Rye is an elegant expression of estate‑grown Minnesota grain distilled in the heart of the north. Its nose greets with soft brown sugar and spicy vanilla weaving through warm oak, its body unfurls with polished grain character and gentle anise‑tinged heat, and the finish lingers with subtle star‑anise warmth and a whisper of pretzel salt.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a rocks glass to underscore its soft spice profile, and pair it with smoked ham or nut‑crusted goat cheese to accentuate its savory sweetness.
aroma: brown sugar, spicy vanilla, warm oak
palate: polished grain, gentle anise heat

name: Spirits Agassiz Vodka
description: A quietly refined vodka drawn from Hazlet winter rye grown on the jet‑black soils once bathed by Ice Age Lake Agassiz, this spirit reflects the character of northern Minnesota in its purity and presence, with a subtle nod to Scandinavian clarity and texture, elegant yet resolute in tone.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender tulip glass or martini, the vodka shines alongside clean seafood, light salads or delicate Nordic‑inspired dishes.
palate: silky and rounded with clean grain clarity

name: Spirits Alander Nordic Style Spiced Rum
description: This Nordic‑style spiced rum unfolds with nuanced warmth: fragrant allspice and nutmeg give way to subtle espresso‑tinged vanilla and butterscotch, finishing with a whisper of caramel and banana‑bread sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or over a large ice cube to admire the spices; excellent with apple‑based desserts or a warmly spiced cake.
palate: espresso‑tinged vanilla and butterscotch

name: Spirits Alander Nordic Style Spiced Rum
description: Alander Nordic‑style Spiced Rum presents an elegant weave of hand‑infused Scandinavian baking spices upon a slender, golden rum base, its nose alive with allspice nutmeg clove and ginger‑snap warmth. On the palate it is deftly poised, inviting root‑beer‑like vanilla and peppermint nuances anchored by a whisper of espresso‑mocha, closing with soft caramel and banana‑bread sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or over a large ice cube to accentuate its spice‑cake charm, and pair with hearty ginger‑bread desserts or dark chocolate tarts.
palate: root beer, vanilla, peppermint, mocha

name: Spirits Bodalen Bourbon Whiskey
description: This single‑estate bourbon exudes an elegant balance of bright sweetness and wintry northern character, with estate‑grown Minnesota heirloom corn and AC Hazlet rye offering both warmth and precision. The aroma brings delicate toffee sweetness and citrus zest while the palate unfolds peppery and vegetal tones grounded in wood‑driven depth. The finish is long and rich with lingering dark chocolate and brown sugar.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature neat or with a single clear ice cube so the rye spice and nuanced sweetness bloom with minimal dilution.
palate: Peppery vegetal entry with woodsy depth
finish: Long, rich and persistent with dark chocolate and brown sugar

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: A fearless Navy‑strength gin crafted grain‑to‑glass from winter rye in Minnesota this Gustaf offers bold and spirited balance. The aromatic weave of meadowsweet thyme cucumber and vanilla frames an assertive rye‑driven backbone for an engaging contemporary profile.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or lightly diluted to temper its 114‑proof heat, pairing beautifully with a crisp tonic or in a minimalist martini to surface subtle herbal and citrus notes.
aroma: meadowsweet thyme cucumber with a rye‑grain hum
palate: fiery rye warmth softened by fennel citrus pepper and vanilla
finish: dry herbal linger with gentle anise warmth

name: Spirits Gustaf Navy Strength Gin
description: This fearless Navy‑strength gin stands proudly at 114 proof offering a bold tapestry of botanicals. Delicate lavender and juniper weave through hints of yuzu‑like citrus while fennel and licorice add spicy depth and enduring character.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a large clear ice cube in a chilled copa glass lightly twisted with lemon zest or in a bold Gimlet where its intensity holds firm.
aroma: lavender and juniper with citrus lift
palate: spicy fennel and warming rye‑driven heat
drinkWindow: Drink now to enjoy its vibrant proof‑driven intensity

name: Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey
description: An elegant expression of cold‑climate terroir this estate‑grown rye whiskey reveals refined warmth and layered grace. Its character is grounded in rich Minnesota soil and her celebrated AC Hazlet winter rye, offering a balance of gentle spice and soft sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly above cellar temperature to unlock fragrant vanilla warmth. Pairs beautifully with hearty cheeses or spiced autumn desserts.
palate: butter‑smooth with roasted almonds and vanilla

name: Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey
description: Far North Spirits Roknar Minnesota Rye Whiskey presents itself with a whisper of northern prairie heritage tempered by thoughtful aging. Gentle aromas of brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla bean and freshly sawn oak lead into a plush, butter‑smooth palate with nuanced echoes of smoked ham and soft-baked pretzel. The result is an elegant expression that balances grain‑forward complexity with warming spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat or with a single large ice cube to allow its layered flavors to unfurl, particularly in rye‑centric cocktails like a Manhattan or Old Fashioned.
aroma: brown sugar, cinnamon, vanilla bean, sawn oak
palate: butter‑smooth, smoked ham, balsa wood

name: Spirits Solveig Anna's Garden Gin
description: A seasonal springtime gin that unfolds bright herbal complexity with a flourish of hibiscus, dill, lemon zest and cardamom awakening the senses with both freshness and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tall Collins glass over ice with tonic or in a light spritz to complement fresh salads or mild seafood dishes.
palate: earthy angelica with cardamom warmth

name: Spirits Solveig Anna's Garden Gin
description: This seasonal gin from Far North Spirits unfurls with herbaceous dill at the forefront, tempered by the earthiness of angelica and lifted by zesty lemon notes. Its pale blue hue and delicate profile evoke an early spring garden kissed by morning dew, offering a graceful yet complex canvas for cocktails.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tall, slim glass with a lemon twist or pair with cucumber‑infused tonic to accentuate the gin’s herbal brightness.
palate: earthy angelica balanced with fresh citrus lift

name: Spirits Solveig Gin
description: Far North Spirits Solveig Gin is an ethereal, contemporary gin distilled grain‑to‑glass from estate‑grown Hazlet winter rye. Vibrant citrus and lavender botanicals mesh with herbal thyme and a whisper of pine in an elegant, refined expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a stemmed Riedel or delicate coupette to appreciate its lifted aromatics or stir into a light gin and tonic with a twist of grapefruit to elevate its brightness.
aroma: citrus and lavender with a hint of pine
palate: creamy lightness with thyme and coriander mid‑palate
finish: cool, lingering grain and olive‑tinged grace
foodPairings: fresh oysters on the half shell

name: Spirits Solveig Gin
description: Lush and verdant, this gin unfolds with bright citrus and aromatic pine on the nose, underpinned by a whisper of lavender, creating an impression of early summer on the prairie. The palate enters creamy yet weightless, evolving with herbaceous thyme and coriander before settling into a rich, lingering tapestry of fresh grain and olive‑tinged warmth.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or in a minimalist martini to allow its delicate botanical interplay to shine, or pair with light seafood or roasted root vegetables to complement its herbal brightness.
aroma: citrus and pine with lavender whisper
palate: creamy yet ethereal evolving with thyme and coriander
finish: rich persistent with olive and fresh grain notes

name: Pinot Noir Bannockburn Central Otago
description: An ethereal yet powerful expression from four Bannockburn vineyards offering a fragrant potpourri of dark petals and Indian spices, underpinned by black cherry fruit and silky, chocolate-tinged tannins conveying both depth and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14–15 °C in a Tulip‑shaped glass, ideally paired with roast duck or mushroom risotto to mirror the wine’s dark fruit and savoury complexity.
palate: black cherry fruit with silky, chocolate‑laden tannins

name: Pinot Noir Block 3 Central Otago
description: A magnetic Pinot Noir with tension and poise, this Felton Road Block 3 2024 delivers cascades of dark cherry, mocha and leather, threaded through with floral spice and herbal complexity. It shows formidable structure yet maintains clarity and elegance true to its Bannockburn origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a large tulip glass at cellar temperature to allow its layered fruit and structure to unfold; pairs especially well with venison or mushroom‑based dishes.
palate: deep dark fruit framed by structured tannins

name: Pinot Noir Block 5 Central Otago
description: A seamless expression of Bannockburn’s finest, crowned by elegance and refinement. The wine unfurls gently then blooms like a peacock’s tail with poised power, polished fruit and silk‑laden tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in large-bowled Pinot Noir glasses to best showcase its aromatic perfume and graceful structure. Pairs beautifully with roasted duck, mushroom‑accented dishes or herb‑crusted lamb.
aroma: Floral perfume of raspberry rose petal and dark cherry
palate: Silky, seamless texture with poised acidity and refined power

palate: Silky, seamless texture with poised acidity and refined power

name: Pinot Noir Calvert Central Otago
description: This 2020 Felton Road Calvert Pinot Noir emanates from a single vineyard in the clay‑rich soils of Bannockburn in Central Otago, revealing a perfume of ripe summer cherries, mulberry and forest floor that is finely laced with peppercorn spice and sandalwood. The palate is tightly wound yet vibrant, with pure bright acidity and supple tannins offering elegant structure and poised density.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large tulip glass to highlight its floral and herbal perfume. Ideal with roast duck, wild mushrooms or modestly spiced game dishes.
aroma: berry‑driven with cherry, mulberry, forest floor and peppercorn spice
palate: tense yet juicy with bright acidity, firm tannins, sandalwood spice
