name: Pinot Noir Cornish Point Centra L Otago
description: The 2020 Felton Road Cornish Point Pinot Noir presents an elegant yet potent expression of Central Otago terroir. It unfurls restrained floral aromas of lavender and violets interwoven with dark plum, clove and a whisper of dark chocolate, while fine tannins lend a velvety texture and underlying structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in a large Burgundy glass to invite the perfume, and pair with roasted lamb, duck with cherry glaze or wild mushroom risotto to complement its spice and depth.
aroma: lavender and violets with dark plum and clove
palate: brooding black plum, mocha, spice, velvety tannins
foodPairings: slow‑roasted lamb with rosemary and garlic

name: Pinot Noir Cornish Point Central Otago
description: An exceptionally perfumed and sensuous Pinot Noir that unfolds with red cherry and black cherry lifted by violet and fresh strawberry aromas and threaded with hints of baking spice The palate is concentrated yet polished with silky fine tannins that provide structure and length, delivering a caressing finish
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass and pair with roasted duck breast or earthy mushrooms to complement its floral spice and refined fruit
palate: concentrated with silky fine tannins and baking spice

name: Pinot Noir Cornish Point Central Otago
description: An exceptionally perfumed and sensuous Pinot Noir that unfolds with red cherry and black cherry lifted by violet and fresh strawberry aromas and threaded with hints of baking spice The palate is concentrated yet polished with silky fine tannins that provide structure and length, delivering a caressing finish
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass and pair with roasted duck breast or earthy mushrooms to complement its floral spice and refined fruit
palate: concentrated with silky fine tannins and baking spice

name: Pinot Noir Macmuir Central Otago
description: In a refined medley of brooding poise and subtle bloom, the 2022 MacMuir Pinot Noir unveils layers of plush berry and violet nostalgia beneath a silken yet structured frame that gently expands over time. It speaks of restrained power and terroir expression, offering a tapestry of depth that invites contemplative enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature in a tulip glass to reveal its fragrant complexity; pairs beautifully with mushroom‑dusted venison or roasted duck for elegant harmony.
palate: silken structure framed by fine‑grained tannins

name: Pinot Noir Macmuir Central Otago
description: In a refined medley of brooding poise and subtle bloom, the 2024 MacMuir Pinot Noir unveils layers of plush berry and violet nostalgia beneath a silken yet structured frame that gently expands over time. It speaks of restrained power and terroir expression, offering a tapestry of depth that invites contemplative enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature in a tulip glass to reveal its fragrant complexity; pairs beautifully with mushroom‑dusted venison or roasted duck for elegant harmony.
palate: silken structure framed by fine‑grained tannins

name: Wines Pinot Noir Block 3 Central Otago
description: An intensely perfumed Central Otago Pinot Noir that marries wild thyme, peony and crushed blackberry with subtle spice and mineral undercurrents, beautifully framed by fine powdery tannins and lifted bright acid. There is a layered richness of dark fruit and gentle chocolate nuances held in check by a refined structure that draws you in
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its herbal nuance and pair with herb‑roasted duck or mushroom risotto that echo its woodland character
palate: silky texture, dark fruit, spice, chocolate

name: Wines Pinot Noir Block 5 Central Otago
description: The 2021 Felton Road Block 5 Pinot Noir evokes the clarity of crushed red cherry laced with rose petals and a whisper of exotic spice, framed by crystalline acidity and a refined tannic structure. It offers an elegant, poised expression of Bannockburn’s north‑facing slopes, with precise depth that unfolds gracefully.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large Burgundy glass to accentuate its perfume and fine structure, pairing beautifully with duck breast, mushroom‑dominated dishes or soft‑boiled egg with truffle butter.
aroma: crushed red cherry, rose petal, white pepper
palate: bright acidity, fine dusty tannins, slate‑tinged fruit

name: Wines Pinot Noir Calvert Central Otago
description: An elegant pinot noir revealing perfumed florals of rose petal and violet entwined with Indian spice and savory earth tones. The dark fruit core—plum, pomegranate and cherry—unfolds with finely chiseled tannins in sublime harmony of site expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a large tulip glass to coax forth its floral perfume; pairs exquisitely with roasted duck, wild mushrooms or a herbed porcini risotto.
palate: dark berry core with spice and savory earth
finish: finely chiseled tannins leading to smooth length

name: Wines Pinot Noir Cornish Point Central Otago
description: A refined expression of Central Otago’s distinctive Cornish Point terroir this 2021 Pinot Noir offers an elegant weave of violet floral whispers and concentrated dark plum framed by subtle oriental spice tones, crescendoing into a poised yet powerful presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar cool temperature to preserve its vibrant acidity and pair with earthy game or poached poultry for balanced harmony.
aroma: violet and dark plum with a hint of distant wood smoke
palate: concentrated dark cherry and cassis with oriental spice and subtle nutty oak
finish: lengthy, with tangy acidity and echo of smoke and apple seed

name: Fernand et Fils Coteaux du Giennois
description: A fine expression of Coteaux du Giennois délicately fashioned from Sauvignon blanc the 2020 vintage reveals luminous clarity and poised freshness It offers a refined interplay of zesty citrus and orchard fruit with a whisper of minerality
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled to accentuate its bright acidity and pair with shellfish or creamy goat cheese for graceful harmony
palate: crisp, mineral‑tinged with vibrant fruit

name: Italia Prosecco DOC Extra Dry
description: An elegant nonvintage Prosecco from Filare Italia offering a gentle orchestration of orchard blossoms and crisp green fruit with a delicate mousse that evokes old‑world charm and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its vivacity, perfect as an aperitif or with light seafood hors d’œuvres.
palate: bright citrus and pear

name: Crazy Grapes
description: This 2018 Finca Bacara Crazy Grapes is a nocturnal Monastrell, swathed in deep purple hue with earthy dark fruit aromas lifted by a smoky whisper and a streak of clove‑tinged chocolate. On the palate it feels dense yet animated, with blackened plum and mocha notes supported by a plush, resonant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature to enhance its freshness—beautiful with herb‑accented grilled lamb or a rich porcini risotto.
palate: Dense, black plum and mocha

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Finca la Mata Do Ribera Del Duero
description: Finca La Mata 2023 from Isaac Fernandez Seleccíon offers a noble expression of Ribera del Duero’s ancient Tinta de Toro vines framed in subtle oak, delivering polished dark cherry and earthy nuance in an assured, elegant style. Its tone is refined with a measured structure that hints at both immediate charm and graceful evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature, ideal with grilled red meats or aged Manchego cheese to enhance its fruit depth and supple tannins.
aroma: dark cherry and pomegranate with cedary oak
palate: full‑bodied, ripe tannins with mineral grip

name: Anecoop Flare Sparkling Moscatel Do Valencia
description: An effervescent jewel from Valencia this nonvintage Flare Sparkling Moscatel captures the sheer radiance of Muscat of Alexandria with bright pear and lychee notes kissed by white floral nuance and a whisper of spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender flute to highlight its playful sparkle; pairs beautifully with fresh fruit, light pastries or as a celebratory aperitif.
aroma: pear and lychee with white florals
palate: sweet tropical fruit with mineral lift
finish: bright and refreshing with spice accents

name: Fleur de Pedesclaux Pauillac
description: Elegant Pauillac refinement emerges in the 2022 Fleur de Pédesclaux, where violet-tinged black fruit and subtle floral whispers mingle with gently polished tannins, evoking a second wine of both immediacy and noble poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve just slightly cool at cellar temperature in fine Bordeaux glasses, pairing beautifully with braised beef or aged sheep’s cheese to elevate its poised freshness.
palate: silky black‑berry and plum framed by refined tannins

name: Az Agr Fontanacota Vermentino Riviera Ligure Di Ponente
description: This 2023 Vermentino from Fontanacota greets the eye with a pale straw hue and offers an enchanting interplay of dried orchard fruit, citrus bloom and deep minerality. It unfolds with gentle viscosity and vibrant balance drawing the taster into a refined Ligurian expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip glass to allow the citrus and saline nuances to breathe; pairs beautifully with seafood crudo or herb‑bright vegetable dishes.
palate: round, viscous, mouthwatering acidity
foodPairings: lean fish with olive oil drizzle

name: Priorat
description: A supple and radiant Priorat garnacha‑carinena that captures the sun‑baked minerals of slate soil, showing gently spiced dark cherry fruit and an undertone of smoky herbal garrigue, wrapped in smooth fine tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 16 °C in medium‑bodied Bordeaux or Burgundy style glasses: a fine match for roast lamb or aged Manchego cheese.
palate: garrigue‑tinged fruit, refined tannins

name: Chateau de Fosse Seche Saumur Blanc Arcane A.o.c
description: The 2016 Château de Fosse‑Sèche Arcane Saumur Blanc is a Chenin Blanc shaped by silex‑rich soils that impart a pronounced mineral clarity and an aromatic whisper of white flowers, quince and honey, unfolding with elegant restraint and old‑world precision. Its presence is refined rather than flamboyant, offering subtle power and crystalline focus that speak of its Loire terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled at 9–12 °C after gentle aeration to open floral lift and mineral drive; pair with oysters, sole meunière or goat cheeses to echo the wine’s freshness and subtle floral tones.
palate: fresh, mineral‑driven, poised

name: Francois Mikulski Beaune 1ER Cru Blanc les Greves
description: The 2023 François Mikulski Beaune 1er Cru Les Grèves Blanc unfolds with a pale golden clarity and a palpable limestone freshness that conjures the sensation of snow and fragile floral petals. The interplay of delicately restrained orchard fruit and brioche undertones gives way to vibrant citrus and saline precision, leaving an impression of refined density without overt flamboyance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accentuate its talcy minerality and pair with butter-poached turbot or scallop and cep mushroom pie to mirror its richness and freshness.
aroma: restrained orchard fruit with alpine florals
palate: citrus‑saline precision layered over brioche

name: Francois Mikulski Bourgogne Chardonnay
description: A refined regional Chardonnay that embodies all the grace of a Meursault’s periphery: pale gold in hue, it unfolds with luminous clarity offering a gentle yet evident presence in the glass, while the palate is supple and ample with a core of generous pear and citrus quietly supported by subtle spice
sommelierNotes: Serve at 10 °C to 12 °C in classic Burgundy stemware, ideally with dishes such as veal Milanese or creamy risotto to complement its textural richness
palate: silky, generous, gently spiced
finish: long, spiced citrus with saline tension
foodPairings: soft cheese such as Brie de Meaux

name: Francois Mikulski Bourgogne Hautes Cotes de Beaune Blanc
description: A pale gold Chardonnay of refined energy showing a luminous core of pear and white peach fused with shimmering white florals such as lily of the valley and freesia, enlivened by a whisper of citron honey and green grass just moistened by rain.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to bring out the poised citrus tension; harmonious with delicate cold‑water fish or a parsley‑buttered razor‑clam gratin.
palate: spiced pear and mandarin with herbal poise
foodPairings: chilled brown crab with Espelette pepper mayonnaise
in a few years: calf’s head with gribiche sauce

name: Francois Mikulski Bourgogne Hautes Cotes de Beaune Blanc
description: A pale gold Chardonnay of refined energy showing a luminous core of pear and white peach fused with shimmering white florals such as lily of the valley and freesia, enlivened by a whisper of citron honey and green grass just moistened by rain.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to bring out the poised citrus tension; harmonious with delicate cold‑water fish or a parsley‑buttered razor‑clam gratin.
palate: spiced pear and mandarin with herbal poise
foodPairings: chilled brown crab with Espelette pepper mayonnaise
in a few years: calf’s head with gribiche sauce

name: Francois Mikulski Meursault 1er Cru les Charmes Vieilles Vignes
appellation: Meursault 1er Cru Les Charmes Vieilles Vignes
description: The 2020 François Mikulski Meursault 1er Cru Les Charmes Vieilles Vignes unveils a radiant cascade of candied white fruits layered with honeyed almond oil and subtle pastry nuance, all grounded in limestone‑tinged minerality that imparts elegance and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve after gentle decanting to allow air to release its spicy citrus lift; shines with rich shellfish or delicate poultry preparations.
palate: opulent white fruit, spice‑laced citrus, creamy texture

name: Francois Mikulski Meursault
description: A pale golden Meursault from François Mikulski, the 2023 bottling unfolds with mineral precision and an airy elegance. Refined citrus and white fruit notes drift from the glass, underpinned by subtle hints of marjoram, bergamot and chalky limestone.
sommelierNotes: Best decanted and served cool, this Meursault will reward gentle cheeses and seafood in buttery sauces; allow six to eight years in the cellar for full harmony.
aroma: fine herbs, white fruits, citrus, chalk dust
palate: broad and expressive citrus and spice
finish: precise, intense, lingering with salty empyreumatic note
foodPairings: double veal chop in sautéed style

name: Francois Mikulski Meursault les Meix Chavaux
description: This 2023 François Mikulski Meursault Les Meix Chavaux glistens with a light gold hue tinged with lime juice, offering an ethereally refined nose of fine herbs such as coriander and chervil, spring flowers, and hints of anise and lavender overlaying airy orchard fruits of white peach, pear and apple; the palate is precise yet intense, with white‑fruit coulis mingled with delicate green and white pepper, juniper, clove and liquorice, all framed by vivid minerality and consummate balance. At once charming and structured this is a wine built for both immediate grace and long‑term unfolding.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C with refined seafood dishes in 5 to 10 years, such as langoustines in citrus butter or scallops in herb‑infused beurre blanc, or age further for lactic complexity to accompany grilled sole or lobster with subtle creamy sauces.
aroma: Fine herbs, spring flowers, delicate white peach and pear
palate: White‑fruit coulis, refined spice, saline minerality
finish: Precise, energetic length with spiced citrus and mineral focus
foodPairings: Grilled sole with delicate creamy sauce
Roasted lobster with subtle herb emulsion

name: Dr Konstantin Frank Dry Rose
description: A luminous 2024 Dry Rosé from Dr Konstantin Frank Winery in the Finger Lakes presents itself like an artisanal fresco in a glass: seven grape varieties interlace to deliver vibrant red fruit clarity with underlying textural grace, while its steel-fermented purity preserves an enchanting, lithe elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to accentuate its balance, perfect alongside light charcuterie or delicate seafood fare.
aroma: bright red berries with citrus lift
palate: layered, generous yet poised

name: Dr Konstantin Frank Semi Dry Riesling
description: A delicate and alluring Riesling born of the storied Finger Lakes tradition, the 2024 Semi‑Dry Riesling from Dr. Konstantin Frank entwines ripe apricot and honeydew melon aromas with a graceful mineral undertone, offering a refined expression of semi‑dry elegance and vivacious freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a slender tulip‑shaped glass alongside lightly spiced Asian fare or fresh seafood to accentuate its bright acidity and subtle sweetness.
aroma: ripe apricot, honeydew melon, delicate floral tones
palate: balanced sweetness and vibrant acidity with tropical and stone fruit layers
finish: long, persistent finish with fruit and mineral linger

name: Weingut Franz Hirtzberger Riesling Hochrain Smaragd
description: A crystalline expression of Wachau Riesling, this 2018 Hochrain Smaragd offers lifted notes of yellow stone fruit and mandarin zest with a whisper of floral perfume, all cast in an elegant, finely chiselled frame of layered extract and poised energy. The texture is silky, the fruit precise, driven by a tensile acidity that carries through to a long, seamless finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C to reveal its intricate fruit and mineral finesse, ideal alongside refined fare such as buttered sole, veal scaloppine or subtly spiced river fish.
aroma: yellow stone fruit and mandarin zest with floral perfume
palate: silky texture, layered extract, poised energy
finish: long, seamless with white fruit nuances

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Alexander Valley
description: A velvety Cabernet Sauvignon from Gabrielle Ashley’s 2020 Alexander Valley, presenting a refined ribbon of black fruits and subtle forest‑floor nuances allied to gentle oak tones
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in a large Bordeaux glass, and pair with grilled lamb or aged cheddar to accentuate the wine’s understated complexity
palate: smooth black fruit framed by soft oak

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve Napa Valley
description: This 2020 Gabrielle Ashley Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve from Napa Valley presents a richly fruit‑driven elegance reflecting its appellation and the skillful hand at Precision Wine Company. Generous notes of black cherry, cassis and plum unfold alongside subtle vanilla and toast from harmonious oak aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to preserve freshness. Pair with grilled red meats or aged cheese for a classic Napa expression.
aroma: ripe black cherry and cassis with vanilla and toasty oak
palate: lush plum and blueberry fruit wrapped in velvety tannins
finish: long silky finish with spice and toast

name: Jn Gagnard Santenay 1er Cru Clos Tavannes
description: This wine offers refined aromas of delicate red cherry and subtle forest floor, unfolding into a medium-bodied, silk‑textured palate with elegant structure and gentle spice nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in slender Burgundy stems: lovely with gently roasted duck breast or autumnal mushroom fricassee.
palate: silky texture, gentle spice

name: Grenache Noir
description: The 2017 Galil Grenache Noir from Upper Galilee unfolds gracefully with a fine weave of red cherry, wild raspberry, and subtle rose petal, framed by an earthy spice through elegant restraint and old‑world poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 14–16 C to highlight its bright fruit and floral nuance; pair with rustic lamb stew or wild mushroom risotto to complement its spice and earth tones.
palate: wild raspberry with earthy spice

name: Merlot
description: This 2017 Merlot from Galil Mountain presents vivid black plum and blackberry fruits set against a weaving of clove, tobacco leaf and herbal underbrush, held together by soft framing oak. The wine wears its Mediterranean heritage with grace, offering depth without brashness.
sommelierNotes: Best served at cellar cool temperatures, it finds harmony with grilled lamb chops or herb‐roasted pork shoulder, where its savory and fruit tones complement each other.
palate: smooth blackberry with clove and gentle oak

name: Mountain Winery Blanc de Noir
description: This Blanc de Noir 2020 from Galil Mountain Winery unfurls with a pale, ethereal hue and a finely wrought texture showcasing hand‑picked Pinot Noir pressed as a delicate white. It evokes gentle orchard fruit framed by a whisper of citrus and refined minerality, all carried with a poised, lithe elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its brightness, pairing beautifully with light fish dishes or creamy soft cheeses.
palate: light texture with mineral lift

name: Winery Rose
description: A lithe and graceful rosé sculpted from Sangiovese, Cabernet Sauvignon and Barbera grown high in the Upper Galilee, revealing a delicate pink hue and a clarity of bright red fruit that dances across the palate
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an aperitif or alongside light summer fare such as goat cheese salads or grilled seafood, its refreshing acidity offering a refined counterpoint
palate: crisp wild red fruits with citrus lift

name: Mountain Winery Aviv Red
description: This youthful Galil Mountain Aviv Red delivers an exuberant harmony of red cherry and berry fruit wrapped in gentle spice, framed by subtle oak-aged warmth. It is vibrant and approachable, yet carries an undercurrent of Galilean structure and freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cooled for elegance; pairs particularly well with herb‑roasted chicken or tomato‑sauced pasta.
palate: fresh berry with oak nuance

name: Mountain Winery Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A youthful Cabernet Sauvignon from Israel’s Upper Galilee, this 2023 bottling unfolds with vivid blackberry, plum jam and black cherry fruit, accented by mint and tobacco leaf hints, all presented with clarity and refreshing energy without oak influence.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool, around 60–65 °F, to enhance its vivacious fruit; it pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops or braised beef.
palate: medium‑full, fruit‑driven with soft tannins

name: Mountain Winery Syrah
description: A richly textured Syrah from the heights of Upper Galilee, this 2023 Galil Mountain Winery offering unfolds aromatic notes of blackberry and mint underscored by a gentle earthiness, framed in a smooth, medium‑to‑full body that lingers with refined subtlety
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to cellar temperature alongside grilled steak or spicy kebabs to echo its savory undertones, or allow it to breathe for enhanced aromatic lift
aroma: blackberry and mint with a hint of earth
palate: medium‑full body, smooth and expressive

name: Mountain Winery Yiron
description: This wine offers a regal presence of dark berry and plum tapestry enriched by subtle waves of vanilla and clove, all cradled in a frame of gently toasted French oak, lending it poised depth and old‑world elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60°F in large tulip glasses to allow its layered fruit and spice to unfurl; pairs beautifully with grilled steak or rich game ragout.
palate: plush plum and cherry underpinned by savory spice

name: Mountrain Winery Aviv White
description: An aromatic Galilean white bearing the youthful charm its name evokes, this 2024 Aviv White blends Viognier’s soft stone fruit character with Sauvignon Blanc’s crisp vitality, delivering a fragrant serenade of citrus blossom, ripe peach and nectarine, all lifted by a fresh, invigorating energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled alongside lightly dressed salads, grilled seafood or as a bright aperitif to awaken the palate.
palate: fragrant fruit vitality with balanced acidity

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: A graceful expression of Galilee Sauvignon Blanc from the 2015 vintage, this wine unfolds with delicate citrus and green apple notes lifted by a hint of tropical nuance guiding the palate. The style feels youthful and finely structured, offering a clean and refreshing impression that reflects the cool vineyard origin.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled alongside light fish, goat cheese, or spring salads to complement its bright acidity and elegant fruit tones.
palate: crisp tropical whisper

name: Yiftah Vineyard
description: This 2015 Galil Mountain Yiftah Vineyard Merlot‑Petit Verdot is richly concentrated yet graceful, its deep purple hue yielding an impression of black‑forest fruit, supported by nuances of vanilla and a hint of coffee toast from extended oak ageing. It reveals an underpinning of velvet tannins and a harmonious texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to release aromas, ideally with herb‑accented lamb or aged cheese to balance its richness.
aroma: black‑forest fruits with vanilla and coffee oak
palate: rich, concentrated, velvety tannins

name: Château Gautoul Cahors
description: This Cahors Malbec from Château Gautoul, vintage 2012, unfurls inky and robust with generous dark-fruit depth, whispers of truffle and dark chocolate, and poised tannins that speak of its Lot Valley origin
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly decanted at cellar cool, alongside hearty fare such as slow‑braised lamb or cassoulet, to temper its structure while highlighting its savory fruit
aroma: cassis and blackberry with truffle undertones
palate: rich dark‑fruit core, firm yet ripe tannins

name: Ancestral Red
description: This Gen5 2024 Ancestral Red presents a richly inviting tapestry of wild blackberry and blueberry pie accented by gentle mocha and baking spices, offering a creamy texture and velvety finish that recalls classic old‑world reds with modern California generosity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below ambient temperature in generous stemware to reveal its layered fruit and spice, perfect alongside grilled lamb chops or mushroom‑infused pasta.
palate: creamy dark fruit, gentle baking spice

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This California Cabernet Sauvignon, fashioned from sustainably tended estate vineyards in Lodi by the Lange family, presents a gracious harmony of black‑currant and cassis underpinned by subtle oak spice, its texture generous and inviting yet balanced.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature or briefly decanted alongside grilled steak, aged Gouda, or mushroom‑rich dishes.
aroma: black‑currant and cassis with toasted vanilla
palate: plush, balanced texture with dark fruit and gentle oak spice

name: Chardonnay
description: A radiant expression of Lodi’s estate‑grown fruit, this youthful 2024 Gen5 Chardonnay offers juicy pear and apple notes framed by gentle vanilla and subtle oak. The wine’s bright acidity and clean, poised structure speak to sustainable farming and thoughtful winemaking.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled to highlight its crisp orchard fruit character: it is an elegant companion to roasted chicken or light seafood.
aroma: ripe pear and golden apple with a suggestion of vanilla
palate: medium‑bodied, lively citrus‑tinged fruit layered with smooth texture

name: Merlot
description: This 2024 GEN5 Merlot offers a gentle introduction to Lodi’s fruit‑driven style, unveiling ripe cherry and plum aromas with a whisper of soft spice, all wrapped in a smooth, broadly textured frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to about 60‑64 °F in a standard red glass to highlight its juicy fruit and supple texture, pairing nicely with grilled meats or roasted vegetables.
aroma: ripe cherry and plum with a hint of spice
palate: smooth, fruit‑driven texture

name: Pinot Noir
description: An engaging California Pinot Noir, ripe in red cherry and raspberry underpinned by subtle cola spice and gentle oak, all woven into a soft, medium‑bodied frame reflective of Lodi’s warmth and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tulip glass around 55–60°F, ideal alongside roasted chicken or creamy mushroom risotto.
aroma: ripe cherry and raspberry with cola spice
palate: juicy red‑berry flavors with silky tannins
finish: supple medium‑bodied finish with baking‑spice lift

name: Pinot Noir
description: An engaging California Pinot Noir, ripe in red cherry and raspberry underpinned by subtle cola spice and gentle oak, all woven into a soft, medium‑bodied frame reflective of Lodi’s warmth and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a tulip glass around 55–60°F, ideal alongside roasted chicken or creamy mushroom risotto.
aroma: ripe cherry and raspberry with cola spice
palate: juicy red‑berry flavors with silky tannins
finish: supple medium‑bodied finish with baking‑spice lift

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: Bright Lodi‑grown Sauvignon Blanc lifted by crisp citrus and tropical nuances elegant in its simplicity with a whisper of white florals and Lodi breeze freshness
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled with light seafood or goat cheese to showcase its vibrant acidity and clean style
palate: bright, crisp, clean

name: Zinfandel
description: Generations of Lange family stewardship in Lodi yield a Zinfandel of deep ruby hue and resonant fruit character: ripe blackberry and boysenberry meld with subtle smoky spice and earthy undertones in a wine that is both generous and poised.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to accentuate its lively freshness, ideal with chargrilled meats or richly seasoned ragù.
palate: velvety dark fruit, soft tannins

name: Domaine Gerard Mugneret Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A refined yet welcoming Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Gérard Mugneret, vintage 2012, that speaks with clarity and youthful freshness. It shows a deep ruby hue and a vibrant, fruit-driven manner, supported by a silk‑textured structure and the varietal’s characteristic precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a tulip flute to reveal red berry brightness. Pair with softly seasoned pork sausages, roasted meats or mild cheeses, enjoying within a few years of release.
aroma: bright red berry and subtle floral lift
palate: silky texture with fresh red fruit clarity

name: Domaine Gerard Mugneret Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A refined yet welcoming Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Gérard Mugneret, vintage 2013, that speaks with clarity and youthful freshness. It shows a deep ruby hue and a vibrant, fruit-driven manner, supported by a silk‑textured structure and the varietal’s characteristic precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a tulip flute to reveal red berry brightness. Pair with softly seasoned pork sausages, roasted meats or mild cheeses, enjoying within a few years of release.
aroma: bright red berry and subtle floral lift
palate: silky texture with fresh red fruit clarity

name: Domaine Gerard Mugneret Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: A refined yet welcoming Bourgogne Pinot Noir from Gérard Mugneret, vintage 2014, that speaks with clarity and youthful freshness. It shows a deep ruby hue and a vibrant, fruit-driven manner, supported by a silk‑textured structure and the varietal’s characteristic precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C in a tulip flute to reveal red berry brightness. Pair with softly seasoned pork sausages, roasted meats or mild cheeses, enjoying within a few years of release.
aroma: bright red berry and subtle floral lift
palate: silky texture with fresh red fruit clarity

name: Domaine Gerard Tremblay Chablis
description: This 2022 Chablis from Domaine Gérard Tremblay unfolds with crystalline clarity and an elemental purity rooted in its storied terroir, offering subtle white‑peach and tilleul‑inflected florality atop a mineral spine of flint and oyster shell.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C to reveal its vivacious acidity and saline nuance; ideal with delicate seafood or creamy coastal cheeses.
palate: crisp citrus framed by stony minerality

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Yountville Ghost Block Vineyard
description: This wine reveals classic Napa Valley poise presenting notes of blackberry compote, plum jam and red and black currant with elegant whispers of crème de cassis and vanilla, all carried by silky tannins that balance bramble fruit with warm fall spice nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in large Bordeaux glasses with herb‑crusted lamb or dry‑aged ribeye, or enjoy alongside wild mushroom risotto or aged Gouda.
palate: silky tannins, bramble fruit, integrated oak
foodPairings: dry‑aged ribeye with roasted root vegetables

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Yountville Ghost Block Vineyard
description: This wine reveals classic Napa Valley poise presenting notes of blackberry compote, plum jam and red and black currant with elegant whispers of crème de cassis and vanilla, all carried by silky tannins that balance bramble fruit with warm fall spice nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in large Bordeaux glasses with herb‑crusted lamb or dry‑aged ribeye, or enjoy alongside wild mushroom risotto or aged Gouda.
palate: silky tannins, bramble fruit, integrated oak
foodPairings: dry‑aged ribeye with roasted root vegetables

name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This 2021 Ghost Block Estate Cabernet Sauvignon displays a deep ruby red color with concentrated aromas of blackcurrant, blackberry and ripe plum layered over whispers of cedar, vanilla and dark chocolate, framed by finely integrated oak. The palate reveals velvety tannins with elegant fruit purity and a harmonious balance that carries through to a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature after gentle decanting to unveil its full aromatic spectrum; it pairs beautifully with grilled rib‑eye or aged hard cheeses.
palate: Silky tannins with pure dark fruit

name: Estate Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Ghost Block Estate Cabernet Sauvignon emerges from the storied Rock Cairn Vineyard in Oakville, Napa Valley yielding a wine of layered elegance and brooding dark fruit perfume. Silky yet structured, the palate balances ripe blackberry and cassis with a counterpoint of tobacco and cedar that underscores its Old World poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in large-bowled glasses decanted for an hour. Ideal alongside herb‑crusted lamb or aged cheeses at the height of its synergy.
palate: silky dark fruit with cedar and spice

name: Estate Zinfandel Napa Valley Pelissa Vineyard
description: A compelling Napa Valley Zinfandel from the renowned Pelissa Vineyard this 2023 Ghost Block Estate Zinfandel unfolds with sumptuous dark fruit and warm spice, its expression rich yet refined, embodying both vibrancy and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve with grilled or barbecue fare at cellar temperature to highlight its brambly fruit and spice, or decant briefly for enhanced openness.
aroma: ripe black cherry, plum, baking spice
palate: velvety texture with blackberry, black cherry, nutmeg
finish: long lingering spice and dark fruit

name: Ghost Block Morgaen Lee Sauvignon Blanc Napa Valley
description: A luminous expression of Yountville Napa Valley Sauvignon Blanc from Ghost Block’s revered MorgaenLee Vineyard, the 2024 vintage presents a perfume of lemon blossom peach and jasmine accented by a whisper of wet stone. The palate unfolds with poised citrus threads of grapefruit and guava layered over pear and golden apple, culminating in a refined vibrant finish that feels both lively and elegant.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 48–52 °F in a tulip glass to accentuate its aromatic lift; this Sauvignon Blanc partners beautifully with simply grilled prawns or a salad of heirloom tomato and burrata.
palate: grapefruit, guava, pear
foodPairings: fresh oysters on the half shell

name: Vigneti Giacomo Boveri Croatina Firangiuli
description: This 2014 Croatina Firangiuli emerges from the storied Colli Tortonesi vineyards of Vigneti Giacomo Boveri offering a noble expression of the Croatina grape, where firm structure meets velvety tannins and rustic red fruit character in an elegant embrace.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in large-bowled glasses to reveal its supple texture. Pair with rich ragus, roasted meats, or aged hard cheeses to complement its depth.
aroma: rustic red cherry and earthy herb
palate: firm yet velvety red fruit with savory grip

name: Brut
description: This 2022 Gilgal Brut from the Golan Heights Winery is crafted in the traditional method using equal parts Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from the northern Galilee. It shows bright, delicate layers of orange blossom, green apple, tropical fruit and wild strawberry atop a refined structure from extended lees aging of at least one year in bottle.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an aperitif or alongside rich or salty fare such as caviar, liver pâté or sushi for elegant contrast.
aroma: Orange blossom, green apple, tropical fruit
palate: Delicate yet energetic, wild strawberry nuances

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Galilee
description: This wine offers a refined Cabernet Sauvignon expression from Upper Galilee its character anchored in vibrant dark berry fruits threaded with subtle herbal lift and a whisper of baking spices
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or decanted with richly flavored rustic fare such as herb‑roasted lamb shoulder or grilled ribeye with sautéed wild mushrooms
palate: ripe dark fruit with black pepper and cocoa
finish: elegant lingering finish with framed oak and herbal nuance
foodPairings: roast lamb with garlic and herbs
drinkWindow: ready to drink now and over next 6–8 years

name: Cabernet Sauvignon/merlot
description: An elegant ensemble from the storied Golan Heights Winery, the 2015 Gilgal Cabernet Sauvignon‑Merlot marries ripe Galilean fruit in an approachable yet refined manner, framed by gentle French oak nuances. Plush cherry and raspberry notes mingle with delicate floral and spice whispers, all supported by balanced structure. This wine offers a friendly charm for everyday enjoyment with old‑world poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to unveil its lush fruit and subtle spice, ideal with rich grilled meats or roasted vegetables to enhance its layered complexity.
aroma: ripe cherry and raspberry with floral and spice hints
palate: plush fruit framed by soft oak and balanced structure

name: Chardonnay
description: A graceful rendition of Golan Heights’ terrain, this 2023 Gilgal Chardonnay presents a luminous core of pear and Meyer lemon elevated by a touch of flinty minerality and subtle French oak nuances, yielding a refined and inviting character.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to showcase its freshness; pairs elegantly with creamy chicken fricassée or herb‑infused grilled fish.
palate: medium‑bodied with gentle oak and flinty minerality

name: Sauvignon Blanc
description: This 2024 Gilgal Sauvignon Blanc from the Golan Heights Winery offers an elegant tension between tropical guava and kiwi fruit, intertwined with bright citrus blossom and a touch of mineral clarity: it is vibrant and medium‑bodied yet refined with a soft textural grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled; this lively Sauvignon Blanc complements light seafood or goat cheese with refreshing poise.
palate: tropical fruit and lemon zest with mineral lift
finish: crisp, clean finish with lingering acidity
foodPairings: steamed fish with lime and coconut

name: Bruno Gobillard Rose Mlle Sophie Brut
description: Pale and ethereal with gentle cherry luminosity, this non‑vintage Champagne exudes refined structure and a delicate mineral backbone, offering the soft perfume of wild strawberry and a whisper of red currant. It frames a precise, bone‑dry expression that speaks of terroir and meticulous vinification.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip flute to preserve its fine mousse and reveal its poised acidity, perfect as an elegant aperitif or alongside simply prepared poached salmon or soft cheeses.
palate: fine red currant tension

name: Lirac Clos de Sixte
description: This 2009 Grand Veneur Lirac Clos de Sixte unveils an inviting tapestry of black cherry, blackberry and garrigue with lavender and crushed rock nuances leading into a rich and polished medium‑ to full‑bodied frame. The texture is supple yet structured with silky tannins and a lift of licorice‑spiced freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool just below cellar temperature to open its aromatic depth, decant gently, and pair with rich Provençal dishes such as daube or tajine to echo its warm fruit and spice tones.

drinkWindow: Drink now to 2020, optimal by about 2015–2022 but enjoyable now

name: Chateauneuf du Pape
description: A wine of regal bearing from a celebrated southern Rhône estate, this 2010 Grand Veneur Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape reveals dense dark berry depth with an undercurrent of garrigue herbs and fine mineral nuance, lending a stately structure to the vibrant fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve just slightly cool at cellar temperature to reveal its fine-grained tannins and pair with slow‑roasted lamb or wild game stews.
palate: silky yet powerful dark fruit and licorice

name: Domaine Grange Cochard Morgon les Charmes
description: This 2019 Morgon "Les Charmes" from Château Grange Cochard exudes refined harmony its bright Gamay fruit balanced by an undercurrent of granite‐inflected minerality and subtle structure The plush red‐berry character is laced with fresh acidity and finely etched tannins offering both immediacy and grace
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14 °C for best refinement Open with roasted poultry or pork dishes that complement the wine’s fruit and structure
aroma: bright red berries with mineral nuance
palate: silky fruit with firm yet elegant tannins

description: The 2018 Domaine Robert Groffier Bonnes‑Mares Grand Cru unfolds with precision and poise, offering a measured yet deep expression of dark cherry and brambly fruit. description: An immediate, vibrant Bourgogne Passetoutgrains from the renowned Domaine Robert Groffier, the 2023 vintage combines 75 percent Pinot Noir with 25 percent Gamay. It offers appealing red and blue berry tones framed with gentle spice and medium weight in a delightfully effortless style.

name: Domaine Robert Groffier Bourgogne Rouge
description: This village‑level Bourgogne Rouge from Domaine Robert Groffier unfolds with generous ripe red berry fruit and a vibrant energy, framed by floral lift and a hint of savory detail. The wine’s depth and fine-grained tannins convey both power and elegance, offering a poised expression of classic Burgundy Grand Cru terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature in generous Burgundy glasses, ideally with modest decanting to release its layered aromas—pairs splendidly with truffle‑accented dishes or aged soft cheese.

palate: Concentrated dark fruit framed by velvety tannins and mineral spice

description: This is a superb Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru from the legendary Les Amoureuses, offering radiant floral perfume and vivid red‑berry clarity, underpinned by an elegant, refined structure that speaks of old‑world Burgundian finesse.

appellation: Chambolle‑Musigny 1er Cru “Les Amoureuses La Grâce des Argiles”
description: The 2022 Dom Robert Groffier Chambolle‑Musigny 1er Cru “Les Amoureuses La Grâce des Argiles” exudes silken red fruit elegance framed by mineral undertones and a refined oak presence, reflecting the clay‑rich terroir with poise. It conveys both seductive charm and structural depth born of whole‑cluster vinification and measured élevage, marrying plush density with energetic clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in fine Burgundy glasses after slight decanting to reveal the wine’s layered floral and berry nuances; pairs exquisitely with duck breast, wild mushroom fricassée or soft‑rind cheeses.
aroma: seductive red cherry and violet perfume
palate: velvety, mineral‑inflected fruit with vibrant energy

name: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Amoureuses la Delicatesse des Sables
appellation: Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru Les Amoureuses La Délicatesse des Sables
description: A shimmering portrait of finesse and mineral transparency this wine delivers an ethereal cascade of pixellated red fruits, delicate chalky tension and intellectual poise that entices without force. It embodies the quiet intensity of Groffier’s Les Amoureuses filtered through the grace of sandy limestone soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine Burgundy stemware to reveal its subtle precision and pair with nuanced dishes like herb‑crusted lamb or mushroom‑infused risotto, allowing the wine’s chalky lift to refresh the palate.
aroma: red cherry, raspberry, pomegranate with chalky mineral lift
palate: bright and lively with melting fine tannins and saline-tinged complexity
finish: long, precise, with saline mineral note

name: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Amoureuses la Grace D'argiles
description: This 2023 Chambolle‑Musigny 1er Cru “La Grâce des Argiles” from Domaine Robert Groffier unfolds with refined richness and energy offering a seamless flow of red cherry, raspberry and macerated fruit framed by lifted floral and mineral undertones. The wine’s clay‑derived texture lends density without weight, revealing a ripe core enlivened by crystalline clarity and poised grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 60‑62 °F in a large bowled glass to appreciate its ethereal perfume; pairs exquisitely with butter‑poached lobster or wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: lifted red cherry, raspberry and floral spice
palate: dense yet refined with silky tannins and mineral clarity

name: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Amoureuses Sables
appellation: Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru "Les Amoureuses La Délicatesse des Sables"
description: This is a refined Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru born of sandy terroir, revealing a gossamer core of black plum and cassis underlaid by gentle earth and whisper of smoke, wrapped in supple texture and a graceful frame.

name: Domaine Robert Groffier Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Hauts-Doix
description: A graceful expression of Chambolle‑Musigny in its most refined form red fruit aromas weave with a floral undertone and poised mineral tension, the palate is lithe yet focused offering sappy cherry and raspberry laced with subtle spice, the impression is one of weightless elegance with fine delineation and saline clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in fine Burgundy glasses, consider a brief decant now or cellar until 2027 to allow for harmony; delightful with lightly grilled veal with woodland mushrooms or roasted duck breast.

palate: pure red fruit, refined tannins, salinity

description: An elegant Chianti Classico from the Guidi family that captures the essence of Tuscany’s gentle hills in San Donato in Poggio: red cherry fruit intertwined with a subtle earthy note and a brush of Tuscan herb, framed by refined structure and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in medium‑bodied red wine glasses paired with rustic fare such as wild boar ragù or aged pecorino for a classic Tuscan experience.
palate: earthy red fruit with balanced structure

name: Famiglia Guidi Chianti Classico DOCG
description: A vivid expression of Guidi’s Tuscan heritage this Chianti Classico unfolds in an intense ruby red hue, unveiling a nose rich with woodland undergrowth and spice nuances. The palate is elegantly structured, offering dry Sangiovese power softened by seamless tannins and a notably persistent finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature to elevate its structural finesse: pairs exquisitely with grilled red meats or pecorino Toscano.
palate: dry, structured, soft tannins

name: Boedgas Margon Pricum Prieto Picudo
description: A profound expression of León’s heritage this 2007 Pricum Prieto Picudo from Bodegas Margón delivers brooding wild berry and dark cherry aromas with delicate underbrush and truffle nuances, framed by noble French oak. The palate reveals a finely structured layering of savory red fruit and graphite with an earthy undercurrent that speaks to the ancient bush vines of Pajares de los Oteros.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to highlight its finesse; pairs beautifully with game birds or slow‑roasted pork with earthy mushroom jus.
palate: savory red fruit, graphite, earthy depth

name: Domaine Hubert Lamy Santenay Rouge Clos des Hates
description: A refined Pinot Noir that whispers of dark cherry and wooded undergrowth framed by subtle spice and a hint of flintiness, offering poise and sculpted focus.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature with fall game or earthy roasted vegetables.
palate: medium‑bodied, precise, cranberry and bergamot tension

name: Family Wines Nuns Canyon Vineyard Moon Mountain AVA
description: A deeply layered wine that evokes the vertical energy of its volcanic Hillside home, it unfolds in the glass with dark cherry and fresh raspberry over subtle peony and forest‑floor nuance, all held taut by refined structure and mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve with robust red proteins such as lamb or venison to complement its saline tannins and iron‑etched persistence.
aroma: fresh raspberry and cherry with peony and forest‑floor nuance
palate: tightly knit, layered structure with arching tannins
finish: powerful, ferrous finish with minerality and salinity

name: Family Wines Stratum Red Sonoma Valley
description: The 2021 Stratum Red unfolds in the glass with a dark ruby hue hinting at its undercurrent of volcanic energy, offering a vibrant chorus of black cherry, raspberry and wild herbs wrapped in an iron‑rich sanguine note. On the palate it conveys layered plum and pomegranate with chalky mineral tannins that extend into a lingering, structured finish, promising graceful evolution over the next several years.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in large goblets to emphasize its mineral tension, pairing beautifully with grilled lamb chops or mushroom‑infused braised short ribs.
aroma: black cherry, wild herbs, rose petals with sanguine mineral undertones
palate: ripe plum, pomegranate, focused tension, chalky mineral tannins

name: Family Wines Stratum Red Wine Sonoma Valley
description: This deeply volcanic expression from Hamel Family Wines offers a profoundly mineral-laced Cabernet–Merlot blend that feels both refined and energetic, with violets, dark cherry and cassis counterpointed by an iron‑tinged earthiness and cedar nuance, all framed by supple, chalk‑textured tannins and refreshing vibrancy.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to highlight its structure, pairing beautifully with grilled lamb, aged beef and earthy mushroom preparations; it will age gracefully over the next decade.
aroma: dark cherry, cassis, violets, cedar, iron
palate: dark fruit enveloping a sanguine mineral core, supple tannins

name: Haut Charmes Sauternes
description: This Sauternes offers a luminous golden hue and a delicate wedding of honeyed apricot and citrus blossom, framed by a subtle floral whisper and a thread of noble acidity. It impresses with refined sweetness that remains elegantly poised, conveying a sense of graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in small tulip glasses, ideally alongside foie gras, blue cheese, or nut‑based desserts to echo its honeyed depth.
palate: silky sweet yet balanced by bright acidity

name: Château Haut Selve Graves Blanc
description: The 2023 Château Haut Selve Graves Blanc unfurls with layered elegance starting with guava, ginger and snipped herbs underscored by tangerine rind aromas, followed by a complex palate enriched with subtle vanilla and almond nuances and a seamless poised finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled where its bright profile complements shellfish and cream‑sauce poultry, bringing out its refined texture.
palate: Complex with vanilla and almond hints

name: Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast
description: This 2021 Headline Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast offers a supremely ripe expression of coastal fruit, weaving black cherry, dark plum and blackberry into a rich, mouth‑filling tapestry with moderate tannins and lively acidity. It presents plush texture and straightforward allure with an underlying energy that speaks of Sonoma Coast’s cooler embrace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to frame its dark fruit and lift mineral nuances. Pair with roast duck breast or mushroom‑glazed pork for elegant balance.
palate: plush fruit with moderate tannins
finish: bright acidity with a slightly sharp close

name: Château Haut Sarthes Haut Montravel Molleux
description: A refined Sémillon moelleux from the evocative terroir of Haut‑Montravel this 2010 Château Haut‑Sarthes offers a luminous pale gold hue and a plush yet vibrant bouquet of honeyed apricot and delicate dried fruit nuances; its texture is rounded and elegantly sustained by a gentle underlying line of minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at 8 to 10 °C it lends itself beautifully to foie gras, blue‑veined cheeses or desserts with stone fruit it also charms as a contemplative after‑dinner pour.
palate: rounded with gentle minerality

name: Château Puy-Servain Montravel Rouge Vielles Vignes
description: This 2010 Château Puy‑Servain Vieilles Vignes Rouge is an opulent expression of old‑vine Merlot framed by Cabernet Franc, offering plush layers of ripe dark fruit and a refined undercurrent of earthy lift drawn from its limestone‑rich soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently below cellar temperature to highlight its silk‑textured tannins, pairing elegantly with roast lamb or mature cow’s milk cheese.
aroma: ripe dark berries with subtle spice
palate: full‑bodied, rich and velvety

name: Château Puy-Servain Terremont(molleux)
description: Château Puy-Servain Calabre's 2015 Terrement Moelleux is a sweet Sémillon with vivid pineapple and quince character. Its generous entry is balanced by fresh acidity, leaving the wine poised rather than heavy.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled as an aperitif or with foie gras, white meats, or blue-veined cheese.
palate: Sweet, generous, lifted by acidity

name: Henri Bourgeois Pouilly Fume
description: Racy and refined this 2023 Henri Bourgeois Pouilly‑Fumé is built on crystalline Loire Sauvignon Blanc with notes of ripe citrus, yellow orchard fruit and subtle flint that speak of clay‑limestone soils, elegant and driven by graceful minerality.

aroma: ripe citrus and yellow orchard fruit with flint
palate: fresh, concentrated and elegant with mineral accents

name: Henri Bourgeois Pouilly Fume
description: Racy and refined this 2024 Henri Bourgeois Pouilly‑Fumé is built on crystalline Loire Sauvignon Blanc with notes of ripe citrus, yellow orchard fruit and subtle flint that speak of clay‑limestone soils, elegant and driven by graceful minerality.

description: A bright and spirited 2025 Henri Bourgeois “Pure” Sauvignon Blanc Vin de Pays presents crisp citrus clarity framed by a whisper of Loire limestone minerality. It combines invigorating freshness with an elegant purity that offers effortless drinking pleasure.

description: This luminous Sancerre Blanc from Henri Bourgeois is a study in flinty refinement, its elegance rooted in a terroir born 56 million years ago, offering a poised interplay of gunflint and spice, kissed by floral sap. It is a wine of concentration and balance that rewards both immediate pleasure and graceful maturation.

name: Henri Bourgeois Sancerre Rose les Jeunes Vignes
description: A luminous rosé, the 2024 Henri Bourgeois Sancerre Rosé “Les Jeunes Vignes” unveils bright red‑berry fruit with a whisper of white peach framed by a sinewy Loire minerality drawn from clay‑limestone hillsides. It reflects the vivacious elegance of Sancerre through delicate salinity and poised structure.

description: This Sancerre rouge from Henri Bourgeois reveals an elegant interplay of Morello cherry and violet framed by subtle oak, leading to a round supple texture and poised astringency that mellows gracefully with age.

description: An elegant expression of the Loire’s western terroir, this 2018 Clos de la Fine Muscadet Côtes de Grandlieu Sur Lie from Domaine des Herbauges pairs crystalline minerality with gentle fruit. It offers a pale gold hue and an expressive bouquet evocative of lime blossom, acacia and citrus, leading to a supple, textured mouthfeel that balances subtle power with a whisper of richness.

name: Macon Chardonnay Clos de la Crochette
description: This Mâcon‑Chardonnay “Clos de la Crochette” 2024 by Les Héritiers du Comte Lafon delivers an elegant and refined expression of southern Burgundy Chardonnay, its poised structure and ripe orchard fruit shaped by sunny clay‑limestone slopes lend both immediacy and depth. Crafted with biodynamic care and matured in large oak foudres and demi‑muids the wine embodies textural richness and a fresh tautness that speaks of refinement and terroir.

description: A crystalline expression of the Wachau in 2016, this Riesling Federspiel Steinterrassen reveals pristine clarity with a refined interplay of orchard fruit and riverbed mineral tones. It opens with luminous green‑tinged yellow, then unfolds generous yet precise exotic fruit facets and a focused tension that speaks of cool vineyard terraces. sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled to highlight its bright acidity and mineral clarity; ideal with subtly seasoned seafood or delicate poultry dishes.
palate: precise exotic fruit framed by crisp acidity

description: This 2011 Hirtzberger Steinporz Weißburgunder (Pinot Blanc) Smaragd presents a medium straw‑gold hue with a layered bouquet of yellow apple blossom, fine honeyed florals and citrus zest leading to a concentrated, expressive palate. The wine deftly balances extract and firm structure, conveying delicate nutty nuances and a lingering resonance that hints at both early charm and graceful development.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled as an elegant aperitif or alongside nuanced dishes such as buttery fish or subtle cream sauces to accent its refined texture and mineral poise.
aroma: yellow apple blossom, citrus zest, fine honeyed florals

finish: long lingering resonance with nutty touch
drinkWindow: Drink now for early grace or cellar further for additional complexity over 5–10 years

name: Simoes Moscatel du Setubel
description: An elegant expression of Setúbal’s fortified heritage the 2021 Horácio Simões Moscatel de Setúbal enchants with a luminous topaz hue and an inviting bouquet of muscat petals autumn spices dried raisins and a whisper of walnut. On the palate it unfolds with a round supple texture that balances freshness and sweetness in harmonious accord. The finish is lingering and crisp, leaving a lasting impression of floral sweetness and nutty warmth.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at about 18 °C as a dessert companion or graceful digestif: it pairs splendidly with almond pastries or a modest blue cheese.

palate: round supple fresh sweet balance

name: Saint Aubin 1er Cru Derriere chez Edouard Rouge
appellation: Saint‑Aubin Premier Cru Derrière Chez Édouard
description: This wine is a refined and delicate expression of Saint‑Aubin Premier Cru, crafted from old‑vine Pinot Noir in the Derrière Chez Édouard climat. It shows a subtle yet persistent weave of red fruit underlain by limestone‑infused structure, culminating in a graceful, lingering texture.

palate: silky red fruit, fine mineral tension

name: Saint Aubin Rouge 1er Cru Derriere chez Edouard
description: This Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru Rouge “Derrière chez Édouard” 2013 from Hubert Lamy unfolds with a courtly essence of red berry fruit and woodland undergrowth, all framed by poised, crystalline minerality that speaks of Côte de Beaune finesse. The texture is lithe and tactful yet layered with subtle complexity from careful élevage and old‑vine concentration.

palate: silky texture, bright red fruit, mineral tension

name: Saint Aubin Rouge 1er Cru Derriere chez Edouard
description: Hubert Lamy's 2014 Saint-Aubin Premier Cru Derrière Chez Edouard Vieilles Vignes Rouge is a rare, finely drawn Pinot Noir with red-fruited lift and a cool, stony profile. Its mature frame favors delicacy, savory nuance, and freshness over weight.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature and give the bottle a gentle decant for sediment; pair with roast quail, duck, or mushroom dishes.
aroma: Red cherry, dried rose, forest floor
palate: Silky red fruit, fine tannin, limestone freshness

name: Santenay Rouge Clos des Hates
description: Hubert Lamy's 2014 Santenay Clos des Hâtes Rouge carries generous Pinot Noir fruit through a silky, concentrated palate. Mouthwatering acidity arrives beneath the wine's breadth, lending shape and complexity to its mature expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15-16°C with a short, careful decant; its savory freshness suits roast poultry, pork, or earthy vegetable preparations.
aroma: Ripe red cherry, plum, gentle earth
palate: Silky, concentrated, mouthwatering

name: Huerta Jalon Gin Monti
description: An artisanal London Dry Gin born of tradition and mountain clarity from the Sierra de Guadarrama, this gin offers a refined interplay of juniper and citrus framed by subtle spice from cinnamon and cardamom, enveloped in a smooth, almost glyceric texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or in a classic gin and tonic with a twist of lemon or a sprig of lavender to accentuate its field‑fresh botanicals.
aroma: fresh juniper with lemon and field herbs
palate: soft citrus and gentle spice
finish: velvety dry with a hint of bitter‑sweet undertone

name: Domaine Humbert Freres Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru Crapillot
description: This 2017 Gevrey‑Chambertin Premier Cru “Craipillot” from Humbert Frères exudes a vibrant interplay of wild cherry and violet underlaid by forest floor and supple earth, delivering both structure and grace in a distinctly Côte de Nuits expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C, ideally decanted in its youth, to reveal its layered complexity; pairs beautifully with game birds or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: wild cherry and violet with forest floor
palate: elegant structure with supple earth

name: Huteau Boulanger Sancere Laetitia Ducroux
description: An elegant Sancerre from Huteau‑Boulanger crafted by Laetitia Ducroux this 2025 bottling whispers of radiant citrus and saline minerality, its clarity and poise reflecting the Loire’s limestone terroir. The purity of expression and slender frame evoke old‑world grace with crisp precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10 °C in a fine white wine glass, to accentuate the wine’s lifted minerality. Excellent with goat cheese or chilled shellfish focusing its saline freshness.
aroma: ripe citrus and green apple with subtle flinty mineral notes
palate: vibrant acidity, precise citrus and mineral clarity

name: Huteau Boulanger Sancerre Laetitia Ducroux
description: The 2024 Sancerre “Laetitia Ducroux” exudes crystalline purity and lithe energy: lemon blossom and wet stone lift from the glass while precise acidity and a mineral spine bring unwavering finesse. The wine presents an elegant Loire profile that whispers of pebbled slopes and coastal freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass, pairing especially well with fresh goat cheese, oysters or simply as an aperitif. The fine acidity makes it versatile with shellfish or white fish.
palate: crisp citrus with minerally tension

name: J&j Archambaud Vosne Romanee aux Reas
description: This wine presents an elegant and refined expression of village‑level Vosne‑Romanée, bearing a silky texture and a poised fruit profile that whispers rather than shouts. It conjures vivid raspberry and crushed strawberry framed by delicate structure and lithe density with a noble restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature in tulip‑shaped glasses; this wine’s graceful acidity and fine tannins pair beautifully with roast duck or wild mushroom dishes.
palate: silky texture with poised structure

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Prestige
description: The 2019 Domaine Jean Royer Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape Cuvée Prestige presents a savoury yet richly fruited expression grounded in Grenache and Mourvèdre harmony, offering notes of dark plum and leather woven with Provençal garrigue and spice. The structure is poised and medium‑full, refined tannins supporting layered depth and fine tension, promising graceful evolution over the next decade.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16 °C in a large-bowled glass to allow the dark fruit and savory nuances to unfurl; it will pair superbly with rosemary‑accented lamb or roasted game with earthy mushroom jus.
palate: medium‑full, structured, layered

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Sables de la Crau
description: From the famed sandy soils of La Crau comes this 2019 Jean Royer Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape Sables de la Crau, a pure Grenache of radiant purity displaying lifted notes of raspberry, wildflowers and a whisper of spice, culminating in a seamless and refined expression. It offers elegance and texture that sustain both immediate pleasure and graceful evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve with care at about 16 °C in a large-bowled glass to coax out perfumed florals and red fruit, pairing beautifully with roast lamb or herb‑driven Provençal dishes.
palate: elegant, silky Grenache fruit

name: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage la Chapelle
description: This 2017 Hermitage La Chapelle from Paul Jaboulet Aîné presents itself with majestic poise deep in the Syrah tradition of the Northern Rhône the wine weaves intense black and blue fruit with graphite and spice in a tapestry of power and elegance, finishing with a regal, multi‑dimensional depth that speaks of its storied terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in large Bordeaux‑style glasses to allow the wine’s aromas to unfurl. It pairs beautifully with richly flavoured red meats, game in sauce, or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: black and blue fruit, violet, graphite
palate: powerful yet velvety, layered, mineral‑infused

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Paso Robles
description: This 2023 Jack Tar Cabernet Sauvignon from Paso Robles unfolds with brooding black cherry and plum overtones gently kissed by vanilla cream and Turkish tobacco, revealing a textured tapestry of grilled plum and cigar box on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve in generous Burgundy‑style glasses at 60‑65°F to allow the dusty tannins to soften; excellent with grilled lamb or aged Manchego.
palate: Grilled plum, cigar box, spice

name: Pago de la Jaraba Vina Jaraba Crianza
description: This Crianza reveals the very Spanish essence of Tempranillo supported by Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot from the elevated soils of La Mancha. It opens with spicy, ripe plum and cherry intertwining with vanilla and smoky nuances derived from twelve months in French oak, culminating in a full‑bodied, meaty expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 60‑65°F in a large glass to allow aromas to unfold: pairs beautifully with roast pork, grilled chicken, or classic paella.
palate: lively black fruit with floral and licorice nuance
finish: firm youthful tannins, smooth lingering finish

name: Jb Jessiaume Rully Blanc 1er Cru Marissou
description: The 2021 JB Jessiaume Rully 1er Cru Marissou Blanc unfurls with refined elegance and layered orchard fruit over a subtle weave of acacia and nutty nuance. Its gilded hue heralds a wine of real poise offering succulent lychee and apricot tempered by a hint of toasted almond.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 13 °C to reveal its expressive clarity: an ideal match for delicate river or sea fish, or elegant creamy poultry preparations.
aroma: lychee and apricot with acacia and almond highlights
palate: succulent orchard fruit with refined nutty undertones

name: Jb Jessiaume Rully Blanc Clos de Bellecroix
description: A pale golden Rully blanc from Domaine Jean‑Baptiste Jessiaume offering delicate aromas of fresh orchard fruits with citrus highlights, framed in subtle florality and almond nuances. The palate is refined and tensile, the texture fine and persistent, capturing a poised freshness that speaks of its chalky hillside origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–13 °C; it will marry beautifully with simply prepared shellfish or a creamy poultry dish.
palate: elegant, long, fresh
foodPairings: poached river fish in cream sauce

name: Jb Jessiaume Santenay 1er Cru Passetemps
description: This Santenay 1er Cru Passetemps 2020 by Jean‑Baptiste Jessiaume offers a refined expression of southern Côte de Beaune terroir with airy freshness and elegant structure. Noble aromas of Morello cherries and wild berries mingle with floral violet, leading to a graciously textured palate of supple tannins and gentle liveliness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at about 15 °C to complement roasted red meats or cheese platters, allowing the wine’s fine freshness and red fruit to harmonize with the dishes.
palate: supple structured tannins with freshness

name: Jc Ramonet Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: The 2021 Domaine Ramonet Bâtard‐Montrachet Grand Cru reveals an elegant core of orchard fruit and toasted brioche balanced by a mineral undercurrent: its poise conveys both intensity and refinement in every sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 11 °C in large white Burgundy glasses: the wine’s supple acidity and luminous structure pair beautifully with subtly rich seafood or creamy poultry dishes.
aroma: orchard fruit, toasted brioche, subtle minerals
palate: pure, mineral‑driven, refined intensity
foodPairings: rich white fish in beurre blanc

name: Jc Ramonet Bourgogne Passetoutgrain
description: A vibrant Bourgogne Passetoutgrain from the elevated tradition of Jean‑Claude Ramonet, the 2021 vintage reveals supple red fruit charm with a gentle whisper of spice, framed by a graceful structure and youthful energy worthy of a convivial table.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool, around 14 °C, alongside rustic fare such as charcuterie or braised game for harmony of texture and flavour.
aroma: bright red cherry and raspberry with a hint of cassis
palate: supple early red fruits underpinned by soft tannins
drinkWindow: drink young, within a few years

name: Jc Ramonet Bourgogne Passetoutgrain
description: A vibrant Bourgogne Passetoutgrain from the elevated tradition of Jean‑Claude Ramonet, the 2022 vintage reveals supple red fruit charm with a gentle whisper of spice, framed by a graceful structure and youthful energy worthy of a convivial table.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool, around 14 °C, alongside rustic fare such as charcuterie or braised game for harmony of texture and flavour.
aroma: bright red cherry and raspberry with a hint of cassis
palate: supple early red fruits underpinned by soft tannins
drinkWindow: drink young, within a few years

name: Jc Ramonet Chassagne Montrachet Blanc
description: This 2021 Domaine Jean‑Claude Ramonet Chassagne‑Montrachet Blanc presents a refined balance of orchard fruit, citrus zest and gentle spice, framed by a fine mineral thread imparting elegance and clarity. The palate is poised with fresh pear and white blossom notes, underlined by softly creamy textures that speak of judicious oak influence. The finish resonates with clean stone and citrus echoes, lingering with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to accentuate its crystalline acidity and floral nuance; a beautiful companion to delicate seafood or creamy poultry preparations.
aroma: orchard fruit, citrus zest, subtle spice
palate: pear and white blossom, soft creaminess, minerally drive

name: Jc Ramonet Chassagne Montrachet Rouge
description: An elegant village‐level Pinot Noir that expresses itself with poised restraint and Burgundian refinement, drawing from Chassagne‑Montrachet soils more celebrated for white wine. It unfolds with delicate red cherry and raspberry framed by subtle earth and mineral whispers, culminating in a finish of refined balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature to reveal its finesse, ideally alongside delicately roasted poultry or a mushroom‑dotted risotto for harmony.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with earthy mineral undertones
palate: elegant, medium‑bodied layers of red fruit and spice

name: Jc Ramonet Chassagne Montrachet Rouge
description: An elegant village‐level Pinot Noir that expresses itself with poised restraint and Burgundian refinement, drawing from Chassagne‑Montrachet soils more celebrated for white wine.
