name: Jc Ramonet Chevalier Montrachet Grand Cru
description: A grand expression of Burgundian Chardonnay from the distinguished Domaine Jean‑Claude Ramonet, this 2022 Chevalier‑Montrachet Grand Cru presents opulent yet refined layers of white flowers, citrus and stone fruit with a whisper of brioche and toasted hazelnut beneath a slate‑like mineral undercurrent.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 11–13 °C, decant lightly if desired; pairs beautifully with lobster in beurre blanc, scallops or fine shellfish, the wine’s tension lifting creamy textures.
aroma: white flowers, citrus zest, wet limestone
palate: ripe stone fruit, acacia honey, mineral precision

name: Jc Ramonet Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: This 2022 Corton‑Charlemagne Grand Cru from Domaine Ramonet offers a refined yet potent expression of white Burgundy with an illuminated golden hue a minerally crystal‑clear backbone and layered aromas of citrus blossom ripe orchard fruit and gentle spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12–14 °C with rich shellfish or creamy poultry; cellar through the early 2030s to reveal its full aromatic harmony.
aroma: citrus blossom, ripe orchard fruit, gentle spice
palate: structured yet tender with crystalline minerality and orchard fruit depth

name: Jc Ramonet le Montrachet Grand Cru
description: A wine of noble reserve and crystalline poise, this 2022 Jean‑Claude Ramonet Le Montrachet Grand Cru delivers a beguiling interplay of electric mineral precision and sun‑ripened stone fruit, framed by delicate brioche and honeyed nuance, all supported by an unerring spine of tension and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine stemware to unveil its layered richness, ideally alongside luxurious shellfish or subtly truffled dishes to mirror its minerality and texture.
aroma: white flowers citrus zest wet limestone
palate: ripe stone fruit acacia honey mineral finesse

name: Jc Ramonet Macon Peronne
description: An aristocratic Chardonnay from Burgundy’s warm sunlit slopes of Péronne, this 2021 Jean‑Claude Ramonet Macon Péronne unfolds with crystalline energy and a refined mineral undercurrent drawing from marno‑calcaire soils. It balances floral brightness with orchard fruit ripeness, articulated through a poised structure and subtle tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled near 10 °C in slender tulip glasses to showcase its vivacious clarity; pairs elegantly with shellfish, chèvre or creamy poultry preparations.
aroma: orchard blossoms and white pear with subtle minerality
palate: crisp white peach framed by taut minerality

name: Jc Ramonet Pernand Vergelesses Belles Filles Rouge
description: The 2021 Domaine Jean‑Claude Ramonet Pernand‑Vergelesses “Les Belles Filles” Rouge offers an elegant expression of Côte de Beaune Pinot Noir combining fresh red cherry and raspberry with violet and subtle spice over a mineral‑tinged foundation. The palate unfolds with fine tannins and bright acidity delivering purity and poised concentration in a lithe, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in medium‑sized glasses to reveal its floral red fruit and minerality. Pair with mushroom tart or herb‑crusted lamb to complement its spice and finesse.
aroma: fresh red cherry, raspberry, violet, subtle spice
palate: fine tannins, bright acidity, mineral clarity

name: Domaine Jean-Francois Chardonnay Sanford & Benedict
description: A refined expression of Sta. Rita Hills Chardonnay that marries the vineyard’s rugged minerality with a graceful orchard fruit core. This wine unfolds with crystalline tension framed by subtle oak nuance and a whisper of floral elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its citrus‑leaning precision; pairs beautifully with seared scallops or a delicate goat cheese tart.
palate: tangy citrus, salty mineral texture

name: Domaine Jean-Francois Pinot Noir Sanford & Benedict
description: An elegant expression of Sta. Rita Hills Pinot Noir: medium ruby in hue with layers of red cherry and raspberry perfume uplifted by subtle violet and tea leaf nuances. The wine offers refined texture, enveloping you in freshness and finely grained tannins that carry through a resonant, haunting finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a delicate tulip glass to showcase its perfumed charm. Pairs exquisitely with duck breast or roasted mushrooms with herbs.
palate: silky red fruit with refined tannins

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Sables de la Crau
description: An elegant southern Rhône red of refined clarity and gentle generosity. The 2011 Les Sables de la Crau unfurls with vivid red berry and floral notes framed by a polished structure and a sense of mineral poise. It offers an inviting balance between fruit purity and supple texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in broad-bowl glasses to reveal its floral perfume and graceful layers, pairing beautifully with roast duck or herb‑infused lamb.
aroma: sweet strawberry, rose petal, raspberry pastille
palate: spicy red cherry, energetic yet silky

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Sables de la Crau
description: An elegant southern Rhône red of refined clarity and gentle generosity. The 2013 Les Sables de la Crau unfurls with vivid red berry and floral notes framed by a polished structure and a sense of mineral poise. It offers an inviting balance between fruit purity and supple texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in broad-bowl glasses to reveal its floral perfume and graceful layers, pairing beautifully with roast duck or herb‑infused lamb.
aroma: sweet strawberry, rose petal, raspberry pastille
palate: spicy red cherry, energetic yet silky

name: Domaine Jean Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Prestige
description: This 2020 Dom Jean Royer Cuvée Prestige from Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape unfurls in the glass with ripe black raspberry and cherry‑liqueur aromas veined with ground pepper, sappy floral notes and a hint of sandalwood. Medium to full in body yet poised and seamless this wine offers textured richness and elegant balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to accentuate its freshness and pair with roasted game or rich stews to complement its spicy depth.
aroma: ripe black raspberry, cherry liqueur, floral spice
palate: medium‑full, textured, balanced

name: Domaine Jean Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Sables de la Crau
description: A noble expression of Grenache from the famed sandy soils of La Crau this wine unfolds with ripe raspberries kissed by kirsch and accented by dried florals and herbs, all rendered with a silken opulence that feels both generous and refined. It carries depth without weight, offering layered fruit and sumptuous structure that articulate the purity of its origin.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 16 °C to reveal its full perfumed complexity and pair with Provençal lamb or herb‑crusted pork for a harmoniously rustic encounter.
aroma: ripe raspberries, kirsch, dried flowers and herbs
palate: layered opulence with silky texture

name: Cotes du Rhone Mon Coeur
description: This gently textured Côtes‑du‑Rhône from Jean‑Louis Chave offers an inviting melody of black cherry and plum framed by Provençal herbs and a whisper of cracked pepper drawing elegance from its rigorously selected parcels
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 16 °C to 18 °C with hearty stews or grilled lamb for a soulful match
aroma: black‑cherry and plum with garrigue herbs
palate: savory fruit core with cracked‑pepper spice

name: Jl Chave Selection Crozes Hermitage Blanc Sybele
description: A luminous white from the venerable J‑L Chave Sélection, the 2023 Crozes‑Hermitage Blanc Sybèle offers a refined interplay of orchard fruits and mineral clarity, with a tension that carries the wine with grace. The texture is rounded yet lithe, suggesting both generosity and precision in balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accent its poise. Pairs beautifully with delicate fish preparations or creamy goat cheeses.
palate: medium‑bodied, juicy with integrated acidity

name: Jl Chave Selection Crozes Hermitage Rouge Silene
description: The 2023 J.L. Chave Sélection Crozes‑Hermitage "Silène" is a finely wrought Syrah from granite‑inflected slopes that balances exuberant red and black fruit with mineral poise, propelled by savory violet‑and‑pepper nuances that lend old‑world nuance to youthful generosity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature to highlight its elegant spicy structure: ideal with braised lamb, cassoulet or mushroom‑rich ragouts.
aroma: bright red and black fruit with violet and pepper
palate: medium‑bodied, juicy, textured with mineral backbone
finish: savory, structured, lingering finish with nutted mineral drive

name: Jl Chave Selection Hermitage Blanches
description: This 2019 Hermitage Blanche from J.L. Chave Sélection is a white Rhône of noble bearing combining Marsanne and Roussanne in elegant balance. It emanates stone fruit and white flower aromatics with a thread of mineral tension and subtle almond richness, its texture both plush and lithe through a powerful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–14 °C allowing its orchard fruit and mineral core to sing; pairs beautifully with rich seafood or poultry with cream‑herbed sauces.
palate: plush and mineral‑tinged with almond nuance
foodPairings: roasted chicken with herb cream sauce

name: Jl Chave Selection Hermitage Farconnet
description: This 2020 Hermitage Farconnet by Jean‑Louis Chave Sélection offers an elegant interplay of poise and power, unveiling peppery game and lavender on the nose before yielding to silky dark berry fruit infused with olive tapenade and cedar undercurrents, all framed in a seamless and focused structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at 16–18 °C alongside roasted lamb or wild mushroom risotto to highlight its refined yet earthy character.
palate: dark berry fruit, olive tapenade, cedar

name: Jl Chave Selection Saint Joseph Blanc Circa
description: A wine of refinement drawn from the granitic slopes of Saint‑Joseph, this 2024 Circa Blanc by J.L. Chave Selection offers a finely woven expression of Roussanne marked by stone‑framed fruit and an enduring, mineral elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled near 10 °C in tulip‑shaped white wine glasses to reveal its delicate stone fruit and waxed floral notes, matching beautifully with creamy poultry or fresh herb‑accented fish.
aroma: elegant stone fruit and white flowers
palate: mineral driven yet generous texture

name: Saint Joseph Offerus
description: An elegant Saint‑Joseph Syrah that marries the stony rigour of its granite‑strewn northern Rhône origins with a perfumed charm, offering vibrant black fruit underpinned by charcoal and violet nuance, all framed by supple, structured tannins and mineral tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool after a 30‑ to 60‑minute decant to release the bouquet; superb with herb‑roasted lamb, charcuterie or Provençal stews.
aroma: crushed violets and cassis with a whisper of graphite
palate: polished dark berries, cracked pepper and granite‑driven minerality

name: Champagne Jl Vergnon Rosemotion Grand Cru Extra Brut
description: This Champagne unveils a pale rose petal hue with effervescent finesse, offering a delicate yet expressive bouquet of red berries, pomelo and faint saffron lifted by a mineral thread. The palate is silky and vibrant, edged with citrus tang and fine chalky texture culminating in a lingering, tangy finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 – 10 °C ideally as an aperitif or alongside lightly cured meats or aged cheese.
palate: fresh, tender effervescence, delicate texture, citrus and red fruit
drinkWindow: Drink now to near term (within 5 years)

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman Nerd Duck
description: This unfiltered red from João Pato’s Duckman project displays a gentle charm anchored in Bairrada’s native vines with understated elegance and forest‐floor nuance.
sommelierNotes: Chill lightly before serving, pair with charcuterie or grilled white meats to harmonize with its soft acidity.
palate: fresh acidity and soft tannins

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman White Duck
description: An evocation of Bairrada’s Atlantic-kissed clarity with pure Bical expression, White Duck 2024 is light in silk yet vibrant in character. Dusty citrus zest and pear blossom mingle with crushed stone nuance drawing the senses into an elegant, unfiltered whisper of terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–12  C, ideal alongside delicate fried bites, soft cheeses or fresh seafood where its bright minerality and citrus lift savory flavors.
palate: pear, lychee, crushed stones

name: Domaine Jouan Chambolle Musigny
description: A refined expression of Chambolle‑Musigny from the modest holdings of Domaine Henri Jouan, the 2018 Vieilles Vignes offers an elegant frame of ripe red cherry, rose petal and warm earth, lightly brushed with nutty oak and gentle spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature in a tall Burgundy glass to allow the perfume to blossom, and pair with simply seasoned duck breast or mushroom‑tarragon ragout.
aroma: ripe red cherry and rose petal with warm earth
palate: silky, finely balanced, with nutty oak and gentle spice

name: Domaine Jouan Clos Saint Denis Grand Cru
description: A refined expression of Clos Saint Denis from the tiny domain of Henri & Philippe Jouan this 2018 captures the indisputable gravitas of the Côte de Nuits with an alluring weave of red cherry and wild raspberry threaded with orange peel and softly loamy earth, finishing with power held in graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool around 14 °C in generous Burgundy glasses a brief decant brings forward its layered fruit and spice; it will enrich gently over the next decade.
aroma: red cherry, wild raspberry, orange peel
palate: concentrated, fleshy, layered

name: Domaine Jouan Clos Saint Denis Grand Cru
description: A refined expression of Clos Saint Denis from the tiny domain of Henri & Philippe Jouan this 2019 captures the indisputable gravitas of the Côte de Nuits with an alluring weave of red cherry and wild raspberry threaded with orange peel and softly loamy earth, finishing with power held in graceful restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool around 14 °C in generous Burgundy glasses a brief decant brings forward its layered fruit and spice; it will enrich gently over the next decade.
aroma: red cherry, wild raspberry, orange peel
palate: concentrated, fleshy, layered

name: Domaine Jouan Gevrey Chambertin aux Echezeaux
description: This Gevrey‑Chambertin Aux Échezeaux from Domaine Jouan 2020 is richly hued and composed, with layers of dark cherry and underbrush that unfurl with grace, retaining classic Burgundy finesse alongside an earth‑driven minerality that suggests both power and poise. There is a subtle iron‑tinged core that grounds the fruit in a tone of terroir, imparting depth and a captivating sense of place.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled to about 16 °C in large tulip glasses to reveal the wine’s perfumed intensity, pairing beautifully with herb‑roasted duck or aged Comté.
palate: silky yet structured red fruit with mineral tension

name: Domaine Jouan Gevrey Chambertin aux Echezeaux

palate: silky yet structured red fruit with mineral tension

name: Domaine Jouan Morey Saint Denis 1ER Cru Clos Sorbes
description: A noble expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis 1er Cru, the 2018 Clos Sorbé from Philippe Jouan unfolds with a tender perfume of wild cherry, rose petal and a hint of loam. The palate is silken and vibrant, with supple berry fruit and an innate tension that speaks of its venerable, eighty‑year‑old vines.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16 °C, best with elegant dishes such as roasted duck breast or mushroom‑infused risotto complemented by a splash of aged demi‑glace.
aroma: wild cherry, rose petal, loamy earth
palate: silky with supple berry depth and tension

description: A noble expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis 1er Cru, the 2019 Clos Sorbé from Philippe Jouan unfolds with a tender perfume of wild cherry, rose petal and a hint of loam. palate: silky with supple berry depth and tension

description: A noble expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis 1er Cru, the 2020 Clos Sorbé from Philippe Jouan unfolds with a tender perfume of wild cherry, rose petal and a hint of loam. The palate is silken and vibrant, with supple berry fruit and an innate tension that speaks of its venerable, eighty‑year‑old vines.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16 °C, best with elegant dishes such as roasted duck breast or mushroom‑infused risotto complemented by a splash of aged demi‑glace.
aroma: wild cherry, rose petal, loamy earth
palate: silky with supple berry depth and tension

name: Domaine Jouan Morey Saint Denis
description: A graceful village‐level Pinot Noir from Morey–Saint‑Denis, this 2020 Dom Jouan presents refined red cherry and rose petal notes, wrapped in gentle earth tones and subtle spice. The texture is silky yet precise, offering an elegant energy that carries through the mid‑palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar temperature with rich mushroom ragout or roasted duck for a harmonious pairing that highlights its nuance and freshness.
palate: silky, precise, elegant energy

name: Champagne Juillet-Lallement Brut Selection Grand Cru
description: An elegant Grand Cru Champagne from the Montagne de Reims where Verzy and Sillery lend chalky minerality to a harmonious blend of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. The NV Brut Sélection Grand Cru shows crisp citrus and white flower aromas, framed by a refined structure and gentle creamy texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8 °C in a tulip glass as an aperitif or alongside fine seafood, soft cheese or delicate hors d’oeuvre.
palate: creamy texture with orchard fruit and toast

name: Domaine Juillot Mercurey 1er Cru Blanc en Sazenay
description: This 2018 Mercurey Premier Cru “En Sazenay” from Domaine Michel Juillot is fashioned entirely of Chardonnay, its floral and orchard‑fruit aromas shaded by a subtle overlay of barrel toast, the mid‑palate rich yet refined, the texture enveloping before a crisp citrus‑tinged conclusion.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 11–13 °C it pairs beautifully with creamy seafood preparations or delicate poultry in herb sauce.
aroma: pear and honeysuckle with discreet oak
palate: rich, dense and smooth

name: Domaine Juillot Mercurey 1er Cru Blanc les Champs Martins
description: A refined expression of Mercurey’s white premier cru terroir with depth and poise, this 2017 blend offers orchard fruit richness alongside a firm mineral underpinning, guiding its structure with grace. It exudes velvet texture with restrained oak influence and impressive subtlety.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 12 to 13 °C after gentle aeration to reveal orchard nuances; harmonizes elegantly with grilled fish or seafood gratin.
aroma: ripe orchard fruit and wet stone notes
palate: velvety texture with mineral tension

name: Domaine Juillot Mercurey 1er Cru Rouge Champs Martin
appellation: Mercurey Premier Cru Les Champs Martins
description: This 2019 Mercurey Premier Cru "Les Champs Martins" from Domaine Michel Juillot offers a refined intertwining of dark cherry and discreet earthy notes, complemented by a whisper of forest undergrowth and menthol nuances on the nose. On the palate it reveals firm noble tannins, a sinewy structure and a balanced tension that speaks of mineral fidelity and a rustic yet elegant temperament.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C; pair with richly flavoured meats or game in creamy or peppered sauces that echo its hints of earth and spice.
palate: firm tannins, mineral, balanced tension

name: Cellars Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon
description: An opulent expression of Napa’s sun‑drenched Cabernet Sauvignon, this wine fills the glass with deep plum and dark berry framed by tawny tile and bark nuances: full‑bodied, layered, with fine structured tannins that are lightly chewy and promise elegant aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in broad tulip‑shape glasses: pairs beautifully with grilled rib‑eye or slow‑braised short ribs with herb jus.
aroma: deep plum and dark berries with tile and bark undertones
palate: full‑bodied, layered, fine‑tannic texture

name: Cellars Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Beckstoffer Georges III
description: This 2018 Beckstoffer Vineyard Georges III Cabernet Sauvignon from Kerr Cellars presents a beguiling bouquet of cassis and blackberry lifted by floral nuance and suggestions of underbrush and cedar chest. The palate is layered and plush with refined tannins framing deep dark‑berry flavors, earth and mineral undercurrents, and a seamless texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60°F in large Cabernet glasses to coax forth its floral lift and silky fruit, pairing beautifully with roasted lamb chops or aged hard cheeses.
palate: layered dark fruit, earth, mineral undergrowth

name: Cellars Sonoma Coast Chardonnay
description: A luminous and finely crafted Chardonnay from Kerr Cellars The 2019 Sonoma Coast reveals a graceful interplay of Asian pear and citrus blossom warmed by subtle vanilla bean and sage This wine has a striking weight yet retains tension and freshness
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to about 60°F in tulip‐shaped white wine glasses Pair with rich seafood or creamy poultry dishes to complement its vibrant acidity and almond nuances
aroma: Asian pear, vanilla bean, citrus blossom
palate: honey, almond, fresh fruit with minerality
foodPairings: grilled chicken with lemon and herbs

name: Winery Cabernet Sauvignon Sonoma County
description: This Cabernet Sauvignon presents a refined intensity, with layers of black cassis, clove spice and dusty earth that emerge from a well‑balanced structure with integrated tannins and poised freshness. It carries a graceful presence yet remains full‑bodied, charming on its own or with food.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature around 60–62°F in a large glass to allow the aromas to unfurl; pairs beautifully with grilled beef or lamb and richer vegetarian fare.
palate: Silky black fruit with anise and integrated tannins

name: Winery Chardonnay Russian River Valley Peter's Vineyard
description: An elegant and inviting Russian River Chardonnay that marries bright lemon curd and white peach with a whisper of sea salt and subtle oak spice, all wrapped in an animated yet refined texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to highlight its lively minerality; pairs beautifully with rich shellfish or creamy poultry preparations.
palate: saline‑driven acidity with fleshy texture
finish: candied lemon peel with sweet oak spice

name: Winery Zinfandel Dry Creek Valley
description: A richly textured Zinfandel of old‑world sensibility crafted in the heart of Dry Creek Valley, the 2021 Kokomo presents a ravishing garnet hue inviting the nose with cherry, anise and underbrush alongside bright black‑cherry and smoky‑plum fruit. Plush yet framed with bright acidity this wine reveals focused flavors of red plum, smoky herb and pepper in a balanced and elegant expression of Zinfandel.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled for balance, pairs beautifully with grilled sausages or tomato‑braised lamb ragu.
palate: red plum, smoky herb, pepper

name: Winery Zinfandel Dry Creek Valley
description: A richly textured Zinfandel of old‑world sensibility crafted in the heart of Dry Creek Valley, the 2022 Kokomo presents a ravishing garnet hue inviting the nose with cherry, anise and underbrush alongside bright black‑cherry and smoky‑plum fruit. Plush yet framed with bright acidity this wine reveals focused flavors of red plum, smoky herb and pepper in a balanced and elegant expression of Zinfandel.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled for balance, pairs beautifully with grilled sausages or tomato‑braised lamb ragu.
palate: red plum, smoky herb, pepper

name: Gerhard Kracher Cuvee Auslese
description: The 2023 Gerhard Kracher Cuvée Auslese (6/375) reveals a radiant pale gold hue, weaving apricot and quince notes with a touch of blossom honey, underpinned by subtle botrytis complexity. The palate is lusciously textured yet lifted by crisp citrus tension, finishing with saline precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip or dessert wine glass around 8 °C, pairing beautifully with fruit‑based desserts or soft blue cheeses.
palate: sweet citrus with botrytis lift

name: Gerhard Kracher Cuvee Beerenauslese
description: An opulent golden‑yellow nectar perfumed with botrytis spice, ripe stone fruits, and candied orange zest this 2021 Beerenauslese Cuvée reveals crystalline apricot and white peach against a backdrop of fine caramel and saline perfume
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10–12 °C this noble sweet wine elevates fruit‑based desserts, spicy Thai red curry, or fine aged cheese with composure
aroma: botrytis spice, ripe apricot, candied orange zest
palate: elegant honeyed stone fruit with balanced acidity
finish: delicate honeysuckle and saline mineral kiss

name: Gerhard Kracher Cuvee Zweigelt Beerenauslese
description: A luminous cherry‑red hue welcomes the 2021 Beerenauslese Zweigelt from Kracher, offering delicate smoky undercurrents beneath layers of red‑berry confiture and nougat‑tinged dried plum. The wine unfolds with elegant, juicy cherry fruit counterbalanced by a judicious mineral accent, culminating in a harmonious, gently sweet finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10–12 °C alongside dark chocolate treats, mature soft cheeses or bold game dishes to echo its depth and balance.
palate: ripe cherry elegance with mineral poise

name: Gerhard Kracher Gruner Veltliner
description: A pale green‑gold Grüner Veltliner that offers an elegant kiss of apple and citrus blossom with a faint whisper of spice, graceful in its clarity and poised with understated finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8 °C to highlight its freshness; ideal with light white meats or subtly herbed fish.
palate: crisp, finely textured, subtle spice

name: Gerhard Kracher Pinot Blanc
description: An elegant white wine of refined character the 2022 Gerhard Kracher Pinot Blanc offers a graceful expression of Austria’s Seewinkel terroir with gentle orchard fruits and a bright, saline clarity. It delivers poise rather than power with harmonious balance and a polished, dry finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass. Complements delicate seafood and light vegetable dishes with subtle acid‑driven pairing.
palate: bright, balanced and polished

name: Gerhard Kracher Pinot Gris
description: A pale green‑yellow Pinot Gris of graceful refinement offering gentle aromas of crisp apple, honey‑melon and subtle meadow herbs, unfolding on the palate with white tropical fruit, citrus brightness and a whisper of salinity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 10–12 °C alongside delicate white meats, fresh seafood or creamy cheeses for a harmonious match.
palate: juicy elegant texture, white tropical fruit, citrus

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslee Mini
description: A lush and honeyed Trockenbeerenauslese from the legendary Kracher estate, this non‑vintage mini half‑bottle seduces with delicate botrytis‑kissed aromas and a seamless sweetness that resonates with old‑world poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 10 °C to reveal its ethereal apricot and honey tones it pairs elegantly with blue cheese or a simple fruit‑based dessert.
palate: silky sweetness with apricot and marmalade notes

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #12
description: Bathed in bright golden‑yellow hues, this 2015 TBA No 12 Nouveau Vague whispers of meadow herbs, stone fruit and lychee, while evolving with pineapple and tropical fruit tones leading to honey‑kissed nuance and a lively grip: a rare liqueur‑like creation under 5 % alcohol yet offering the magnificence of a trockenbeerenauslese.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in delicate tasting glasses after a contemplative meal: it is sublime on its own or alongside blue cheese or fine dark chocolate.
palate: fresh, vibrant with pineapple and tropical fruits

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #2 Welschriesling NV
description: This Trockenbeerenauslese No 2 “Zwischen den Seen” from Kracher’s 2018 Kollektion is a lusciously botrytized white of crystalline precision The nose suggests shimmering apricot and spritely green apple framed by a whisper of herbaceous nuance The palate unfolds with succulent white peach and orchard fruit bound by racy acidity and a pillowy texture that carries the sweetness with noble restraint
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–12 °C to preserve freshness Pair with refined desserts or rich blue cheese to accentuate the wine’s gilded sweetness
palate: creamy orchard fruit with elegant acidity

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #3 Grand Cuvee NV
appellation: Trockenbeerenauslese No. 3 Grande Cuvée Nouvelle Vague (Kracher Collection)
description: This 2021 Kracher Collection Trockenbeerenauslese No. 3 Grande Cuvée Nouvelle Vague offers a succulent harmony of candied apricot, delicate caramel popcorn and toasty oak flavors. It exudes a saline purity and refined precision that carries both richness and vibrancy in equal measure.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10‑12 °C in small dessert‑wine glasses alongside rich foie gras terrines, apricot‑filled crêpes or fine blue cheese to highlight its luscious sweetness and balancing acidity.
aroma: candied apricot with toasted oak and caramel popcorn
palate: pure, vibrant fruit framed by saline precision
drinkWindow: Drink or hold over the next decade

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #4 Rosenmuskateller NV
description: This Trockenbeerenauslese from Gerhard Kracher’s 2021 Kracher Collection evokes a delicate tapestry of rose oil and candied cherry lifted by underlying notes of mocha and subtle floral tea. It is both concentrated and elegant with vibrant fruit purity held in balance by lively acidity and fine tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a small tulip glass around 10 °C paired with dark chocolate desserts, cherry pie or rich cheesecake to mirror its lush sweetness.
palate: elegant, concentrated, lemony freshness
finish: long, with candied lemon and grapefruit notes
drinkWindow: Very long ageing potential, likely several decades

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #6 Welschriesling NV
description: A luminous golden nectar brimming with crystalline sweetness and vibrant tension, this Trockenbeerenauslese #6 Welschriesling from Kracher’s 2020 collection unfolds layers of tropical fruit, candied citrus and a whisper of honeyed salinity with refined clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at 6–8 °C in a tulip glass to temper sweetness and highlight its vivacious acidity, ideal alongside blue‑cheese or apricot‑tart desserts.
aroma: ripe tropical fruit, candied orange, delicate nutty nuance
palate: dense, creamy, honey blossom and peach, balanced by crisp acidity

name: Gerhard Kracher Trockenbeerenauslese #6 Welschriesling Zds
description: This Trockenbeerenauslese embodies profound clarity and precision its bouquet layering bergamot and lavender over quince and lemon. The palate is lush and succulent yet balanced with a saline finesse and silky density.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 50–54 °F, pairing exquisitely with delicate tarts or tangy aged goat cheeses to offset its majestic sweetness.
palate: rich oily yet savory

name: Gerhard Kracher Zweigelt
description: A refined expression of Zweigelt from Kracher’s 2020 vintage offering a deep ruby red hue, lifted aromatics of sour cherry and ripe dark cherries with subtle floral freshness and gentle vanilla accents, all supported by juicy plum and dark berry flavors and fine soft tannins for elegant balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around eighteen °C to enhance its vibrant fruit and fine spice. Pair it with hearty red‑meat dishes or rich pasta preparations.
aroma: sour cherry and ripe dark cherries with floral freshness
palate: juicy plum and dark berries, subtle spiciness, gentle tannins

name: Domaine Kraft Vouvray Demi-Sec
description: An elegant expression of Vouvray from a warm 2016 vintage offering a pale hue with subtle green highlights. The bouquet unfolds gentle notes of fresh pear, white flower and citrus blossom framed by a whisper of minerality. On the palate it is refined and gracious with a wash of orchard fruits and a soft sweetness that balances vibrant natural acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 10 °C to showcase its balance. Ideal with creamy poultry preparations or subtly sweet desserts.
palate: orchard fruit framed by lively acidity
finish: lingering gentle sweetness and mineral clarity

name: La Ca'nova Barbaresco DOCG
description: Brimming with old‑world poise and focused energy this 2022 La Ca’ Nova Barbaresco reveals an elegant tapestry of red and black cherry enriched by licorice and rose petal nuances, grounded by a thread of chalky soil and woodsmoke.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool to explore its finely tuned structure; pair with earthy mushroom‑studded pasta or braised game to heighten its aromatic grace.
aroma: red and black cherries with rose and woodsmoke
palate: elegant, fresh, harmonious with fine tannins

name: La Ca'nova Barbaresco Montestefano DOCG
description: A classically composed Nebbiolo from Barbaresco’s famed Montestefano vineyard, offering a brooding yet perfumed expression of dark cherry, violet, anise and graphite, framed by mineral underpinnings and a firm structural core. It marries aristocratic poise with Montestefano’s signature density of fruit and savory spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve after decanting for an hour at 16–18 °C, with game or rich ragù accented by umami and leather‑driven sauces.
palate: Dense mid‑palate of cherry, licorice, tobacco

name: La Dame de Montrose Saint Estephe
description: In a graceful expression of Saint‑Estèphe elegance La Dame de Montrose 2019 unfolds with poised black fruit and graphite nuances enlivened by a hint of cedar, its structure refined yet assured.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature to accompany roasted lamb or mushroom‑dusted duck, allowing its tension and plush tannins to emerge.
palate: medium‑bodied supple dark fruit with fine tannins

name: La Rosalie Sauvignon Blanc Igp Atlantique
description: A bright expression of coastal southwest France, this Sauvignon Blanc radiates vibrancy with citrus blossom and grapefruit peel perched upon fresh‑cut herbal nuances, reflecting the breezy terroir of IGP Atlantique.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C highlighting its crisp acidity, ideal with shellfish or light vegetarian fare.
palate: Bright, saline lemon‑lime fruit

name: Pinot Noir Pays D'oc
description: A polished ruby hued red from the southern slopes of Languedoc this 2021 La Tène Pinot Noir reveals subtle floral whispers of iris entwined with sunlit wild strawberry and bramble. The palate is silky and generous lifting bright red fruit across a supple frame with a delicate savory brush of tannin at close.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled about 12 °C to enhance its freshness and pair it with simply prepared poultry or grilled salmon for a refined yet approachable harmony.
palate: silky, juicy, bright red fruit

name: Château Lilian Ladouys Saint Estephe
description: The 2018 Château Lilian Ladouys reveals a refined richness born of its Saint‑Estèphe lineage. It exudes an elegant core of red and black fruit framed by subtle mint and violet accents, all supported by a noble structure of polished oak and succulent tannins.
sommelierNotes: Best served at cellar temperature with roast lamb, venison or richly sauced beef—it will unfurl with decanting and reward patience.
aroma: raspberry, cherry, blackberry mingling with mint and violet
palate: rich fruit and polished tannins, refined oak melting into salted butter‑caramel

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis 1er Cru les Vaillons
description: This 2019 Chablis Premier Cru Les Vaillons from Domaine Thierry Laffay, crafted from 100 percent Chardonnay, offers an elegant and poised expression : bright orchard fruit meets stony mineral clarity in a refined texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled at roughly 50 °F, perfect alongside delicate seafood or subtly sauced white meats to echo its crystalline minerality.
palate: bright, mineral‑driven and finely etched

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis 1er Cru les Vaillons
description: A crystalline and vibrant Chablis premier cru showing razor‑sharp clarity of line and flinty minerality framed by discreet notes of pear and lemon blossom, threaded through with a hint of chalky salinity for structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip wine glasses to preserve the wine’s subtle mineral bouquet, ideal with oysters or simply on its own as an elegant aperitif.
palate: vibrant acidity with saline precision

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis
description: The 2022 Dom Thierry Laffay Chablis reveals crystalline purity and chiseled mineral tension underscored by a subtle glimmer of white flowers and lime. It embodies the restrained elegance of northern Burgundy, with a poised structure that speaks of slate and sea‑shell soils tempered by vibrant acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in fine white wine glasses to showcase its precise clarity and racy freshness, and enjoy alongside lightly seasoned seafood or mild goat cheese.
palate: steely minerality with citrus drive

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis Vieilles Vignes
description: This Chablis Vieilles Vignes from Domaine Thierry Laffay offers an elegant interplay of chalky mineral tension and vibrant orchard fruit, where pear and quince converge with crystalline clarity, finishing with an undercurrent of saline energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip‐shaped glass to showcase its bright acidity and minerality; pairs exquisitely with oysters, sole meunière or a delicate goat cheese.
aroma: pear and quince with chalky mineral lift
palate: silky texture framed by brisk, saline acidity

name: Domaine Thierry Laffay Chablis Vieilles Vignes
description: A crystalline Chablis from Domaine Thierry Laffay et Filles the 2022 Vieilles Vignes is built upon venerable vines planted by the family matriarch in 1968 it offers a vibrant mineral thrust layered with citrus clarity and white floral undertones
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 °C it pairs splendidly with oysters or delicate seafood and rewards short‑term cellaring through 2029
aroma: white flowers, green apple, lemon peel
palate: vivid citrus energy, striking salinity

name: Domaine Lamarche la Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole
description: This 2017 La Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole from Domaine François Lamarche reveals an exquisite fusion of silken black‑cherry richness and floral grace with a whisper of forest floor that evokes the distinguished Vosne‑Romanée tradition. A refined structure frames the pure fruit with mineral underpinnings and a poised tension that promises graceful evolution over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16–18 °C after decanting for an hour to unveil its full aromatic bloom: ideal alongside herb‑crusted lamb or sautéed morels.
aroma: black‑cherry and violet with forest‑floor nuance
palate: silky texture with vibrant red fruit and mineral precision

name: Domaine Lamarche la Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole
description: This 2017 La Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole from Domaine François Lamarche reveals an exquisite fusion of silken black‑cherry richness and floral grace with a whisper of forest floor that evokes the distinguished Vosne‑Romanée tradition. A refined structure frames the pure fruit with mineral underpinnings and a poised tension that promises graceful evolution over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16–18 °C after decanting for an hour to unveil its full aromatic bloom: ideal alongside herb‑crusted lamb or sautéed morels.
aroma: black‑cherry and violet with forest‑floor nuance
palate: silky texture with vibrant red fruit and mineral precision

name: Santenay Rouge 1er Cru Clos des Gravieres
appellation: Santenay Premier Cru Clos des Gravières
description: This wine offers a refined expression of Premier Cru Santenay through its youthful and mature vine parcels. The nose evokes yellow orchard fruit and chalky mineral tones, while the palate reveals clean, pure fruit with a subtle richness and lengthy mineral finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C in a tulip glass to highlight its bright fruit and mineral character, an ideal companion to scallop ceviche or rich shellfish preparations.
aroma: yellow orchard fruit with chalky mineral edge
palate: clean, pure fruit with subtle richness

name: Champagne Paul Launois Monochrome Blanc de Blancs
description: An impeccably poised Extra‑Brut Blanc de Blancs from Mesnil‑sur‑Oger this Monochrome NV offers crystalline finesse and chalk‑driven precision, its pulse of delicate bubbles unveiling subtle almond‑and‑brioche nuances luminous as crushed chalk.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass its refined structure enhances shellfish and creamy fish dishes.
palate: crisp citrus intensity, salinity

name: Le C de Calon Segur Saint Estephe
description: The 2019 Le C de Calon Ségur offers an enchanting blend of dark berry brightness and refined structure, evoking Saint‑Estèphe’s classic gravely terroir while retaining a fresh, youthful appeal. Its character leans toward elegance rather than overt power, suggesting a wine built for immediate pleasure with latent depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature for graceful expression, pairing beautifully with roast lamb or mushroom‑rich dishes to complement its vibrant fruit and subtly stony texture.
aroma: ripe dark berries with a hint of spice
palate: fresh, medium‑bodied with balanced tannins

name: Le Pere Jules Calvados Pays D'auge Ten Year Old
description: An elegantly aged Calvados from the heart of Pays d’Auge, this ten‑year‑old Le Père Jules evokes the gentle warmth of baked apple compote kissed by soft vanilla and a whisper of spice, refined by a decade of oak maturation to reveal a poised yet expressive character.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a tulip glass at room temperature as a contemplative digestif; it also harmonizes beautifully with strong Norman cheeses or as a subtle finishing touch to a coffee ritual.
aroma: baked apples with vanilla and spice
palate: rich orchard fruit wrapped in gentle oak warmth
foodPairings: a fine espresso or cigar accompaniment
drinkWindow: Now through many years if stored properly

name: Le Pere Jules Calvados Pays D'auge Three Years Old
description: A graceful youthful calvados that offers a delicate orchard‑fresh apple character supporting a subtle oak embrace, finishing with a refined clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in a tulip glass, perfect as a digestif or alongside ripe cheeses or apple‑based desserts.
aroma: crisp green apple with light vanilla
palate: fresh orchard fruit framed by gentle oak spice

name: Le Pere Jules Poire Brut
description: A lively, naturally effervescent poiré from the venerable Le Père Jules estate in Normandy, offering the delicate crispness of freshly bitten pear in a gently playful style true to old‑world perry. The modest alcohol accentuates its purity and graceful balance, reflecting biodynamic orchard heritage.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender flutes or chilled tumbler, an elegant match for delicate seafood or served as a refreshing apéritif on warm summer evenings.
palate: light pear flesh with subtle minerality
drinkWindow: drink now to within 2–3 years of purchase

name: Le Vignerons de Florensac Picpoul de Pinet
description: A crisp and elegant Picpoul de Pinet from Les Vignerons de Florensac offers pale yellow hue with green highlights its aroma suggests grapefruit and citrus framed by delicate stone‑fruit nuances the palate is lively and fresh with bright citrus energy underscored by gentle lees‑driven roundness
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled alongside oysters or light seafood the brisk acidity cleanses the palate and complements creamy preparations
palate: lively citrus with lees‑driven roundness

name: Domaine Lebreuil Savigny les Beaune 1er Cru aux Grand Liards
description: This 2020 Savigny‑lès‑Beaune “Aux Grands Liards” expresses an elegant core of red cherry and raspberry framed by subtle earthy nuance and fine-grained tannins, offering both finesse and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to brighten its vibrant fruit—pairs beautifully with veal, game birds or light red meats in sauce.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with earth
palate: fine‑grained tannins, elegant fruit

name: Domaine Lebreuil Savigny les Beaune
description: A charming Savigny‑lès‑Beaune from Domaine Lebreuil vintage 2022, this Pinot Noir unfolds with a poised elegance and clarity of red berry expression. The wine shows harmonious structure and gentle tannin framed by Burgundian finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to reveal its floral fruit profile, ideal with subtly seasoned poultry or soft cheeses.
palate: refined fruit with soft acidity

name: Chambolle Musigny
description: An elegant Chambolle‑Musigny from the venerable Domaine Lécheneaut 2011 vintage, revealing a refined intensity of red cherry and rose petal supported by a fine mineral undercurrent and silken tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C, allowing the fragrant rose and red berry character to emerge; pair with lightly roasted duck or mushroom‑fricassée.
palate: silky tannins with mineral lift

name: Chorey les Beaune
description: A graceful Bourgogne rouge from the house of Lécheneaut the 2006 Chorey‑les‑Beaune shows a light supple frame yet reveals admirable depth of character Its lively crimson hue preludes a delicate aroma of raspberry and Morello cherry interwoven with subtle licorice and forest floor
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C in slender Burgundy glasses to highlight its vivacious red fruit and elegant structure Pair with earthy dishes or roast poultry to complement its finesse
palate: Light, round, with balanced structure
finish: Lingering red fruit and gentle earth

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Bourgogne Hautes Cotes de Nuits Blanc
description: A subtly golden Chardonnay from the heights west of the Côte de Nuits this 2012 Bourgogne Hautes‑Côtes de Nuits Blanc from Domaine Lecheneaut unfolds with delicate hawthorn and honeysuckle notes intertwined with apple, lemon, and gentle hazelnut nuances, held within a structure at once supple and precise.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a fine white Burgundy glass to welcome its freshness and subtle oak aging; ideally accompanied by shellfish in buttery sauces or mild goat cheese.
palate: buttery yet fresh, solid build with elegant density
drinkWindow: drink now to next few years

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Borniques
description: This 2020 Domaine Lécheneaut Chambolle‑Musigny 1er Cru Les Borniques unfolds with an elegant density and beautifully refined structure, presenting a bouquet of red fruits and subtle rose petal perfume. It is a wine of power and finesse, delivering the harmony of an iron hand in a velvet glove.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool around 16 °C, ideally with richly flavored yet delicate dishes such as roast duck breast or wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: delicate red fruits and rose petal
palate: silky tannins with refined density
foodPairings: filet of beef in red wine sauce

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Chambolle Musigny
description: A graceful expression of Chambolle‑Musigny village from Domaine Lécheneaut 2021 offering elegant poise and purity of cherry‑blossom fruit framed by a fine stony tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in translucent crystal to reveal its perfumed charm. Ideal with delicate dishes such as herb‑roasted poultry or soft cheeses.
aroma: scented red fruit with cherry blossom and floral lift
palate: clean, elegant, floral‑tinged, silken texture with mineral grip
finish: focused and poised, with white‑stone energy

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
appellation: Clos de la Roche Grand Cru
description: A wine of true pedigree from Morey‑Saint‑Denis the 2012 Clos de la Roche Grand Cru from Domaine Lécheneaut offers a lithe yet powerful expression of Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir. It is sleek and vinous with core of dark berry fruit threaded with fine spicy tension and chalk‑tinged structure.

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Nuits Saint Georges
description: A robust yet refined expression of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges, drawn from a tapestry of venerable parcels. The 2013 vintage reveals an invigorating alchemy of cherry and black‑currant scents, woven with hints of rose and licorice, offering admirable structure and poised elegance.

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Nuits Saint Georges Au Chouillet
description: This 2012 Domaine Lécheneaut Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Au Chouillet unfolds with refined energy and gracious poise, its silky texture framing a nuanced tapestry of sweet red berries, menthol, tobacco and spice, offering an inviting expression of northern Côte de Nuits terroir.

aroma: sweet red berries, menthol, tobacco, spice
palate: silky and gracious, red fruit with spice lift

name: Domaine Lecheneaut Vosne Romanee
description: This 2021 Domaine Lécheneaut Vosne‑Romanée unveils a refined ruby hue and a floral‑tinged red fruit perfume, evolving with graceful accents of red cherry, raspberry and warm spice drawing from well‑rooted 57‑year‑old Pinot Noir vines

aroma: red cherry and raspberry with spice
palate: elegant red fruit framed by balanced acidity and soft tannins

name: Nuits Saint Georges 1er Cru les Pruliers
description: This Nuits‑Saint‑Georges 1er Cru Les Pruliers 2011 by Domaine Lécheneaut presents a brooding elegance rooted in impeccable terroir. A deep robe heralds a beguiling bouquet of fresh red berries, wild prune and gentle licorice entwined with spicy rose leveled by an undercurrent of earthy woodland. With maturity it unfolds generous sensuality, balanced by a subtly firm structure that promises compelling evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in tall tulip‑shaped glasses to reveal layered nuances. Ideal alongside herb‑crusted rack of lamb or wild mushroom‑rich dishes, its earthy depth and silky texture will shine.
aroma: fresh red fruit, wild prune, licorice, spiced rose
palate: generous sensual smoothness with earthy depth

name: Nuits Saint Georges Au Chouillet
description: A noble expression of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges from Lécheneaut’s venerable old vines in Au Chouillet this 2011 vintage reveals restrained wild berry and floral aromas that deepen with age into alluring confit strawberry and pale tobacco nuances drawn from the rich, marly‑alluvial terroir. The palate is compact and structured promising graceful evolution rather than immediate generosity. Sommelier Notes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to showcase the evolution of its earthy complexity and pair elegantly with simply roasted game birds or richly sauced pork.
sommelierNotes: Allow a gentle decant to reveal its layered earthy and wild fruit tones, alongside roast duck or mushroom‑rich dishes.
palate: compact and structured
finish: evolving confit fruit and subtle tobacco

name: Leda Pucci Chianti Classico DOCG
description: A bright ruby red wine of inviting charm it offers gentle aromas of forest berries and underbrush with a smooth elegant structure marrying fruit and grace in seamless balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 18 °C and pair with classic Tuscan fare such as roast meats or baked pastas to complement its harmony.
palate: smooth, elegant and harmonious

name: Leda Pucci Chianti Classico DOCG

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Legado de Moncayo Garnacha Do Campo de Borja
description: A refined modern Garnacha that marries vibrant red and black fruit and subtle herbaceous lift to clear expression of slate and limestone terroir. The palate offers vivid fruit intensity while maintaining poise and clarity through to a fresh and lingering close.

aroma: red and black berries with herbal nuance

name: Maison Leroy Meursault 1er Cru les Genevrieres
description: A luminous example of late‑1970s Burgundy from Maison Leroy offering fine golden hues a graceful patina of mature Meursault charm and refined depth reminiscent of old‑world precision and mineral elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 10‑12 °C in a large white Burgundy glass to reveal nuances of aged Chardonnay; pairs beautifully with butter‑roasted lobster or softly sautéed scallops.
palate: rich and textured with graceful acidity

name: Maison Leroy Puligny Montrachet 1er Cru
description: A poised and introspective white Burgundy from 1978, this Maison Leroy Puligny‑Montrachet Premier Cru exudes noble restraint. Mature aromatics of honey, cold stone and a whisper of aubépine emerge with grace accompanied by an austere yet noble fruit character.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass. Pair with rich poultry or lobster to highlight the wine’s refined tension.
palate: elegant, austere fruit unfolding with poise

name: Maison Leroy Maranges
description: A graceful expression of Maison Leroy’s southern Côte de Beaune, this 2010 Maranges unveils bright red berry and violette whispers, caressed by an undercurrent of earthy spice. The medium‑bodied frame is refined and poised, backed by gentle tannins that suggest both elegance and early approachability.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool, around 15 °C, to reveal its supple texture and subtle complexity; ideal with gently roasted poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes to complement its delicate spice and earth nuances.
aroma: fresh red berries with violet and peppery spice
palate: silky, medium‑bodied with earthy red fruit and supple tannins
finish: lingering subtle spice and clean freshness

name: Les Forts de Latour Pauillac
description: A noble expression of Pauillac from Château Latour’s second wine the 2019 Les Forts de Latour offers an elegant yet powerful presence framed by deep black fruits and fine cedar overtones, with a mineral precision that speaks of its gravelly terroir. The texture is refined and poised with linear tannins guiding long poised persistence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 17 °C after decanting to soften its structure pair with roast lamb or beef Wellington to echo its depth.
palate: fresh dark fruit, spice, finely grained tannins

name: Les Griffons de Pichon Baron Pauillac
description: This is a second‑wine Pauillac from Château Pichon‑Longueville Baron that offers refined intensity and precise structure. The 2019 vintage unfolds in an intense purple hue and captivates with delicate black‑fruit aromas underscored by subtle spice and minerality, balancing generosity with elegant tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature to emphasize its freshness and tannic grip. Pairs wonderfully with slow‑roasted lamb shoulder or aged hard cheeses like Comté to mirror its rich structure and textural depth.
aroma: Delicate black fruits with subtle wood spice
palate: Generous and structured, fleshy with tension

name: Les Pagodes de Cos Saint Estephe
description: This 2018 Les Pagodes de Cos presents an alluring convergence of dense black fruit and exotic spice, offering a seamless weave of cassis, blackberry and hints of violet, all framed by smoky cedar nuances and refined oak presence. The texture is velvety yet structured, with refreshing saline tension and elegant tannins that promise both immediate charm and graceful mid‑term evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in large-bowl glasses after an hour of airing to reveal its nuanced perfume; pairs exquisitely with lamb, roast duck or aged hard cheeses.

name: Château Lestrille Entre Deux Mers Blanc
description: This Château Lestrille 2019 Entre‑Deux‑Mers Blanc unfurls with vibrant citrus and white stone fruit, redolent of lime blossom and apricot, lifted by a subtle mineral undertow, offering a delightful interplay of vivacity and richness. The palate is fresh yet rounded, its mouthwatering texture framed by balanced acidity lending a generous, nuanced presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve well-chilled in spring or early summer alongside simply prepared seafood or goat cheese, where its bright fruit and gentle weight will sing.

name: Rosso Piceno DOC Rubideo

description: This Bourgogne Rouge 2021 from Lignier‑Michelot is a graceful expression of Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir, presenting bright red cherry and bilberry notes, gently underpinned by violet floral perfume and a hint of cassis. sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled, around 14 °C, after minimal aeration to showcase its fresh red‑fruited charm alongside soft tannins.
palate: medium‑bodied with vibrant acidity and cassis depth

name: Domaine Lignier-Michelot Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru Faconnieres
description: A finely poised expression of Morey‑Saint‑Denis Premier Cru from Lignier‑Michelot, the 2021 Les Faconnières reveals elegant red cherry and raspberry aromas framed by subtle floral nuance and gentle spice, its medium‑bodied allure underpinned by a poised mineral thread indicating terroir clarity.

name: Domaine Lignier-Michelot Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru les Cheneverey
description: This 2017 Morey‑Saint‑Denis Premier Cru Les Chenevery from Domaine Lignier‑Michelot reveals a richly perfumed core of rose petal and cherry framed by dark spice and nuanced sauvage undertones, its profile balanced yet compelling with a poised substance that promises graceful unfolding over time.

aroma: rose petal, dark cherry, sweet spice
palate: medium‑full body, layered fruit, fine grain tannins

name: Domaine Lignier-Michelot Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru les Chenevery
description: This Morey‑Saint‑Denis Premier Cru Les Chenevery 2021 by Domaine Lignier‑Michelot reveals fine‐boned elegance and mineral poise. Crafted with approximately seventy percent whole‑cluster, it unfolds with taut red fruit and limestone‑infused tension that suggests both restraint and latent grandeur.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a gentle decant to open its layered texture. It will pair beautifully with roasted lamb or enriched fowl dishes.
aroma: taut red cherry and subtle spice
palate: mineral‑tinged, elegant structure

name: Domaine Lignier-Michelot Morey Saint Denis 1er Cru Lis Chenevery
description: This is a strikingly poised Pinot Noir from a distinguished parcel within Morey‑Saint‑Denis. It presents refined red fruit framed by taut mineral energy and elegant structure, hinting at both power and restraint. It feels noble and youthful, promising captivating evolution.

palate: silky, taut structure with precise red fruit

description: A refined village‑level Pinot Noir from over half‑century old vines in Morey‑Saint‑Denis, showing deep red and black fruit woven with spicy and floral accents framed by supple, structured fruit from a generous yet elegantly balanced cuvée.

palate: fresh yet generous tart fruit

name: Lismore Estate Chardonnay
description: An elegant expression of South African cool‑climate Chardonnay, the 2018 Lismore Estate Reserve offers bright citrus and stone‑fruit character intertwined with jasmine and walnut complexity framed by gentle oak nuance and a mineral‑tinged core.

name: Château Loumelat Blaye Cotes de Bordeaux Rouge

name: Château Loumelat Bordeaux Blanc

The palate reveals a pleasing interplay of vivacious acidity and soft texture with hints of white pear and soft mineral undertones. It offers an enduring, subtly saline finish that echoes its maritime terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 °C: it complements delicate seafood or simply shines as a refined aperitif.
palate: vivacious acidity with white pear and subtle minerality

name: Luis Pato Baga Espumante Bruto

palate: bright acidity, red berry fruit, subtle tannic grip

name: Luis Pato Maria Gomes
description: A gracious expression of Bairrada’s native Maria Gomes grape lightly buoyed by Bical, this 2025 offering from Luís Pato unfolds with delicate floral perfume and a subtly fruit‑tinged allure. The palate brings balanced vibrancy, with softened citrus and orchard fruit tones carried on a poised medium body.

palate: crisp citrus, yellow plum

name: Luis Pato Vinha Velhas Blanco

aroma: pear and white flowers with almond nuance

name: Luis Pato Vinha Velhas Tinto

palate: vibrant red fruit framed by firm yet silky acidity

palate: fresh morning‑dew brightness meets California richness

name: Wines Essence Santa Maria Valley
description: The 2023 Essence from Lumen Wines in Santa Maria Valley captures a luminous rust‑hued skin‑contact Pinot Gris with a scent of grapefruit blossom, passion fruit, and hazelnut. The sip reveals bright lemon curd and mango basil, all framed by a round warmth that belies its subtlety.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a white glass, pairing beautifully with spiced shellfish, creamy curries or aged cheese.
palate: lemon curd and mango basil

name: Wines Grenache Santa Barbara County
description: In the glass this Grenache reveals a luminous ruby hue and youthful brightness. Aromas of wild strawberry and violet mingle with whispers of white pepper and crushed herbs offering an elegant yet vivacious expression of Santa Barbara fruit. The palate is fresh with bright red berry flavors threaded through fine spice and a lithe structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to accentuate its vivacity, ideal with grilled duck breast or herbed lamb with a touch of acidity to complement its spice.
palate: bright red berries with fine spice

name: Wines Pinot Noir Sanford & Benedict Vineyard
description: A graceful expression of Sta. Rita Hills terroir from a historic site Lumen’s 2020 Pinot Noir melds bright red fruits with savory earth, showing both energy and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55 °F in a large wine glass to highlight its aromatic complexity; pairs beautifully with roasted quail or mushroom risotto.
aroma: Bing cherry and strawberry with loamy undertones
palate: Ripe, dense fruit opening into wild herb and toasted sage

name: Wines Pinot Noir Santa Maria Valley
description: The 2022 Lumen Wines Pinot Noir from Santa Maria Valley unfolds with a vivid tableau of wild strawberry and savory sage framed by subtle spring grass notes, giving way to under ripe Bing cherry, tart cranberry and a whiff of smoked duck, all poised on a mineral-tinged and lingering canvas.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a medium stem glass around 55–58°F to highlight its savory fruit and bright acidity; pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast or grilled pork with herb accents.
palate: under ripe Bing cherry, tart cranberry, smoked duck, mineral clarity
finish: savory and long with piercing fruit

name: Bodegas Luna Beberide Mencia Do Bierzo
description: This youthful 2025 Luna Beberide Mencía presents a bright, raspberry‑red hue and unfolds with an arresting purity of fresh cherry and red berries lifted by fine mineral threads, conveying both vitality and devotion to the Bierzo terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at 12–14 °C allowing its vivacious fruit and elegant acidity to accentuate light tapas or grilled vegetables.
aroma: bright red cherry and mineral lift
palate: vivid red fruit, balanced, unoaked clarity
finish: long, subtly sweet with fine tannins

name: Vosne Romanee 1er Cru les Gaudichots
description: Machard de Gramont's 2014 Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Gaudichots offers fragrant Pinot Noir in a cooler, more linear register. Red and black cherry, woodland spice, and fine tannin gather toward a long mineral finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature after a careful decant for sediment; pair with roast duck, veal, or game birds.
palate: Silky fruit, fine tannin, mineral line

name: Vosne Romanee 1er Cru les Gaudichots
description: Machard de Gramont's 2015 Vosne-Romanée Premier Cru Les Gaudichots is an exceptionally rare Pinot Noir with dark cherry fruit, floral perfume, and finely wrought spice. The palate is concentrated yet composed, with mineral tension carrying a long, savory close.
sommelierNotes: Decant gently for sediment and serve at 15-16°C with duck, veal, or feathered game; the wine can continue to develop in a sound cellar.
palate: Concentrated, silky, mineral

name: Wines Chardonnay Mount Carmel Vineyard Santa Rita Hills
description: This 2021 Mail Road Wines Chardonnay from Mount Carmel Vineyard in Sta. Rita Hills reveals ripe melon and brioche lifted by acacia blossoms and chalky mineral energy, weaving a layered, medium‑bodied elegance with crisp acidity and saline length.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool in tulip‑shaped glass to highlight the wine’s purity and vibrant structure, pairing harmoniously with oysters, grilled scallops or creamy risotto.
palate: layered medium body, chalk‑driven depth

name: Wines Chardonnay Santa Rita Hills
description: The 2023 Mail Road Chardonnay from Santa Rita Hills is a radiant expression of Mt. Carmel’s unique terroir presenting layers of honeyed mango, chalk and chamomile tea gently threaded by ginger spice character. The wine balances richness and precision with seamless minerality and scintillating acidity that speak of both power and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its complexity, pairing beautifully with seared scallops or creamy shellfish pastas.
palate: chalky minerality with ginger spice

name: Wines Pinot Noir Mount Carmel Vineyard Santa Rita Hills
description: The 2021 Mail Road Wines Pinot Noir Mount Carmel Vineyard offers a clarion expression of Sta. Rita Hills terroir with ripe red and black fruit perfumed overtones accented by scorched earth graphite and white pepper. It embodies a beguiling synthesis of concentration and grace, finely poised and built for long‑term development.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to unveil its purity alongside delicately seasoned poultry or forest‑floor inspired dishes, and allow a few breaths in glass to reveal its layered detail.
aroma: ripe red and black fruits, scorched earth, graphite, white pepper
palate: medium‑to‑full body, integrated acidity, ripe building tannins

name: Wines Pinot Noir Santa Rita Hills
description: This 2023 Mail Road Wines Sta. Rita Hills Pinot Noir unfolds with radiant red berry perfume—cranberry and wild strawberry—framed by salinity and delicate floral lift, evoking the cooling ocean breezes of its limestone‑rich Mount Carmel origins. It offers a lithe yet textured profile with seamless red fruit and subtle herbal spice, lingering in precise focus.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 55°F in a medium tulip glass to accentuate its brightness. Pairs exquisitely with roasted quail or mushroom‑creamed pappardelle, enhancing its floral and savory undertones.

name: Maison Camille Giroud Auxey Duresses Blanc
description: This voluptuous Auxey‑Duresses Blanc 2020 by Maison Camille Giroud unfolds with pale golden hues and an expansive appeal it presents gentle almond‑paste nuances and yellow‑fruit aromas touched with toasty oak drawn from traditional barrel fermentation and maturation techniques ([louislatour.com](https://www.louislatour.com/pdf/en/auxey-duresses-blanc-2020-2772.pdf?utm_source=openai))

sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10°C to spotlight its racy acidity it partners beautifully with shellfish or lightly sauced poultry

description: The 2020 Maison Camille Giroud Bourgogne Rouge is an elegant Pinot Noir blend drawn from the Hautes‑Côtes, Pommard and Mercurey that offers a silken tension underpinned by chalky minerality and vibrant red fruit energy. A graceful Bourgogne in the old‑world tradition, the wine unfolds with pure raspberry and blackcurrant accents brightened by subtle spice and a sleek tannic thread.

description: From this premier‑cru Chassagne‑Montrachet Les Vergers 2022 by Maison Camille Giroud emerges a poised, mineral‑inflected Chardonnay whose character is defined by fresh orchard fruit and subtle floral intensity lifted by saline tension : the concentrated texture speaks of cool limestone soils and fifty‑year‑old vines drawn from the historic Les Vergers climat, imparting both depth and restraint.

name: Maison Camille Giroud Meursault les Vireuils
description: A poised and mineral Meursault from Maison Camille Giroud, the 2022 Les Vireuils captivates with its refined expression of pear and ripe orchard fruit framed by subtle hazelnut and floral whispers, all lifted by a chalky limestone clarity on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 11–13 °C to highlight its vibrancy before dinner with seafood or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: chalky minerality with tension and finesse

name: Maison Camille Giroud Morey Saint Denis Clos des Godelles
description: This elegant Pinot Noir from Maison Camille Giroud reveals classic Morey‑Saint‑Denis character with refined blueberry and chalky minerality, framed by a graceful sense of poise and structure that belies its first vintage. Its texture is supple yet lithe offering a whisper of rose petal and vibrant energy on the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature around 14°C to showcase its finesse; pairs especially well with roasted game birds and mushroom‑rich terrines.
palate: elegant, refined, rose petal lift

name: Maison Camille Giroud Morey Saint Denis Clos des Godelles

Its texture is supple yet lithe offering a whisper of rose petal and vibrant energy on the palate.

name: Maison Camille Giroud Puligny Montrachet 1er Cru les Referts
description: This 2020 Maison Camille Giroud Puligny‑Montrachet 1er Cru “Les Referts” unfurls with a pale yellow hue and a subtle floral elegance. It offers a refined core of yellow fruit and whispers of vanilla and almond, all wrapped in a supple, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 – 14 °C, alongside delicate fish or shellfish, or lingering over fine cheeses, to let its caressing texture and gentle floral lift sing.
aroma: yellow fruit and soft vanilla floral whiffs
palate: ample and round with almond and subtle vanilla

name: Maison Camille Giroud Volnay
description: The 2022 Maison Camille Giroud Volnay offers refined Burgundian charm with a delicate bouquet and graceful structure. Silken notes of bright red cherry and subtle violet interplay with gentle earth beneath a poised frame, delivering admirable balance and nuanced depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature to showcase its finesse, pairing beautifully with savory cuts such as roast duck or mushroom‑braised game.
palate: silky red fruits with subtle earth

name: Maison Camille Giroud Vosne Romanee les Chalandins
description: This 2018 Maison Camille Giroud Vosne‑Romanée “Les Chalandins” presents refined density and youthful poise underpinned by mineral precision and vivid red fruit clarity : it exudes energy and structure without heaviness, offering floral clarity and saline grip.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 15 °C in tulip‑shaped glasses and pair with roasted veal or game birds to complement its balance of red fruit and fresh tannins.
palate: sleek red‑fruit core with mineral tension

name: Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand Vergelesses Blanc les Belles Filles
description: A luminous Chardonnay from Pernand‑Vergelesses, this wine unfolds with refined elegance, its pale golden‑green hue leading to delicate floral and mineral perfume with a whisper of salinity and citrus lift. The palate combines vibrant freshness and vivacity with an underlying creamy texture, delivering graceful precision and a lingering saline‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–14 °C to reveal its floral and mineral nuances. Ideal with delicate seafood, shellfish or light creamy poultry preparations.
palate: fresh and vibrant with creamy texture

name: Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand Vergelesses Rouge 1er Cru les Vergelesses
description: A poised expression of Côte de Beaune Pinot Noir from Domaine Pavelot this 2020 Pernand‑Vergelesses 1er Cru Les Vergelesses reveals a harmony of compote‑like red fruit and delicate spice, laced with chalky mineral depth and framed by well‑integrated tannins derived from subtle oak aging.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 14 °C in fine Burgundy glasses to showcase its elegance; lovely with pan‑roasted duck breast or soft‑ripened brie.
aroma: ripe red cherries, subtle spice, earthy minerality
palate: supple yet structured red fruits and refined tannins

name: Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand Vergelesses Rouge les Belles Filles
description: Bright ruby in hue this 2020 Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand‑Vergelesses Rouge “Les Belles Filles” offers a refined interplay of fresh red cherry and raspberry scents underpinned by an elegant spicy thread and gentle earthiness. The palate is supple yet structured by fine tannins that carry the fruit with poise and grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C, gently decanted if young, and pair with roast poultry or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: fresh red cherry and raspberry with subtle spice
palate: supple structure, fine tannins, poised fruit

name: Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand Vergelesses Rouge les Belles Filles
description: Bright ruby in hue this 2022 Maison Hugues Pavelot Pernand‑Vergelesses Rouge “Les Belles Filles” offers a refined interplay of fresh red cherry and raspberry scents underpinned by an elegant spicy thread and gentle earthiness. The palate is supple yet structured by fine tannins that carry the fruit with poise and grace.

aroma: fresh red cherry and raspberry with subtle spice
palate: supple structure, fine tannins, poised fruit

name: Maison Jacques Parent Ladoix
description: A quietly noble burgundy from Domaine Parent expressing the soul of Ladoix 1er Cru in a restrained yet expressive voice. Silken layers of wild cherry and bramble framed by underbrush and a gentle touch of forest floor. This wine carries a tone of structure and grace that promises both immediate appeal and graceful evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature in large-bowled glasses to reveal nuance: divine with roasted duckling, wild mushrooms or rich game terrine.
aroma: wild cherry and bramble with forest floor
palate: silken with refined yet firm tannins

name: Maison Jacques Parent Pommard 1ER Cru les Argillieres
description: This 2019 Pommard Premier Cru Les Argillières from Maison Jacques Parent reveals a graceful balance between structure and delicacy, nuanced by clay‑limestone terroir and refined élevage in a portion of new oak, yielding an elegant and seductively poised red Burgundy.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, decant briefly to soften its supple yet refined tannins Pair with red meats or roasted game for harmony.
palate: suave red and black cherry underpinned by fine-earthy spice

name: Maison Morey-Blanc Saint Aubin 1er Cru en Remilly
description: The 2023 Maison Morey‑Blanc Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru En Remilly reveals itself with an elegantly stony presence and floral undertones complemented by a whisper of hazelnut smoke, reflecting the northeast‑facing mid‑slope terroir near Chassagne‑Montrachet. The palate is precise and mineral‑driven with crystalline acidity and a structured yet graceful texture that promises refined evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tall stemware to showcase its tension and clarity, making an excellent match for delicate shellfish or subtly roasted chicken in a lemon‑butter sauce.
aroma: hawthorn and elderflower with subtle smoky hazelnut
palate: crisp mineral‑driven graininess with fine acidity

name: Maison Morey-Blanc Saint Romain sous le Chateau
description: This 2020 Saint‑Romain Sous le Château by Maison Morey‑Blanc unfolds with quiet breadth revealing mineral clarity and precise concentration accented by acidity that enlivens delicate yellow fruit and floral suggestions.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C to highlight its sappy minerality and vibrant acidity; pairs gracefully with seafood or subtly seasoned poultry.
aroma: white flowers, yellow fruit, mineral clarity
palate: concentrated, crisp, energetic, vividly mineral

name: Maison Morey-Blanc Volnay 1er Cru les Pitures
description: Maison Morey‑Blanc’s 2023 Volnay 1er Cru “Les Pitures” unfolds with refined poise: a polished core of red cherry and wild strawberry adorned with delicate rose petal and bitter orange nuances and underpinned by cool earth and mineral tension, offering a sense of finesse rather than flamboyance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in delicate glasses to reveal its fragrant profile Pair with refined fare such as roasted pheasant with root vegetables or soft-ripened cheeses.
aroma: rose petal, wild strawberry, bitter orange
palate: silky red fruit with mineral freshness
finish: elegant, cool earth and subtle grip on finish
