name: Morey-Blanc Volnay 1er Cru les Pitures
description: The 2021 Maison Morey‑Blanc Volnay 1er Cru “Les Pitures” exudes an elegant fragrance of violet‑tinged red and darker berries with a subtle hint of anise‑like perfume. It delivers refined tension and energy with a poised mid‑palate and finely chiselled structure that promises graceful development with time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C after a brief decant of 30 minutes to reveal floral nuance. Pair with duck breast with berry jus or roasted guinea fowl for an old‑world harmony.
palate: refined and poised mid‑palate with energy

name: Maison Philippe Viallet Savoie Blanc Aop
description: A bright Savoie blanc from Maison Philippe Viallet that carries the alpine freshness of its Savoyard heritage, elegant yet approachable with light floral and mineral undertones, offering an inviting clarity that recalls crisp mountain air.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 10–12 °C. Lovely as an aperitif or alongside delicate freshwater fish or mild cheeses.
palate: bright, fresh, gently rounded

name: Domaine Roy Chardonnay Dundee Hill
description: This 2017 Domaine Roy & Fils Iron Filbert Vineyard Chardonnay from Dundee Hills offers a refined expression of Willamette Valley terroir, with delicate notes of quince, Mirabelle plum and ripe lemon framed by gentle waxy and brioche nuances. It conveys grace and poise, presenting an articulate texture that announces both precision and charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass for best aromatic lift. Pairs beautifully with roasted chicken, buttery scallops or creamy alpine cheeses.
aroma: quince, ripe lemon, Mirabelle plum, beeswax
palate: elegant, juicy and precise with fine definition
finish: good length with suavity and minerally grace
foodPairings: pan‑seared scallops in a cream sauce
soft alpine cheeses like raclette or fontina

name: Incline Pinot Noir
description: An elegant estate‑selected Pinot Noir revealing a refined interplay of rose petal and red berry perfume, unfolding into a palate of pure Willamette Valley fruit with poised structure and polished tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in fine crystal: complements roast duck or wild mushroom risotto with grace.
aroma: rose petal and fresh red berries
palate: pure red fruit, balanced structure

name: Incline Pinot Noir Dundee Hills
description: Maison Roy & Fils' 2014 Incline Pinot Noir blends red fruit, dried herbs, and citrus peel in a graceful, finely layered style. The palate has depth without heaviness, carrying the vintage's ripeness with measured freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15-16°C with duck, cedar-plank salmon, or porcini risotto; a gentle decant is appropriate for sediment.
aroma: Red berries, dried herbs, citrus peel
palate: Deep yet light-footed, supple, fresh

name: Albert Mann Gewurztraminer Furstentum Grand Cru Vieilles Vignes
description: An elegantly intense Gewurztraminer from Albert Mann’s venerable Vieilles Vignes in the Furstentum Grand Cru, the 2012 vintage unites exotic spice and varietal perfume with a crystalline minerality drawn from the calcareous soils of Kientzheim and Sigolsheim ([grandcru.cz](https://www.grandcru.cz/cs_CZ/produkt/gewurztraminer-furstentum-grand-cru-vieilles-vignes-2012/?utm_source=openai))
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip glass to reveal its floral spice and silken texture, a graceful companion to spiced dishes or rich soft cheeses ([grandcru.cz](https://www.grandcru.cz/cs_CZ/produkt/gewurztraminer-furstentum-grand-cru-vieilles-vignes-2012/?utm_source=openai))
palate: great liveliness and fruit expression
foodPairings: duck brochette with sesame spices and honey
strong cheese such as Munster or Epoisses

name: Albert Mann Riesling Schlossberg Grand Cru
description: This 2013 Albert Mann Riesling Schlossberg Grand Cru presents an elegant tension between crystalline mineral clarity and refined citrus purity drawing from its steep granite terroir, while a subtle weight of ripe orchard fruit brings a harmonious, measured presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C in fine stemware to highlight the vibrant acidity and mineral drive, ideally alongside delicate seafood or refined vegetarian dishes.
aroma: Refined citrus oils with a whisper of floral minerality
palate: Taut and crystalline with orchard fruit underpinned by vivid acidity
finish: Lingering stony clarity with delicate salinity

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: This Bulzai Ginjo sake is a refreshing artisan expression from Niigata’s Sado Island crafted by Obata Shuzo under the Manotsuru label, elegantly balancing bright yellow apple and citron notes with a fine mineral undertone. It offers a refined sense of clarity and that invigorating zest one expects from a meticulously milled Ginjo sake.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to highlight its bright fruit and spiced nuance; pairs gracefully with delicate sushi or simply butter‑sauteed white fish.
aroma: yellow apple, citron, subtle tropical fruit
palate: refreshing minerality with touch of white pepper

name: Bulzai Ginjo Sake
description: Manotsuru “Bulzai” Ginjo presents a crisply invigorating expression of Niigata’s refined sake tradition, showing delicate citron and yellow apple on the forefront, with a whisper of white pepper and stony mineral, precisely balanced in its ginjo clarity. The nama‑chozo method lends it a bright, zest‑laden energy that evokes the sea‑cooled mornings of Sado Island.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a narrow wine glass to highlight its delicate fruit and peppery minerals; ideal alongside salt‑grilled fish or subtly butter‑seared seafood.
palate: white pepper and mineral briskness

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: A luscious Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake, Manotsuru “Countless Visions” unfurls a veil of creamy cloudiness that gives way to a softly sweet, refreshingly balanced palate. Tropical whispers of starfruit and guava interlace with delicate anise and melon, culminating in a gentle spicy crescendo that evokes quiet contemplation.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled after a gentle shake to harmonize its fine rice sediment; beautifully suited to contrast spicy cuisine or to accompany light fried fish for an elegant interplay of texture and flavor.
palate: silky sweet fruit with anise‑melon nuance

name: Countless Visions Nigori Sake
description: This Junmai Ginjo Nigori sake presents itself with an inviting cloudy hue and a light sweetness tempered by gentle sourness. Fragrant notes of starfruit and guava unfold to a refreshing and animated style.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled after an attentive shake to reincorporate the sediment, paired with lively dishes such as spicy Mexican tacos or delicate fried fish to complement its creamy spice.
palate: light sweetness with gentle acidity

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: This Manotsuru Crane Junmai offers an elegant serenity that whispers of Niigata’s blessed terroir, the clarity of its soft Sado waters reflected in delicate nuances of pistachio and forest floor, its texture pure and unadorned, a quiet embodiment of craftsmanship without flourish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its soft umami and gentle nuttiness, a harmonious companion to sukiyaki, tamagoyaki or subtly seasoned grilled tofu.
palate: mild umami with soft nutty tones
drinkWindow: Drink now to enjoy its fresh aromatic clarity

name: Crane Junmai Sake
description: An elegant junmai sake from Niigata’s artisanal Obata Shuzo, Manotsuru Crane exudes a refined purity with whispering stone fruit and delicate pistachio nuances framed by a subtle kiss of white chocolate. The palate is poised and silky, offering a gently structured yet graceful presence. This is a sake of understated harmony and old‑world craft.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to appreciate its soft fruit elegance or at cool room temperature to reveal deeper umami layers: an excellent companion to sukiyaki or lightly seared tofu.
palate: silky, balanced, subtly nutty

name: Crane Karakuchi Sake
description: This honjoso sake, Manotsuru Crane Karakuchi, offers a beautifully refined experience with bright citrus florals and delicate almond undertones a silkily elegant expression of Niigata’s dry ‘‘karakuchi’’ tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to reveal its taut freshness or gently warmed to enhance its smooth silkiness ideal with simply seasoned poultry or light seafood.
palate: silky, elegant, dry

name: Daimyo Honjozo
description: This Honjozo from Manotsuru speaks in an understated yet confident voice its gentle refinement reflecting the four treasures—rice, water, brewers and terroir—that define its origin. The palate is dry and soft yet subtly engaging, with airy harmony rather than overt bravado. Drinking it brings a whisper of Sado Island’s misty morning in every sip.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly warmed or at room temperature to reveal its delicate umami and soften the gentle driest finish.
palate: dry with gentle umami balance

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: An exceptionally dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo’s Manotsuru label this sake presents a crisp clarity with echoes of dried fruit, aromatic herbs and a faint whisper of cinnamon drawing the palate into its penetrating austerity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to enhance its sharp precision and pair with delicate raw seafood or subtly seasoned rich meats to balance the intense dryness.
palate: crisp super‑dry austerity

name: Demon Slayer Tokubetsu Honjozo Sake
description: A rigorously dry Tokubetsu Honjozo from Obata Shuzo on Sado Island, “Demon Slayer” delivers a poised mid‑weight presence carving through notes of dried fruit, meadow herbs and a brush of cinnamon, culminating in a crystalline, minerally air of perfection.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled or softly warmed to reveal elegant herb and dried fruit nuances; perfect alongside sushi, fresh sashimi and oysters.
palate: meadow herb and cinnamon mid‑weight

name: Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Kanadel Orikarami Junmai Daiginjo reveals a delicate interplay of fizz and finesse with lifted notes of ripe melon and lychee carried on a whisper of effervescent silk. It unfolds with gentle aromatic grace and finishes with subtle persistence like the echo of a haiku's last line.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip glass to preserve its soft sparkle, ideally alongside light seafood or elegant hors d’oeuvre to accent its airy clarity.
palate: light, bouncy, gently fizzy

name: Lucky Toki Junmai
description: A pure‑rice junmai imbued with the spirit of Sado Island and the auspicious toki crane it honors. Gentle stone‑fruit and soft white‑chocolate tones glide across a sleek, dry frame with subtle depth, inviting contemplative sipping.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or gently warmed to reveal both its delicate fruit‑like nuance and warming umami: pairs beautifully with sashimi or lightly seasoned fare.
palate: elegant, dry, refined

name: Maho Daijinjo Sake
description: This Manotsuru Maho Daiginjo presents a lush aroma of ripe peach, orange peel and faint cotton‑candy perfume, giving way to an elegantly mild yet racy entry and a refined, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or about 15 °C in a wine glass to reveal its layered nuance: its gentle elegance pairs beautifully with creamy caviar or rich hors d’oeuvres.
palate: elegant, mild and racy entry

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo
description: Manotsuru “Pure Bloom” Sweet Junmai Ginjo presents a delicate floral elegance grounded in refined sweetness, a soft and light expression born of Sado Island’s pure waters and artisanal tradition. Subtle notes of lychee and cherry blossom drift through its graceful texture, lingering with creamy nuance and poised transparency.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to highlight its floral and sweet character, pairing beautifully with creamy desserts or light tomato‑based salads.
palate: soft, elegant sweetness with white chocolate undertones

name: Pure Bloom Junmai Ginjo Sake
description: An ethereal and delicate junmai ginjo that feels like spring in a glass offering a soft, floral aroma threaded with subtle lychee and honeyed warmth, its gentle 12 percent spirit carrying a light, elegant sweetness floating on a whisper of vanilla and milk.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its floral nuance: pairs beautifully with light appetizers and fresh summer desserts.
aroma: soft floral bouquet with lychee and honey
palate: elegant, lightly sweet with vanilla‑milk whispers
drinkWindow: drink now to fully enjoy its fresh floral purity

name: Diom Marcel Deiss Alsace Langenberg
description: This wine unfolds with crystalline citrus lift and an airy floral character, its voice shaped by the austere granite of Langenberg and the artistry of complantation. It feels like a sunlit breeze across Saint‑Hippolyte’s terraced slopes, simultaneously light in texture and braced by a saline mineral spine.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in fine white stemware: exquisite with fresh goat cheese or simply grilled shellfish to reveal its mineral clarity.
aroma: lemon blossom and white flowers with flint
palate: elegant citrus clarity framed by vibrant mineral tension

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Engelgarten
description: This 2020 Engelgarten from Marcel Deiss is an elegant field blend that expresses the noble gravelly terroir of Bergheim with a luminous pale-gold robe and a warm, mineral-laced character. Its aromatic tapestry weaves together hints of hot stone, citrus and white florals with a quietly determined, dry structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–12 °C, ideally alongside grilled rich fish or subtly spiced shellfish to complement its sapidity.
aroma: warm stone and citrus floral tones
palate: dry, mineral, gently fat with sapidity

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Engelgarten
description: This 2022 Engelgarten from Marcel Deiss is an elegant field blend that expresses the noble gravelly terroir of Bergheim with a luminous pale-gold robe and a warm, mineral-laced character. Its aromatic tapestry weaves together hints of hot stone, citrus and white florals with a quietly determined, dry structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10–12 °C, ideally alongside grilled rich fish or subtly spiced shellfish to complement its sapidity.
aroma: warm stone and citrus floral tones
palate: dry, mineral, gently fat with sapidity

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Grand Cru Altenberg de Bergheim
appellation: Alsace Grand Cru Altenberg de Bergheim
description: A deeply cerebral Alsace Grand Cru that marries weight and finesse, drawing its essence from the rich limestone and marl terroir of Altenberg de Bergheim, offering layered nostalgia of ripe peach, apricot and honeyed botrytis over a crystalline structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 10–12 °C, ideally ahead of time to reveal its profound texture; excels with foie gras or terrine, or nuanced blue cheeses.
palate: rich, creamy and saline yet refined
finish: highly elegant and mineral long finish

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Grand Cru Schlossberg
description: A crystalline and mineral‐fueled expression of Alsace’s storied terroir from the famed Schlossberg site, this 2018 vintage unveils a tension between ripeness and austerity. Meyer lemon and white orchard fruit glide across a lean, tensioned framework textured by cool granite undercurrents.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10 °C to accentuate vivid acidity and mineral poise. A thrilling companion to shellfish in butter sauces or subtly spiced Asian fare.
palate: fresh orchard fruit, taut mineral tension

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Grand Cru Schlossberg
description: A crystalline and mineral‐fueled expression of Alsace’s storied terroir from the famed Schlossberg site, this 2021 vintage unveils a tension between ripeness and austerity. Meyer lemon and white orchard fruit glide across a lean, tensioned framework textured by cool granite undercurrents.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 10 °C to accentuate vivid acidity and mineral poise. A thrilling companion to shellfish in butter sauces or subtly spiced Asian fare.
palate: fresh orchard fruit, taut mineral tension

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Langenberg
description: This 2021 Langenberg from Marcel Deiss is a finely wrought Alsatian field blend, its granular granite soils imparting a mineral thread that underpins a tapestry of citrus and white florals, all framed by vibrant, tactile acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to coax forward its citrus clarity and poised structure, a graceful partner to seafood or spring vegetables.
aroma: citrus and white florals over a mineral base
palate: harmonious and textured with sleek acidity

name: Domaine Marcel Deiss Alsace Ribeauville
description: The 2022 Dom Marcel Deiss Riquewihr is a composed Alsatian white blend combining Pinot Gris and Riesling in biodynamic complantation. Salivating and structured, it offers crystalline precision and mineral depth from siliceous soils atop deep marl, revealing a stately austerity that softens into flesh with maturity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10 to 12 °C to refine its texture. It partners exquisitely with shellfish, elegant fish, or delicate vegetable preparations.
palate: salivating mineral power with dense yet fresh structure

name: Marchesi Antinori Antica Estate Cabernet Sauvignon Townsend Vineyard
description: The 2018 Antinori “Antica Estate” Cabernet Sauvignon from Townsend Vineyard unfolds with a noble presence, offering finely etched dark fruit and mineral-driven intensity supported by a muscular yet poised frame sourced from Napa Valley’s Atlas Peak. The wine reveals a sense of refined structure, with a balance of brooding black fruit, tension and notable depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a gentle decant of 30–45 minutes at around 16 °C to reveal layers of complexity. Excellent alongside richly seasoned lamb or mushroom‑infused beef dishes.
aroma: taut black fruit with mineral sparks
palate: firm structured tannins, muscular black fruit

name: Marchesi Antinori Antica Estate Chardonnay A26
description: An elegant Napa Valley Chardonnay of refined mountain pedigree, the Antica Estate “A26” 2019 unfolds with subtlety and depth, offering delicate notes of stone fruit and citrus framed by gentle oak nuances. The wine is poised and structured, its texture creamy yet lithe, conveying a harmonious balance that speaks of both place and lineage.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in tulip glasses to showcase its vibrant acidity; splendid with grilled seafood or buttery poultry dishes.
aroma: stone fruit and citrus with gentle oak nuances
palate: creamy yet lithe texture with balanced fruit and freshness

name: Margaux de Brane Margaux

name: Mount Hermon Galilee Rose
description: This wine is an expressive rosé from Israel’s Galilee, fashioned by Golan Heights Winery under the Mount Hermon label. The blend of Syrah, Tempranillo and a hint of Tinta Cao yields a luminous salmon hue and a fragrance of fresh raspberry, strawberry and delicate citrus flower nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 8–10 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass. It brings brightness and poise to light fare and Mediterranean flavors, particularly salads, grilled fish or mild cheeses.
palate: light‑medium body, refreshing, fruit‑driven

name: Rioja Gran Reserva
description: Garnet‑tinged and refined the 2014 Monte Real Rioja Gran Reserva offers a harmonious meld of black cherry and plum overtones what hints of cigar smoke and cedar from its well‑managed oak evolution highlight its old‑world pedigree.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 60‑65 °F in large-bowl glasses to coax out its layered fruit and fine tannins pairs beautifully with roasted lamb or aged Manchego.
palate: velvety, structured, balanced acidity

name: Rioja Reserva
description: The 2018 Monte Real Rioja Reserva presents a graceful intersection of ripe red fruit and refined oak influence its cherry‑red robe framed by subtle earthen notes and savory spice. The palate is plush yet poised with blackberry and cassis suggestions, a whisper of dark chocolate and violet emerging beneath soft tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently below cellar temperature in broad redwine glasses to allow its aromatic layers to bloom pairs beautifully with roast pork, aged Manchego or game birds.
aroma: raspberry, milk chocolate, black olive paste
palate: blackberry, cassis, almond toffee

name: Domaine Gilles Morat Pouilly Fuisse Belemnites
description: This wine offers a delicate interplay of flinty minerality and soft orchard fruit framed in gentle oak, an elegant expression of the Beaune’s clay‑rich terroir showing finesse
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 10 °C to reveal its tension and texture, ideal with refined poultry or shellfish preparations
aroma: silex and smoke with mirabelle essence
palate: nectarine and honeyed chalky tension
foodPairings: Poulet de Bresse à la crème
Filet mignon de porc aux morilles

name: Domaine de la Mordoree Cotes du Rhone Rose
description: This rosé unfolds with a delicate blush and an alluring bouquet of strawberry blossom, pink grapefruit and soft citrus, weaving floral perfume with subtle minerality in an elegant expression of Southern Rhône grace. The palate is balanced and fresh with a rounded profile, offering ripe red fruit and a whisper of rose petal, culminating in a refined delicate finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 8 °C to 10 °C, ideal for summer aperitifs or paired with shellfish, grilled white meats or light Asian fare.
palate: ripe red fruit with rose petal softness

name: Calvados Morin Selection
description: This non‐vintage Calvados Morin Sélection 12 evokes refined apple orchard character and gentle oak harmony: it opens with bright notes of baked apple and subtle orchard spice, evolving into a velvety, mellow body with a whisper of toasted woodiness.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or at cellar temperature in a tulip‐shaped glass to best appreciate its orchard fruit and delicate spice; ideal as a contemplative digestif or paired with buttered tart Tatin or aged Comté.
aroma: baked orchard fruit with warm spice
palate: smooth mellow apple fruit and soft oak

name: Moulin D'issan Bordeaux Superieur Rouge
description: The 2022 Moulin d’Issan Bordeaux Supérieur unfolds with generous ripe red fruit embraced by a warm silken texture, subtle spice, and an elegantly smooth structure reminiscent of classic Margaux tradition.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled close to cellar temperature to showcase its supple tannins and fruit forward charm, ideal alongside roasted meats or well‑seasoned pâtés.
aroma: ripe red fruit with gentle spice
palate: velvety and harmonious

name: La Mouliniere Bordeaux Blanc
description: This 2024 La Moulinière Bordeaux Blanc reveals a vibrant spirit: citrus-laced and brisk, enlivened by fresh green fruit and a suggestion of delicate floral lift, all bound by a poised mineral undercurrent that speaks of its gravel‑clay Bordeaux origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 8‑10 °C; this clean, bright white partners beautifully with light fish dishes, salads or soft, fresh cheeses.
palate: crisp, bright fruit framed by subtle mineral tension

name: La Mouliniere Bordeaux Rouge
description: A medium‑bodied Bordeaux rouge from a Lynch‑pin of right‑bank tradition, this 2023 La Moulinière unfolds with vivid red‑berry tones, offering vibrant strawberry and raspberry lifted by supple, refined structure. Its freshness and dry clarity speak of Merlot‑led harmony with a dash of Cabernet Sauvignon to enrich the experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in the mid‑to‑high 60s °F to spotlight its red fruit vibrancy alongside grilled meats or dry, nutty cheeses.
palate: dry, fresh, with supple tannins and abundant red fruit

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This 2022 Mount Hermon Cabernet Sauvignon from the Golan Heights pours a deep ruby hue, offering a refined interplay of bright red and darker berry tones underscored by a subtle herbal suggestion and a gentle earthiness. The wine presents an approachable structure with modest tannins balanced by a vibrant yet grounded character.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool for a red, around 60°F, in a medium-large Bordeaux glass, ideal with grilled lamb chops or herb‑infused roasted vegetables.
aroma: red and black berries with herbal nuance
palate: medium‑bodied with bright fruit and gentle earthiness

name: Mount Hermon Cabernet Sauvignon
description: Mount Hermon Cabernet Sauvignon 2025 unfolds with an unassuming serenity yet palpable presence: a medley of fresh cherry and raspberry infused with a whisper of garden herbs. It balances approachable fruit and structure in an elegant, everyday fashion suitable for convivial enjoyment.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar cool temperatures this young Cabernet will sing alongside spiced lamb burgers or garlic‑herb mushroom pasta.
aroma: fresh cherry and raspberry with herbal undertones
palate: medium‑bodied with satisfying fruit and subtle herb note
drinkWindow: Enjoy now through three years from harvest

name: Mount Hermon Indigo
description: The 2024 Mount Hermon Indigo is a gracious red blend from the Golan Heights that unfolds layers of ripe plum and dark berry fruit woven with whispers of smoke, earth and subtle spice, offering supple medium‑bodied elegance and seamless drinkability.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature with grilled lamb or herb‑kissed thin‑crust pizza to accentuate its smoky and savory fruit character.
palate: smooth, medium‑bodied, savory fruit
foodPairings: thin‑crust pizza with sage and olives
drinkWindow: Best enjoyed within about three years from harvest

name: Mount Hermon Red
description: A refined expression of the Golan Heights terroir this youthful 2025 Mount Hermon Red unfurls vibrant red cherry and raspberry tones alongside a whisper of orange zest and gently herbal earthiness. Its medium frame is graceful and nuanced lending a fresh yet layered personality.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 16 °C to accent its fruit vibrancy enjoy with roasted lamb or grilled beef for a harmonious match.
aroma: cherry and raspberry with orange zest
palate: medium-bodied with herbal depth

name: Mount Hermon White
description: This 2024 Mount Hermon White from Golan Heights Winery presents a luminous, inviting character lifted by citrus and orchard fruit notes. Its elegant interplay of green apple, melon and peach carries floral echoes, grounded in the bright vitality of its cool‑climate origins. Approachable and poised it offers a refined everyday white wine experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8–10 °C alongside delicate seafood or creamy poultry dishes to accentuate its refreshing fruit layers.
palate: ripe melon and peach with flinty vitality
drinkWindow: Ready now, best within a couple of years of vintage

name: Quinta Do Mouro Dourado (Gold Label)
description: Deep and commanding yet refined this 2018 Quinta do Mouro Dourado reveals a noble blend anchored by Alicante Bouschet yet graced with layers of red and black fruit framed by subtle spice and earth. The texture is sumptuous velvet underpinned with firm, polished tannins entwined with integrated oak, drawing one toward a long, graceful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 16 °C, perhaps from a Bordeaux‑style glass, to best marry its dark fruit and spice with dishes such as roast lamb or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: red and black fruit with subtle spice and earth
palate: velvety texture with structured refined tannins

name: Quinta Do Mouro Trincadeira
description: This singular 2018 Quinta do Mouro Trincadeira exudes elegant poise and refined structure. Its vivid ruby hue frames an ensemble of ripe black and blue fruit underpinned by subtle florals, forest floor and mushroom undertones, all held in harmonious balance by bright freshness and graceful structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar‐like coolness to accentuate its vivacious acidity; pairs beautifully with grilled red meats or robust mushroom dishes.
aroma: ripe black and blue fruit with forest florals and earthy mushroom notes
palate: structured yet fresh with vibrant acidity and fine balance

name: Quinta Do Mouro Vinha de Malho
description: This 2017 Quinta do Mouro Vinha do Malhó, born of unique hybrids of Cabernet Sauvignon, unfolds with an intense ruby hue and a compelling aromatic web of black and blue fruits, earthiness and spice offering both power and poise. On the palate it maintains that concentrated profile balanced by a striking acidity that lends refined structure and a vibrantly precise, fresh finish, a wine of real class and presence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled at 15 to 17 °C to accent fresh vitality. Pair with roasted meats, game, or mature cheeses for a harmonious counterpoint.
aroma: black and blue fruit, earthy spice
palate: concentrated fruit balanced by marked acidity

name: Quinta Do Mouro Vinha Do Mouro Branco
description: This 2020 Vinha do Mouro Branco exhibits poised refinement: a luminous pale straw hue leads to a serenely mineral‑inflected scent suggestive of citrus and white stone fruit, followed by an elegant palate of poised structure and vibrant acidity, concluding in a lingering cool finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender white glass at approximately 10°C alongside grilled sea bass or a fresh chèvre salad for harmonious contrast.
palate: Bright, structured and fresh

name: Mullineaux Schist/granite Mixed Case
description: A lean and mineral‑driven Shiraz from the heart of Swartland expressing its terroir with precision and poise. The wine reveals lean black‑fruit and savory herbal accents underscored by a distinct stony structure. It presents youthful restraint promising rewarding drink beyond its early evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted at cellar‑cool temperatures to allow the wine’s structural tannins and aromatic purity to unfurl, especially alongside grilled lamb or earthy mushroom ragout.
palate: precise mineral‑driven structure

name: Adegas Gran Vinum Nessa Albarino
description: Nessa Albariño 2023 from Adegas Gran Vinum delights with a lustrous straw‑yellow hue tinged with green, offering a lively array of tropical and white fruit aromas framed by jasmine and orange blossom, all underpinned by a seam of Atlantic salinity and floral lift. On the palate it unfolds with fresh white fruit—apple, melon and citrus—with vibrant acidity and a fine lees‑borne balance that gives energy and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10–12 °C to accentuate its brisk freshness. Ideal with shellfish and light seafood preparations or as an elegant aperitif.
aroma: tropical and white fruit with jasmine and orange blossom
palate: fresh citrus‑tinged white fruit, balanced acidity

name: Nicole Lamarche Cote de Nuits Villages Blanc
description: This 2021 Cote de Nuits‑Villages Blanc by Domaine Nicole Lamarche presents a poised elegance as fruit‑driven and quietly assured. Delicate orchard blossoms emerge upon the nose followed by a mid‑weight palate that balances gentle ripeness and graceful poise. The finish whispers with subtle mineral lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 10 °C to 12 °C to reveal its fine clarity and minerality: ideal with shellfish or light poultry dishes.
palate: mid‑weight, elegant white fruit with refined minerality

name: Nicole Lamarche la Grande Rue Grand Cru
description: A silken expression of Vosne‑Romée’s rarest Grand Cru from Nicole Lamarche’s monopole, 2021 unveils rose petal and red plum perfume, a hint of softly smoked tobacco, and flowing, finely woven tannins that frame an inviting succulence and mouthwatering lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar‑cool, around 16 °C after decanting, ideally paired with game birds or duck dressed with autumnal fruits.
aroma: rose petal, red plum, subtle smoke
palate: silky tannins, vibrant acidity, refined succulence

name: Nicole Lamarche la Grande Rue Grand Cru
description: A silken expression of Vosne‑Romée’s rarest Grand Cru from Nicole Lamarche’s monopole, 2021 unveils rose petal and red plum perfume, a hint of softly smoked tobacco, and flowing, finely woven tannins that frame an inviting succulence and mouthwatering lift.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated at cellar‑cool, around 16 °C after decanting, ideally paired with game birds or duck dressed with autumnal fruits.
aroma: rose petal, red plum, subtle smoke
palate: silky tannins, vibrant acidity, refined succulence

name: La Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole
description: A wine of rare nobility from the Côte de Nuits this Pinot Noir Grand Cru Monopole unfurls with profound elegance and restrained allure fragrant layers of rose‑petal and wild red and black fruits glide across the palate, while whispers of licorice, smoke and crushed stone echo the limestone soils surrounding La Grande Rue vineyard.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in large Burgundy glasses to unveil its floral perfume and delicate structure Pair with refined dishes like duck breast or roasted pheasant.
aroma: rose‑petal infused red fruit with a touch of spice
palate: ethereal, medium‑bodied wine with lithe tannins and wild berry elegance

name: La Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole
appellation: La Grande Rue Grand Cru Monopole
description: A graceful expression of La Grande Rue that marries red fruit perfume with refined spice and floral nuance, the 2019 vintage unfolding with elegance and inner tension that speaks of its noble terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature in large Burgundy glasses, ideal with roast duck or wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: rose‑petal red fruit with exotic tea and spice
palate: medium‑bodied, lithe tannins, poised and refined

name: Château Nicot Bordeaux
description: A supple elegant Bordeaux, this 2019 Château Nicot presents dark ruby hues and a graceful medium‐bodied profile, marrying ripe black currant fruit with a whisper of smoke and well integrated tannins, reflecting the refined tradition of the Dubourg estate.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool to moderate red (around 16 °C), decanted briefly and paired with grilled red meats or hearty rustic fare for harmonious enjoyment.
aroma: ripe black currant with smoky nuance
palate: medium‑bodied structure with elegant tannins and dark fruit

name: Chardonnay Hyde Vineyard
description: This 2022 Nid Tissé Chardonnay from the storied Hyde Vineyard presents a crystalline expression of Carneros elegance, offering taut orchard fruit enfolded in finely honed mineral tones and a steely backbone that speaks of place and restraint. The wine’s poise and knitting of delicacy and tension evoke an old‑world sensibility rendered through a Californian paradigm.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 50–55 °F in fine white Burgundy stems, ideally paired with rich shellfish such as lobster thermidor or creamy crab beurre blanc.
aroma: orchard fruit and crushed oyster shell
palate: taut mineral tension with apple and citrus

name: Pinot Noir Radian Vineyard
description: This 2022 Nid Tissé Pinot Noir Radian Vineyard is pale ruby in hue, conjuring a refined tension between fresh rose petals and wild red berries framed by a whisper of savory white pepper and Tonka bean nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to preserve its lithe structure; the wine will pair beautifully with duck breast with herb crust or a fragrant mushroom risotto.
aroma: violets, dried rose petals, red berries
palate: cranberry, red plum, currant with bright acidity
foodPairings: Soft goat cheese on grilled sourdough

name: Winery Oakville Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: A resonant expression of Napa’s Oakville terroir framed in rich dark-red fruit and classic mountain underbrush, this Cabernet Sauvignon offers polished depth and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature alongside grilled sirloin or aged hard cheeses to heighten its vibrant dark fruit and subtle spice nuances.
aroma: black cherry and cassis with a whisper of fresh roses and clove
palate: structured medium‑bodied with round tannins and cassis‑inflected core
finish: elegant long finish with spice and cedar threads

name: Winery Zinfandel Napa Valley
description: The 2022 Oakville Winery Zinfandel from Napa Valley delivers sumptuous intensity with lush blackberry and black cherry woven through whispers of allspice and baking spice, offering a captivating mouthfeel that is both rich and balanced, with a velvety touch and seamless structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or at cellar‑cooling temperatures with hearty fare like grilled sausages or spiced tomato ragù to highlight its fruit depth and spice resonance.
aroma: ripe blackberry and black cherry with warm baking spices
palate: velvety tannins and vibrant acidity in harmony
finish: lingering smooth finish tinged with subtle spice

name: L'ame Soeur Syrah de Seyssuel
description: The 2004 Ogier L’Âme Sœur Syrah de Seyssuel is a finely tailored expression of Seyssuel’s mica‑rich slopes: the bouquet unfolds with gentle black and red berry nuances lifted by delicate floral hints, while the palate offers a poised interplay of silken fruit and precise mineral structure, culminating in a lingering, refined finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 16‑17 °C in tulip‑shaped glasses to appreciate its floral‑mineral aromas; pairs exquisitely with roast lamb or venison with herb jus.
aroma: black and red berries with floral lift
palate: silky fruit framed by mineral precision

name: M&s Ogier Syrah L'ame Soeur
description: A jewel of northern Rhône Syrah from Stéphane Ogier this 2011 L’Âme Sœur unveils an exotic perfume of violet-tinged dark fruit and graphite melding into warm blackberry and spice, with refined tannins that speak of both depth and elegant restraint.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool, around 16 °C, with richly sauced red meats or honey‑glazed duck to accentuate its plush fruit and spice.
palate: dense dark fruit with graphite and fine tannins

name: Daniel Olivier Cabernet Franc/merlot
description: The 2018 Daniel Olivier Cabernet Franc–Merlot from Bergerac presents itself with genteel austerity and refined poise, offering lifted scents of ripe red berries and a hint of underbrush, with a structured, polished palate that carries graceful weight and focus.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature to allow its aromatics of brambly fruit and subtle earth to unfold; pairs elegantly with roasted duck or herb‑toasted lamb.
palate: structured yet polished red and brambly fruit

name: Vina Otano Vina Otano Rioja Crianza Do Rioja
description: This Viña Otano Crianza 2020 reveals deep ruby hues with a youthful violet shimmer, leading into an aromatic core of cassis and black raspberry subtly woven with Rioja spice cedar and a whisper of cigar ash. The palate is bright and full‑bodied with vibrant soil expression and ripe, structured tannins promising graceful evolution. Each element speaks to a tempranillo of backbone and early allure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature around 60‑64 °F to showcase its freshness alongside roasted lamb, grilled mushrooms, or aged Manchego cheese.
palate: bright, full‑bodied, ripe tannins

name: Vina Otano Vina Otano Rioja Gran Reserva Do Rioja
description: Viña Otano Gran Reserva 2016 reveals a noble presence of dark berry compote and cassis framed by tobacco leaf and mocha nuances, its texture refined yet grounded in a fine mineral backbone, demonstrating both precision and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool from cellar temperature in a large Bordeaux glass, ideally decanted to encourage its layered palate to blossom; pairs beautifully with grilled rib‑eye or aged Manchego.
aroma: dark berries, cigar smoke, coffee grounds
palate: full‑bodied, deep, savory with tension

name: Vino Otano Vina Otano Rioja Crianza Do Rioja
description: A poised Rioja Crianza from Viña Otano, this 2019 vintage marries the grace of Tempranillo with a whisper of Mazuelo for depth, framed by judicious American and French oak aging, yielding a harmonious red with subtle spice and polished structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled (around 16 °C), ideally decanted briefly. Complement grilled lamb chops, mushroom‑sauced pork tenderloin, or aged Manchego.
palate: supple, with textured red fruit and a touch of earth

name: Vina Jaraba Cosecha Do Jaraba
appellation: Vino de Pago de La Jaraba
description: The 2021 Pago de la Jaraba Viña Jaraba Cosecha unfolds with vibrant notes of red cherry and gentle spice layered over delicate floral whispers, showcasing a refined synergy between Tempranillo and Cabernet. It carries an elegant medium body framed by smooth texture and a well-balanced structure rooted in the La Mancha terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature to highlight its fruit freshness; ideal with aged Manchego or savory charcuterie.
aroma: floral and gently spicy red fruit
palate: medium body smooth texture

name: 1990 Luis Pato Vinhas Velhas Branco
description: A wine of serene maturity and noble lineage this 1990 Vinhas Velhas Branco from Luís Pato offers a rare glimpse into the evolution of Bairrada’s white terroir. Its gently aged voice speaks of lingering citrus and stone fruit framed by a graceful salinity and whispers of honeyed complexity. The presence of balanced oak aging lends it a refined structure despite its softly amber glow.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to allow its complex aromatics to unfurl pair it with rich seafood or delicate poultry dishes to complement its mineral tension.
palate: saline mineral depth with aged orchard fruit
drinkWindow: ready now, maintains vibrancy for years more

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman Ducking Pet Nat
color: white (pét‑nat with slight skin contact hue)
description: A playful yet refined pét‑nat from Bairrada this 2022 Duckman Ducking Pet Nat, crafted from skin‑contact Sercialinho, offers a lively tension between orchard fruit and mineral energy. It presents as a softly effervescent, textured white that marries charm with a hint of wild honesty.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a rounded white glass to highlight its delicate sparkle, ideal with creamy seafood pâtés or a chilled goat cheese and herb crostini.
aroma: citrus blossom and green orchard fruit
palate: textured orchard fruit with brisk acidity

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman Maria Duck Pet Nat
description: This naturally effervescent Pet‑Nat from João Pato’s Duckman project captures the spirit of Bairrada in a bottle, its hazy golden hue hinting at five days' skin contact of Maria Gomes before wild fermentation continues in the bottle. The wine delivers playful yet refined energy with citrus and tropical fruit notes balanced by fine chalky salinity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C in a tulip or white wine glass to preserve its lively fizz; its brightness lends charm alongside spicy Asian dishes or light seafood preparations.
palate: tropical fruit and chalky salinity
drinkWindow: drink this year or within two years of bottling

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman Nerd Duck
description: A playful yet sophisticated natural red from Bairrada that upends expectations: vibrant Fernão Pires (a.k.a. Maria Gomes) spirit entwined with fine Baga tannins, offering a lithe and juicy expression with dancing red fruit clarity and a whisper of wild fermentation energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or at cellar cool (around 14–16 °C) to highlight its freshness alongside light charcuterie, grilled sardines, or aged cheese.
palate: juicy red cherry, lively acidity, subtle tannin grip

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman Rosa Duck Special Edition
description: This Rosa Duck Special Edition is a delicately textured pét‑nat rosé drawn from Fernão Pires with a whisper of Baga. It greets with a soft pink hue and luminous, fine bubbles that evoke coastal breezes and saline freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 6‑10 °C in tulip glasses; pairs beguilingly with light seafood and summer salads.
aroma: fresh strawberries and citrus‑tinged sea air
palate: crisp, gently effervescent with bright red fruit and lively acidity

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman White Brut
description: This 2023 Duckman White—or Espumante Brut—by Maria João Pato is a bright and spirited artisan sparkling white from sandy Bairrada soils. It delivers a playful tension between citrus zest and saline minerality, with a fine mousse woven under natural minimal‑intervention craftsmanship.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 7‑9 °C in a slender flute: the brisk acidity and textured effervescence render it a superb aperitif or an accompaniment to shellfish or light seafood dishes.
palate: saline minerality and crisp acidity

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman White Duck
description: An expressive and subtly textured white from Bairrada elegant and unpretentious it is crafted from 100 percent Bical by Maria João Pato under the Duckman alias offering clarity of variety and place, showcasing vibrant maritime freshness and a clean stainless‑steel ferment.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10–12 °C alongside shellfish or delicate white meats to accentuate its bright acidity and pure varietal charm.
palate: bright citrus zest with flinty mineral lift.

name: Joao Pato Aka Duckman White Duck
description: An expressive and subtly textured white from Bairrada elegant and unpretentious it is crafted from 100 percent Bical by Maria João Pato under the Duckman alias offering clarity of variety and place, showcasing vibrant maritime freshness and a clean stainless‑steel ferment.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10–12 °C alongside shellfish or delicate white meats to accentuate its bright acidity and pure varietal charm.
palate: bright citrus zest with flinty mineral lift.

name: Luis Pato Espumante Maria Gomes Bruto
description: A finely poised Portuguese sparkling wine, this NV Luís Pato Espumante Maria Gomes Bruto presents a luminous citrine hue and offers an elegant dance of fresh white fruit enlivened by toasty brioche nuances and floral undertones. The gently persistent mousse carries precise acidity and a refined texture that speaks of its classical-method vinification.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled at around 8 °C, it makes a bright aperitif or a graceful companion to delicate seafood, white meats or vegetable dishes.
aroma: sweet‑floral fruits with toasty biscuit notes
palate: fresh citrus and apple framed by fine acidity

name: Luis Pato Quinta de Moinho Beiras
description: A resonant expression of Baga cultivated on the limestone-rich soils of Quinta do Moinho this 2000 vintage reveals deep, dark berry fruit underlined by savory eucalyptus and tobacco nuances accentuated by fine-grained grip and layered soil complexity. Time and restrained oak integration permit a poised elegance to emerge alongside a backbone of vivid structure, hinting at graceful further maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature after gentle decanting, paired delightfully with braised meats or aged hard cheeses to balance its earthy depth and refined tannins.
aroma: dark berries with eucalyptus and tobacco
palate: structured, full-bodied, mineral-driven mid palate

name: Luis Pato Quinta Do Ribeirinho Sercialinho
description: This exuberant single‑vineyard white unveils an elegant interplay of citrus brightness and mineral clarity, refined by the gentle presence of chestnut‑barrel aging, imparting a subtle herbal and spice nuance it remains vibrant yet poised. It reflects a rare, almost extinct heritage variety preserved in the Bairrada clay‑limestone terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, around 12 to 14 °C, alongside refined seafood or creamy fish dishes to highlight its tactile acidity and aging potential.
palate: bright acidity with herbal‑spice complexity
foodPairings: creamy cod in white wine sauce

name: Luis Pato Vinha Pan
description: A singular Baga born of the esteemed Vinha Pan vineyard in Bairrada preserves the Atlantic’s quiet mineral pulse beneath layers of ripe dark cherry and graphite shading. The structure is defined, the tannins powdered and chalky, yet the fruit remains buoyant, delivering an elegant, ageworthy silhouette.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16 to 18 °C in a tulip‑shaped glass, decant if young, and pair with game, mature cheese or rich pork preparations.
palate: vibrant red fruit, fine chalky tannin
drinkWindow: up to 15 years from vintage (i.e. until about 2035)

name: Luis Pato Vinhas Velhas Tinto
description: An elegant red of noble presence, the 2022 Luís Pato Vinhas Velhas Tinto blossoms with a poised core of ripe black cherry, raspberry, and plum framed by forest underbrush, resin and a subtle whisper of pine. Firm yet refined, its tannins etch lively structure while fine oak lends a hint of vanilla and chocolate, promising graceful evolution over the years.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at around 16°C to highlight its brightness and pair with classic roast red meats or aged cheeses for a refined counterpoint.
palate: vivid acidity, fine tannins, plum and chocolate undertones
finish: long fresh finish with pine and spice accents

name: Bourgogne Pinot Noir
description: From a gentle 2012 harvest in the Côte de Nuits the Bourgogne Pinot Noir by Patrice Rion reveals an elegant medium ruby hue evolving toward brick tones. The bouquet, restrained yet evocative of small red berries, leads to a supple palate where silk‑like tannins soften a vibrant core of red fruit. This wine offers a refined presence without excess yet with enough structure for short‑term cellaring.
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 16 °C accompanied by classic family fare such as roasted chicken or mushroom‑gratin dishes. Enjoy now through around 2022 to catch the wine in its prime evolution.
aroma: small red berries with restrained perfume
palate: silky structure and supple tannins enfolding vibrant red fruit
finish: elegant gentle fade with lingering fruit clarity

name: Pattini Pinot Grigio Delle Venezia DOC
description: This elegant 2025 Pattini Pinot Grigio delle Venezie DOC presents a luminous straw‑yellow hue drawing from the mineral‑tinged limestone soils of Veneto. The wine shows poised aromas of white pear and citrus blossom leading into a palate that combines vibrant acidity with a gentle hint of almond.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10‑12 °C alongside light antipasti or delicate seafood, where its fresh, floral character will truly sing.
palate: vibrant acidity with a gentle hint of almond

name: Pattini Prosecco DOC
description: This Pattini Prosecco DOC NV offers a gentle sparkle and poised elegance inviting the senses with fresh orchard fruit brightness and a whisper of soft floral charm.
sommelierNotes: Chill gently in the fridge before serving at 6–8 °C pour into slender flutes and pair with light hors d’oeuvres or seafood for effortless delight.
palate: crisp pear and citrus

name: Pauillac Pichon Pauillac
description: This Pauillac from Château Pichon Baron 2019 is a classical yet radiant grand vin: the dark garnet hue with purple glints preludes a precise, intense bouquet of ripe black fruits and subtle spice notes. On the palate it is fleshy, powerful, with abundant yet silky tannins that carry the wine through an elegant, fruit-laced and distinguished finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below room temperature decanted to round the powerful tannins: it accompanies rich red meats or aged cheeses and will develop beautifully over decades.
aroma: intense ripe black fruits with fine spice
palate: fleshy, powerful, silky tannins

name: Paul Aegerter Beaune 1er Cru les Greves
description: The 2019 Paul Aegerter Beaune Premier Cru “Les Grèves” offers brooding garnet hues and vivid aromas of ripe red and black fruits, roasted strawberry undertones, crème de cassis and an elegant herbal whisper of thyme and savory. On the palate it is layered and generous showing both density and volume, leading to a finish of noble, persistent tannins framed by gentle spices.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly aerated around 15 °C in a Burgundy glass to showcase the wine’s plush texture and spicy complexity; pair with richly textured meats—rosé‑roasted pigeon or a pink duck breast with roasted white asparagus.
aroma: ripe red and black fruit with herbal spice
palate: voluminous dense red‑fruit core
finish: long tannic finish with sweet spices
foodPairings: pink duck breast with roasted white asparagus

name: Paul Aegerter Clos Vougeot Grand Cru
description: A stately and alluring wine from one of Burgundy’s grandest terroirs the 2019 Paul Aegerter Clos-Vougeot Grand Cru unfolds with a garnet robe leading to an evocative bouquet of rose petals and violets entangled with ripe raspberry and a wisp of wild mint This wine speaks of refined old‑world poise with plush texture and lingering charm
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below cellar temperature to showcase its finesse Pair with sumptuous, gentle meats and rich soft cheeses
palate: elegant, fleshy, sappy

name: Paul Aegerter Hautes Cotes de Nuits Rouge les Dames de Huguettes
description: A refined expression of Hautes‑Côtes de Nuits from the venerable Aegerter estate these Les Dames Huguettes reveal a garnet‑tinged robe overlaid with a perfumed bouquet of red and black berries floral whispers and a subtle trace of white pepper. Silky on the palate with poised freshness harmonious fruit and polished tannins they deliver a fine framed finish that lingers with poised elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at 14 °C to 16 °C alongside gently roasted duck breast or a savory pork cutlet enriched with peppered jus to complement the wine’s balance and fruit-driven character.
aroma: basket of red and black fruits with floral whispers and white pepper
palate: round and supple with poised freshness
finish: fine supported tannins leading to a balanced lingering close
foodPairings: Bigorre pork chop with a smooth pepper‑accented sauce

name: Paul Aegerter Huits Saint Georges
description: The 2020 Paul Aegerter Huits Saint‑Georges offers a vibrant garnet hue with a graceful bouquet of red and black berries enlivened by subtle forest underbrush and a whisper of earth. On the palate the wine unveils fine‐tuned tannins and poised structure, revealing both youthful energy and the promise of elegant evolution.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 15–16 °C to accentuate its bright fruit and refined structure; pair with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑accented poultry to enhance its earthy complexity.
aroma: red and black berries with forest and earth nuances
palate: elegant tannins and poised structure

name: Paul Aegerter Nuits Saint Georges #4
description: A wine of refined poise sourced from a judicious selection of the four finest barrels of Nuits‑Saint‑Georges Les Plateaux, this 2020 Paul Aegerter cuvée reveals a crimson robe and a nose brimming with black and bramble fruits underpinned by a subtle spice. The palate is structured and youthful yet promises an elegant evolution over time.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C to 16 °C, decanted when young. Pair with roast veal, duck breast or aged cow’s‑milk cheeses to complement the wine’s fine-grained tannins.
aroma: black and bramble fruits with a hint of spice
palate: structured, refined and youthful

name: Paul Aegerter Pernand Vergelesses Blanc
description: The 2021 Paul Aegerter Pernand‑Vergelesses Blanc displays refined Burgundian elegance the brilliant yellow color is luminous like a candle glow and the nose offers gentle white and yellow fruit underpinned by a subtle spice whisper. The palate is both crisp and generous, with a firm structure that leads into a rich lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve between 11 °C and 13 °C to preserve its brightness and pair with delicate fish dishes or an elegant tuna tartare.
aroma: white and yellow fruit with a subtle spice touch
palate: crisp yet generous with structure

name: Paul Aegerter Savigny les Beaunes
description: This refined 2020 Savigny‑les‑Beaune from the house of Aegerter unfolds with a luminous ruby hue guiding the eye to a nose brimming with small red fruits and a whisper of woodland spice rooted in its limestone and sandy terroir
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to preserve its freshness, pairing beautifully with Burgundy classics like œufs en meurette or grilled Bigorre pork to elevate its elegant structure
aroma: small red fruits with light woodland spice
palate: fresh yet gently rich with fine oak nuance

name: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage la Chapelle
description: The 2018 Hermitage La Chapelle from Paul Jaboulet Aîné is a profound Syrah of regal bearing, exuding intense aromas of crushed stone violets and mineral‑infused black and blue fruits. The palate offers velvety espresso‑tinged dark berries wrapped in luxurious texture and tension, culminating in a finish of licorice‑laced freshness and resonant length.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted at 16–18 °C to reveal its aromatic breadth; pair with richly flavoured game or herb‑crusted red meats to match its depth and intensity.
aroma: crushed stone and violet‑tinged black‑fruit perfume
palate: velvety espresso‑infused dark berries with polished tannin

name: Domaine Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage la Chapelle
description: The 2019 Hermitage La Chapelle from Paul Jaboulet Aîné is a profound Syrah of regal bearing, exuding intense aromas of crushed stone violets and mineral‑infused black and blue fruits. The palate offers velvety espresso‑tinged dark berries wrapped in luxurious texture and tension, culminating in a finish of licorice‑laced freshness and resonant length.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted at 16–18 °C to reveal its aromatic breadth; pair with richly flavoured game or herb‑crusted red meats to match its depth and intensity.
aroma: crushed stone and violet‑tinged black‑fruit perfume
palate: velvety espresso‑infused dark berries with polished tannin

name: Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage Vin de Paille
description: This extraordinary 2015 Hermitage Vin de Paille from Paul Jaboulet Aîné captures the sun‑kissed richness of late‑harvest Marsanne in a lusciously concentrated elixir. It wafts with honeyed apricot, crystallized citrus and delicate floral lift framed by a spine of bright acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in small glasses, ideal alongside blue‑veined cheeses or a fine fruit tart, or simply as a contemplative dessert wine.
palate: lusciously concentrated with bright acidity
finish: long and lingering with delicate floral lift
drinkWindow: Now and over the next 10–15 years

name: Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage Vin de Paille
description: This extraordinary 2015 Hermitage Vin de Paille from Paul Jaboulet Aîné captures the sun‑kissed richness of late‑harvest Marsanne in a lusciously concentrated elixir. It wafts with honeyed apricot, crystallized citrus and delicate floral lift framed by a spine of bright acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in small glasses, ideal alongside blue‑veined cheeses or a fine fruit tart, or simply as a contemplative dessert wine.
palate: lusciously concentrated with bright acidity
finish: long and lingering with delicate floral lift
drinkWindow: Now and over the next 10–15 years

name: Paul Jaboulet Aine Hermitage Vin de Paille
description: This extraordinary 2015 Hermitage Vin de Paille from Paul Jaboulet Aîné captures the sun‑kissed richness of late‑harvest Marsanne in a lusciously concentrated elixir. It wafts with honeyed apricot, crystallized citrus and delicate floral lift framed by a spine of bright acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in small glasses, ideal alongside blue‑veined cheeses or a fine fruit tart, or simply as a contemplative dessert wine.
palate: lusciously concentrated with bright acidity
finish: long and lingering with delicate floral lift
drinkWindow: Now and over the next 10–15 years

name: Wines Chardonnay Ma Jolie Peake Ranch Vineyard Santa Rita Hills
description: The 2023 Paul Lato “Ma Jolie” Chardonnay from Peake Ranch Vineyard in Sta. Rita Hills unveils a cool‑climate elegance, its flinty and reductive notes of toasted hazelnut and orange peel framing a texture of creamy intensity and subtle floral nuance. The wine is supple yet structured with gentle acidity and a long, floral‑inflected finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a tulip glass to appreciate the wine’s satin texture and restrained minerality: pairs beautifully with poached scallops, soft‑rind cheeses, or leek and herb tart.
palate: creamy, rounded mouthfeel with floral nuance

name: Wines Chardonnay Matinee Santa Barbara County
description: The 2024 Paul Lato “Matinee” Chardonnay from Santa Barbara County presents a graceful balance of cool coastal freshness and gentle oak nuance. Aromas of golden apple and honeydew melon yield to a palate of wet stone and lemon, with finely tuned acidity bringing poise and clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled and pair with delicate seafood or creamy vegetarian dishes to highlight the wine’s mineral interplay and fruit purity.
palate: wet stone, lemon, balanced acidity

name: Wines Pinot Noir Matinee Santa Barbara County
description: Paul Lato’s 2024 Matinee Pinot Noir appeals with a medium ruby clarity and an inviting bouquet of ripe red cherry, raspberry and a whisper of rose petal and baking spice, offering an elegant expression of Santa Barbara County’s cool coastal influence and artisan spirit. The palate is supple and fresh showcasing vivid red fruit, soft spice and earth underpinned by fine tannins and luminous acidity for graceful precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in a burgundy glass to highlight its lifted fruit and fine structure; pairs beautifully with roast chicken, seared duck or mushroom risotto.
aroma: ripe red cherry, raspberry, rose petal
palate: supple vivid red fruit with soft spice and earth
finish: elegant with fine tannins and bright acidity

name: Wines Pinot Noir Prospect Rancho Real Vineyard Santa Maria Valley
description: A glimmering expression of Santa Maria Valley finesse this 2023 “Prospect” Pinot Noir from Rancho Real Vineyard offers vibrant red cherry and wild strawberry framed by a whisper of orange peel revealing the site’s luminous clarity. The palate unfolds with juicy pomegranate and hibiscus tea softened by an earthy undertone, culminating in a clean silky finish that resonates with elegant energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to accentuate its bright aromatics, and pair with duck breast with cherry gastrique or mushroom risotto for a seamless harmony.
aroma: bright red cherry and wild strawberry with orange peel hint
palate: juicy pomegranate and hibiscus tea with soft earth
finish: clean silky finish of elegant energy

name: Wines Pinot Noir Seabiscuit Zotovich Vineyard Santa Rita Hills
description: A wine of lithe elegance and discerning poise this 2023 Seabiscuit Pinot Noir from Zotovich Vineyard exudes a translucent ruby hue, unfolding floral spice and mulberry‑tinged raspberry set against loamy forest floor and rose nuances. The palate glides with poised energy framed by silky dusty tannins and refined herbal undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled approximately 55°F in larger Burgundy stemware to highlight its finesse suggest pairing with mushroom‑dusted duck breast or delicate game birds.
aroma: floral spice with mulberry and rose
palate: sleek, lifted with raspberry and cherry core
finish: herbal, clean finish with black tea and crushed rock nuance

name: Château Paveil de Luze Margaux
description: A polished Margaux of classic gravitas with a dark garnet hue and poised elegance. It reveals fragrant violets and ripe cassis framed by savory tobacco and graphite nuances in refined harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 16 °C with richly sauced red meats or game while aging gracefully for the next decade.
palate: savory red fruit and firm powdery tannins

name: Château Pajzos Furmint Sec T Dry
description: A crystalline Tokaji Furmint from the renowned Pajzos estate, this 2019 vintage offers refined tension and vibrant precision. Orchard fruits and citrus peel glide across a taut frame underlined by mineral verve and a whisper of spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 10 °C in a slender white-wine glass to lift its citrus-accented freshness, ideally alongside shellfish or subtly spiced fare.
aroma: green apple and pineapple accented by guava and quince
palate: lemon pith and lemon curd with a fine spicy undertone
finish: bright and floral with lingering acidity

name: Chardonnay Sunchase Vineyard Petaluma Gap AVA
description: This 2015 Pellet Estate Chardonnay from the Sunchase Vineyard in the nascent Petaluma Gap offers a luminous expression of coastal California chardonnay ripe with orchard fruits and a whisper of savory complexity. It unfolds with sun‑kissed pineapple, honeydew melon and early‑season nectarine underlain by green apple and cut hay, finishing with a creamy almond nuance for depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature in fine stemware, alongside delicate seafood or roasted poultry with a gentle cream sauce, or allow graceful aging into the next decade.
aroma: pineapple, honeydew melon, green apple blossom
palate: silky texture with nectarines, almond cream underlying
finish: savory hay and almond cream linger

name: Henry's Reserve Napa Valley
description: A dense Napa Cabernet of true presence, the 2015 Henry’s Reserve unfolds with richly layered red fruit and a hint of floral brightness supported by fine-grained tannins and stately structure. It suggests both immediacy and longevity, a wine that bridges opulence and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve with a generous decant, and pair with a classic roast lamb or herbed beef to match its depth and persistence.
palate: silky tannins with cassis and spice

name: Domaine Paul Pernot Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: This 2022 Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru from Domaine Paul Pernot shows expressive floral and mineral aromas with a core of orchard fruit and vibrant energy. The palate is finely textured, joyful and layered, with a luminous mid‑palate and impeccable balance. The finish delivers clarity and tension with lingering mineral precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a fine white‑wine goblet, ideally with rich seafood, delicate poultry or creamy cheeses.
palate: textured orchard fruit with energy

name: Domaine Paul Pernot Bienvenue Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: The 2022 Domaine Paul Pernot Bienvenues Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru presents an alluring marriage of chalk‑infused minerality and rich stone‑fruit character touched by honeyed florals and a whisper of hazelnut. It offers a poised balance between fleshy generosity and tense acidity reflecting Puligny‑Montrachet’s signature finesse, carrying through its long, harmonious expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12–14 °C in fine stemware, allowing a moment to breathe; pair with dishes that possess both richness and subtlety, such as shellfish in creamy sauces or delicately roasted white poultry.
aroma: white peach, citrus blossom, crushed hazelnut
palate: creamy stone‑fruit with chalky mineral tension

name: Domaine Paul Pernot Puligny Montrachet 1er Cru Chalumaux
description: A gently woven Puligny‑Montrachet that balances tensile citrus clarity with an undertow of flinty mineral energy, the 2022 Chalumaux unfolds with a lingering core of white‑peach flesh framed by a subtle phenolic grip and lithely refined structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in slender white wine glasses to emphasize the bright citrus tones and mineral tension. Ideal with butter‑poached lobster, herb‑brushed scallops, or a light cream sauce on delicate fish.
palate: supple white‑peach fruit with phenolic grip

name: Domaine Perrachon Julienas les Mouilles
description: A supple and refined expression of Gamay from the heart of Juliénas, the 2018 Les Mouilles offers ripe cherry and red fruit aromas and a graceful structure with well‑integrated tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to highlight freshness, ideal with rustic French fare such as coq au vin or roasted poultry.
palate: silky red fruit, balanced tannins

name: Domaine Perrachon Julienas les Vignes Centennaire
description: From one of Julienas’s most revered parcels this Gamay offers an elegant yet brooding expression of ripe black cherry and plum firmened by dark mineral undertones and a gentle oak embrace.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to highlight its fresh acidity, ideal alongside roasted game or aged charcuterie.
aroma: ripe black cherry with subtle minerality
palate: silky plum and dark fruit framed by fine oak

name: Domaine Perrachon Morgon Corcelette
description: This 2020 Morgon Corcelette from Laurent Perrachon reveals a beguiling expression of ripe cherries, raspberries and forest‑floor nuances. The medium‑bodied palate is textured and plush with integrated tannins, framed by a core of mineral‑tinged fruit that carries a subtle peppery spice into a refined finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 14–16 °C alongside braised lamb or game birds, or alongside a selection of semi‑hard cheeses for graceful complementarity.
palate: plush texture with integrated tannins and peppery spice

name: Domaine Perrachon Morgon Corcelette
description: This 2022 Morgon Corcelette from Laurent Perrachon reveals a beguiling expression of ripe cherries, raspberries and forest‑floor nuances. The medium‑bodied palate is textured and plush with integrated tannins, framed by a core of mineral‑tinged fruit that carries a subtle peppery spice into a refined finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at 14–16 °C alongside braised lamb or game birds, or alongside a selection of semi‑hard cheeses for graceful complementarity.
palate: plush texture with integrated tannins and peppery spice

name: Domaine Perrachon Morgon Cote du Py
description: A wine of noble Beaujolais lineage, this 2021 Morgon Côte du Py exudes a deep intense hue and persistent aromas of kirsch and black pepper, drawn from century‑old Gamay vines rooted in schist and granite soils, offering both structure and finesse.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 14 °C, decant before enjoying alongside braised duck or game to elevate its spicy, savoury notes.
palate: dense black fruits with firm structure

name: Canto Petirrojo Golfo 8 L
description: A graceful old‑vine Tempranillo from Toro that offers a delicate balance of bright red fruit and fine earth tones, elegant rather than rustic in character, drawing softly on the region’s bold heritage.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled in warm weather or at cellar temperature in cooler months to reveal its supple fruit and graceful tannins, pairing beautifully with lamb chops or creamy manchego.
palate: elegant red fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Petit Paveil Bordeaux Rouge
description: This Petit Paveil 2018 unfolds with poised charm, offering a softly layered mosaic of ripe blackberry and cassis nuanced by a whisper of tobacco and warm earth, all framed in refined structure and elegant length.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature, ideally alongside roasted duck breast or a simple cassoulet where its gentle tannic backbone and fruity harmony can shine.
aroma: ripe blackberry and cassis with tobacco
palate: fresh, elegant fruit with refined structure
finish: warm earth and subtle graphite length

name: Domaine Petroni Rouge Corse Aop
description: This radiant 2019 Dom Petroni Rouge Corse AOP presents a refined tapestry of red fruit and Mediterranean spice, wrapped in a framing minerality drawn from the island’s sandy clay soils, gentle yet persistent in its presence. There is an elegance in its supple texture balanced by vivid freshness, offering both depth and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled, around 16 °C, ideal with grilled meats or rustic pizza, or enjoyed alongside a plateau of sheep’s milk cheese for a graceful pairing.
aroma: Expressive red fruits with delicate spice and light mineral thread.
palate: Supple entry with red fruit and subtle roasted nuance.
finish: Ample finish with silky tannins and lingering length.

name: Château Peyros Madiran Vielles Vignes
description: A robust and refined expression from Madiran’s southernmost terroir this 2019 Vieilles Vignes by Peyros offers dense black fruit underpinned by gentle spice and a polished structure. It balances powerful presence with elegance in a lineage of tradition and stony clay‑silt soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to highlight its freshness and pair with richly flavored meats: grilled lamb or duck in sauce.
palate: full‑bodied, round, supple with fresh core
drinkWindow: Drink now through 12–15 years from vintage

name: Carmignano Riserva DOCG
description: A noble opus of Carmignano refined with composure and intensity: this 2020 Piaggia Carmignano Riserva delivers ripe dark berries poised with tobacco and bittersweet chocolate, while framed in a structure of elegant tannins that promise graceful ageing.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently cooled to cellar temperature in generous Burgundy stems, a regal match for grilled lamb chops or mature pecorino with quince paste.
aroma: ripe cassis with tobacco and sweet spice
palate: structured, elegant with refined tannins

name: II Sasso Carmignano DOCG
description: A noble expression of Carmignano from Piaggia the 2022 Il Sasso reveals deep ruby crimson in the glass with a layered aroma of forest fruits sweet spice and subtle balsamic undertones, offering a polished yet enveloping palate of ripe cherries and blackberries with a thread of fine-grained tannins and cocoa‑tinged complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16°C in a large tulip glass to frame the plush fruit and fine structure, ideal with Tuscan grilled lamb chops or aged pecorino.
aroma: forest fruits with sweet spice and balsamic nuance
palate: ripe cherries blackberries, polished tannins, cocoa complexity
finish: persistent and balanced with gentle spice

name: Weingut Pichler-Krutzler Riesling Ried Loibenberg
description: A crystalline expression of Wachau’s famed Loibenberg, this Riesling from 2018 reveals poised stone‑fruit and citrus brightness, supported by a taut mineral spine and invigorating energy, inviting contemplation of its Old‑World pedigree
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to accompany delicate seafood or richer fish, or enjoy solo as a refined aperitif
palate: juice‑driven with lemon freshness and purity

name: Pichon Comtesse Reserve Pauillac
description: The 2018 Pichon Comtesse Réserve is gracious and refined with a silk‑touched texture cascading across the palate, its wealth of dark red and black fruits underpinned by violet and graphite whispers that unfold slowly
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to 60–62 °F in large Burgundy‑style glasses, ideal alongside roasted lamb, duck breast or aged cheeses
aroma: blackberry and violet with graphite nuance
palate: silky dark fruit with elegant tannins

name: Pichon Comtesse Reserve Pauillac
description: The 2019 Pichon Comtesse Réserve is gracious and refined with a silk‑touched texture cascading across the palate, its wealth of dark red and black fruits underpinned by violet and graphite whispers that unfold slowly
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to 60–62 °F in large Burgundy‑style glasses, ideal alongside roasted lamb, duck breast or aged cheeses
aroma: blackberry and violet with graphite nuance
palate: silky dark fruit with elegant tannins

name: Pierre Amadieu Gigondas Cuvee Romane Machotte Blanc
description: A refined expression of Gigondas in white form this cuvée melds the sandy warmth and limestone freshness of its terroirs into a seamless aromatic tapestry, subtly woven with citrus, white flowers and apricot underpinned by graceful structure and minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 12 °C and pair with fresh goat cheese enhanced by fine herbs or gently grilled sea bass.
palate: fresh and structured with minerality
foodPairings: fresh goat cheese with fine herbs

name: Pierre Amadieu Gigondas Cuvee Romane Machotte Rouge
description: The 2022 Pierre Amadieu Gigondas Cuvée Romane Machotte Rouge offers an elegant yet powerful expression of southern Rhône terroir. The nose opens with a poised blend of black and red berries layered with Provençal herbs such as thyme, laurel and rosemary, supported by a whisper of black pepper. The palate reveals silky yet muscular tannins, a core of dark fruit and vibrant garrigue that leads into a long balanced finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at approximately 15 °C, after decanting to unveil its aromatic complexity and to pair beautifully with herb‑infused beef stews or roasted lamb.
aroma: black and red berries with Provençal herbs
palate: silky powerful tannins, dark fruit and garrigue

name: Pierre Amadieu Gigondas le Pas de L'aigle
description: This 2022 Gigondas Le Pas de l’Aigle from Pierre Amadieu offers a noble and concentrated expression of high-altitude Grenache with just a hint of Syrah, revealing its stony terroir with seamless power and finesse
sommelierNotes: Serve at about 17°C in large stemware to allow red and black fruit layers to unwind; pair with truffle‑infused dishes or slow‑braised beef for a grand and elegant match
palate: silky full‑bodied with candied black fruit and delicate red fruit

name: Pierre Amadieu Igp Mediterranee Blanc (Viognier/clairette)
description: An elegant expression of southern sunlit vineyards this 2022 IGP Méditerranée Blanc from Pierre Amadieu combines Viognier’s floral generosity with Clairette’s crisp structure offering apricot and white peach notes framed by vivacious freshness, all lifted by a saline Mediterranean tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 12–14 °C alongside creamy risotto, shellfish or light grilled fish to highlight its refreshing fruit and graceful acidity.
palate: vibrant fruit framed by vivacity

name: Bourgogne Aligote
description: Pierre Morey's 2015 Bourgogne Aligoté is a dry, medium-bodied white with lively acidity and a clear Meursault-grown mineral character. Citrus, green apple, and subtle almond tones move through a lean, refreshing palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 9-11°C as an aperitif or alongside oysters, gougères, freshwater fish, or goat cheese.
palate: Dry, brisk, lightly textured

name: Bourgogne Chardonnay
description: Pierre Morey's 2013 Bourgogne Chardonnay offers a mature white Burgundy profile shaped by orchard fruit, citrus, and gentle nutty development. The palate is rounded yet held in line by clean acidity and a chalky, understated finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 11-12°C without overchilling; pair with roast chicken, sole meunière, or a creamy mushroom dish.
palate: Rounded orchard fruit, bright acidity, light cream

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Batard Montrachet Grand Cru
description: This 2021 Domaine Pierre Morey Bâtard‑Montrachet Grand Cru unfurls with sumptuous concentration and vibrancy, revealing a veil of rich white fruit and an undertone of mineral electricity. It offers both poetic elegance and depth of structure in its youth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled and pair with finely prepared seafood or creamy poultry dishes to complement the wine’s radiant intensity.
palate: powerful and vivid with broad minerality

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Bourgogne Cote D'or Pinot Noir
