description: Elegant and refined Bourgogne Côte d’Or 2021 from Domaine Pierre Morey reveals red cherry and wild strawberry perfume layered with a gentle spice nuance, framed by supple structure and delicate mineral undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature its freshness will lift pork tenderloin or mushroom risotto, adding finesse without overwhelming the dish.
aroma: red cherry and wild strawberry with subtle spice
palate: supple, balanced, mineral‑tinged

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault les Terres Blanches
description: A crystalline expression of Meursault from a chalky parcel beneath Gouttes d’Or, this 2020 reveals brisk orchard fruit and refined mineral clarity, wrapped in a bright yet poised profile. The wine is illuminated by lemon‑zest lift and underlying salinity, balancing amplitude and precision with a beautifully tempered finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in open white Burgundy glasses to emphasise freshness: complementary with creamy shellfish or subtly sauced fish dishes.
palate: ample yet incisive, bright acidity with chalky minerality

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault les Terres Blanches
description: The 2021 Meursault Les Terres Blanches from Domaine Pierre Morey exudes a pale golden hue with a crystalline clarity, reflecting its chalky hillside soils. It reveals delicate aromas of white flowers, crushed almonds and a whisper of fresh pear, leading to a lithe, mineral-driven palate, fine-boned and luminous.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 12 °C after a brief decant or one hour in glass to awaken its floral complexity: pairs elegantly with sole meunière or creamy poultry dishes.
palate: lithe mineral purity with pear and citrus zest

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault les Tessons
description: The 2020 Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault “Les Tessons” offers an elegant expression of Meursault’s famed minerality with pear and citrus notes finely threaded with crushed chalk nuances, unfolding in a medium‐weight, refined weave.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at about 10–12 °C in fine stemware to showcase its poised freshness; superb with delicate seafood or creamy poultry dishes.
aroma: pear and citrus with chalky mineral lift
palate: refined medium‐weight, scintillating minerality
foodPairings: roasted chicken in light cream sauce

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault les Tessons
description: The 2021 Domaine Pierre Morey Meursault “Les Tessons” offers an elegant expression of Meursault’s famed minerality with pear and citrus notes finely threaded with crushed chalk nuances, unfolding in a medium‐weight, refined weave.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at about 10–12 °C in fine stemware to showcase its poised freshness; superb with delicate seafood or creamy poultry dishes.
aroma: pear and citrus with chalky mineral lift
palate: refined medium‐weight, scintillating minerality
foodPairings: roasted chicken in light cream sauce

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Monthelie (Rouge)
description: A graceful expression of Monthelie 2021 from Domaine Pierre Morey, this red offers pure, bright cherry and crushed strawberry aromas complemented by soft violet lift. The palate is elegantly poised with sappy red fruit and a gentle sinewy tannic thread, imparting youthful charm and clarity. Served with poise now or allowed a few years to mellow.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C, decant briefly if you wish to round the sinewy edge; pairs beautifully with roast rabbit or veal in a light jus.
palate: sappy red fruit with violet nuances

name: Domaine Pierre Morey Volnay 1er Cru les Santenots
description: The 2021 Volnay Premier Cru Les Santenots from Domaine Pierre Morey unfolds with gentle elegance: ripe cherry and delicate floral notes lifted by a whisper of savory earth. Finely structured and silky, the wine bears the hallmark velvet texture of its Meursault-born terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a large Pinot Noir goblet to coax its perfume Pair with roast duck or wild mushroom risotto for a graceful match.
palate: silky, elegant, savory undertones

name: Morey-Blanc Bourgogne Chardonnay
description: A remarkably clear expression of Meursault’s mineral-laced terroir this 2012 Morey‑Blanc Bourgogne Chardonnay offers crystalline notes of ripe yellow fruit underscored by lively tension and a gracefully structured frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 12 °C with richer seafood or lightly sauced poultry to match its poised acidity and finesse.
palate: crisp, tensioned fruit framed in subtle weight
drinkWindow: can age gracefully for several years unlocking more minerality

name: Domaine Pierre Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Mon Aieul
description: This 2018 Cuvée de Mon Aïeul from Domaine Pierre Usseglio is a vibrant expression of venerable old‑vine Grenache from Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape. It unfolds with sumptuous dark‑berry preserves, subtle herbes de Provence and crushed stone, all rendered with an airy texture and poised freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C in broad Bordeaux‑style glasses, pairing beautifully with braised lamb, Provençal herb‑accented dishes or aged cheeses.
aroma: black fig and boysenberry preserves with crushed thyme and stone
palate: pure‑fruited Grenache with weightless texture and feathery tannins
foodPairings: braised lamb with herbs de Provence

name: Jo Pithon Anjou Blanc les Pepinaires
description: A gently evolved Chenin Blanc from Jo Pithon’s Anjou vineyards, the 2005 Les Pépinaïres shows a refined marriage of ripeness and minerality, shaped by barrel aging and organic viticulture, offering a poised expression of its sandstone and carboniferous soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to highlight its salinity and nuanced texture, accompanied by fresh goat cheese or simply enjoyed as a contemplative aperitif.
aroma: orchard fruit with a hint of honeyed warmth
palate: textured, gently oxidative with bright mineral drive
foodPairings: sea scallops with butter and lemon
drinkWindow: up to now or short term for primary character

name: Jo Pithon Quarts de Chaume les Varennes
description: An elegant expression of botrytized Chenin Blanc from Quarts de Chaume with a pale gold hue and a captivating interplay of honeyed generosity and vibrant freshness, this 2003 Jo Pithon “Les Varennes” reveals refined dried fruit and ginger‐infused complexity framed by poised acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in modest stemware to preserve its balance and lift; ideal with foie gras, blue‑veined cheese, or subtly sweet almond‑based desserts.
palate: toffee, dried fruits and ginger

name: Pomerol By Clinet
description: A refined expression of Pomerol’s noble essence this 2020 By Clinet presents ripe plum and black cherry framed by subtle violet and truffle nuances, unfolding with a graceful density and softly plush tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in large Bordeaux stems to reveal its layered fruit and earthy undertones, an elegant companion to roasted duck or aged Comté.
palate: smooth, plush plum and cherry

name: Vintage Porto
description: The 2003 Portal Vintage Porto reveals mature allure with silky sweetness and nostalgic depth It exudes cocoa‑tinged dark berry fruit and gentle spice weaving a refined richness that unfolds gracefully
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted at cellar cool around 16 °C in a sturdy port glass shouldering its soft tannins well Pairs elegantly with aged Stilton or praline‑accented desserts
palate: soft elegant tannins, ripe sugar, cocoa‑berry meld
finish: long sweet finish with spice echo

name: Winery Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve Kiona Vineyard Red Mountain
description: The 2017 Powers Winery Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon from Kiona Vineyard on Red Mountain reveals a deeply concentrated expression of Washington Cabernet with lusciously layered dried cherry and plum tones enriched by hints of licorice and tobacco, all framed in a compellingly structured form. It speaks with old‑world poise and firm tannins that promise graceful ageing and a polished finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve moderately chilled at cellar temperature, decanted for aeration and ideally paired with rich fare such as grilled flank steak or aged Gouda.
aroma: dried cherry and plum with licorice undertones
palate: structured, layered fruit with tobacco nuance
finish: firm tannic grip with polished length

name: Winery Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve Sheridan Vineyard Yakima Valley
description: A poised and structured Washington Cabernet Sauvignon that reveals polished dark fruit beneath a layer of refined oak spice, conveying tension and elegance in equal measure. It carries a dignified presence with concentrated plum and blackberry framed by subtle herbal undercurrents, culminating in a graceful, poised character.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cooler than cellar temperature to showcase its vibrant acidity, and pair with grilled lamb chops or mushroom‑braised short ribs to complement its depth and structure.
aroma: dark plum and black cherry with a whisper of herbs
palate: layered black fruit framed by fine tannins and subtle spice
finish: elegant long finish with mineral tension

name: Winery Merlot Columbia Valley
description: This 2017 Powers Winery Merlot from Columbia Valley unveils an inviting bouquet of crushed berries and subtle spice, lending an elegant, old‑world sensibility to its richly structured core. The palate unfolds with refined tannins enmeshed with notes of cocoa, Oolong tea and strawberry preserves before drifting toward a decadent, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 60 °F in broad‑bowled glasses to highlight its nuanced fruit and soft spice character, pairing beautifully with roasted poultry or mild cheeses.
palate: round with cocoa, Oolong tea and strawberry preserves

name: Sparkling Wine
description: A pale, gently golden sparkling wine that charms with a floral and orchard‐fruit perfume followed by a softly sweet, buoyant palate, elegantly balanced by bright acidity and fine bubbles.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in flutes or stems to preserve the mousse; pairs beautifully with light hors d’oeuvres or casual celebrations.
palate: softly sweet with tropical and orchard fruit notes

name: Château Puynormand Montagne Saint Emilion
description: This wine reveals a radiant garnet hue and a perfumed bouquet of ripe red fruits, subtly framed by mineral lift and a hint of spice, offering a graceful balance of flesh and finesse. The palate unfolds with rounded Merlot warmth supported by Cabernet Franc structure, delivering plush texture and polished tannins in an elegant, poised style.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to cellar temperature in a large-bowled glass to frame its supple fruit and fine tannins; pairs exquisitely with roast lamb or mushroom ragout.
aroma: ripe red berry with mineral spice
palate: plush Merlot fruit with structured Cabernet Franc

name: Quinta Do Mouro Vinha Do Mouro Tinto Reserve
description: This Vinha do Mouro Reserva 2020 unfolds with a medium‑ruby hue and a refined aromatic tapestry of vivid red and black fruit, subtle spices, woodland and a faint green flourish. On the palate it shows balanced structure and polished tannins enlivened by lively acidity and a persistent, vibrant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at about 60 °F in a large-bowled glass to display its freshness and layers. Pair with grilled lamb, mushroom ragout or aged cheeses to complement its fine tannins and spice nuances.
aroma: fresh red and black fruit with subtle spice and woodland
palate: balanced structure with elegant tannins and marked freshness

name: Weingut Rainer Wess Riesling Loibenberg
description: This Riesling from Rainer Wess’s Loibenberg vineyard is an elegant marriage of tropical stone fruit and mineral clarity, revealing yellow peach, mango, and a whisper of white flowers grounded by a sinewy mineral core drawn from ancient gneiss soils. With its refined texture and firm acidity this wine unfolds with precision and poise while promising further grace with time.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a fine Riesling glass at around 10 °C: it will lift off seafood of delicate nature such as oysters or scallops, or stand in beautiful counterpoint to richer white meats or creamy fish preparations.
aroma: yellow peach and mango with white floral nuance
palate: mineral‑driven precision and vibrant acidity
foodPairings: poached white fish in beurre blanc

name: Jc Ramonet le Montrachet Grand Cru
description: This 2020 Ramonet Le Montrachet Grand Cru unfurls with pristine white‑flower and citrus blossom on the nose, overlaid with a faint brioche warmth Suggestive of mineral clarity and poised richness it offers a symphony of orchard fruit and gentle hazelnut nuances
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in fine stemware to showcase the wine’s sculpted elegance Its stony minerality and depth partner splendidly with lobster in beurre blanc or an elegantly sauced white fish
palate: orchard fruit with brioche and mineral clarity

name: Domaine Jj Archambaud Echezeaux Grand Cru
description: A pale ruby‑tinged Pinot Noir from Rapet, this 2021 Echezeaux Grand Cru offers elegant precision, its red‑fruit clarity framed by softly structured tannins and a whisper of mineral drive. The wine’s refined character and persuasive freshness speak of gentle extraction and September’s benevolent weather during a low‑yield vintage.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15°C in a large burgundy glass to reveal its delicate layers; pair with herb‑roasted pheasant or mushroom‑studded risotto to complement its red‑berry clarity and subtle earth tones.
aroma: red cherry with a hint of earth
palate: silky, precise red‑fruit framed by fine tannin

name: Domaine Jj Archambaud Vosne Romanee 1er Cru les Petits Monts
appellation: Vosne‑Romanée Premier Cru Les Petits Monts
description: From a scarce hillside parcel perched above Romanée‑Conti this 2021 Rapet Dom JJ Archambaud Vosne‑Romanée 1er Cru Les Petits Monts unfolds with a poised blend of red cherry and fine spice, its texture lean yet refined, framed by a mineral undercurrent of limestone tenor. It exudes an old‑world grace with an elegantly layered structure that speaks of Burgundian terroir and a restrained natural sweetness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C in Burgundy glasses after brief decanting; pairs seamlessly with lightly roasted poultry or gently seasoned mushroom risotto.
palate: lean, refined texture with limestone minerality

name: Domaine Rapet Beaune 1er Cru les Cents Vignes
appellation: Beaune Premier Cru Les Cents Vignes
description: This Beaune Premier Cru Les Cents Vignes 2023 offers a refined expression of elegant Burgundy Pinot Noir, where silken red and black cherry echoes glide over a frame that balances supple grace with measured structure. The wine unfolds layers of discreet depth and mineral intensity, suggestive of cellaring potential yet approachable in its youthful charm.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at about 15°C to reveal its harmony of fruit and terroir; pairs beautifully with roasted lamb or duck breast, highlighting its finesse and depth.
aroma: red and black cherry with subtle violet and spice
palate: silken, elegant, mineral-tinged red fruit

name: Domaine Rapet Beaune 1er Cru les Greves
description: Lithe and refined, the 2023 Rapet Beaune 1er Cru Les Grèves is a graceful Pinot Noir emerging from ancient vines trained on mineral‑rich scree. It offers a fragrance of red berries and citrus peel atop a velvet‑textured palate marked by understated power and a saline, lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‐cool temperature in a tulip glass to coax out its perfume; pairs beautifully with roast duck or mushroom‑accented dishes.
aroma: red berries with a hint of orange zest
palate: medium‑bodied, ample texture with melting tannins

name: Domaine Rapet Bourgogne Rouge en Bully
description: A gently perfumed Bourgogne Rouge bearing the hallmark terroir of Pernand‑Vergelesses, offering a charming interplay of cherry and raspberry wrapped in a velvety texture that lingers softly on the palate. Crafted with minimal handling and careful vinification as laid out by Domaine Rapet, it reveals a well‑integrated palate with a gracious balance of fruit and refined tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in classic Burgundy stemware around 14 °C, pairing beautifully with roast leg of lamb or richly sauced beef dishes to complement its silky texture and red fruit notes.
palate: silky tannins, generous fruit

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: A confident expression of the Corton‑Charlemagne Grand Cru from Rapet Père & Fils 2023 presents layers of stone‑infused peach, white flowers and hazelnut elegantly woven into a satiny, powerful texture
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C in Burgundy tulip glasses; ideal with rich shellfish or creamy poultry preparations
aroma: peach and pear, white flowers, wet stones, hazelnut
palate: full‑bodied, satiny, layered, racy acidity

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: A confident expression of the Corton‑Charlemagne Grand Cru from Rapet Père & Fils 2023 presents layers of stone‑infused peach, white flowers and hazelnut elegantly woven into a satiny, powerful texture
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 12 °C in Burgundy tulip glasses; ideal with rich shellfish or creamy poultry preparations
aroma: peach and pear, white flowers, wet stones, hazelnut
palate: full‑bodied, satiny, layered, racy acidity

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Rouge Grand Cru
description: A lucid garnet‑hued Pinot Noir of noble Corton stature, this 2020 Domaine Rapet Corton Rouge Grand Cru delivers a refined melody of ripe red berries and warm earth notes, its polished structure framed by poised tannins and an elegant, spice‑tinged finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 14–16 °C with rich game or roasted poultry, allowing the wine’s tension and red‑fruit core to shine through.
palate: suave yet structured, firm tannins

name: Domaine Rapet Corton Rouge Grand Cur
description: A noble Corton Rouge from Rapet’s hands, the 2023 vintage reveals deeply resonant aromas of both red and black pinot fruit underlined by discreet floral notes and earthy mineral undertones, framed by a judicious touch of cedary oak: poised, refined, and embodying the weight and lineage of old vines.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar cool, and allow this majestic wine to unfold alongside roasted game or rich poultry, or aged cheeses to elevate its layered texture.
aroma: red and black cherry, floral, earthy minerality
palate: full‑bodied, defined fruit, chalky tannins

name: Domaine Rapet Coton Charlemagne Grand Cru
description: This 2020 Domaine Rapet Corton‑Charlemagne Grand Cru unveils a refined harmony of ripe yellow fruit and toasted almond notes, underscored by a subtle smoky minerality reflecting its renowned Pernand‑Vergelesses terroir, with a rich yet nervy concentration that promises both power and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C to accentuate its tension and fine texture, and pair with lobster, foie gras or delicate shellfish to let the wine’s mineral spine and creamy vibrance shine.
aroma: almonds and yellow stone fruit with smoky nuance
palate: unctuous and concentrated yet nervy

name: Domaine Rapet Pernand Vergelesses 1er Cru Iie de Vergelesses
appellation: Pernand‑Vergelesses Premier Cru Île de Vergelesses
description: This red Burgundy from Domaine Rapet Père & Fils is an elegant and refined expression of Pernand‑Vergelesses Premier Cru “Île de Vergelesses” 2023. It reveals a graceful, floral‑tinged profile with gentle ripeness underpinned by finely tuned tension, showcasing the purity of its limestone and iron‑rich hillside terroir. The wine is silky and tactile yet poised, hinting at both early charm and long‑term refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve at around 15 °C in medium‑wide glasses; drink now through 2038 to enjoy its bright floral lift or cellar briefly to savour evolving silkiness.
palate: silky sensual texture

name: Domaine Rapet Pernand Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru sous Fretille
description: A crystalline expression of Pernand‑Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru, this 2023 from Rapet unveils an inviting interplay of airy orchard fruit and palpable mineral tension, carried on a sleek and vibrant structure that balances generosity with lithe precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled; ideal with shellfish or subtly herb‑inflected creamy dishes to echo its tension and minerality.
palate: satiny yet racy orchard fruit with saline underpinning
foodPairings: succulent chicken breast with cream sauce

name: Domaine Rapet Pernand Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru sous Fretille
description: A crystalline expression of Pernand‑Vergelesses Blanc 1er Cru, this 2023 from Rapet unveils an inviting interplay of airy orchard fruit and palpable mineral tension, carried on a sleek and vibrant structure that balances generosity with lithe precision.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled; ideal with shellfish or subtly herb‑inflected creamy dishes to echo its tension and minerality.
palate: satiny yet racy orchard fruit with saline underpinning
foodPairings: succulent chicken breast with cream sauce

name: Domaine Rapet Savigny les Beaune 1er Cru aux Fournaux
description: The 2019 Rapet Savigny‑lès‑Beaune 1er Cru Aux Fournaux unveils an elegant fusion of Morello cherry and blackcurrant, layered with hints of iron‑tinged soil and bonfire smoke, finely framed by cedar and delicate coriander seed. The palate is bright, full‑bodied yet poised offering a creamy core from venerable vines, supple mineral energy and polished tannins leading into a long and balanced finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at 15 °C alongside red meats or game birds, or allow further complexity to emerge over the next decade of cellaring.
aroma: Morello cherry, blackcurrant, bonfire, cedar, coriander seed
palate: Bright and full‑bodied with creamy old‑vine core, fine‑grained tannins, mineral drive

name: Domaine Rapet Savigny les Beaune 1er Cru les Fournaux
description: A wine of discernible Burgundy pedigree from Rapet Père & Fils this 2020 Savigny‑lès‑Beaune Premier Cru “Aux Fournaux” offers vivid fruit expression and refined structure, the result of gentle winemaking and terroir of deep, ferruginous soils. Silky yet powerful, it reveals savoury cherry and cassis underpinned by an earth‑tinged grace
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15 °C, ideally with roasted meats or game birds, to appreciate its talc‑fine tannins and lingering undergrowth nuance
palate: silky concentration of red and black fruit, refined tannic texture

name: Domaine Rapet Savigny les Beaune
description: The 2023 Rapet Savigny‑lès‑Beaune “Aux Fournaux” unfurls with a bright tapestry of morello cherry, raspberry and cassis underscored by a whisper of iron‑tinged earth a hallmark of its ferruginous soils, elegant in poise yet quietly powerful in structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in fine Burgundy glasses after a brief decant to reveal its vibrant fruit and savoury depth, and pair with roast autumnal game birds or red meats with subtle herbs.
palate: fine tannins with poised red fruit

name: Domaine Rapet Vergelesses Blanc les Combottes
description: A striking village‐level Chardonnay from one of Pernand‑Vergelesses’ oldest families, born on steep, marly slopes, with refined floral and orchard fruit over a caressing mineral spine. This 2023 reveals a poised freshness with subtle spice and honeyed nuance grounded in chalk‑stone clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool and still reveal its elegant tension, ideally with shellfish and gentle white‑meat preparations at around 12 °C.
aroma: fresh orchard fruit with spice and honeyed mineral lift
palate: lively and balanced with precise acidity and silky texture

name: J&j Archambaud Hautes Cotes de Nuits
description: This 2022 J & J Archambaud Hautes‑Côtes de Nuits is a supple Pinot Noir from high‑altitude vines above Nuits‑Saint‑Georges, offering refined red fruit notes framed by lively energy and a discreet earthy underpinning derived from ferruginous limestone soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 14 °C in a Burgundian tulip glass to showcase vibrant cherry notes, elegant structure that pairs beautifully with simply prepared duck or grilled mushrooms.
aroma: red cherry and wild strawberry with earthy nuance
palate: fresh red fruits carried on graceful acidity with delicate minerality
finish: clean, sappy finish with gentle iron‑tinged lift

name: J&j Archambaud Vosne Romanee
description: This 2022 J & J ARCHAMBAUD Vosne‑Romanée is a village‑level Pinot Noir of subtle pedigree. It offers a graceful interplay of red cherry and plum aromas underscored by a hint of forest floor, while the palate is refined, vivid and poised with structure and clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature around 55°F in Burgundy glasses with roasted duck or creamy mushroom dishes.
aroma: red cherry and plum with forest floor nuance
palate: refined, vivid, poised structure

name: Carlos Raposo Impecavel Red Wine
description: An elegant and unadorned expression of Touriga Nacional from the Dão, this wine offers a delicate, floral-scented profile with violet and bergamot notes, framed by lively red fruit and vivid mineral clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16–18 °C in fine tulip glasses; pairs beautifully with roast poultry, herb‑accented charcuterie, or mushroom risotto.
palate: bright red fruit with herbal freshness

name: Domaine Raymond Usseglio Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Girard
description: An elegant and velvety Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape from Domaine Raymond Usseglio, the 2021 Cuvée Girard offers a richer texture born of old‑vine Grenache, delivering concentrated black‑cherry fruit anchored by polished structure and spicy undertones.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or after decanting to reveal harmonic layers, ideal with hearty roast lamb or Provençal herb‑accented dishes.
palate: concentrated, velvety, with fine tannins

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Récoltant Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley is plush and inviting a deep crimson presence leading into luxurious aromas of vanilla nutmeg clove and a touch of cracked pepper inviting the senses into its graceful embrace. On the palate the wine unfolds with layered notes of cranberry and warm baking spice poised upon a frame of fine tannin and balanced acidity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in a tulip‑shaped glass allowing the vibrant acidity to enliven grilled pork chops or aged cheddar cheese.
aroma: French vanilla nutmeg clove cracked pepper
palate: layered cranberry baking spice refined tannins

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Reserve Napa Valley
description: A gracious expression of Napa Valley Cabernet focused on deep black-cherry fruit framed by gently toasted oak and a fine, velvety structure. Elegant rather than overtly opulent, this Reserve captivates with harmony and a subtle undercurrent of dried herbs enhancing its graceful poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve at just below cellar temperature in a generously shaped glass. Decant briefly to allow its refined layers to coalesce. Pairs beautifully with grilled lamb chops or a classic beef tournedos.
aroma: black cherry with a touch of cedar
palate: silky texture with dark fruit and mild spice
finish: long and supple with refined tannins

name: Château Reynier Bordeaux Superieur
description: An inviting portrait of the 2019 Château Reynier Bordeaux Supérieur, where juicy black cherries and cassis mingle with delightful whispers of cardamom, dried floral notes and chocolate orange. The medium-bodied palate unfolds with velvety tannins and mellow, seamless fruit leading to a lingering, graceful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool, around 60°F, alongside roasted lamb or mushroom‑dusted rostis to accentuate its plush yet precise texture.
aroma: black cherry, cassis, dried flowers, cardamom
palate: medium‑bodied, velvety tannins, mellow fruit

name: Isaac Fernandez Seleccion Rios de Tinta Do Ribera Del Duero
description: This wine offers vivid impressions of ripe red plums and black cherries blended with earthy soil tones and a whisper of cigar wrapper spice, framed by a polished and youthful energy. The palate unfolds with concentrated fruit, vibrant acidity, modest tannic structure and a subtle warmth at the close, suggesting both immediacy and the promise of maturation. Pairing suggestions: grilled lamb chops, aged Manchego cheese, roasted mushrooms.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16 °C in wide Bordeaux‑style glasses to enhance its fresh fruit and fine acidity. It pairs beautifully with grilled meats, savory stews or charcuterie.
aroma: ripe black cherry with cigar‑wrapper spice
palate: concentrated red fruit with tangy acids

name: 16/17/18 Rocca Di Montegrossi Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto San Marcellino DOCG
description: This Chianti Classico Gran Selezione from Rocca di Montegrossi, vintage 2016, is drawn from the estate’s revered San Marcellino vineyard. Its presence is defined by deep plum and dark cherry nuances woven into a structure that marries creamy texture with energetic minerality and refined tannins, emanating layers of licorice, subtle spice, tobacco and smoke.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted, ideally alongside grilled red meats or aged Tuscan cheeses, to allow its layered complexity and lifted acidity to unfold.
palate: creamy texture, refined tannins, chalky minerality

name: Chianti Classico
description: A graceful and finely poised Chianti Classico from Rocca di Montegrossi’s Monti in Chianti estate, this 2022 vintage presents a polished interplay of ripe red cherry and forest berry notes with subtle spice and violet whispers, offering both elegance and clarity that speak of its mineral‑rich limestone soils.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature alongside hearty Tuscan fare to bring out the wine’s bright acidity and savory tannins.
aroma: ripe cherry and violet with a hint of forest spice
palate: fresh red berries, lively acidity and refined tannins

name: Chianti Classico DOCG
description: The 2022 Rocca di Montegrossi Chianti Classico DOCG is a graceful and refined expression of Sangiovese with harmonious red cherry and raspberry layers accented by delicate floral spice and an undertone of Tuscan earth.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature in large stemware to appreciate its lively tension and balanced grip: pairs beautifully with grilled pork, mushroom ragout or aged pecorino.
palate: elegant with firm tannins and mineral tension
finish: long balanced finish with herbal nuance

name: Chianti Classico Gran Selezione DOCG Vigneto San Marcellino
description: This Chianti Classico Gran Selezione from Rocca di Montegrossi offers a tapestry of dark fruit and spice where plum and black cherry entwine with whispers of violet and graphite framing a sinewy structure, precise tannins and a compelling tension of minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at 16–18 °C in large tulip glasses to coax forth the dark fruit and spice accents. Pair with well‑seasoned bistecca alla fiorentina, aged pecorino or mushroom‑infused ragù.
palate: structured, mineral‑lined dark fruit

name: Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto San Marcellino
description: The 2016 Rocca di Montegrossi Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto San Marcellino offers a refined expression of Sangiovese supported by a whisper of Pugnitello. Bright ruby in the glass it reveals a symphony of dark cherry and raspberry framed by violet and elegant mineral spice accents, all beneath a polished structure marked by poised tannins and harmonious freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in broad glasses to release its floral and spice nuances. Pair with herb‐studded roast lamb or mushroom risotto to complement its earthy fruit and sapid backbone.
palate: refined red/black fruit, poised tannins

name: Chianti Classico Gran Selezione Vigneto San Marcellino

name: Toscana Rosso Geremia
description: An expressive Super‑Tuscan of fine lineage showcasing deep Tuscan soil and Bordeaux heritage. The 2018 Geremia offers a polished yet powerful presence, rich with dark berry undertones and softly rendered spice tones. Its texture is velvety yet tensile, balancing intensity with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve from decanter at cellar‑cool temperature around 60 °F, pairing splendidly with robust red meats or rustic pasta dishes.
aroma: ripe blackberry and black cherry with pepper and malt tones
palate: lush, layered core of dark berries with silken tannins
finish: long, spicy, with a subtle saline echo

finish: long, spicy, with a subtle saline echo

name: Toscana Rosso Geremia
description: An expressive Super‑Tuscan of fine lineage showcasing deep Tuscan soil and Bordeaux heritage. The 2018 Geremia offers a polished yet powerful presence, rich with dark berry undertones and softly rendered spice tones. Its texture is velvety yet tensile, balancing intensity with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve from decanter at cellar‑cool temperature around 60 °F, pairing splendidly with robust red meats or rustic pasta dishes.
aroma: ripe blackberry and black cherry with pepper and malt tones
palate: lush, layered core of dark berries with silken tannins
finish: long, spicy, with a subtle saline echo

name: Toscana Rosso Geremia IGT
description: A noble Tuscan blend that unfolds with generosity and grace: the 2017 Geremia IGT Toscana Rosso by Rocca di Montegrossi marries velvety Merlot with structured Cabernet Sauvignon to evoke dark berry and wild cherry nuances, underpinned by subtle oak whispers of vanilla licorice and chocolate. Its texture is seamlessly balanced between power and elegance reflecting the stony minerality of Monti in Chianti.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar cool temperature in large-bowled glasses to allow the plush yet erect tannins to unwind. Ideal with richly seasoned braised meats or aged cheeses.
aroma: dark berries with vanilla and licorice
palate: velvety yet structured with wild cherry and mineral depth
finish: long and balanced with mocha and subtle oak

description: A noble Tuscan blend that unfolds with generosity and grace: the 2017 Geremia IGT Toscana Rosso by Rocca di Montegrossi marries velvety Merlot with structured Cabernet Sauvignon to evoke dark berry and wild cherry nuances, underpinned by subtle oak whispers of vanilla licorice and chocolate. palate: velvety yet structured with wild cherry and mineral depth
finish: long and balanced with mocha and subtle oak

Its texture is seamlessly balanced between power and elegance reflecting the stony minerality of Monti in Chianti.

palate: velvety yet structured with wild cherry and mineral depth
finish: long and balanced with mocha and subtle oak

name: Toscana Rosso IGT Ridolfo
description: Composed with noble precision Ridolfo 2016 presents an expressive blend of Cabernet Sauvignon and Pugnitello offering dark blackberry and dried plum intertwined with rustic sour cherry and pepper. The structure is refined yet powerful, with integrated eucalyptus and licorice lifting the rich fruit and a firm acidity that frames its complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently aerated in large-format pours at 16–18 °C to highlight its refined tannins and savoury complexity; pairs elegantly with robust red meat or game preparations.
aroma: Blackberry, dried plum, sour cherry with herbal spice
palate: Silky yet powerful tannins, layered fruit and spice
finish: Long, slightly austere, with driving energy
foodPairings: Beef cheek with juniper or exotic spices
Spiced Tuscan beef stew (stufato alla Sangiovannese)
Grilled game birds (pigeon) with caramelized figs and mustard

name: Toscana Rosso Ridolfo
description: The 2015 Ridolfo Toscana Rosso by Rocca di Montegrossi offers a sumptuous and exotic encounter, where robust dark fruit and mocha mingle with licorice, menthol and dried herbs in a structure both opulent and graceful. Crafted only in magnums and jeroboams, it speaks of organic finesse and the union of Cabernet Sauvignon and Pugnitello in seamless harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted to reveal its layered complexity; a fine match for hearty Tuscan roasts or game in rich sauces.
palate: plush, opulent fruit with seamless tannins
finish: structured with depth and lingering spice

name: Toscana Rosso Ridolfo
description: The 2017 Ridolfo Toscana Rosso by Rocca di Montegrossi offers a sumptuous and exotic encounter, where robust dark fruit and mocha mingle with licorice, menthol and dried herbs in a structure both opulent and graceful. Crafted only in magnums and jeroboams, it speaks of organic finesse and the union of Cabernet Sauvignon and Pugnitello in seamless harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted to reveal its layered complexity; a fine match for hearty Tuscan roasts or game in rich sauces.
palate: plush, opulent fruit with seamless tannins
finish: structured with depth and lingering spice

name: Vinsanto Del Chianti Classico DOC
appellation: Vin Santo del Chianti Classico DOC
description: A lustrous amber dessert wine of rare poetry from Chianti Classico enthralling the senses with concentrated notes of dried apricot and toasted almonds, framed by elegant oxidative complexity and a slow-built sweetness
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in small cordial glasses allowing the honeyed richness to pair beautifully with nut‑based pastries or aged blue cheeses
palate: velvety and richly sweet with caramel undertones

name: Fine White Port
description: An elegantly fragrant White Port that greets the nose with layers of sweet orchard fruit, honeyed warmth and a subtle whisper of wood, followed by a velvety, full‑bodied mouthfeel and a long, richly satisfying finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled as an aperitif or elevated with tonic and mint over ice; especially complementary with salted almonds or olives.
aroma: sweet orchard fruit, honey, light wood
palate: velvety, full‑bodied

name: Lbv Port
description: This wine presents deep garnet hues and a richly perfumed bouquet of dark berry fruit and discreet spice framed by a subtle menthol lift. On the palate it unveils layered blackcurrant and plum wrapped in velvety tannins balanced by gentle sweetness and a poised structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature allow to breathe slightly before decanting, harmonious with bittersweet chocolate or aged blue cheeses.
aroma: ripe blackcurrant and plum with a hint of spice
palate: velvety dark fruit underpinned by balanced structure
drinkWindow: ready to enjoy now, will reward medium‑term cellaring

name: Reserva Latina Tawny
description: This non‑vintage Romariz Reserva Latina Tawny offers layered nuances of dried fruits and soft nuts mingling with whispers of caramel and a touch of spice, all carrying the gentle warmth of time‑touched oak.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool after dinner perhaps with modest sweets or a rich coffee for contrast and sophistication.
aroma: dried fruit and gentle nutty spice
palate: soft dried raisins with caramel warmth

name: Klee Pinot Noir Willamette Valley
description: A lithe and expressive Pinot noir imbued with lifted red cherry and raspberry layers, framed by an undercurrent of earthy spice and bright acidity, in a style that reflects the genteel terroir of the Yamhill‑Carlton and broader Willamette Valley
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to showcase the fresh red fruit tones; a natural partner for grilled salmon, duck confit or herbed mushroom tartines
palate: bright acidity, delicate tannin, vibrant red fruit

name: Klee Willamette Valley Pinot Noir Cans
description: Bright and inviting this non‑vintage Klee Pinot Noir in can captures Willamette Valley’s vibrant charm with silky red cherry, a whisper of forest floor and soft spice flourishing in each sip. It feels graceful yet approachable making it a pleasure for everyday indulgence.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a large Burgundy glass to warm slowly allowing the cherry and earthy notes to blossom, ideal with mushroom‑dusted poultry or roasted autumn vegetables.
palate: silky red fruit with gentle spice
drinkWindow: drink now to enjoy its freshness

name: Pinot Gris Autre Monde
description: The 2022 Roots “Un Autre Monde” Pinot Gris emerges with an airy elegance, offering delicate aromas of green apple, catmint and lemon‑verbena tea balanced by a sleek texture and restrained acidity that carries subtle flavors of spiced apple, lychee and lavender water across the palate.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled alongside simple seafood preparations or spring salads to complement its floral nuance and graceful structure.
palate: spiced apple, lychee, lavender water.

name: Wine Sheboygandy Pinot Noir Yamhill-Carlton
description: A refined homage to Yamhill‑Carlton’s lithe terroir the 2023 Roots "Sheboygandy" Pinot Noir presents a graceful weave of wild red cherry and rose petal wrapped with subtle earth‑laden spice and a whisper of forest floor. Its texture is poised refined approaching weightless yet anchored by a transparent core of Oregon sedimentary minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool 55–58 °F in Burgundy stemware to reveal lifted aromatics; ideal with mushroom‑rubbed duck breast or a soft goat cheese tart.
aroma: wild red cherry with rose petal and forest‑floor spice
palate: elegant, silky, mineral‑etched red fruit

name: Estate Chardonnay Eola-Amity Hills
description: A finely poised Chardonnay from Rose & Arrow’s Eola Springs site, the 2022 vintage offers a graceful interplay of stone‑inflected minerality and subtle floral charm: a delicate wash of white blossoms overlaid with crisp orchard fruit and a whisper of saline tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip‑shaped stemware to preserve its aromatic lift; pairs beautifully with oysters, buttery fish or soft‑curd cheeses.
aroma: white flowers, wet stone, citrus blossom
palate: crisp orchard fruit, mineral texture, saline lift
foodPairings: seared scallops with lemon beurre blanc

name: Estate Pinot Noir Gathered Stones
description: This 2021 vintage of Rose & Arrow Estate Gathered Stones Pinot Noir unfolds in the glass with violet floral and pepper spice aromas, then drifts toward humid forest floor, wet granite and anise, all held in graceful harmony by lively, poised acidity and supple tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 55°F in tulip‑shaped glasses to highlight its stony drive and fine tannin structure, and pair with mushroom‑scented dishes or Herbes de Provence roast chicken.
palate: humus, wet granite, anise tones with lively acidity
finish: supple tannins tapering into mineral‑tinged length
foodPairings: roasted chicken with Herbes de Provence
duck breast with juniper berry jus

name: Estate Pinot Noir Highland Close Chehlaem Mountains
description: This wine unfolds with a serene, old‑world grace showcasing ripe Nanking cherry and red spice embraced by whispers of fresh rain and fresh‑ground cocoa beans, reflecting the rugged volcanic soul of Chehalem Mountains. It is shapely and tranquil its fine‑grained texture and deliberate acidity weaving a graceful, lingering experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a gently shaped Pinot Noir glass around 55–60°F to highlight its elegant aromatics and ethereal red fruit; pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑savory dishes.
palate: fresh rain, cocoa bean minerality

name: Estate Pinot Noir Hopewell Hills Eola-Amity Hills
description: The 2021 Rose & Arrow Estate Pinot Noir from Hopewell Hills reflects volcanic terroir with expressive layers of blue and black fruit mingled with pink peppercorn and minerally tension framed by a luxurious, silky mouthfeel.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55 °F in a tulip-shaped glass. Pair with earthy dishes such as roast duck with mushrooms or porcini‑infused risotto, which mirror its forest‑floor nuances.
aroma: blue and black fruit with pink peppercorn
palate: silky, mineral‑driven fruit

name: Estate Pinot Noir Red Label Willamette Valley
description: The 2021 Rose & Arrow Estate Red Label presents a graceful expression of Willamette Valley Pinot Noir: bright red fruit and a fine mineral thread intertwine with rounded, polished texture reflecting the delicate tension of volcanic terroir. This vintage’s allure lies in its balanced structure and an inviting, lingering finish that speaks of both freshness and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to preserve its vibrant purity; an ideal companion to roasted poultry or wild mushrooms, enhancing both earth and fruit tones.
palate: silky red fruit and subtle rocky grip

name: Estate Pinot Noir Red Label Willamette Valley
description: The 2022 Rose & Arrow Estate Red Label presents a graceful expression of Willamette Valley Pinot Noir: bright red fruit and a fine mineral thread intertwine with rounded, polished texture reflecting the delicate tension of volcanic terroir. This vintage’s allure lies in its balanced structure and an inviting, lingering finish that speaks of both freshness and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to preserve its vibrant purity; an ideal companion to roasted poultry or wild mushrooms, enhancing both earth and fruit tones.
palate: silky red fruit and subtle rocky grip

name: Estate Pinot Noir the Point Chehalem Mountains
description: A vibrant expression of volcanic Chehalem Mountains terroir this 2021 Rose & Arrow Estate The Point Pinot Noir presents elegant red fruit and mineral depth in seamless balance. Silky and refined yet quietly powerful it unfolds with raspberry and plum nuances and a whisper of black tea and river stone.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in a large Burgundy glass to coax out its fine-grained texture and pair with roasted duck breast or wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: raspberry and plum with black tea undertone
palate: silky texture with mineral-driven red fruit

name: Estate Pinot Noir Touchstone
description: The 2021 Rose & Arrow Estate Touchstone Pinot Noir unfolds with an elegant poise its structural precision and striking mineral tension are lithe yet commanding. Deep black raspberry and spiced cherry notes interlace with graphite and crushed rock nuances in a seamless dance of finesse and force.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in a large Burgundy glass to accentuate its fine-grained tannins lively acidity and layered texture. It pairs beautifully with roast duck breast, seasoned game birds or earthy mushroom risotto.
aroma: black raspberry and spiced cherry with graphite undertones
palate: silky texture, mineral-driven depth, fine-grained tannins

name: Rose & Arrow Touchstone Pinot Noir
description: This 2022 Rose & Arrow Estate Touchstone Pinot Noir captures the elegant tension of Eola‑Amity Hills volcanic terroir in a wine of poise and structure. Deep notes of black raspberry and spiced cherry mingle with crushed rock and graphite nuances lending coiled energy and refined power. The texture is supple yet firm with fine‑grained tannins and a slow‑building, resonant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a cool to moderate temperature to reveal its mineral precision; pairs beautifully with roasted duck or mushroom‑risotto – dishes that echo its earth‑driven elegance.
aroma: black raspberry with subtle graphite musk
palate: spiced cherry framed by mineral tension

name: Château Sainte Roseline Cotes de Provence Cru Classe Rose le Cloitre
description: An elegant pale salmon pink rosé from Château Sainte‑Roseline’s Cru Classé vintage, offering refined brightness and Provençal grace, enlivened by a playful nip of grapefruit edged with fresh cut grass and subtle herbal nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled at around 10 °C to highlight its citrus freshness. A graceful partner to simply prepared seafood or Provençal salads.
palate: well‑balanced, mouthcoating, citrus‑tinged

name: Famille Rotalier Beaujolais Villages sous le Chemin
description: An inviting Beaujolais‑Villages with supple grace and direct charm: ripe black cherry and gentle pepper swirl through a textured core of fresh berry fruit and subtle mineral nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled to heighten its vivacity its delicate spice and vibrant fruit make it a delightful partner to charcuterie or grilled meats.
aroma: ripe black cherry and peppery spice
palate: fresh berry fruit with textured mineral undertone

name: Famille Rotalier Brouilly Pisse Vieille
description: The 2021 Famille Rotalier Brouilly Pisse Vieille offers an elegant ruby hue and reveals bright aromas of black cherry underscored by earthy spice and mineral whispers. On the palate it is supple and poised, marked by gentle tannins and a delicate wave of wild strawberry and spice that lingers thoughtfully.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool at around 14 °C to accentuate its lively fruit and finesse. It pairs beautifully with charcuterie or soft cheeses, enhancing the wine’s graceful balance.
palate: supple, wild strawberry, gentle tannins

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Cuvee Prestige
description: This 2017 Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape from Domaine Jean Royer unfolds in refined layers of red cherry and raspberry cordial infused with Provençal garrigue and subtle game notes imparted by well‑judged maturation.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature it partner’s rustic lamb shoulder or wild mushroom ragout and benefits from moderate decanting to reveal its purity.
aroma: red cherry and raspberry with garrigue
palate: silky, focused, sweet red and blue fruit preserves
finish: long, sappy, with spice and floral echo

name: J.m. Royer Chateauneuf du Pape Sables de la Crau
description: This 2017 Châteauneuf‑du‑Pape “Les Sables de la Crau” from Domaine Jean Royer offers an alluring tapestry of sweet red fruits and floral overtones woven around sensuous, silky Grenache from sandy La Crau soils. It reveals elegance and purity, with a graceful medium‑bodied texture and a refined sense of energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve just at cellar temperature in a large glass, its bright red fruit and gentle spice complement Provençal lamb dishes or herb‑suffused ratatouille.
palate: silky medium‑bodied Grenache

name: Pinot Noir Classic Cuvee
description: A refined California Pinot Noir that captures the cool fog‑influenced allure of the Russian River Valley with purity of red cherry and soft earthy nuance, elegant and poised yet approachable in its youth.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 58 °F in a tulip‑shaped glass: it marries beautifully with roasted duck breast or grilled salmon.
aroma: red cherry with a whisper of forest floor
palate: silken texture with bright strawberry and cranberry notes

name: Saint Damien Cotes du Rhone Vieilles Vignes Plan de Dieu
appellation: Côtes du Rhône Villages Plan de Dieu
description: A beautifully wrought red from the southern Rhône this 2018 Saint‑Damien Côtes du Rhône‑Villages Plan de Dieu Vieilles Vignes presents harmonious notes of sun‑ripened black cherries and fragrant garrigue seasoned by gentle briny undertones, all enveloped in a finely balanced, plush texture that speaks of its venerable Grenache and Mourvèdre roots. The wine unfolds gracefully with a subtle sense of terroir‑driven elegance emerging from deeply rooted vines planted on stony clay‑rich soils in Plan de Dieu.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar temperature to accentuate its silky body; pairs exquisitely with herb‑crusted lamb, Provençal stews, or aged Comté to echo its savory nuance.
palate: silky, full‑bodied, briny undertones

name: Pinot Blanc
description: An elegant Alsace Pinot Blanc from Domaine Saint‑Rémy Ehrhart, the 2018 vintage presents a delicate yet crystalline personality with subtle orchard fruit and a hint of floral allure revealing its Burgundian echoes, refined and expressive in a graceful frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 8–10 °C in a classic white tulip or flute shaped glass, pairing beautifully with simply prepared freshwater fish or mild creamy dishes.
palate: fresh, stone‑fruit ripeness with gentle weight
finish: clean and lingering with a hint of almond

name: Pinot Blanc
description: An elegant Alsace Pinot Blanc from Domaine Saint‑Rémy Ehrhart, the 2020 vintage presents a delicate yet crystalline personality with subtle orchard fruit and a hint of floral allure revealing its Burgundian echoes, refined and expressive in a graceful frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 8–10 °C in a classic white tulip or flute shaped glass, pairing beautifully with simply prepared freshwater fish or mild creamy dishes.
palate: fresh, stone‑fruit ripeness with gentle weight
finish: clean and lingering with a hint of almond

name: Saint Remy Pinot Gris Grand Cru Brand
description: From a cool granite‑soiled hillside in Brand this Pinot Gris vintage unfolds with elegantly sun‑kissed candied citrus and quince‑paste framed by a subtle raisiny richness, all underpinned by breathable structure and textural grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C in wide tulip glasses to best reveal its poise; its gentle sweetness and mineral lift suit foie gras, poached pear, or mushroom‑accented poultry.
palate: raisiny richness with refined structure

name: Saint Remy Riesling Vieilles Vignes
description: A lithe and radiant expression of old‑vine Alsace Riesling, the 2019 Vieilles Vignes from Domaine Saint‑Rémy offers a crystalline core of lemon and green apple framed by fine mineral tension and a delicate floral undertone, finishing with elegant clarity and whisper of salinity.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at around 8–10 °C to enhance its bright acidity. Ideal with simply grilled seafood or light goat‑cheese preparations.
aroma: lemon blossom with green apple and flint
palate: bright citrus edged by fine mineral structure

name: Sarget de Gruaud Larose Saint Julien
description: The 2018 Sarget de Gruaud‑Larose unfolds with refined elegance offering plump black‑and blue‑berry fruit laced with subtle herbal nuance and a whisper of mint and cedar that lifts its mid‑weight frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool to reveal its freshness alongside roasted lamb shoulder or mushroom risotto to highlight its graceful fruit and fine tannins.
palate: mid‑weight fruit with herbal nuance and fine tannins

name: Château Haut Sarthes Bergerac Rouge
description: An eminently approachable Bordeaux‑style red from the eastern slopes of Bergerac, Château Haut Sarthes 2020 delivers ripe Merlot‑driven plushness and a gentle structure of Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc, offering easy charm with underlying depth derived from the iron‑rich soils of the region. It presents supple red fruit and an inviting warmth that promises both immediate pleasure and modest ageability.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in a medium tulip glass to reveal soft plum and warm berry nuances, complementing roast lamb or wild mushroom tart with its supple fruit and velvety texture.
aroma: plush red fruit with subtle earthy undertones
palate: soft, structured with gentle tannins

name: Haut Sarthes Montravel Blanc
description: A refined white Bordeaux from the southwest this 2023 Haut Sarthes Montravel Blanc unfolds with bright orchard fruit and gentle citrus brightness, anchored by a whisper of floral nuance and a cool mineral spine.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in slender glasses to showcase its crisp clarity; pairs beautifully with oysters or delicate seafood.
palate: fresh, elegant, mineral-tinged
drinkWindow: drink young to enjoy its freshness

name: Chardonnay
description: An elegant expression of Spring Mountain Chardonnay this wine reveals bright orchard fruit and citrus with a subtle nod to hazelnut and warm oak on the finish, unfolding in the glass with poise and refined tension.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 50–54°F in tulip glasses to best appreciate its clarity. Lovely with roasted chicken in a light cream sauce or grilled trout dressed simply with lemon and herbs.
palate: lively, refined tension
foodPairings: roasted chicken with light cream sauce
grilled trout with lemon and herbs

name: Vinho Verde Branco
description: A scintillating white from the cool Vinho Verde hills its whispers of citrus blossom and green apple tempered by vivid mineral clarity. Elegantly poised with vivid acidity it is a crisp, refined expression of Arinto and Azal in pristine harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 50 °F to elevate its bright freshness ideal alongside oysters or a simple goat cheese salad.
palate: zesty green apple and mineral drive

name: Chambolle Musigny Baudes
description: An elegant Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru from the modest yet noble Domaine Sérafin, the 2004 Les Baudes presents an understated bouquet of red and black fruit lifted by a whisper of spice, its texture refined and its structure gentle yet assured.
sommelierNotes: Serve just cool for maximum lift, alongside tender poultry or subtly gamy fare to echo its poised grace.
palate: silky, understated red‑fruit depth

name: Charmes Chambertin
description: An elegant and refined Grand Cru Pinot Noir from the Côte de Nuits, this 2004 Serafin Charmes‑Chambertin unfurls with precise aromas of ripe red cherries, mineral nuance and subtle earth, offering silky structure and supple richness grounded in tradition and concentration.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature in large Burgundy glasses to highlight its perfume and refined texture and pair with roasted loin of venison or classic boeuf en croûte.
palate: silky and refined with supple tannins

name: Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru les Cazatiers
description: A graceful expression of Côte de Nuits Pinot Noir this 2004 Sérafin Gevrey‑Chambertin Les Cazatiers unfolds with refined elegance, layering delicate red cherry and forest floor notes under a soft veil of toasted oak. The texture is poised with fine tannins and lingering mineral undertones that speak of its noble hillside origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 15 °C in a large-bowled glass to reveal its nuanced aromatics; pairs beautifully with roasted duck or earthy mushroom dishes.
aroma: red cherry and forest floor with a hint of toast
palate: elegant red fruit framed by fine tannins

name: Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru les Fontenys
description: This 2004 Serafin Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Les Fontenys shows the signature personality of the Côte de Nuits with a harmonious blend of lush cherry fruit and deftly integrated oak, layered over a firm spine of mineral‑tinged earth and subtle spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature to reveal the wine’s finesse and pair with richly flavored game or roasted lamb for a classic Burgundy match.
palate: earth‑driven and structured

name: Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes
description: The 2004 Sérafin Gevrey‑Chambertin Vieilles Vignes unfolds with discreet refinement showcasing old‑vine concentration, nuanced red cherry and forest floor underpinned by gentle oak detail and elegant structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in medium‑bodied decant; pairs beautifully with roast duck breast or coq au vin.
palate: elegant structure with gentle oak framing

name: Morey St. Denis Millandes
description: This 2004 Domaine Sérafin Morey‑Saint‑Denis “Les Millandes” 1er Cru unfolds with refined elegance its old‐world lineage, offering lifted notes of red cherry melded with subtle forest floor undertones, framed by an undercurrent of gentle spice and dusty earth. The texture is graceful yet focused, carrying fine tannins that suggest patience and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve it lightly chilled, around 14 °C, to reveal its nuance alongside game birds or a wild mushroom risotto.
aroma: red cherry, forest floor, gentle spice
palate: elegant, focused, fine tannins
foodPairings: duck breast with red berry reduction

name: Pere et Fils Bourgogne Rouge
description: This Bourgogne Rouge from Serafin Père et Fils 2012 presents a graceful weave of dark cherry and forest floor, framed by gentle oak that lends both depth and refinement. The structure is poised with fine-grained tannins and a lingering note of earthy spice, the type of Burgundy that rewards patience and quiet contemplation.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature to reveal its perfume of ripe red fruit and subtle underbrush, an ideal companion to roast duck or mushroom risotto.
palate: fine-grained tannins with earthy spice

name: Pere et Fils Bourgogne Rouge
description: Sérafin Père et Fils' 2014 Bourgogne Rouge shows mature Pinot Noir in a savory, quietly polished register. Red berries and plum meet cedar-toned spice, with enough freshness to keep the palate composed.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 15-16°C and open shortly before service; choose roast chicken, grilled lamb, or a simple mushroom tart.
palate: Soft red fruit, light earth, fine tannin

name: Pere et Fils Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru le Fonteny
description: An impeccably poised Pinot Noir from the revered domaine of Sérafin Père et Fils, the 2008 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Le Fonteny offers intense concentration and aristocratic bearing. It presents pure cassis and dark red berry essence underscored by subtle spice and refined structure. The oak is present yet harmoniously integrated yielding a wine of grace and power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in large tulip glasses to reveal its layered red fruit and earth tones, ideally paired with roast lamb or mature beef and aged mushroom dishes.
aroma: pure cassis and dark red berries
palate: elegant concentration with fine tannins and subtle spice

name: Pere et Fils Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru le Fonteny
description: An impeccably poised Pinot Noir from the revered domaine of Sérafin Père et Fils, the 2012 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Le Fonteny offers intense concentration and aristocratic bearing. It presents pure cassis and dark red berry essence underscored by subtle spice and refined structure. The oak is present yet harmoniously integrated yielding a wine of grace and power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in large tulip glasses to reveal its layered red fruit and earth tones, ideally paired with roast lamb or mature beef and aged mushroom dishes.
aroma: pure cassis and dark red berries
palate: elegant concentration with fine tannins and subtle spice

name: Pere et Fils Gevrey Chambertin 1er Cru le Fonteny
description: An impeccably poised Pinot Noir from the revered domaine of Sérafin Père et Fils, the 2014 Gevrey‑Chambertin 1er Cru Le Fonteny offers intense concentration and aristocratic bearing. It presents pure cassis and dark red berry essence underscored by subtle spice and refined structure. The oak is present yet harmoniously integrated yielding a wine of grace and power.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in large tulip glasses to reveal its layered red fruit and earth tones, ideally paired with roast lamb or mature beef and aged mushroom dishes.
aroma: pure cassis and dark red berries
palate: elegant concentration with fine tannins and subtle spice

name: Pere et Fils Gevrey Chambertin Lex Corbeaux
description: This 2011 Gevrey‑Chambertin Les Corbeaux from Sérafin Père et Fils offers an elegant expression of Côte de Nuits terroir, combining bright red and blue fruit perfume with a subtle smoke‑mineral thread and refined structure. The balance leans toward finesse rather than weight, with supple texture embracing firm yet poised tannins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, in the 14–16 °C range, with richly flavored fare such as roast venison or cabbage‑wrapped roulades.
palate: Elegant red‑fruit core, firm structure
foodPairings: Rare roast beef with seasonal vegetables

name: Pere et Fils Gevrey Chambertin Vieilles Vignes
description: A noble Burgundy of elegant stature from Serafin Père et Fils, its 2012 Vieilles Vignes exudes refined dark cherry and subtle floral silk with a whisper of earthy spice suggesting quietly brooding depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve with gentle aeration, best alongside roast game or autumn mushrooms to echo its forest‑floor nuance and supple tannin structure.
palate: silky red fruit with earthy spice

name: Domaine Serol Cote Roannaise Rouge Eclat de Granite
description: An elegant expression of Gamay Saint‑Romain grown on Côte Roannaise’s granite slopes: the 2018 Éclat de Granite unfolds with a deep ruby hue and vibrant aromas of red and black berries accompanied by a fine mineral and spicy thread. The palate is silky with seamless fruit, a tender yet precise mineral undercurrent, culminating in a lingering, mouthwatering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 14‑16°C to accentuate its freshness, pairing beautifully with light charcuterie, white meats or fresh cheeses.
aroma: red and black berries, mineral, spice
palate: silky, fruit‑driven, mineral‑tinged

name: Domaine Serol Cote Roannaise Rouge les Blondins
description: A supple Gamay Saint‑Romain from a granitic hillside of the Côte‑Roannaise the 2018 Les Blondins offers vibrant red fruits with a whisper of spice and a mineral undertow, rendered with restraint and clarity. It is poised yet graceful carrying elegance in every sip paired with unforced structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 14°C in a tulip glass to let its red fruit brightness and saline lift breathe. Fine with roast chicken or charcuterie platters for convivial enjoyment.
palate: fresh fruit framed by mineral clarity

name: Domaine Serol Turbullent Petillant Rose
description: An exuberantly bright pétillant rosé crafted in the ancestral tradition from Gamay Saint‑Romain grown on granitic, sandy foothill soils of the Loire Volcanique this wine offers joyous vivacity and crystalline freshness. The gently effervescent mousse carries notes of ripe raspberry, pear and delicate floral lift in a light, graceful frame. A delightfully playful wine showcasing the minerality and elegance that is the hallmark of Domaine Sérol.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–11 °C; an ideal companion to summer canapés or light seafood preparations to accentuate its vivacious red‑fruit sparkle.
palate: bright red‑berry freshness with minerally lift

name: Domaine Serol Turbullent Petillant Rose
description: An exuberantly bright pétillant rosé crafted in the ancestral tradition from Gamay Saint‑Romain grown on granitic, sandy foothill soils of the Loire Volcanique this wine offers joyous vivacity and crystalline freshness. The gently effervescent mousse carries notes of ripe raspberry, pear and delicate floral lift in a light, graceful frame. A delightfully playful wine showcasing the minerality and elegance that is the hallmark of Domaine Sérol.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled around 10–11 °C; an ideal companion to summer canapés or light seafood preparations to accentuate its vivacious red‑fruit sparkle.
palate: bright red‑berry freshness with minerally lift

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: This 2021 Shibumi Knoll Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley unfolds with a deep garnet-purple hue and an entrancing chorus of black raspberries, cassis, and black cherries followed by whispers of graphite and baking spices. The full‑bodied palate offers juicy black fruit layers framed by fine‑grained tannins and lively freshness, culminating in a long, spicy finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve with slight aeration at 60–64°F, an ideal companion to grilled rib‑eye or herb‑crusted lamb, cheeses such as aged cheddar or Comté.
aroma: black raspberries, cassis, black cherries, graphite, baking spices
palate: juicy black fruit, fine‑grained tannins, lively freshness

name: Chardonnay Buena Tierra Vineyard Russian River Valley
description: The 2022 Shibumi Knoll Chardonnay Buena Tierra Vineyard unfurls with a refined elegance, offering Meyer‑lemon brightness and a whisper of peach that feels at once inviting and precise. The texture is satin‑like, supported by soft acidity and a subtle savory undertone that lends the wine clarity and poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass to highlight its nuanced citrus and stone‑fruit layers. Pairs beautifully with seared scallops, creamy risotto or mild triple‑cream cheeses.
palate: delicate pear, roasted nectarine, soft acidity

name: Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast
description: A poised and elegant Pinot Noir that speaks of Sonoma’s coastal soul, it wafts red currant jelly and kirsch from a medium ruby‑purple glass, rounded by whispers of cinnamon stick and forest underbrush, delivering a lush, expressive palate with plush texture and refined lift on the close.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 55°F in a large Pinot stem to reveal its aromatic facets; pairs beautifully with roasted duck breast or mushroom risotto.
palate: plush expressive with herbal lift

name: Cantina Sorelli Chianti
description: An elegant red from the esteemed Sorelli house rooted in Tuscany’s storied Chianti tradition this wine unfolds in the glass with a refined ruby hue enveloping gentle violet accents and a subtle perfume of wild violet and ripe red berries. On the palate it is harmonious and dry with a sapid undercurrent and gentle tannic structure that resolves into a soft velvety texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to bring forth its aromatic clarity and pair with tomato‑based dishes or flavorful salumi for a classic Tuscan communion.
palate: harmonious, sapid, gently tannic

name: Chardonnay
description: Bright and inviting stainless‑steel fermented Chardonnay, its nose unfolding with orange blossom and violet then giving way to vivid impressions of lychee and kaffir lime leaf: a fresh and refined expression of California Chardonnay.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 50‑54°F in tulip glasses: the brightness of citrus and exotic fruit offers an elegant foil for creamy seafood dishes or mildly spiced Asian fare.
palate: lychee and kaffir lime

name: Conde de Subirats Cava Brut Rose
description: A delicate non‑vintage Cava from Subirats, the Conde de Subirats Brut Rosé presents a pale salmon hue and fine, frothy mousse. The wine offers a subtly floral and red‑fruit driven bouquet and a crisp, precise palate with a refined minerality and elegant balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip flute; pairs beautifully with smoked salmon, light seafood appetizers or fresh berries.
palate: crisp precise fruit with chalky minerality

name: Conde de Subirats Cava Brut Rose
description: A refined non‑vintage Cava from Subirats that presents a graceful salmon‑pink hue with lively, frothy bubbles, offering an elegant blend of cherry, blood‑orange and clove, underpinned by chalky soil tones and a subtle floral and bread‑dough nuance, delivering a crisp and full‑bodied expression with both depth and poised minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled as an aperitif or alongside delicate seafood, cured ham or citrus‑accented tapas, enhancing its bright acidity and precise mousse.
aroma: cherry and blood‑orange with clove and chalky soil
palate: crisp, full‑bodied with frothy mousse and precise minerality
finish: long, balanced grip with lingering chalky nuance

name: Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Saint Aubin 1er Cru les Frionnes
description: The 2021 Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Saint‑Aubin Premier Cru Les Frionnes offers poised finesse and refreshing clarity, delivering a mineral‑driven expression marked by citrus zest and a hint of toasted nuance, all framed in elegant structure. It reveals crystalline precision yet is generous with layered subtlety, reflecting the cool limestone soils of this under‑appreciated cru.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C after a brief decant to open the aromas, pairing beautifully with fine shellfish or creamy pasta dishes.
palate: mineral‑driven clarity with elegant structure

name: Domaine Sylvain Langoureau Saint Aubin 1er Cru sur le Sentier du Clou
appellation: Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru "Sur le Sentier du Clou"
description: An artful expression of Saint‑Aubin 1er Cru in a restrained 2021 vintage, this Chardonnay unfolds with fine citrus tones, crisp orchard fruit and an undertow of mineral clarity, all wrapped in a poised mid‑weight texture.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 12 °C to temper its racy acidity. A brief decant or glass resting will reveal its layered nuance.
aroma: citrus and orchard fruit with mineral clarity
palate: mid‑weight texture, crisp and poised
foodPairings: turbot or bar with light sauces

name: Domaine Sylvain Pataille Marsannay Chardonnay Rose
description: This luminous and beguiling Chardonnay Rosé from Marsannay shows delicate precision and nuanced old‑world elegance. The bouquet layers citrus blossom with a whisper of saline minerality and acacia perfume, leading to a refined mouthfeel that balances tension and subtle richness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 10 °C, allow a brief rest in the glass to ease any residual CO₂, and pair with shellfish or light seafood sauces for ideal harmony.
palate: tonic and vibrant with saline minerality
foodPairings: filet of John Dory with citrus butter
ceviche of royal prawns with citrus supremes

name: Sauvignon Blanc Marlborough
description: A pale straw hued Sauvignon Blanc from Marlborough it greets the glass with lively notes of citrus and passionfruit alongside a whisper of fresh-cut grass and subtle minerality, dancing across the palate with crisp, vibrant acidity and generous fruit purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tall white wine glass offering freshness and precision; pairs beautifully with chilled shellfish or delicate green salads.
palate: crisp vibrant acidity with fruit purity
foodPairings: oysters with a squeeze of lime

name: Alta Collection Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A polished expression of high‑elevation Mendoza Cabernet boasting vivid ruby hue, where ripe blackberry and plum jam unfurl with aromatic grace, while whispers of eucalyptus underscore the fruit, and oak‑touched coffee, vanilla and dark chocolate lend depth and warmth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in a large glass to coax forth its generous fruit tones and supple tannins; an ideal companion to grilled rib‑eye or aged hard cheeses.
palate: rich fruit framed by soft coffee, vanilla, dark chocolate

name: Alta Collection Chardonnay
description: This elegant Mendoza Chardonnay from Tapiz’s Alta Collection 2021 unfurls bright pear, citrus blossom and subtle tropical fruit notes framed by a whisper of French oak, offering a seamless interplay of freshness and depth. The high­altitude vineyard’s cool nights lend clarity and poise to the medium-bodied structure inviting contemplation now or over the next few years.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in tulip­shaped white wine glasses to appreciate its refined acidity and layered fruit. Pair with delicate seafood dishes such as seared scallops or creamy risottos enriched with herbs.
palate: ripe citrus and pear with oaky richness

name: Alta Collection Malbec
description: This Tapiz Alta Collection Malbec 2022 presents a noble garnet core with lifted aromas of blackberry and plum alongside a floral weave and a whisper of spice, all carried by elegant oak‑induced notes of vanilla and toasted almond. It unfolds with refined intensity and balance, offering a volumous yet poised expression of high‑altitude Mendoza.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled or at cellar temperature in a large Bordeaux glass to showcase its freshness. Pair with grilled short ribs or a rich tomato‑based pasta to complement its dark fruit and spice.
palate: refined intensity, balanced, smooth tannins

name: Black Tears Malbec
description: This expressive Malbec announces itself with a deep, purplish‑red hue and unfolds aromas of ripe red berries dried plum and fig, punctuated by subtle floral and menthol whispers, while its oak aging introduces dark chocolate and roasted coffee nuances, anchoring a poised and harmonious profile. The palate is richly layered yet refined with succulent compote‑like fruit framed by sweet, ripe tannins and an assured balance. Further coaxed by gentle oak, this wine exudes elegance with a compelling structure and persistent depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to showcase its vibrant fruit and silky tannins; pairs beautifully with grilled lamb, roasted beef or mushroom‑rich dishes.
aroma: ripe red berries, dried plum, fig, subtle floral and menthol
palate: compote‑like fruit, sweet ripe tannins, dark chocolate and coffee

name: Sparkling Malbec Rose
appellation: San Pablo Estate, Uco Valley, Mendoza
description: This non‑vintage Tapiz Sparkling Malbec Rosé exudes an elegant burst of cherry and strawberry accented by subtle red berries, carried aloft by persistent, fine perlage. The bright pink hue speaks of high‑altitude Mendoza fruit, while the extra‑brut profile lends a refined freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a flute or coupe to preserve its delicate mousse, an ideal palate cleanser before seafood or as a sparkling partner to light hors d’oeuvre.
palate: Fresh fruity balance

name: Sparkling Torrontes
appellation: Mendoza (San Pablo I.G., Valle de Uco)
description: This Tapiz NV Sparkling Torrontés exudes pale yellow hues with a green tinge and delicate bubbles that glide upward with refined persistence, offering an elegant interplay of citrus brightness and floral grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled, ideally with light seafood or crisp appetizers, to celebrate its vibrant acidity and aromatic charm.
palate: balanced acidity with varietal expression
finish: fresh and crisp with lingering florality
drinkWindow: drink now to within next 2–3 years

name: Chardonnay Do Atacama Valley
description: A luminous expression of northern Chile, this 2021 Tara Chardonnay unfolds in the glass with crystalline clarity and a saline whisper that speaks of its desert origins, layered with ripe white fruit and a radiant citrus seam.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‐shaped white wine glass to highlight the bright acidity and mineral texture, a superb companion to grilled scallops or buttery shellfish.
aroma: grapefruit and pear with a saline, mineral undercurrent
palate: creamy lees texture with quince, citrus and a touch of ginger

name: Tara Chardonnay Do Atacama Valley
description: A luminous expression of northern Chile, this 2022 Tara Chardonnay unfolds in the glass with crystalline clarity and a saline whisper that speaks of its desert origins, layered with ripe white fruit and a radiant citrus seam.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‐shaped white wine glass to highlight the bright acidity and mineral texture, a superb companion to grilled scallops or buttery shellfish.
aroma: grapefruit and pear with a saline, mineral undercurrent
palate: creamy lees texture with quince, citrus and a touch of ginger

name: Pinot Noir Do Atacama Valley
description: From the high, salt‑laden terraces of the Huasco valley in Chile’s Atacama Desert this Pinot Noir unfurls with a resonant mineral core and crystalline dark‑berry fruit framed by floral whispers, a wine sculpted by sea fog and stony soils, marked by precision and subtle austerity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C, ideally decanted; pairs gracefully with roasted duck, earthy mushrooms, and herb‑accented game.
aroma: black cherries, wild berries, floral and stony tones
palate: structured, linear, persistent acidity with mineral tension
foodPairings: game such as venison or wild boar

name: V8 Tara Viognier Do Atacame Valley
