description: This Tara Viognier V8 is a rare and thoughtful white wine born of the solera tradition in Chile’s Atacama Desert. Its aromatic profile unfolds in layers of candied orange peel, orange blossom, lime, sponge cake and dried fruit, all wrapped in a crystalline saline complexity that speaks of its austere, mineral soils. The palate is defined by tension and freshness yet broad structure and a persistent, saline finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled to around 10‑12 °C in a tulip glass to reveal the wine’s layered aromatics; will pair beautifully with seared duck, oily fish or rich shellfish, accentuating both its saline edge and textural depth.
aroma: candied orange peel, orange blossom, lime
palate: broad yet tense, fresh and structured
drinkWindow: up to 7–8 years from solera blend creation

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Monterrey Peninsula
description: A polished California Cabernet from Monterey’s coastal vineyards offering generous blackberry and cassis tones layered with a hint of vanilla and cedar. Medium‑bodied with supple tannins and gentle spice framing the fruit core, elegant yet approachable.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled at cellar temperature to showcase its plush fruit and structure. Complements grilled red meats or aged cheddar.
palate: medium‑bodied, supple tannins, dark fruit core
drinkWindow: Drink now to short‑term cellaring (3–5 years)

name: Chardonnay Monterrey Peninsula
description: The 2024 Tassajara Chardonnay from Monterey California is richly textured yet gracefully cut by brisk acidity. Its charm lies in a seamless fusion of ripe stone fruit with a subtle toasty oak presence, rendering it inviting and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 50 to 54°F in a classic white Burgundy glass. Lovely alongside creamy seafood dishes or subtly spiced poultry preparations.
aroma: ripe stone fruit with soft toasty oak
palate: elegant stone fruit framed by balanced acidity
foodPairings: clam chowder with leeks and bacon

name: Pinot Noir Monterrey Peninsula
description: This 2023 Tassajara Pinot Noir from Monterey Peninsula evokes sun‑warmed dark cherry and blackberry tempered by a whisper of sage and subtle earthiness, offering an elegant and soothing sip with an old‑world sense of place. Its profile is refined yet accessible, a wine that feels both softly plush and grounded in coastal terroir.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to enhance its brightness, pairing beautifully with simply prepared poultry or mushroom risotto to complement its earthy and red fruit expression.
palate: lush blackberry, gentle herbal lift

name: Sauvignon Blanc Monterrey Peninsula
description: This 2023 Tassajara Sauvignon Blanc from Monterey County unveils a bright and spirited profile marked by invigorating citrus, guava and grapefruit aromas, gently weaving into a palate of green apple and apricot accented by delicate herb notes. It carries an elegantly refreshing energy with clarity and focus, reflecting the cool coastal influence of Monterey.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip-shaped glass to enhance aromatic clarity; pairs beautifully with chilled seafood, goat cheese salads or light pasta with fresh herbs to complement its crisp vivacity.
palate: green apple, apricot, fresh herbs

name: Tempo D'angelus Bordeaux Rouge
description: This red Bordeaux offers refined structure and a graceful flow of dark fruit accented by gentle oak: it conveys clarity and poise rather than overt power. It balances Bordeaux pedigree with youthful accessibility, inviting enjoyment now while retaining composure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to around 16 °C in medium-bowled glasses, pair with roasted meats or firm cheeses to echo its supple texture and bright acidity.
aroma: fresh red berries with subtle oak
palate: vertical, fresh fruit with fine acidity

name: Tempo D'angelus Bourdeaux Rouge
description: A wine of refined structure and vibrant energy this Tempo d’Angelus 2019 delivers clarity of dark red fruit with an underpinning of gentle oak. It is elegantly framed yet approachable exhibiting purity of fruit and a poised architecture.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16–18 °C and pair with roasted lamb or aged cheeses to balance its freshness and subtle tannic grip.
aroma: fresh red berries with discreet oak
palate: vertical, with fine acidity and pure fruit
finish: lingering with subtle roasted oak notes

name: Tenuta Olim Bauda Barbera D'asti la Villa
description: A precise expression of Asti’s youthful intensity this Barbera d’Asti “La Villa” 2024 offers a vivid ruby‑red hue, with a scented bouquet of cherry and wild berry accented by floral undertones, a tone‑perfect harmony of generous fruit and uplifted freshness.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled around 16°C to heighten its vivacity, an elegant companion to Italian salumi or gently spiced pastas.
palate: full‑bodied yet fresh and well‑balanced
finish: long, pleasant, balanced between acidity and structure
foodPairings: Tagliatelle with Robiola di Roccaverano and zucchini flowers

name: Domaine de la Terre Rouge Garrigue Sierre Foothills
description: The 2014 Garrigue from Terre Rouge is an evocative red blend where two‑thirds Syrah and one‑third Cabernet Sauvignon coalesce into a wine redolent of Sierra Foothills terroir. Savoury and darkly fruited the wine offers spine and sophistication with its herbal, earthy nuances conjuring the local chaparral.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in a broad‑rimmed glass to highlight savory complexity, ideal with grilled lamb chops or mushroom‑infused dishes.
palate: earthy savory with black‑fruit depth

name: Domaine de la Terre Rouge Syrah Ascent
description: This commanding Syrah ascends with extraordinary concentration and aromatic intensity, as the finest eight barrels of the vintage are selected from varied Sierra Foothills sites rooted in granite and volcanic soils   the 2016 bottling unfolds layers of deeply concentrated spicy black fruit, smoky nuances and a mineral-edged structure wrapped in fine tannins
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar temperature where its velvety texture and architectural tannins can unfold   ideal with richly seasoned roasted meats or aged charcuterie
aroma: deep spicy black fruit, smoky wood tones
palate: meaty Syrah flavors, exotic spices, mineral undertones
finish: long structured finish with fine tannins

name: Domaine de la Terre Rouge Syrah les Cotes de I'ouest
appellation: Clements Hills AVA blending Sierra Foothills
description: A vibrant expression of Sierra Foothills Syrah that speaks with an elegant voice of wild raspberry and smoky game wrapped in gentle sage and olive‑herb nuances, its deep hue hinting at both power and refinement.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in wide bowls to reveal its savory complexity pairing beautifully with grilled lamb or rich charcuterie.
aroma: wild raspberry, smoky game, pepper, cinnamon
palate: silky, savory wild fruit with sage and olive‑herb tones

name: Domaine de la Terre Rouge Tete a Tete
description: With elegant richness and an inviting Californian sensibility this wine unfolds generous boysenberry and wild berry aromas infused with a smoky, gamey undercurrent that speaks of rugged Sierra foothills terroir, its texture creamy and mouth filling yet balanced
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature in generous glasses to allow the savory undertones to open, lovely with grilled lamb or hearty stews
aroma: deep boysenberry with smoky gamey nuances
palate: sappy, spicy, mouth filling with creamy texture
finish: lengthy and smooth with savory persistence

name: Syrah Ascent
description: This is a formidable expression of California Syrah: intensely concentrated yet refined layers of black-plum and exotic spices emerge through a smoky undercurrent, while firm tannins and minerally depth lend age-worthy structure and complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted to open the spicy, meaty aromas; excellent with grilled lamb or braised short ribs.
palate: dense, meaty, smoky layers

name: The Cider Farm Classic Dry Cider
description: This Classic Dry Cider presents a noble expression of English cider apples in a crisp, refined style. Crafted from varieties such as Kingston Black, Dabinett, Major, Somerset Redstreak, Chisel Jersey alongside a backbone of Liberty for balance it offers firm tannic structure and a clean finish steeped in old‑world orchard character. It evokes the elegance of traditional cider making where the apple’s own personality is the leading note.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a tulip or stemmed glass to showcase its tannic clarity and interplay of apple complexity. Pair it with aged cheddar, charcuterie, or a platter of savory pork sausages to complement its dry framing.
palate: structured tannin‑driven apple clarity

name: The Cider Farm Equinox Cider
description: An elegant cider framed by the subtle herbaceous character of Equinox hops, this offering marries green grassy freshness with citrus brightness reminiscent of a New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc, underpinned by the depth and structure of true cider apples organically grown on‑site.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in tulip or white wine glass to accentuate its wine‑like freshness, pairs beautifully with soft chèvre or light seafood salads.
palate: bright citrus with herbaceous clarity

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Gris Estate
description: A pale straw‑gold Pinot Gris that combines Old‑World restraint with Oregon’s structural clarity, marked by delicate floral and orchard fruit layers and a lingering whisper of salinity and almond nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip glass to retain its perfume; pair with oysters, soft goat cheese or light herb‑ridden poultry.
aroma: honeysuckle and pollen with golden apple
palate: ripe pear, apricot, white pepper
finish: long, polished with a hint of almond cookie

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Gris the Eyrie
description: The 2023 The Eyrie Vineyards “The Eyrie” Pinot Gris offers a graceful interplay of ripe melon and honeyed citrus underscored by beeswax and tarragon, all lifted by savory mineral undertones and an elegant glycerin richness. It is compelling yet light on its feet, with a polished and lingering finish that reflects the vintage’s dynamic character.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 50–52°F to accentuate its freshness. Ideal with shellfish, delicate poultry or mildly spiced Asian fare.
palate: medium‑full body with glycerin richness and savory mineral lift
finish: long polished finish with bitter almond nuance

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Daphne
description: The 2022 Eyrie Vineyards Daphne Pinot Noir is a refined expression of Dundee Hills elegance. It unfolds with crystalline clarity, revealing rose petal, pine‑needle herb, wild strawberry and dark cherry layers that dance over a mineral‑laced structure. The wine exhibits a graceful poise that balances tension and lush ripeness in seamless harmony.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to open its floral lift, ideally alongside game birds or earthy mushroom risottos to complement its aromatic depth and silky texture.
aroma: rose petal, wild strawberry, pine herbs
palate: pure dark cherry, herbal lift, silken tannins

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Estate Dundee Hills
description: A refined expression of Dundee Hills terroir emerges in this 2022 Eyrie Vineyards Estate Pinot Noir, offering an elegant interplay of forest floor and vibrant red fruit. It presents vivid notes of wild raspberry and rose petal underpinned by warm spices and a fine mineral thread that accentuates its poised balance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature in a burgundy glass to best reveal its perfume and energy. Pair with duck à l’orange or mushroom‑risotto to echo its earth and fruit harmony.
aroma: wild raspberry, rose petal, forest floor
palate: bright red fruit, silky tannins, mineral spice

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Outcrop
description: The 2022 Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Outcrop delivers a pale ruby hue and an expressive floral perfume of candied raspberries and sweet alpine herbs, its savoury structure marked by tea leaf and mountain herb nuances. This medium‑bodied cuvée, from north‑north‑east facing Wadenswil clone plantings in Dundee Hills, exhibits elegant balance and a lingering complexity born of precise organic viticulture.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature, ideal with roast duck or mushroom‑laden dishes to echo its herbal complexity.
aroma: candied raspberries and sweet alpine herbs
palate: savory tea leaf and mountain herb structure

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir Roland Green
description: The 2022 Eyrie Vineyards Roland Green Pinot Noir presents an upright frame of refined texture and depth, marked by layers of fresh black raspberry, mossy forest floor and cherry blossoms that unfold with air. It balances muscular architecture with elegant poise and savory undertones that speak of its volcanic Dundee Hills roots.
sommelierNotes: Serve in a generously sized tulip glass after gentle aeration to appreciate its layered nuance. Pair with roasted duck breast or mushroom‑risotto for a match to its earth‑borne complexity.
palate: muscular yet elegant with savory earth

name: The Eyrie Vineyards Pinot Noir the Eyrie
description: From the Willamette Valley’s original planting by David Lett, this 2022 ‘The Eyrie’ Pinot Noir welcomes the glass with transparent ruby tones and evocative scents of cherry‑driven fruit, crushed pine needles, wild floral notes, mineral underbrush and subtle savory spice, all underpinned by a sinewy structure and a long resonant finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled or at cellar cool temperatures in tulip‑shaped glasses to allow the wine’s fine‑grained tannins, bright acidity and forest‑floor nuances to unfold. Pair with forcemeat–laden terrines, wild mushroom risotto, or slow‑roasted duck breast.
aroma: wild cherry, pine needles, forest underbrush
palate: silky, cherry‑fruited, mineral‑taut

name: Domaine Lucien Thomas Pouilly Fuisse
description: A refined Pouilly‑Fuissé from the swooping slopes of Mâconnais bearing Lucien Thomas’s signature style, the 2022 vintage unveils a luminous golden hue. On the palate it offers a graceful interplay of citrus‑tinged freshness and gentle orchard fruit, framed by a whisper of minerality that nods to its terroir’s clay‑limestone character.
sommelierNotes: Serve cool in a slender tulip glass at around 10–12 °C to reveal its purity, particularly charming alongside delicately sauced veal or creamy shellfish preparations.
palate: fresh orchard fruit underpinned by fine minerality

name: Domaine Lucien Thomas Saint Veran
description: This wine reveals a radiant clarity with crisp green apple and citrus zest, enlivened by a subtle mineral undercurrent that speaks of Maconnais limestone.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled to accentuate its focused acidity and pair with delicate seafood or a creamy pasta, enhancing its freshness and refined structure.
palate: crisp, mineral-driven, focused

name: Kenward Family Wines Cabernet Sauvignon Oakville
description: A richly layered Oakville Cabernet from TOR, the 2022 Kenward Family Wines Oakville offers a vibrant fusion of red, black and blue fruit with graphite-tinged minerality and a subtle forest‑floor allure, elevated by warm baking spices such as cinnamon, clove and nutmeg drawn from its iron‑rich Double H and Renteria 360 vineyards.
sommelierNotes: Serve decanted to reveal its layered complexity enjoy with grilled ribeye or braised short ribs.
aroma: blackberry and black cherry with forest floor nuance
palate: rich dark fruit balanced by graphite minerality and baking spice
finish: long savory finish with spice dusting

name: Tor Kenward Family Wines Charddonnay Hyde Cuvee Susan
description: This 2023 TOR Kenward Family Wines Hyde Vineyard Cuvée Susan Chardonnay presents an elegant richness underpinned by pure Carneros tension, exuding refined layers of magnolia blossom, Asian pear and honeydew, complemented by subtle ginger warmth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled in a broad-bowled glass to reveal the wine’s textural silkiness, and pair with a buttery lobster roast or seared fatty ahi tuna.
aroma: magnolia blossom, Asian pear, honeydew melon
palate: rich and dense with lanolin texture and touch of ginger

name: Tor Kenward Family Wines Chardonnay Curvee Torchiana
description: This 2023 Tor Kenward Family Wines Chardonnay Cuvée Torchiana delivers a refined expression of Napa’s storied Carneros terroir: perfumed with green gage plum and pineapple on the nose it presents a sappy yet elegant allure; the medium-bodied palate is finely textured and luminous across its length, revealing a satisfying silkiness through the finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 50–54 °F; its harmonious texture and bright fruit make it an exquisite companion to seared scallops with beurre blanc or grilled halibut.
palate: fine silky medium‑bodied texture

name: Kenward Family Wines Pure Magic Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: Plush yet refined, the 2022 TOR Kenward Family Wines Pure Magic reveals itself with a seamless flow of black cherry and violet overtones graced by a whisper of white pepper, weaving through rich dark chocolate and espresso that linger long after the glass is sipped.
sommelierNotes: Serve just below cellar temperature to accentuate elegance, and pair with rare roast beef or grilled portobello with truffle butter for a sublime match.
aroma: black cherry and violet with white pepper
palate: silky sweet/round tannins and dark chocolate

name: Winery Willamette Valley Pinot Gris
description: This Willamette Valley Pinot Gris from Torii Mor offers a luminous pale hue, inviting with a gentle whisper of ripe pear and citrus blossom followed by refined mineral brightness and a touch of ginger-scented fruit.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to emphasize its bright acidity, pairing beautifully with light shellfish, lemon‑dressed salads, or subtly spiced Asian cuisine.
palate: fresh mineral brightness with ginger‑tinged fruit

name: Winery Willamette Valley Pinot Noir
description: The 2023 Torii Mor Willamette Valley Pinot Noir unfolds with a refined melody of red cherry and raspberry beneath a whisper of forest floor and rose petal. Elegant and poised, the palate delivers polished tannins and vivid acidity framing vibrant red fruit, with subtle baking spice lingering softly.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to open up nuanced floral notes. Pair with roasted duck breast or mushroom risotto to harmonize with the wine’s earth‑bright character.
palate: silky red fruit, bright acidity, refined tannins
finish: long graceful red‑fruit echo with spice

name: Cava Brut Rosado
description: A charming Rosado crafted by the venerable Torre Oria House this NV Cava presents a delicate raspberry‑pink hue, its fine bubbles rising in elegant rosaries, exuding a bright, clean aromatics of fresh red berries woven with lively subtlety. On the palate the mousse is refined and harmonious, a balanced structure with an ample personality and natural, gently persistent effervescence.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C as a refreshing aperitif or with light seafood hors d’oeuvre, smoked salmon canapés or delicate salads.
aroma: fresh red berries with crisp raspberry lift
palate: balanced, ample structure with fine persistent mousse

name: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Bourgogne Cote D'or
description: A gracious Bourgogne Côte d’Or from Domaine Cécile Tremblay the 2019 vintage unfurls with cherry brightness and fine mineral underpinnings a seamless weave of Vosne‑Romanée and Chambolle‑Musigny provenance adds structure and energetic purity.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool cellar temperature to highlight lifted red fruit and vibrant acidity pairs elegantly with modest roast poultry or tender game birds.
aroma: cherry and wild berries with subtle soil nuance
palate: satiny texture, powdery tannins, bright acids

name: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Bourgogne Rouge Cote D'or
description: An elegantly poised Bourgogne Rouge from Domaine Cécile Tremblay’s 2017 vintage presents refined red fruit underpinned by subtle earth and spice accents, its texture silky and its structure harmonious, offering an elegant expression of Côte d’Or origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled around 16 °C in Burgundy glasses to reveal its delicate perfume, paired beautifully with roast duck or wild mushroom risotto.
palate: silky red fruit with earthy spice

name: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Chambolle Musigny 1er Cru les Feusellottes
description: This 2017 Domaine Cécile Tremblay Chambolle‑Musigny Premier Cru Les Feusselottes unfolds with an ethereal bouquet of wild red cherry, rose petal and delicate forest floor nuances, layered over a whisper of exotic spice and fine oak. On the palate there is a graceful interplay of silk‑fine tannins, vibrant red fruit and a chalk‑inflected minerality, culminating in a lingering, subtly perfumed finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool 16 °C in a medium‑bowl Pinot Noir glass; pairs beautifully with roasted duck, game birds or rich mushroom preparations for a harmony of texture and finesse.
aroma: wild red cherry and rose petal
palate: silk‑fine tannins, vibrant red fruit with chalky minerality

name: Domaine Cecile Tremblay Chambolle Musigny les Cabottes
description: An elegant expression from Chambolle‑Musigny, this 2017 Les Cabottes by Domaine Cécile Tremblay unfolds with discreet floral notes that give way to a generous core of dark cherry and spice, underscored by a subtle mineral tension from uncompromised Pinot Noir in whole‑cluster vinification.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 16 °C after an hour in the decanter to reveal its silk‑like texture; particularly enchanted by roasted duck breast or a delicately aged Époisses.
palate: velvety, concentrated red fruit, mineral lift

name: Château Boyd Cantenac Margaux
description: A wine of stately refinement this Margaux bears a deep garnet hue, suggesting presence and poise. On the palate it delivers succulent black fruit and cedar‑tinged nuance interwoven with firm noble tannins in an elegant, assured structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool around 17 °C to showcase its elegant cabernet‑led architecture. It will reward patience over the next decade alongside lamb, roasted game or aged cheeses.
palate: ripe black fruit with refined tannins

name: Txakoli Zudugarai Txakoli Malda
description: A crystalline expression of traditional Basque Txakoli from Getariako Txakolina this 2024 Zudugarai Txakoli Malda sings with coastal charm: brisk lime zest, crunchy green melon and white blossoms on a frame of sea salt and minerality, offering a bright and insinuating tension that both refreshes and intrigues.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in slender glasses to accentuate its vivacious acids make it a spellbinding companion to oysters clams or grilled sardines.
aroma: lime zest, green melon, white blossoms
palate: crisp, soil‑driven, citrus and herbal nuances

name: Folias de Baco Uivo Moscatel Galego Branco
description: An elegant and airy white crafted from organic Moscatel Galego Branco vines at altitude in Cima‑Corgo Portugal, this 2022 Uivo offers a refined floral‑tinged lilt of rose and lychee over fresh herbal notes and minerality with a crisp balanced frame.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C to showcase its lift and minerality, ideal as an aperitif or alongside delicate fish and shellfish.
palate: vibrant, mineral‑driven, refreshing

name: Folias de Baco Uivo Pt Nat Branco
description: Pale yellow and softly effervescent, this pétillant naturel displays a delicate play of green apple and grapefruit peel underscored by floral wild‐flower notes it conveys a refreshing sense of place and minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6–8 °C alongside shellfish or light summer salads to let its vivacious acidity sing.
aroma: ripe tropical fruit and wild flowers
palate: medium bodied with delicate lingering acidity

name: Folias de Baco Uivo Pt Nat Curtido
description: A delicate natural sparkling petillant‑naturel from Folias de Baco’s Uivo project youthful and effervescent with a soft pale yellow hue and a lively bead expressing ripe tropical fruit and wild floral perfume with an ethereal cloudiness.
sommelierNotes: Serve ice‑cold between 6 °C and 8 °C. Perfect as a solo aperitif on a warm afternoon or alongside shellfish, lightly flavored fish, and crisp summer salads.
aroma: ripe tropical fruit and wild flowers
palate: medium‑bodied with delicate persistent acidity

name: Folias de Baco Uivo Renegado Vinhas Velhas
description: A field blend from Douro’s ancient vines that captures a beguiling elegance its pale red hue and lively red‑berry energy are underlined by subtle herbal whispers and a faint toast nuance that intrigue the senses.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled at 8‑10 °C to highlight its refreshing brightness it complements grilled meats or rich fish and shines on its own during a languid summer eve.
aroma: bright red berries with herbal and toasty undercurrents
palate: light and refreshing with salivating acidity

name: Bodegas Uvaguilera Palomero Vendemia Seleccionada (Do Rivera Del Duero)
description: The 1999 Bodegas Uvaguilera Palomero Vendimia Seleccionada emerges gently from time, offering an editorial elegance of quintessential Ribera del Duero character, woven with refined notes of aged noble fruit and whispering leather against a backdrop of subtle spice.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar temperature in large crystal glasses to invite the wine’s tertiary complexity, pairing it beautifully with roasted venison or aged Manchego for balance.
palate: ripe dark fruit with fine-grained tannins

name: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Blanc le Pave
description: Le Pavé 2020 from Domaine Vacheron offers an elegant, mineral‑charged expression of Sancerre Sauvignon Blanc, where oyster‑shell and wild‑flower aromas meld with pear and lemon zest in a refined, steely architecture, culminating in a poised yet powerful experience.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled around 50 °F in a tulip glass to accentuate its precision and pair with oysters, delicate shellfish, or chèvre frais.
palate: pear and lemon zest with steely minerality

name: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Rouge
description: A refined and expressive Loire Valley Pinot Noir that speaks of Sancerre’s noble flint‑ridden terroir, the 2022 Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Rouge presents vibrant cherry and raspberry aromas underlined by rose petal and subtle savory undertones, evolving into a silky mid‑palate of red fruit purity and poised minerality.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled in fine‑bowled glasses to showcase its delicate clarity, pairing beautifully with roasted poultry or charcuterie to match its elegance and lively acidity.
palate: silky red fruit with mineral precision

name: Domaine Vacheron Sancerre Rouge Belle Dame
description: The 2016 Domaine Vacheron “Belle Dame” Sancerre Rouge opens with a refined bouquet of dark cherry and forest berry laced with rosemary and juniper herbaceousness held aloft by the clarity of its flint‑strewn terroir. On the palate the wine is lithe yet structured a poised dance of earthy black fruit and fine tannin culminating in a mineral‑tinged, pepper‑spiced finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at around 15 °C after light aeration to reveal its silk‑textured elegance a splendid match for grilled venison or aromatic river fish.
palate: mineral‑tinted dark berries, herbal spice

name: Albarino
description: This 2020 Vara Albariño presents a refined and luminous expression of California Albariño, offering lively lime peel and kiwi aromas underpinned by grassy nuance, followed by a palate of apricot and nectarine framed by citrus pith and crisp structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled alongside light seafood or citrus‐accented salads to highlight its bright, electric acidity and invigorating fruit clarity.
palate: apricot, nectarine, citrus pith

name: Vara Albarino
description: This 2021 Vara Albariño presents a refined and luminous expression of California Albariño, offering lively lime peel and kiwi aromas underpinned by grassy nuance, followed by a palate of apricot and nectarine framed by citrus pith and crisp structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled alongside light seafood or citrus‐accented salads to highlight its bright, electric acidity and invigorating fruit clarity.
palate: apricot, nectarine, citrus pith

name: Fine Spanish Brandy
description: This Fine Spanish Brandy from Vara caresses the palate with gentle warmth and refined elegance, offering subtle whispers of Medjool dates and toasted coconut alongside a plush, honeyed sweetness and a whisper of saddle‑leather complexity. The solera aging contributes a creamy, rich character framed by soft dark caramel and nutmeg nuances.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or in a snifter to reveal its depth: pairs beautifully with dusky chocolate desserts or a fine aged cheese plate.
palate: Honey, dark caramel, nutmeg rich and mouth‑filling
drinkWindow: Ready to enjoy now, holds well over next several years

name: Garnacha
description: A graceful, unfussy expression of Spanish Garnacha, this youthful 2020 bottling from Vara offers inviting red-cherry and wild strawberry notes that mingle with a subtle touch of black olive and dried cranberry, all lifted by bright, playful energy.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 60–62 °F in a standard red glass to accentuate its freshness, pairing beautifully with roast chicken or autumnal root‑vegetable dishes.
palate: fresh, juicy with dried cranberry brightness

name: High Desert Gin
description: A velvety artisan gin that evokes the stark elegance of New Mexico’s high desert. Crafted from a grape‑based high spirit and thirteen botanicals, it greets the nose with juniper and citrus overtones, enriched by sage and anise before revealing a serene, creamy nuttiness.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled or in refined cocktails such as a Collins or Gin and Tonic to awaken its floral facets; a gentle drop of water or ice unlocks deeper aromatics.
palate: bright citrus with coriander and creamy nuttiness

name: Paso Uno
description: This clear unaged artisan brandy is crafted by Vara Distillery in New Mexico, born from a single alquitara distillation of local wine. It offers graceful pear and floral whispers on the nose, and a smooth medium‑bodied texture with white plum and lily nuances that speak of an elegant unfiltered spirit.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled or on the rocks to appreciate its fresh orchard fruit and floral clarity, or lengthen with soda or tonic and a twist for a refined aperitif.
palate: white plum, pear, rose and lily
foodPairings: tonic with a citrus peel twist

name: Rum Anejo
description: Vara Rum Añejo is an artisanally crafted New Mexico rum distilled from rich dark molasses and patiently aged to achieve harmonious complexity. Its aromas of caramelized sugar and vanilla glide seamlessly into a palate that murmurs of wood spice, caramelized sugar, and roasted nuts.
sommelierNotes: Serve neat in a snifter to appreciate its warm, inviting depth or elevate a Dark ’n Stormy with gentle character.
palate: wood spice, caramelized sugar, roasted nuts

name: Rum Blanco
appellation: New Mexico: Vara Winery and Distillery
description: A bright crystalline blanco rum from Vara Winery and Distillery in New Mexico presenting a gentle herbal and tropical fruit bouquet with underlying grassy undertones, the elegantly layered spirit offers an engaging balance that recalls classic white rum tradition while remaining supple and refined.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled or over ice in a highball glass garnished with fresh citrus; works superbly in mojitos mingling mint and lime, or in delicate daiquiris that accentuate its nuanced structure.
aroma: tropical fruit and green herbal lift
palate: earthy balance with clean vibrant character
drinkWindow: Drink now through next few years

name: Silverhead Brut
appellation: Ancient Lakes AVA, Washington and Alt Penedès DO, Spain
description: A refined celebration in a bottle, the Silverhead Brut Non‑Vintage glimmers with delicate mousse carrying bright pear, grapefruit and almond aromas. An elegant interplay of creamy texture and lively acidity leads to layered flavors of green apple, chamomile and toasty brioche that linger in a long, graceful finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in slender flutes to preserve its finesse. It pairs beautifully with oysters, lobster mac and cheese or light fried hors d’oeuvres.
palate: creamy mousse, green apple, honeysuckle, brioche

name: Silverhead Brut Rosado
appellation: Ancient Lakes AVA, Washington / California blending
description: A pale rosy jewel pouring delicate mousse against a warm grey backdrop this American sparkling rosé exudes refined grace. Notes of wild raspberry, red currant and gentian blossom emerge on the nose while the palate unfolds with quince, tangerine zest and a whisper of shortbread in a focused, dry framework.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled as an elegant aperitif or alongside richer fare such as roast duck with fig and fennel, or red beet risotto with crispy jamón.
palate: quinces and tangerine zest with creamy mousse
foodPairings: roasted duck with figs and fennel
red beet risotto with crispy Spanish jamón
wild mushroom pâté with blackberry glaze

name: Tempranillo
description: A youthful expression of Tempranillo from the Vara estate offering vivid red fruits and a note of earth that speaks of honest craftsmanship, this 2020 bottling brings a direct and approachable energy to any cellar.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 60 °F in a broad-bowled glass to enjoy its bright fruit and subtle minerality: it pairs well with grilled meats or rustic charcuterie.
palate: bright red fruit with grounded structure

name: Vermut Anejo Dulce
description: An elegant vermouth that speaks of old‑world ritual through New Mexico craftsmanship, this NV VARA Vermut Añejo Dulce unfolds in layered sweetness balanced by aged oak depth
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a rocks glass over large ice cube, with an orange twist or as the sweet counterpoint in a Manhattan
palate: rich dried fruit wrapped in gentle woody bitters

name: Vermut Seco
description: This vermouth presents a delicate interplay of chamomile and white tea atop a soft honeyed weave supported by a crisp thread of mint and alpine herb nuance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled or on the rocks as a refined aperitif its poised herbal character harmonizes with light seafood or creamy soft cheeses.
palate: honeyed with mint and alpine herbs

name: Albarino
description: Veiga Naúm Albariño 2020 presents a pale straw‑yellow robe, delicate yet expressive, with floral notes of jasmine and orange blossom mingling with orchard fruits such as pear and apple. On the palate it unfolds with energetic freshness and a creamy mid‑palate, offering vibrant citrus and stone‑fruit flavors underpinned by saline minerality and a lingering finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled around 6 to 8 °C alongside shellfish or light summer fare for a bright contemporary expression of Rías Baixas.
palate: creamy citrus with saline minerality

name: Jane Ventura Cava Gran Reserva
description: A noble expression of Penedès tradition, this 2015 Gran Reserva from Jané Ventura marries Macabeo and Xarel·lo in a refined interplay of textural elegance and quiet power, showing delicate pastry notes beneath a core of ripe orchard fruit and gentle citrus lift. The extended ageing imparts subtle layers of brioche and hazelnut that enrich without overpowering, delivering a wine of poised radiance and poised endurance.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled to unveil fine mousse and fresh orchard aromas; an ideal partner to light seafood starters or buttery shellfish, or to contrast with creamy mild cheeses.
palate: creamy texture with citrus‑tinged ripeness

name: Helen Keplinger Wines Vermillion Red Blend
description: This 2022 Vermillion Red Blend by Helen Keplinger offers a sumptuous tapestry of California’s Rhône‑styled fruit with beguiling layers of blackberry, spiced plum and dark cherry, enriched by aromatic accents of star anise, crushed lavender and cocoa, delivering a richly textured yet gracefully balanced expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly below room temperature to reveal silky tannins and vibrant acidity, ideal alongside grilled red meats or herb‑accented dishes.
palate: silky, fruit‑driven, well‑balanced

name: Wines Beckstoffer Dr Crane Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This 2023 Vice Versa wines Beckstoffer Dr. Crane Cabernet Sauvignon is a brooding and noble expression of gravel‑strewn St. Helena terroir intensity rendered with unwavering grace and poise, a wine of density and refined precision. It layers dark cassis‑tinged florals with graphite‑tinged red fruit texture in an artful interplay of power and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in a large-bowled glass after a decant to reveal its floral lift and satin tannin; pairs well with slow‑roasted beef rib or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: crème de cassis and violets with wet‑stone minerality
palate: dense layered black fruit texture with precise tannins
foodPairings: roasted rib‑eye with herbes de Provence

name: Wines Beckstoffer Dr Crane Cabernet Sauvignon
description: This 2023 Vice Versa wines Beckstoffer Dr. Crane Cabernet Sauvignon is a brooding and noble expression of gravel‑strewn St. Helena terroir intensity rendered with unwavering grace and poise, a wine of density and refined precision. It layers dark cassis‑tinged florals with graphite‑tinged red fruit texture in an artful interplay of power and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cellar‑cool temperature in a large-bowled glass after a decant to reveal its floral lift and satin tannin; pairs well with slow‑roasted beef rib or aged hard cheeses.
aroma: crème de cassis and violets with wet‑stone minerality
palate: dense layered black fruit texture with precise tannins
foodPairings: roasted rib‑eye with herbes de Provence

name: Wines Beckstoffer Georges III Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A majestic expression of Rutherford, this 2023 Vice Versa Cabernet Sauvignon from Beckstoffer Georges III Vineyard reveals brooding layers of ripe black currant and dark plum woven with graphite and dusty earth. It exudes aristocratic poise with polished tannins and a refined, long‐lasting finish.
sommelierNotes: Serve at 60–62 °F in large Bordeaux tulip glasses to allow its complex aromatic spectrum to unfurl. It pairs splendidly with grilled flank steak with herb‑infused jus or aged Comté.
palate: ripe dark plum, polished tannins, balanced structure
finish: long regal finish with mineral lift
foodPairings: grilled flank steak with herb jus

name: Wines Beckstoffer Las Piedras Cabernet Sauvignon
appellation: Beckstoffer Las Piedras Vineyard, St. Helena, Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Vice Versa Wines Beckstoffer Las Piedras Cabernet Sauvignon reveals a hauntingly dark ruby hue and a perfumed bouquet of blackberry, dark fig, and cherry liqueur, edged by old cedar box, tobacco spice, and dark cocoa powder, an elegant invocation of the rocky terroir. On the palate it unfolds with harmonious layers of boysenberry, black plum and chalky minerality, its silhouette built of supple yet tensile tannins and vibrant acidity, offering early approachability with fine aging potential.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled toward 60–62 °F in a large Bordeaux–style glass, decant for an hour for optimal integration, and pair with grilled rib‑eye, braised short ribs or aged Gouda.
palate: boysenberry, black plum, chalky mineral

name: Wines Beckstoffer Las Piedras Cabernet Sauvignon
appellation: Beckstoffer Las Piedras Vineyard, St. Helena, Napa Valley
description: The 2023 Vice Versa Wines Beckstoffer Las Piedras Cabernet Sauvignon reveals a hauntingly dark ruby hue and a perfumed bouquet of blackberry, dark fig, and cherry liqueur, edged by old cedar box, tobacco spice, and dark cocoa powder, an elegant invocation of the rocky terroir. On the palate it unfolds with harmonious layers of boysenberry, black plum and chalky minerality, its silhouette built of supple yet tensile tannins and vibrant acidity, offering early approachability with fine aging potential.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled toward 60–62 °F in a large Bordeaux–style glass, decant for an hour for optimal integration, and pair with grilled rib‑eye, braised short ribs or aged Gouda.
palate: boysenberry, black plum, chalky mineral

name: Wines Spinning Plates Cabernet Sauvignon
description: An elegant and muscular Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon that weaves opulent black berry fruit with graphite and tobacco leaf into a seamless tapestry of refinement. Dark chocolate and herbal undertones lend depth and poise to the concentrated yet impeccably balanced structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature with a rich lamb tagine or aged Gouda, allowing its fine ripe tannins and savory finish to sing.
palate: dark chocolate, black cherry, savory herbs

name: Wines Spinning Plates Cabernet Sauvignon
description: An elegant and muscular Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon that weaves opulent black berry fruit with graphite and tobacco leaf into a seamless tapestry of refinement. Dark chocolate and herbal undertones lend depth and poise to the concentrated yet impeccably balanced structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature with a rich lamb tagine or aged Gouda, allowing its fine ripe tannins and savory finish to sing.
palate: dark chocolate, black cherry, savory herbs

name: Wines Spinning Plates Cabernet Sauvignon
description: An elegant and muscular Napa Valley Cabernet Sauvignon that weaves opulent black berry fruit with graphite and tobacco leaf into a seamless tapestry of refinement. Dark chocolate and herbal undertones lend depth and poise to the concentrated yet impeccably balanced structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled at cellar temperature with a rich lamb tagine or aged Gouda, allowing its fine ripe tannins and savory finish to sing.
palate: dark chocolate, black cherry, savory herbs

name: Vignes de Coulous Cadillac Liquoreux
description: This sweet Cadillac from Les Vignes de Coulous 2020 draws from an ancient parcel of old‑vine Sémillon planted before 1960. It offers a vibrant sweetness and tension born of its gravelly terroir and biodynamic ethos.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled, between 8 and 12 °C, as a refined companion to foie gras, blue cheese, or fruit‑based desserts.
palate: luminous sweetness balanced by crisp freshness

name: Villa Amelie Chardonnay Non Alcoholic Wine
description: This alcohol‑removed Chardonnay from Villa Amélie exudes an elegant clarity rooted in classic French tradition: bright orchard fruit and pear blossom unfold with precision and poise, crafted via a meticulous de‑alcoholization method that preserves purity while evoking the essence of Chardonnay.
sommelierNotes: Serve chilled in a tulip‑shaped glass to reveal its subtle floral lift, ideal with chilled shellfish or a light summer salad.
palate: pure, fresh, light

name: Villa Amelie Merlot Cabernet Non Alcoholic Wine
description: An elegant alcohol‑removed red crafted in southern France from estate Merlot and Cabernet, this nuanced pour balances gentle dark fruit whispers with subtle spice accents offering a refined and expressive character without compromise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled, a modern wine‑style alternative splendid with light hors d’oeuvres or a thoughtful evening shared in mindful company.
aroma: dark berry and soft spice notes
palate: silky mouthfeel with balanced fruit and faint structure

name: Villa Amelie Sparkling Non Alcoholic Wine
description: An elegantly effervescent non‑alcoholic Blanc de Blancs from Villa Amélie, crafted from Souvignier Gris grapes, offering refined freshness and delicate fruit charm without artifice. Each bubble carries the gentle grace of white‑fleshed fruit and floral nuance in a purely natural expression.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a flute or tulip glass to heighten its delicate mousse, perfect as a refined aperitif or with light hors d’oeuvres such as citrus‑dressed shellfish or fresh salads.
palate: fresh, delicate fruit with refined mousse

name: Avenger
description: The 2022 Villa Creek Avenger unfurls like a deep oxblood tapestry rich in black fruits, smoked meats and Moroccan spice layered with sweet tobacco and caramel. The palate is luxuriously textured, offering plum and bacon‑fat nuances underpinned by vibrant energy, making it both inviting now and worthy of time in the cellar.
sommelierNotes: Serve at cool room temperature after brief decanting to allow its smoky, savory layers to bloom and pair it confidently with grilled ribeye or spiced lamb.
aroma: seductive dark fruits with smoked meats and Moroccan spices
palate: rich black plum, caramel and bacon‑fat, energetic

name: Farmhouse Red Paso Robles
description: This radiant Farmhouse Red offers lifted spice notes and citrus‑tinged sour cherry across an inviting bouquet, while silken textures mingle with mineral‑kissed red berries and a whisper of savory complexity.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 60 °F in generous stemware and pair with lamb ragù or herbed roast chicken to complement its spicy, hedonistic nature.
aroma: citrus‑zest and sour cherries with savory spice
palate: silken textures, juicy red berries, mineral lift
finish: lingering licorice and sage with fresh acidity

name: Farmhouse White Paso Robles
description: This is a lithe and sun‑kissed white from Paso Robles exuding orchard brightness and floral nuance. It brings a lovely tension of soft stone fruit and pear framed by tangy saline lift and a whisper of lemon rind.
sommelierNotes: Serve this gracefully chilled in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass and pair with light fare such as shellfish or delicate salads to let its shimmering acidity sing.
palate: white peaches, cream‑touched orchard fruit
finish: lemon rind with lively mineral lift

name: Villa Creek Farmhouse White Paso Robles
description: This is a lithe and sun‑kissed white from Paso Robles exuding orchard brightness and floral nuance. It brings a lovely tension of soft stone fruit and pear framed by tangy saline lift and a whisper of lemon rind.
sommelierNotes: Serve this gracefully chilled in a tulip‑shaped white wine glass and pair with light fare such as shellfish or delicate salads to let its shimmering acidity sing.
palate: white peaches, cream‑touched orchard fruit
finish: lemon rind with lively mineral lift

name: Sunseeker Red Paso Robles
description: The 2024 Villa Creek Sunseeker Red shows a joyful bounce of wild mountain strawberry and mint lifting red cherry‑tinged fruit in a lively, charming expression. A soft, round texture carries a core of juicy berry fruit enlivened by a whisper of clove and sage rooted in Paso Robles’s minerality, all finishing with grace.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly chilled around 56‑58 °F to heighten freshness, perfect with spring‑herb roasted chicken or a field‑blend inspired charcuterie plate.
aroma: wild mountain strawberry, mint, red cherry
palate: juicy berry core, soft round texture, sinewy mineral lift
finish: long, tension‑filled finish with rose‑tones and tart raspberry

name: Baker & Hamilton Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley
description: This 2022 Baker & Hamilton Cabernet Sauvignon from Vine Hill Ranch offers a richly layered expression of Oakville terroir, brimming with dark currant fruit, sappy floral underbrush and earthy accents. It unfolds with opulent structure and remarkable energy, the fine-grain tannins and vibrant acidity lending both breadth and elegance.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to cellar temperature around 60–62°F in large Bordeaux glasses and pair with roasted lamb, aged beef or wild mushrooms to balance its tannic structure and savoury depth.
aroma: dark currants, smoke tobacco, sappy flowers
palate: dense plum and boysenberry with fine-grain tannins
finish: lengthy, spicy and driven by vibrant acidity

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Napa Valley Vine Hill Ranch Vineyard

sommelierNotes: Serve well chilled in a flute or tulip glass at around 45°F to preserve its delicacy; it pairs beautifully with delicately flavored seafood, fine charcuterie or fresh berry desserts.
palate: fresh, lively, mineral-driven
drinkWindow: drink now or cellared for up to a decade

name: Yarden Wines Cabernet Sauvignon
description: A commanding Cabernet Sauvignon from Israel’s storied Golan Heights expresses poised concentration with ripe blackcurrant and cherry framed by tobacco, earth and French oak, offering a regal sense of structure and depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted at cellar temperature to match rich roasted lamb or beef dishes, allowing the wine’s elegant concentration to resonate.
aroma: ripe black and red fruits, tobacco, earth
palate: full body, concentrated flavor, French oak spice
drinkWindow: drink now or cellar for 10+ years

name: Wines Chardonnay
description: A refined expression of Chardonnay drawn from the elevated volcanic terrain of the Golan Heights, this 2024 Yarden Chardonnay offers layers of bright citrus, pear and tropical flower notes enfolded in gentle French oak nuances, its full body grounded with a refined texture and poised clarity.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently chilled to reveal its elegant interplay of fruit and oak; ideal with creamy poultry or subtly spiced seafood, or a soft cheese platter.
palate: full‑bodied, flavorful, fresh with balanced acidity
foodPairings: pan‑seared halibut with lemon caper sauce

name: Wines El Rom Cabernet Sauvignon
description: From the sun‑kissed volcanic heights of northern Golan, this elegant 2021 Yarden Cabernet Sauvignon El Rom unfolds layers of lush red and black fruit over subtle herb, cassis, cocoa and earthy undertones, framed by 18‑month French oak integration. The result is a full‑bodied expression of poise and depth with real old‑world structure.
sommelierNotes: Serve with rich lamb confections or roasted red meats to marry the wine’s dense fruit and noble tannins; decant gently to reveal its harmony.
aroma: ripe black and red fruit with cassis, herb, cocoa
palate: full‑bodied, concentrated dark fruit, fine‑grained tannins
finish: lingering spice, earth and tobacco whispers
foodPairings: beetroot risotto with sage and hazelnuts

name: Wines Galilee Rose
description: This Yarden 2021 Galilee Rosé offers a graceful interplay of vibrant red fruits and energetic acidity balanced with a hint of floral intrigue.
sommelierNotes: Serve well‑chilled in a slender tulip glass to preserve its freshness and pair with light Mediterranean fare.
palate: watermelon and lime zest

name: Wines Katzrin Cabernet Sauvignon Merlot
description: A regal and plush red Bordeaux blend from the Golan Heights under the Yarden Katzrin label offering layered complexity and gravitas. Rich black cherry and plum fruit mingle with dark chocolate, aromatic herbs and subtle blood‑orange zest delivering a poised and concentrated expression. Structured yet alluring the wine unfolds with a lingering finish fit for memorable occasions.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled at cellar temperature allow gentle decanting to reveal its layers. Ideal beside grilled steak or roast lamb with herb accents.
aroma: ripe black cherry, dark chocolate, herbs and orange zest
palate: full‑bodied and concentrated with black fruit, earth and spice
foodPairings: roast lamb with rosemary and garlic
drinkWindow: peak in few years, excellent for over a decade

name: Yarden Wines Merlot
description: This 2022 Yarden Merlot offers layered aromas of ripe red and black fruits with a whisper of Provençal herbs and tangerine peel, all framed by supple French oak integration. Full‑bodied yet refined it displays depth and balance that speak to the complexity of its Golan Heights origins.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool around 16 °C to highlight its fresh fruit character. Ideal with roasted lamb or richly sauced beef.
aroma: ripe red and black fruit with herbs and tangerine
palate: full‑bodied and balanced with integrated oak
foodPairings: rack of lamb with Merlot glaze

name: Wines Sauvignon Blanc
description: A refined expression of Israeli Sauvignon Blanc drawn from the cool volcanic soils of the northern Golan Heights, this 2024 Yarden Sauvignon Blanc offers lifted aromas of guava, passionfruit, lime and melon, the faint suggestion of French oak lending gentle depth.
sommelierNotes: Serve lightly chilled with fresh goat cheese, grilled fish or a herb‑bright salad to let its vibrant fruit and subtle texture sing.
palate: green apple with flinty mineral tones and medium body
foodPairings: goat cheese ravioli with lemon pesto

name: Wines Syrah
description: A regal and sumptuous Syrah from Israel’s famed Golan Heights this 2021 Yarden exudes layered aromas of blackberry, cassis, and blueberry, entwined with whispers of earth smoked meat and exotic spice, revealing both muscular structure and elegant poise.
sommelierNotes: Serve gently decanted to reveal its full harmony, splendid alongside rich lamb dishes or a wild mushroom ragout.
aroma: blackberry cassis blueberry with smoked meat and spice
palate: full bodied dark fruit and polished tannins

name: Cabernet Sauvignon
description: The 2023 Zolo Cabernet Sauvignon from Mendoza reveals an inviting bouquet of ripe red berries with a whisper of mint and spice, flowing into a fresh mid‑weight palate layered with juicy dark fruits and soft oak nuances. The wine draws the senses into a harmonious dance of fruit and subtle structure crafted for pleasure.
sommelierNotes: Serve slightly cool in sturdy crystal glasses to accentuate the bright fruit character. Delightful alongside grilled lamb or herb‑roasted chicken.
aroma: ripe red berries, mint, gentle spice
palate: fresh dark fruits with soft oak

name: Cabernet Sauvignon Reserva
description: This Mendoza Cabernet Sauvignon Reserva 2019 by Zolo presents a polished ensemble of ripe plum and cassis framed by subtle notes of black pepper and dark chocolate drawn from oak influence, delivering well‑balanced richness and structure with a refined sense of length.

name: Malbec
